{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"👠 [External] Virtual Try-On (VTO)","url":"https://www.notion.so/342c370222d580d881e2c0e92ebffff6","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/342c370222d580d881e2c0e92ebffff6 as of 2026-04-15T15:57:09.381Z: {"title":"\\[External\\] Virtual Try-On (VTO)"} FLUX VTO lets you generate virtual try-on results from a person image plus one or more garment references. It is optimized for low latency and is currently available to approved partner organizations. You can try it out directly here: [Black Forest Labs - Frontier AI Lab](https://showcase-vto.preview.bfl.ai/) Your domain should be already whitelisted, but in case that you do not have access to the app: please let us know! ## Before / After examples ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/4c6dc6ab-0a98-4845-94a2-af6b47c76abc/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466TSKXVHBY%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151853Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJIMEYCIQC0IU1KnT7VUhHSIqkgiQ5AwoArcU%2F06ihVF1LUHbzxOQIhAPQIMbmN70dEIW7PirEXkNehDdbvEAll20eCWlSzNA0GKv8DCAgQABoMNjM3NDIzMTgzODA1Igx9fZNbpog3WtobzVYq3AMBb0KJtRgFhZ7mTVx2T9hwgLO7MnCtSoCwAbXJKnS6Fslwc%2FWlFluDFLzJUqGrc0BQ2cretuUBPuG3Lyzb04fUEv2e9eLKzOXY%2FTjng7cDQVcnYF%2BhgFahOcq3917dktQEqyo8R%2BtQRh9%2BldhiCtocjcH82GW3%2BMLD44Va3dspMsDStoiN1zHYWW4BJWl2iiwb7MerXfjJ2VxfuFYzij%2FWlIiSXISIND4gbZIJ4yLauKc5nlv2qdzHLkXNQ%2FR0RFvTGtrfeLMUVc9P%2Fj3hPXIde1H7fljQlWREZzPD3POf%2BSfrBFLJYQJ2ef%2BycTz0DwA5r34%2FvAtGrePMvnyb3cpfOU7c%2BFT6BIvcA283D4GQVPYt7aTPvbjPYNa2LBj%2B4cBEV7P9eDf8PGCfApVsfu61jcHc%2BHYknHl0fPilDqQI%2B7dkfREyuG809lok%2B%2BCoJj0Ta8jC8pcFBco1RWuJ1SJKi0I4ZLmiyKm3MzXBFT9yJEKrPiIwjuUlp12%2BN4rM3%2BwyW2PZfvHYPm%2FxDzEffLej%2B1IUgULCVqtOQvxdisshcmnZVfRxtFv9KhEZd8aCS61ocpqr6zlu1sunX5hgp5boeE0pYQP0kCgSYa%2BAQ2KqSzWoUrHvHg6ckzKgUDDC0JPPBjqkATlpW6N7IbwxoHMFBHethhyf6d8rFGu7Yy%2BDn5vfQnsZZeeVKM7cdH3jxAUBv6FVzWMk0ZNf0D8V78SQk7FlgKPgodXblp7R1WvROVy40N2h2zEeHpV7EB7HE6jjXqLgUwUtDVG503DS5NG%2FFQnX%2BBvWABKQTfVzdCpbKaJzhe4EkNTqyrEZKKFwwD%2FZ%2F2jccClSpXZ5LhhjrTZ%2FEkGG%2B3I3%2BFpn&X-Amz-Signature=ec61712daf7593c57223c6e926290f6c8dbb44bdfdb134bf3c9cf8fd507c6397&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) --- ## Get started in 30 seconds **1. Get access + API key** You need: - an approved API key - organization access to the VTO route If you are not sure your project is allowlisted, contact the BFL team. **2. Submit a VTO request** ```bash PERSON_B64="$(base64 < /path/to/person.png | tr -d '\n')" GARMENT_B64="$(base64 < /path/to/garment_top.png | tr -d '\n')" # Optional second garment (for bottom, jacket layer, etc.) GARMENT2_B64="$(base64 < /path/to/garment_bottom.png | tr -d '\n')" jq -n \ --arg person "$PERSON_B64" \ --arg garment "$GARMENT_B64" \ '{ prompt: "model is wearing the provided garments, realistic studio lighting, clean background", person: $person, garment: $garment, garment_2: (if $garment2 == "" then null else $garment2 end), width: 1024, height: 1024, output_format: "png" }' > /tmp/vto_request.json curl -sS -X POST "https://labs.eu2.bfl.ai/v1/flux-try-on" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Key: $BFL_API_KEY" \ --data-binary @/tmp/vto_request.json ``` Response: ```json {"id":"xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx","polling_url":"..."} ``` **3. Poll for your result** ```bash curl -sS "https://labs.eu2.bfl.ai/v1/get_result?id=YOUR_TASK_ID" \ -H "X-Key: $BFL_API_KEY" ``` When `status` is `"Ready"`, use `result.sample`. --- ## Performance tip If you want to send 2 or more garment images, we recommend merging them into a single canvas first to keep latency down. In our testing, we could not notice any quality degradation from doing this. ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/ca070cd9-81da-4dfc-af0d-3fdc829da054/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466TSKXVHBY%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151853Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJIMEYCIQC0IU1KnT7VUhHSIqkgiQ5AwoArcU%2F06ihVF1LUHbzxOQIhAPQIMbmN70dEIW7PirEXkNehDdbvEAll20eCWlSzNA0GKv8DCAgQABoMNjM3NDIzMTgzODA1Igx9fZNbpog3WtobzVYq3AMBb0KJtRgFhZ7mTVx2T9hwgLO7MnCtSoCwAbXJKnS6Fslwc%2FWlFluDFLzJUqGrc0BQ2cretuUBPuG3Lyzb04fUEv2e9eLKzOXY%2FTjng7cDQVcnYF%2BhgFahOcq3917dktQEqyo8R%2BtQRh9%2BldhiCtocjcH82GW3%2BMLD44Va3dspMsDStoiN1zHYWW4BJWl2iiwb7MerXfjJ2VxfuFYzij%2FWlIiSXISIND4gbZIJ4yLauKc5nlv2qdzHLkXNQ%2FR0RFvTGtrfeLMUVc9P%2Fj3hPXIde1H7fljQlWREZzPD3POf%2BSfrBFLJYQJ2ef%2BycTz0DwA5r34%2FvAtGrePMvnyb3cpfOU7c%2BFT6BIvcA283D4GQVPYt7aTPvbjPYNa2LBj%2B4cBEV7P9eDf8PGCfApVsfu61jcHc%2BHYknHl0fPilDqQI%2B7dkfREyuG809lok%2B%2BCoJj0Ta8jC8pcFBco1RWuJ1SJKi0I4ZLmiyKm3MzXBFT9yJEKrPiIwjuUlp12%2BN4rM3%2BwyW2PZfvHYPm%2FxDzEffLej%2B1IUgULCVqtOQvxdisshcmnZVfRxtFv9KhEZd8aCS61ocpqr6zlu1sunX5hgp5boeE0pYQP0kCgSYa%2BAQ2KqSzWoUrHvHg6ckzKgUDDC0JPPBjqkATlpW6N7IbwxoHMFBHethhyf6d8rFGu7Yy%2BDn5vfQnsZZeeVKM7cdH3jxAUBv6FVzWMk0ZNf0D8V78SQk7FlgKPgodXblp7R1WvROVy40N2h2zEeHpV7EB7HE6jjXqLgUwUtDVG503DS5NG%2FFQnX%2BBvWABKQTfVzdCpbKaJzhe4EkNTqyrEZKKFwwD%2FZ%2F2jccClSpXZ5LhhjrTZ%2FEkGG%2B3I3%2BFpn&X-Amz-Signature=8ed28db84ac290dbae0dacd5fb38349e10f7bf89d83f3d9ea5ec859a0ede5886&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) --- ## Python quick start ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 import base64 import os import time import requests API_KEY = os.environ["BFL_API_KEY"] BASE = "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai" HEADERS = {"X-Key": API_KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json"} PROMPT = "model is wearing the provided garments, realistic fabric detail" PERSON_PATH = "/path/to/person.png" GARMENT_PATH = "/path/to/garment_top.png" GARMENT2_PATH = None # optional with open(PERSON_PATH, "rb") as f: person_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() with open(GARMENT_PATH, "rb") as f: garment_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() payload = { "prompt": PROMPT, "person": person_b64, "garment": garment_b64, "width": 1024, "height": 1024, "steps": 2, "output_format": "png", } if GARMENT2_PATH: with open(GARMENT2_PATH, "rb") as f: payload["garment_2"] = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() submit = requests.post(f"{BASE}/v1/flux-try-on", headers=HEADERS, json=payload) submit.raise_for_status() meta = submit.json() task_id = meta["id"] poll_url = meta.get("polling_url", f"{BASE}/v1/get_result?id={task_id}") while True: r = requests.get(poll_url, headers={"X-Key": API_KEY}) r.raise_for_status() result = r.json() status = result.get("status") if status == "Ready": print("Result URL:", result["result"]["sample"]) break if status in {"Error", "Request Moderated", "Content Moderated", "Task not found"}: raise RuntimeError(f"VTO failed with status: {status} | payload: {result}") time.sleep(1) ``` --- ## Input fields Use `person` + `garment` as the minimum payload.
Field Type Required Notes
--- --- ---: ---
`prompt` string yes Natural-language styling instruction
`person` base64 string no\* Person image (mapped to `input_image`)
`garment` base64 string no\* Garment reference/references (mapped to `input_image_2`)
`width` int no `>=64`, max total output 4MP
`height` int no `>=64`, max total output 4MP
`steps` int no `1-4`, defaults to 4
`seed` int no For reproducibility
`output_format` string no `jpeg` (default), `png`, `webp`
`webhook_url` URL no Async callback
`webhook_secret` string no Signature secret
- In practice, provide at least `person` and `garment` for useful try-on behavior. --- ## Prompting tips - Keep prompts focused on fit, pose consistency, lighting, and material realism. - Mention garment category and desired drape, for example: denim jacket, oversized tee, tailored trousers. - If identity preservation matters, explicitly ask to preserve face, hairstyle, and body proportions. Example prompts: - `person wearing provided bomber jacket, preserve face and pose, realistic fabric wrinkles` - `swap upper body garment only, preserve lower body clothing and background` - `fit provided top and bottom garments, full body fashion photo, clean studio lighting` --- ## Key details
**Endpoint** `POST https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/v1/flux-try-on`
**Auth** `X-Key: $BFL_API_KEY`
**Result polling** `GET https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/v1/get_result?id=`
**Access** Restricted allowlist (partner orgs + internal)
--- ## Troubleshooting - `403 Forbidden`: your project or org is not allowlisted for VTO. - `422`/validation errors: check base64 encoding and field types. - Poor garment transfer: tighten prompt wording and ensure garment reference is clean and well-lit. "}

This should be tested in the next pre-train phase where image editing is included. ## Smaller Text Encoder --- The current plan is to have Klein as a 9B model and Schnell as a 4B model. A 24B text encoder is too large for users. The strategy for swapping out the text encoder is to train in 3 phases
1. txt_in layer only (rand. init), use LR=1e-4, no warmup 2. all txt layers: txt_in and double_txt blocks, use LR=3e-5, warmup 3. all layers (with LR=3e-5, warmup) ### Phase 1 Using a high learning rate allows the new txt_in layer to quickly adapt:

Here’s a breakdown: - The post-train set is roughly 1-2 million samples. The baseline did: - 10k initial steps, then swapped the text encoder and did 5k double txt block steps and 5-15k all param steps (depending on the eval). - In total that’s 10k steps on 64 nodes and 10-20k steps on 32 nodes. With batch size of 1, that gives 3.8-5.1 million samples total. - Max tokens used was: 24576, a 1k image is around 4096 tokens, so in the pure t2i case we have batch size of 6 (not considering text tokens). A reasonable estimate is an average batch size of 2-3. - A very rough estimate is that we’ve seen each image around 7 times ### Mid-Train Redo There were a few issues with the previous mid-train → post-train approach: 1. Adapting a new text encoder at post-train complicates experiments 2. Text rendering isn’t great 1. Likely needs more steps to align the new encoder 3. For some reason Klein 4B at 26k (2k safety) steps looks particularly good for i2i. This is likely noise, however we will use it anyways. (so klein 9b - 20k and klein 4b - 26k). After, ran dpo for 1k steps for both 9B and 4B. ### Realism Sweeps - mu = \[0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0\] - t2i ratio = \[0.33, 0.5, 0.66, 0.75\] Varying these parameters has a minimal effect ### Hockey Stick Sampler - take 2x smaller steps near the end of the schedule - very minimal effect when using 100 steps (low prio, moving on) ### PAG Distillation - Teacher and student initialized to model after realism tune - Prepare sample as \[uncond, cond\] - Teacher makes prediction using PAG - Student makes prediction without PAG - (this ensures the conditional predictions are unchanged) The quality of the samples without pag look much more reasonable after the realism fine-tune. {"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"[Marketing Agencies] Our Partnership Strategy","url":"https://www.notion.so/26cc370222d5801688aad3f676a3262e","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/26cc370222d5801688aad3f676a3262e as of 2026-04-15T12:57:26.542Z: {"title":"\\[Marketing Agencies\\] Our Partnership Strategy"} ### TL/DR Marketing agencies are reorganizing around AI to move from slow, manual creative work to fast, automated, performance-driven production, supported by internal platforms like Omni, Vermeer, and Song. To serve them, BFL should offer a modular Agency License, API access, dev models, client-hosted rights, and optional reseller terms, anchored in clear licensing and meaningful minimum commits. ## Summary --- 1. Marketing Agencies mainly want AI **to make campaigns faster, cheaper, and more effective;** creating content automatically, updating it in real time, and moving away from slow manual work and hourly fees toward results-driven production. 2. To achieve this, these companies are rapidly re-organizing around by: - Creating **dedicated innovation labs** and **technical teams** that blend creatives, engineers, and data experts. - They are also building **internal AI platforms** that sit across the entire organization, giving thousands of employees access to generative tools inside unified systems (e.g., Omnicom’s “Omni”, Havas’s “Vermeer”, Accenture’s “Song AI”, etc.). - Agencies also aksi **shifting their business models** toward high-velocity, on-brand, AI-assisted production, focusing on workflows like iterative editing, brand-specific generation, and automated content pipelines instead of traditional handcrafted creative. 3. As a result, **Agencies need a flexible AI offering** that allows for API access for thousands of employees, dev models for technical labs to customize and fine-tune, and client-hosted rights for delivery work. Agencies are uniquely positioned to provide brand interpretation and workflow expertise, which would be challenging for BFL to replicate at scale. Our goal is to offer high-performance models, clear licensing terms, and well-aligned incentives to ensure that customers realize the value of our models, and that it directly translates to increased revenue for us and the agency. 4. The best way forward is a **modular Agency License** with four components: 1) API Access, 2) Dev Model Access, 3) Client-Hosted Add-On, and 4) Reseller Add-On. We will leverage minimum commits to capture value up-front, output caps to avoid losing value on scale, and rev shares/referral fees on efforts that require deeper partnership or commitment from BFL and the Agencies. ### 📊 Marketing Agency Landscape {toggle="true"} - The **Marketing Agencies** market size is estimated at \$453Bn in 2025, and is expected to reach USD 571.53 billion by 2030, at a CAGR of 4.8%. The key trends include **increased adoption of AI in creative development**, rapid scaling of performance-based pricing contracts, and cookie-less personalization technologies are reshaping how brands evaluate agency partnerships. [Source](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/global-marketing-agencies-market) - The key players continue to be fairly concentrated, with the top five groups: WPP, Omnicom, Publicis Groupe, Interpublic Group, and Dentsu, collectively accounting for a significant portion of 2024 billings. Omnicom’s planned merger with Interpublic, valued at over \$13Bn, is set to create the world’s largest holding entity and unlock substantial procurement and back-office synergies. **We collected feedback and use cases from both Omnicom and IPG (and a handful of their subsidiaries)**. WPP defends its leadership by funneling AI spend into its proprietary Open AI Studio that automates copy, imagery, and media-mix forecasting. **WPP has also expressed interest in our models, and we will be setting up time with them next week**. - **We’re already following through on inbound from some of the biggest Agency Holding Companies: **WPP, Omnicom, and IPG. Once we have these deals in place, we can approach the rest: Dentsu, Havas, and Stagwell, in addition to smaller creative agencies: *VML, TBWA, RAPP, Razorfish, Havas, Doner, Digitas, Huge, Publicis Sapient or* Media Agencies: Mindshare, Starcom, Magna, Carat, Assembly, OMD. ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/6207aea2-e0c8-4aad-a666-8edeecdac89a/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4664GLBYYSB%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151857Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJGMEQCIC%2F88J2SRHS1%2FwjWqnrfYiepziy5LekMC5UhUUg5FFfjAiAIP2pS%2F95QYpkxhxqwKSSL1wWdBvQIbKg1Hrqw84pmfSr%2FAwgIEAAaDDYzNzQyMzE4MzgwNSIMUziIYCNJNoTgzMD9KtwDbQr%2B0LzULVtBv%2FVRReyl2wcXM764KYhbi0ZMf9VyIMc1mieAx0Ozeb%2By5Hgy5mAT%2F5CtGICHpC%2FWGZm3NaWQW4ZfZHFNJ3VkBJWcimOVYmbNxmkgow1IwfJYTtEInr5eClLK2Cwnz0RMV40Q53aTugXi%2FK9wZdHA2%2Bmbh2sFeWM%2FBIY5TNZr9rG6R6AtcpBNxWbZjmtGp%2FbvWIzBIGoB6vcR4uQDClM4v66febcnI%2FBxJ00LKogmNQTUFEsNM8cewGzi%2BTT5O%2BaivJNUanQe3XTX%2BUlIeeuzLXPjNneA81Mx%2B01N5H6EhDkpFvMo6aAGT5uegFqlz%2BEzFzSHm44B1qB8k9teYgaCyTw3ucQ9rFbhnOJO9zG2g7ouANVf0JSPDmWCmIVU%2BcMXwrXESmW2e%2FrrOHMa1mS1BVA0Bk6HmhrO4gmiYY%2FPrj%2F5eiIJIUyeD8za5509mzDqrOd8%2BJDtwoGSvNc4ZuCzKRSzVzSwcpCfFW6nnkLLyBHldtck3mHoo6g6VzVbL4nefy7E%2BKRxPOlIWQTeI8ZJM9%2Fpepde85%2Fe89h%2F5h8PibaeckUURPW9gSCp7Vj3vwSDvH0rhHdJe2KyYCnekm1vHACPP1bHUQmnwNdW4wP1BgNCeKMwxdSTzwY6pgEv1wsorxeXc7OdPgd3i7CxjlMmNyfCilZTtumSkdvbuWn9Yapd7CE1F%2BBe5bWekEdL%2BLKJvvpNKd59BOsfA6L1WMNkagdqbtfQhXwZA4z%2FEkdZzxbZo2HZ05D%2BIAMz%2B%2FLt6pYvNl7bwOkvrxriVkzuLauFIhgGwnwsTC0%2FLdnxab4f1pLxe8i4Jh3jbH8ZTPtBiWwotEMcIJIzOXkjI%2FW5AoQevLEO&X-Amz-Signature=e596b4725246daaa01bf8d9d16a7ddf2fb1cff3415f781dcb1e84dd0d28814ce&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) View of Account & Partner Notes  # **1. How agencies are working w/ GenAI ** --- Feedback collected from: Omnicom (includes IPG, Craft, Grabarz, and PSG), Accenture, Havas (including Prose on Pixels), and Superside. *Upcoming calls: WPP* ### **AI is implemented in three layers across most Marketing Agencies / Large Professional Service Providers**
**1. Internal Creative Tools (employee-facing)** - Where most image requests originate (pitch decks, concepts, mockups, internal ideation). - BFL access typically embedded into internal platforms or plugins. **Internal tools mentioned:**

• Managed hosting, fine-tuning support, training sessions (upsell)
### How are agencies structuring deals w/ other LLM providers? How are they passing fees through to their customers? ---
Network What they’re pushing (AI products/stack) How it’s typically packaged to clients Deal size signals Fixed vs. variable components (what to expect)
**WPP** “WPP Open” + **major AI partnerships** (new 5-year, \~\$400M pact with Google for Gemini/Veo; InfoSum acquisition for privacy-safe data collaboration) ([Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/ccf5ea33-1398-4b9d-8bf6-a403f2f5493e?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) AI is embedded across **media + creative SOWs**; increasingly a **platform line-item** inside retainers for “Open/WPP tech” enablement; project add-ons for AI production (e.g., gen-video, image) The **\$400M** Google commitment is WPP’s internal investment scale, not a fee to a single client—but it signals **enterprise-level AI line items** bundled into major accounts. ([Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/ccf5ea33-1398-4b9d-8bf6-a403f2f5493e?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) **Fixed:** platform/enablement fee inside retainer; solutioning & integration hours.
**Variable:** usage (gen-assets), traffic/QPS; sometimes **media-linked** optimization fees. ([wpp.com](https://www.wpp.com/-/media/project/wpp/files/investors/2025/annual-report/wpp_annual_report_2024_strategic-report.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
**Omnicom** **Omni** (data/activation OS); network-wide AI tie-ups and platform incentives in media (example: client incentives on X via OMG partnership); ongoing AI stack consolidation with IPG rumored/covered context. ([Omnicom Group](https://www.omnicomgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/OMC-CES-Recap_FINAL.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) Commonly **retainer + media SOW**, with **tech platform access** bundled; AI features pitched as **performance uplift** in campaigns; project spikes for pilots. Public incentives + holding-co scale deals imply **six–seven-figure annual SOWs per enterprise client** when AI is embedded across media/creative; exact AI price lines aren’t public. ([Adweek](https://www.adweek.com/agencies/exclusive-omnicom-offers-clients-up-to-200k-for-spending-on-x-leaked-docs-show/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) **Fixed:** platform (Omni) access/support; services hours. **Variable:** media-based optimization fees; **asset generation usage** if a gen-content module is switched on. ([Omnicom Group](https://www.omnicomgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/OMC-CES-Recap_FINAL.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Big ongoing AI capex (€100M in 2024; multi-year plan). ([Marketing Dive](https://www.marketingdive.com/news/publicis-adobe-generative-ai-coreai-platform/742756/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) Tends to sell as **“Power of One” transformations**: **retainer + platform access** (CoreAI), with **project SOWs** for buildouts (personalization, gen-creative, identity). Publicis’ disclosures show **material, multi-year AI investment** and data M&A; client deals for data-led personalization routinely hit **7-figures** annually; AI is bundled—no public rate card. ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/publicis-forecasts-slower-2025-remains-confident-outperformance-2025-02-04/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) **Fixed:** Core platform/program fees; integration; data contracts. **Variable:** content generation, identity match volumes, activation events. ([Marketing Dive](https://www.marketingdive.com/news/publicis-adobe-generative-ai-coreai-platform/742756/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

The Intelligence Node deal (\~\$100M) signals scale of commerce/AI bets; enterprise retainers with AI components typically **7-figures** across portfolio clients. ([Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/articles/interpublic-group-buys-retail-analytics-company-in-deal-valued-at-nearly-100-million-4817de39?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) **Fixed:** data/identity subscription; enablement.
**Variable:** lookups, enrichments, retail-AI events, asset output volumes. ([Campaign Live](https://www.campaignlive.com/article/ipg-unifies-acxiom-kinesso-one-leader/1878900?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

([Marketing Dive](https://www.marketingdive.com/news/dentsu-programmatic-know-how-index-exchange-chalice-ai/760005/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) Media SOWs with **algorithmic trading fees** and **platform access**; **pilot projects** for AI agents; may bundle as **optimization add-ons**. Index/Chalice announcements imply **network-wide** activation; client-level packages are embedded in media scopes (fees scale with spend). ([Marketing Dive](https://www.marketingdive.com/news/dentsu-programmatic-know-how-index-exchange-chalice-ai/760005/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) **Fixed:** platform & service layer; algorithm configuration. **Variable:** **impressions/optimizations** processed by AI agents; performance-based bonuses. ([Marketing Dive](https://www.marketingdive.com/news/dentsu-programmatic-know-how-index-exchange-chalice-ai/760005/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

([havas.com](https://www.havas.com/press_release/havas-accelerates-transformation-and-pivots-to-become-an-ai-driven-organization-fueled-by-human-ingenuity/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) **Creative + content subscriptions** (tooling access) inside retainers; **project fees** for AI video/production; potential **studio-style pricing** per output. Public statements point to **scaled rollout** rather than per-client pricing disclosures; expect **six-figure** SOW add-ons for enterprise content programs using Vermeer. ([MediaNews4U](https://www.medianews4u.com/havas-unveils-ai-powered-product-suite-as-it-accelerates-tech-transformation/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) **Fixed:** suite access, enablement. **Variable:** **per-video/per-asset** generation, render minutes, revisions. ([havas.com](https://www.havas.com/press_release/havas-accelerates-transformation-and-pivots-to-become-an-ai-driven-organization-fueled-by-human-ingenuity/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Investor guidance points to AI-driven margin/cost moves. ([Finviz](https://finviz.com/news/101989/stagwell-stgw-launches-ai-driven-media-platform-for-global-client-solutions?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) More **productized subscriptions** (app licenses) alongside **project services**; SMB–mid-market friendly bundles via SMC; enterprise via bespoke SOWs. Investor updates set a growth narrative; app-led pricing suggests **seat/tenant + usage**; enterprise SOWs where custom integrations are needed. ([Stagwell](https://www.stagwellglobal.com/stagwell-stgw-will-host-2025-virtual-investor-day-and-announce-5-billion-revenue-target-by-end-of-fy29/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

**Google** ### **Imagen (Text-to-Image AI)** - Back in early 2024, Google integrated **Imagen 2** into its **Performance Max** campaigns, enabling advertisers to generate realistic images—including of people—in ads across Search, YouTube, Gmail, and more. These AI images are watermark-protected to indicate they're synthetic, helping avoid misuse.[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/technology/google-upgrades-ai-product-advertisers-with-gemini-models-2024-02-22/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) - Through **Google Ads' AI Image Editor**, brands can now pull product imagery from the Merchant Center feed and apply AI-powered enhancements or generate fresh visuals. These go into the Asset Library for use in Performance Max campaigns.[Google Help](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/15205259?hl=en&utm_source=chatgpt.com) - More recently, Google released features that let advertisers generate images directly within **Ads** and **Merchant Center**, showing products in action or stylized creative scenes. This functionality is rolling out and will soon be accessible via the upcoming **Asset Studio**, centralizing these creative tools.[blog.google](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/google-ai-ads-creative/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) - Google’s AI help documentation confirms these capabilities: Asset Studio (coming soon) and the ability to do **image-to-video transformations** using both **Veo and Imagen**, already available in Ads and Merchant Center.[Google Help](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/13580022?hl=en&utm_source=chatgpt.com) --- ### **Veo (AI Video Generation)** - Announced in late 2024 as part of **Vertex AI**, **Veo** allows business users to generate high-quality videos from text or image prompts, with consistent visuals and built-in watermarking safeguards.[The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/2024/12/4/24312938/google-veo-generative-ai-video-model-available-preview?utm_source=chatgpt.com) - Since May 2025, Google has started pushing **image-to-video transformation** features powered by Veo—initially available in Merchant Center, with a rollout to Google Ads forthcoming.[blog.google](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/google-ai-ads-creative/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) - Independent reports highlight **Veo 3**, the latest iteration showcased at Google I/O 2025, which adds **native audio generation** (dialogue, ambient noise, music) to high-definition video outputs—greatly streamlining ad production workflows.[ValueX2](https://www.valuex2.com/how-google-veo-3-will-make-your-ads-go-viral/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[Syllaby](https://syllaby.io/blog/how-to-create-ads-in-google-veo-3/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) --- ### What Google *has* announced / is enabling for programmatic 1. **Veo 3 Fast** - Google recently released *Veo 3 Fast*, a cost- & speed-optimized version of the Veo 3 video generation model. It supports *text-to-video* and *image-to-video* modalities. [Google Developers Blog](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/veo-3-fast-image-to-video-capabilities-now-available-gemini-api/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) - In the announcement, Google explicitly calls out *programmatic advertising* as a “use case” for Veo 3 Fast: “Powering backend services that automatically generate ad creatives” is listed among the ideal choices. So they anticipate Veo 3 / Veo 3 Fast being used in automated/large-scale ad creative generation. [Google Developers Blog](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/veo-3-fast-image-to-video-capabilities-now-available-gemini-api/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 2. **Imagen for generating “humans in ad creative”** - Google has added the ability for advertisers to generate human imagery using **Imagen 3** for ad creative — e.g. for Performance Max, Demand Gen, Display, or App campaigns. This lets brands generate images of people (with demographic / attribute control) without doing a photoshoot. [digitalposition.com](https://www.digitalposition.com/resources/blog/ppc/google-ads-can-now-generate-humans-in-ai-ad-creative/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) - These AI-generated images are being integrated into Google Ads’ creative tools/assets. This suggests they are usable in a programmatic/automated way, since many Google campaigns are at least semi-automated (assets are chosen dynamically). [digitalposition.com](https://www.digitalposition.com/resources/blog/ppc/google-ads-can-now-generate-humans-in-ai-ad-creative/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"🪚 [Product Shop] Standard User Interface for Video Models","url":"https://www.notion.so/32ec370222d580cda806c600a8e064ad","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/32ec370222d580cda806c600a8e064ad as of 2026-03-31T15:38:53.557Z: {"title":"\\[Product Shop\\] Standard User Interface for Video Models"} > *We build the standard for visual intelligence.

***The standard **means high performance and quality, lean, open, fast, affordable, always available; not clunky – a beautiful, minimalistic, reliable, no-bullshit product which makes it a no-brainer to use because it is so ridiculously easy to build on and get good results.

**Visual intelligence** is the ability to understand and simulate (i.e. create) the underlying geometry, relationships, and interactions between objects in a physical universe. True intelligence will require reasoning across all of these domains, and an understanding of what is persistent over time and what not.

A truly visually intelligent system can simulate the physical world, and enable both humans and agents to explore it, interact with it, and learn from it. ### Goal We need to build the best and most intuitive user experiences around FLUX 3. We need to start exploring directions right away and build for future. #### What is UI/UX? The UI layer is our abstraction to make the value proposition of our model capabilities easy to grasp. We see it already today with some of our customized endpoints: Endpoints are abstract and not necessarily intuitive. We can make clients understand our capabilities WAY easier, if we just showcase the intended use and what it actually generates within a frontend. We see this pattern already today with images and this will be even more amplified once we add more modalities on the input and output. ### Why? - ### What is / (not) the shop? - ### Our path 1. **Competitor & market analysis:
**Check every possible model and product in the world to understand their strengths and weaknesses. 2. **User interviews:
**Talk to creators and power users to understand what are their pain points, what’s working and what’s not working. 3. **Build with insights:
**Coding is not the challenge, building the right thing is. We need to understand the gaps in the workflows from super users and address them in our product. 4. **Feedback research:
**As an outcome, build Product x Research muscle. Regular exchange between product and research, where user and use-case insights inform training priorities and model capabilities shape product direction. ### Team Team of 5 from each department **Product:** **FDE:** **Creative Tech:** **GTM / Sales:** TBD **Research:** TBD ## Questions - Realtime support
Will FLUX 3 be real-time? if so how? - Where will this application live in?
Is it Playground or separate standalone app? - ## Action Items - Finalize the question bank - all - - Tasks Tracker "}

content: {"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"[WIP] BFL Data Strategy 2026","url":"https://www.notion.so/336c370222d580c6af9de408d1adeb0a","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/336c370222d580c6af9de408d1adeb0a as of 2026-04-14T18:18:31.496Z: {"title":"\\[WIP\\] BFL Data Strategy 2026"} --- ### Primer - The importance of data for generative modeling The goal of generative modeling is to approximate a data distribution and - in the case of current frontier AI models - to be able to sample from that distribution in order to create new datapoints from that distribution. The learning algorithm which is employed ensures that the model can approximate the true (and unknown) distribution of the data the model is trained on as good as possible and is therefore the first central cornerstone for training a frontier model. However, the second - and sometimes underestimated - component, is the dataset which is used to train the model. This dataset represents the data distribution the model is targeting learning. It’s easy to imagine that a model won’t be competitive even with the most powerful learning algorithm, if the data distribution it’s trained on (aka the training dataset) is containing low quality training examples - garbage in, garbage out. This is why training data acquisition and processing is strategically extremely important for every foundation model company. As a result of this, we need to treat data as a first class citizen at BFL as well. ### Use Cases vs. Model Capabilities - Separating the target distribution from the conditioning method **The difference between targets and the conditioning ** The training data for foundation models has two main interfaces with the learning algorithm during training, which are the following 1. The* target: *The target is the actual ‘training example’ and it’s used as a reference point to calculate how good the model is performing the task it’s trained to do. From the difference between the model output and the target, the loss is calculated and then backpropagated through the model to update the weights. In fact, for most probabilistic approaches, the target also gives rise to the model input at training time. In those cases, the model input is often a transformation of the target (e.g. a more noisy version of the training example in the case of diffusion models). 2. The* conditioning: *Under conditioning, we subsume all additional input signals that go into the model (at both training and inference), apart from the random variable, that the model learns to generate. These conditioning inputs are what make the model controllable in the end. So if we take e.g. text-to-image models, we want to be able to generate images based (or conditioned) on text prompts. That means that, at train time, we need to have text prompts for each training image we want to use. Note that the conditioning can be more than one additional inputs, e.g. in the case of image-to-video, where we both use a text prompt and an image as conditionings to create a video. (The name image-to-video is very unfortunate, since it’s actually text+image-to-video). From a data perspective, it’s important to separate these two interfaces from each other since they affect different aspects of what the model learns during training. 1. The targets define the visual properties, the data that the model learns to generate will follow. For instance, if a model was only trained on illustrated content, it would not understand photorealism and no matter if I would prompt for ‘a blue bird’, or ‘a photorealistic blue bird’, the model would always create images that would resemble illustrations 2. The conditioning defines how users can interact with the model and how they can apply control to the data that the model generates. For instance, if I only have a dataset of paired text prompts and images, and train a model to generate images conditioned on the text prompts, users cannot use that model for image editing, since training an image editing model would require to always have a set of images (e.g. two images showing the same person in different environments) and (one or more) text prompts describing how to arrive at one image based on one (or multiple) other image(s) in that set. In that sense, the conditioning define the set of tasks that the model is generally capable to do. The above separation is helpful to understand the dimensions along which we should be thinking when it comes to data acquisition. We need to understand what we need along both these dimensions in order to create a well suited dataset for training a state of the art model. Failure to do so will make it likely that we end up with sub-optimal decisions for data acquisition and will make blind spots in our data strategy more likely. **Separating use cases from model capabilities** Based on the above separation of the targets (or target distribution) and the conditioning, we make the following definitions. **Use Case** A *use case* describes the requirements for the targets that we would like to have in a training dataset. Understanding the *use cases* our models are used for will help us answer the question: *How should the target distribution look like, that the model learns to generate during training?* Example: If the use case would be film making, we would rather be looking to license data from movie studies and other types of data, e.g. ads, would not be super important. Note that this is independent of the conditioning and does not tell us something about the model capability that we need. For instance, one could look for image editing data based on this use case, but also every other task, e.g. text-to-video. **Model Capability** A *model capability* describes how users can interact with the model, i.e. it is directly connected to the conditioning information we need at training time. We need to be clear on the model capabilities we want in our model. After we know that, we can answer the question: *How well does our data support the conditioning we want to use to make sure we reach SOTA accuracy and controllability?* Example: If we want our model to be good at multi reference image editing, this tells us that we need training training examples which contain not only a text+image pair (as it would be the case for t2i), but also reference images, containing some visual aspects/objects/characters that are present in the target example as well. However this *doesn’t *tell us something about the the target distribution should look visually. **So what?** Making the distinction between use cases and model capability can help us to get data in a more targeted way and will reduce the probability of blind spots on the data acquisition side. - By selecting use cases we tailor the output distribution to what our customers actually need. - Listing und selecting certain model capabilities we ensure to not forget any interesting new applications that we could takle with a new model. especially for multimodal and general models, it’s important to be clear about which combinations of conditionings we want to support since the number of possibilities is a superlinear function of the number of conditionings. ### Who defines what data we need? There are many stakeholders giving input on which data we need within different time frames. The following picture maps out those stakeholders and connects them to the data acquisition function which is executing on the needs that are put forward from the different stakeholders. ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/077b9bfd-2fd0-4ddb-9c4d-4efa44a81f1a/Screenshot_2026-02-20_at_10.09.47.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB46644ZEVO57%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151900Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJHMEUCIQDk94SRUkVDXqERYMrmi%2FfjwTAKxyEceQbKl98lhuhhHAIgBRADpx%2B4z4VM8JnAU3uP6EDRHH7JNqqJ2qtBcGbmtb0q%2FwMICBAAGgw2Mzc0MjMxODM4MDUiDNC%2BqBRwMam41YRwMircA2P0u5U%2FzMBnF5ilMWXBJaqNOhYwW%2BWWXjLJ5cHKc2eV4q%2BPOgOnE2RmxGBZJlpOTFo1z%2B%2BvGQYtgp7cgWWRKpp5tkDOoO7%2BLEd3BREBaKbZHiKhVuh0cRw9iXD%2F%2BzoF3WWWP4sgZY5YUE4y2%2F2o3UBpkBUVuhveOPftS%2Fo7z%2B4%2BfzIxpqbWi9O9ARY9t6W2RjW8DhD6w7d%2F7IS%2FYG8kVldcTpcxB05rHalUzwzIBrMjmA5mgo0vEyHSK4YuSRlLFI5eT2zajJ8voZOXn4UzYYik0QXDRkrSr2gEDrNsjATKfEKXHomcUm6iTj5n706qr7%2BGVkdiaghR6tblbamqv0LcRvFLZLZRw%2BzUw9n6CBAGz0IDATs4X00O10kDOGZr1QjU1xamlEpBfALhzUo088lvH7zHGz47c0xXYhA6%2FQPRtXzo%2Bd7pal8IBdCvWzseacSIFJZGmqvRcVYF%2FwcL04xcCDqv6%2B%2FYR7GKRO5gn4MhLejrzgwddB7XTcf6zojNmM60EGmMGbKiz2VpbDzH626Uy2vCbNCKb06mpZliu5mMILLY%2FQGHneU%2Fnesw0%2BxbRl3Aud1V8wDNkAECYbuqDlhinYSh5FCUAMSYlUvglKtkX%2BBFVM1ogXgmuK5IMP7Tk88GOqUBk4gnE%2FWEx6Ykw8Mpw7H7%2F9ETgTW%2FxvuL5wqS7WnVbulVe5KcJD7TUoOx3H5%2FUe0AhTt%2BuPaRJn2SPJrwI%2F2MqB6Stkb9xGR6ZHtcWlGBcaF02A3B1%2BcsyOaQ%2BO%2FnbX%2FGfwJ82NEKVuTViVlQsIIZi6872m2rQVmMm0YRC1C3BjIEWk%2BYj4JzRkeFOJ7jFZ8SybISrJrADvdJixXes0cJg8kgh98m&X-Amz-Signature=2150e4bf49e1be4d8ed42d5cb621c989539c562845e2d47776a81f72b5363b71&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) Some further explanation on how the interaction looks like: - Product: - Short/mid term needs - Communicates customer feedback, which define the reactive bets we - **Important: **customer feedback is most often a bit more noisy and here it’s highly important to explain the difference between use cases and capability (see above). - Research (input/datasets needs collected [here](/329c370222d580e8b37fc360fc2b191f?pvs=25)): - Task Force: - Short/mid term needs - defined by proactive bets on model capabilities and use cases - Research Shops: - short/mid term needs - the vast majority of shop research should be doable using open source datasets/benchmarks, but if needed - Research Leads: - Long term needs - defined by research direction Inputs from the research and products will be defined on a rolling basis. - For research ⇒ data needs, there’s the weekly research council sync where data needs are discussed. - For product → data needs: Will be discussed and re-defined on a frequent basis and needs will be updated accordingly. In the beginning, Andi and Morgan will discuss this and set up a tracker ### How to understand the best way to acquire a dataset We have various options on how to acquire a dataset supporting certain capabilities and use cases. Each project has its own dedicated page for detailed notes, updates, and comments. --- ## 🗂️ Project Tracker *Add your projects to the database below. Switch between views using the tabs: List, Board (by priority), and Timeline (Gantt).* --- ## 📌 Quick Reference
Priority Meaning
🔴 Critical Blocking other work or has an imminent deadline
🟠 High Important, should be actioned this sprint
🟡 Medium Scheduled work, good progress expected
🟢 Low Nice to have, no immediate pressure
--- ## 📝 How to Use This Space
Adding a new project 1. Click **New** in the Project Tracker database 2. Fill in: Project Name, Owner, Start Date, End Date, Priority, Status, and Category 3. Open the project page to add detailed description, milestones, and running update log 4. Use the **Timeline view** to visualise the Gantt chart
Updating project status Open the project record and: - Change the **Status** field to reflect current state - Add a dated entry in the **Update Log** section of the project page - Use **@mentions** in comments to flag blockers or decisions needed
Reviewing priorities Switch to the **Board view** to see projects grouped by priority. Review weekly as part of Finance team standup or planning sessions.

content: {"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"💭 2026 Data Planning","url":"https://www.notion.so/2ccc370222d5802aa87ed5e5b2c21abb","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/2ccc370222d5802aa87ed5e5b2c21abb as of 2026-02-09T20:52:14.714Z: {"title":"2026 Data Planning"} - **Moat**: build something that will be exclusively ours - custom datasets - Branch 1: Third parties offer building datasets based on instructions - Branch 2: Scale dataworks and build expertise internally - Unique tooling - Systematically identify failure points in VLMs - camera movement - counting - left/right - … - Build custom models that can give this information consistently → feed into captions --- - Tooling - Easy and cheap way to train classifier - concrete: improved nsfw annotation - understand dataset - oversample special data: e.g. train classifier to detect in the wild typography - Procedural generation of 3d scenes - setup for custom object detection finetunes networks - Build an automatic refresh engine for pretraining sets with up-to-date content - standardized evaluation framework for simple t2i and t2v datasets - global database to query datasets together - → global data viewer - Research - What do we need from a pretraining set, can we increase convergence speed by better selection (e.g. demystifying clip) - finalize: research into defect tokens - these are maybe with Axels Team - dataset curriculum - unlearning vs forgetting vs consistent annotation - IQA / VQA we are happy with - full data and real usage taxonomy - Infrastructure - Better understand bottlenecks (especially for small models) and resource requirements - Can we optimize storage cost for datasets by mixing more tiers - Do we need higher performance languages than python for dataloading - Efficiently store and retrieve 100PBs of data - Human annotation - increase max throughput of data works as high skilled labeling - use human to get exclusive data → actual moat ? --- - T2I - Fresh-up for pumpkin and generally extend. Target 5-6B total → very roughly one month of pretraining - note: pumpkin currently transcodes to jpeg90, in future, keep original encoding (unless it’s obscure) - Typography - Rendered Rich Text dataset for pretraining, scale to theoretic O(1B) of on-the-fly images - Rendered websites for midtraining, 200M samples - Better pumpkin subset - specialized datasets - raw, unedited photography - typography in the wild - info graphics and slides - localized datasets and special world knowledge (either for RAG or training) - video-stills to rare photography, e.g. backflips … - “natural” transparency dataset - Revisiting post training dataset - Image Editing - single ref scale up existing efforts massively \~100M each - local edits - identify video with static camera - inpainting data - reference-based edits - global edits - mutliref - build proper classification of possible edits - build datasets across relevant categories of \~100M samples - custom, exclusive datasets (e.g. data vendors or data works) - full analysis what are people doing with classic Photoshop → need to make sure we hit those things in editing - Video - Finalize current \~500M clip dataset - iterate on categories for videos & improve split for midtraining - Get to 1B good clips - Proper diversity filtering - iterating on all filters - Video Editing - i2v: same targets as for image editing - + video to video editing - editing that actually changes the video - attribute editing - camera angle - global changes - reference insertion (multiref equivalent) i+v2v - everything else probably a i2v case - Audio - get first hire and start collecting some initial sets - target: full pre, mid, post set - Interleaved data / VLM / Image and Video understanding - Text - get first hire and start collecting some initial sets - target: full pre, mid, post set - Game-Engine-Model-Data “World-Models” - Software that captures video & keystroke - pay people to play games - SVG / Vector graphics - Exploratory 1M set - use for logo set The People’s Needs "}

title: 2026 Planning
content:
{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"2026 Planning","url":"https://www.notion.so/2b5c370222d580929d6cc8052da09ca5","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/2b5c370222d580929d6cc8052da09ca5 as of 2026-03-02T12:11:23.924Z: {"title":"2026 Planning"} ### **3 Pillars of Growth/marketing ** {toggle="true"} **Fuel: Content and Brand** - → content, creative design, \[comms & PR, events & community, DevRel\] **Foundation: Product Marketing** - → research & positioning, launches, enablement, \[ecosystem & partners\] **Engine: Growth Marketing** - → inbound & web, outbound & demand gen, lifecycle, \[ops\] ### Scenario planning {toggle="true"}
**Scenario** **What We Have** **Target Customer** **Primary Growth Motion** **Marketing Focus** **Team Structure** **Q1 Priorities** **Revenue Model** **Key Risks**
**A: Studio Success** Production-ready Studio with collaboration, templates, brand kits, team features Prosumer (\$10-50/mo), SMB teams (\$100-500/mo), Agencies (\$1K+/mo) **Product-led growth loops**• Viral template sharing• Collaboration invites• Branded outputs• Word-of-mouth from "lovable" moments **Fuel-heavy:**• Creator economy (YouTube, TikTok)• Founder social• UGC campaigns• Community building Growth: 3-4
PMM: 2
Content/Creative: 2-3
DevRel: 1		 1. Build template sharing loop2. Launch YouTube influencer program (20-30 creators)3. Onboarding optimization (instant try)4. 15 customer case studies5. Tier 2 weekly launches Freemium → Paid tiers(\$10/\$50/\$100+/mo)**Target: \$13M ARR** • Not a destination (still pre-production tool)• High churn if use cases are one-off• Canva/Adobe have distribution advantage• Video delay limits use cases
**B: Playground Exploration** R&D/experimentation platform for testing FLUX capabilities, model feedback, community showcase Developers, AI enthusiasts, early adopters, researchers **Community-driven loops**• Share amazing outputs → Drive sign-ups• Developer feedback → Product improvement• Social proof/inspiration gallery **Foundation-heavy:**• Technical content• Developer education• Reddit/Twitter engagement• Research transparency Growth: 1-2
PMM: 1
DevRel: 2
Content: 1		 1. Build inspiration gallery with viral sharing2. Developer documentation3. Reddit/Discord community activation4. "Best of Playground" weekly showcases5. API education content Freemium/loss leader for brand awareness**Target: \<\$5M ARR** • Not viable revenue stream at scale• Acquisition tool only, not retention• Expensive to run (GPU costs)• Competes with API customers
**C: FDE Motion Success** Custom model training, dedicated support, white-label solutions, enterprise SLAs Enterprise (\$300K+ ACV):E-commerce platforms, gaming studios, media companies, creative agencies **Enterprise sales-led**• Account-based marketing• Proof-of-concept projects• Custom implementations• Partner ecosystem **Foundation-heavy:**• Enterprise positioning• Industry-specific case studies• Sales enablement• Analyst relations• Event sponsorships PMM: 2-3
Demand Gen: 2
Field Marketing: 1-2
Sales Enablement: 1Partners: 1		 1. Verticalize by industry (pick 2-3)2. Build 5 reference customers3. Sales playbook + battle cards4. Security/compliance certification (SOC2)5. Partner with system integrators Enterprise contracts\$300K-\$1M+ ACV**Target: \$30-50M ARR** • Long sales cycles (9-12 months)• Unproven scalability (how many FDEs needed?)• Image-only = "non-critical" function• Procurement blockers• Margin pressure from customization
**D: Hybrid (Studio + FDE)** Studio as enterprise UI + customization layer for FDE clients SMB through Studio → Enterprise through FDE upsell path **Land-and-expand**• Studio PLG acquires users• Usage signals enterprise intent• FDE motion for customization **Balanced across all three pillars:**• PLG for acquisition• Enterprise ABM for expansion• Content for both segments Growth: 3PMM: 3Content: 2Demand Gen: 2DevRel: 1 1. Studio PLG loops (acquisition)2. Enterprise signal detection (product qualified leads)3. Verticalize Studio for enterprise use cases4. Build upgrade path to FTE5. Dual case study library (SMB + Enterprise) **Blended model:**Studio: \$10-15M ARRFTE: \$30-40M ARR**Total: \$45-55M ARR** • Split focus = slower execution• Different GTM motions compete for resources• Product-market fit unclear for both• Team needs to context-switch constantly
**E: Playground → API Funnel** Playground as top-of-funnel → Convert to API customers → Upsell to enterprise Developers → Startups → Scale-ups → Enterprise **Developer-led growth**• Playground inspires → API adoption• Usage-based monetization• Developer advocates• Ecosystem partnerships **DevRel + Product Marketing:**• Technical content• API documentation• Developer community• Integration showcases• Hackathons/contests DevRel: 2-3PMM: 2Developer Marketing: 1-2Partnerships: 1 1. Playground → API conversion funnel2. Developer onboarding optimization3. Integration marketplace4. Monthly hackathons5. Technical blog (3x/week) **Usage-based API:**Free tier → Pay-as-you-go → Enterprise contracts**Target: \$20-30M ARR** • Resellers capture more value• Not a destination problem persists• Price competition with other models• Commoditization of image generation
- If we could only pick ONE scenario to win in Q1, which has highest probability of success? - What would make Studio "great and competitive" enough to drive word-of-mouth at PLG velocity? - Can FDE motion actually scale, or is it just 5-10 white-glove clients max? - Is Playground burning cash for brand awareness worth it if we're losing mind share anyway? - Which scenario solves the "not a destination" problem? - What does video timeline do to each scenario's viability? ### **Guiding Questions - our bets ** {toggle="true"} **I. Critical Bottleneck (Pick ONE to solve in Q1)** - What's the single biggest problem that, if solved in Q1, unlocks everything else? - people (hiring, using externals) - given we dont have Studio, its fulltime creatives/ influencer bet - EDUCATIONAL CONTENT - bringing out the magic what our models can do - double down on community and open weights, we rely on externals currently to tell others how to train our models - Scenarios - Low shipping velocity - If we could only fix ONE thing that would make everything else easier, what is it? - Bandwidth / hiring - What's the highest-leverage motion we're NOT doing because we're too busy executing low-impact work? - educational content - personality/ faces of BFL, founder marketing - **Brand positioning that makes us feel bigger** - we compete with Google/OpenAI but don't show up that way - **Systematic founder visibility** - Robin/Patrick should be recognized names in visual AI **II. Pre-Mortem: Failure Scenario (December 2026)** - It's December 2026. We're struggling and competitors are winning. What did we fail to do in Q1 2026? - Community (highest leverage point for dev focused) - the way the models are released, we drop weights and let people figure it out, need to make sure what it can do, how to train it, when you should train it - approach to safety is v strict limiting growth - the way we launch in general: needs to be treated as product and not just “i am dropping code” - own parts of application layer via studio and serve creators - we need to double down on things we know we win in, known for certain sectors/ categories / segments - didnt manage to get into creative world (researchers and engs building for creative industry) - we didnt nail positoning - we are still only research focused company without apps - we dont use enough agents internally - we arent riding the agent adoption wave at all - from external product - We arent owning any particular space, not image and video is happening without us - What are we pretending not to know about why customers aren't converting/retaining? - models arent as good as we were hoping for, sitting in between google (quality) and china (cheap, open weights) - the fact that our models are distilled - our brand isnt as strong, we are known in niche sector - Playground - value prop not strong enough: not a platform where you stay, destination platform, - What's the gap between our growth story to VCs vs. the reality on the ground? - video: internally more of an expensive 20-30m exploration but investors/ market waiting and betting on this **III. Validation & Experimentation** - What do we believe about our ICP/acquisition channels/conversion that we haven't actually validated with data? - If we could only run 3 experiments this quarter that would move revenue, what would they be and why? - content: video and media based - channels: - Direct: X, LI - Indirect (through infuencers): Youtube, Tiktok, Reels - experiences, creative offline: SF, London, Art Basel, NYC, LA - partnerships where value props are complementary and audiences overlap / fuel each other - leverage a16z media guys more - What's working accidentally right now that we haven't systematized yet? - Optimising weights with Nvidia &Comfy for flux 2, content **Simplified Planning Framework for Q1 Bets** - **What will marketing do to drive growth next year?**
Define 3–5 big bets for the year, each with: Goals, Audience, Creative approach, Channels, and Stakeholders - **How much budget does marketing need? HARD → Is our Marketing budget 20M or 5m next year? **
Start with marketing efficiency metrics to ballpark the right budget range - **Marketing, can you hit this revenue target? HARD **
Build a bottom-up forecast to see if your top-down target is realistic **Resources & Decisions Needed** - **Headcount priorities:** Which pillar gets hired first? - Growth marketer: product marketing - in house - foundational marketer - in house - Growth Engineer / Hacker - frontend leaning (recommended second growth hire) - Frontend leaning engineer with a strong interest in growth, ability to write engaging copy and do design. They’ll be able to spin up SEO pages, create interactive homepages, optimize your activation and subscription flows, and create viral mini-tools. - Growth Engineer / Hacker - backend leaning - Backend leaning engineer with a strong interest in growth, ability to scrape data and integrate tools. They’ll be able to run large scale automated outbound campaigns, set up referral/affiliate programs, and set up the data needed for performance marketing. - Website Designer / Builder - in house - An excellent designer who’s comfortable with Webflow/Framer. Your website is the highest leverage sales person you’ll ever have — for selling to future customers, partners and candidates. This person owns the core pages of the website and collaborates with the Growth Engineer / Hacker on SEO pages. - Brand Designer / Graphic Designer - test freelancer - Create the static assets for your website, email campaigns, launches, and pitch decks. - Motion Designer / Videographer / Creative Producer - test freelancers - Create the videos for your launches, social media, website, customer stories and more. Videos are dominating social media algorithms and are still underrated. - **Budget allocation:** How much goes to paid acquisition vs content production vs events/community? - **Agency vs in-house:** What do we build internally vs outsource - **Tooling & infrastructure:** What martech stack do we need to execute at this velocity? - **Cross-functional dependencies:** What do we need from research, engineering, and product to move fast? - clarity, comms chain - we need a “WHY” - why do people care - basic operations, who does what, how do we not become each other bottleneck, decision and execution ### Exercise: Defining our aspirational growth loops {toggle="true"} - **why** is everyone sharing NB? Learn - barrier of getting started - no mobiel experience - Suno: in less than 10 seconds registered and created song - TIME TO VALUE - randomised prompt **Step 1: Map the current loop ** Draw it out together: - **Input:** New user discovers FLUX - **Action they take:** \[What do they do that creates value?\] - **Output generated:** \[What gets created/shared?\] - **New input created:** \[How does this bring more users?\] **Step 2: Identify the multiplier ** - What % of users complete the action? - What % of outputs convert to new inputs? - Where's the biggest drop-off? **Step 3: Stress test ** - Does this work when we ship daily? (Velocity test) - Does this work without marketing spend? (Product-led test) - Does this compound over time? (Sustainability test) - Can competitors easily copy this? (Moat test) **Step 4: Pick ONE lever to improve ** If we could only improve one part of this loop in Q1, what would unlock 10x growth? **Reference Examples:** **Dropbox's Product Loop (60% of acquisition)** - Input: New user uploads files - Action: User shares file/folder with colleague - Output: Recipient gets shared link - New input: % of recipients sign up to access/collaborate - *Multiplier boost: "Give storage to get storage" incentive accelerated the loop* **Lovable's Word-of-Mouth Loop** - Input: New user tries vibe coding - Action: First app build is so magical it exceeds expectations - Output: User posts "holy shit" moment on X/LinkedIn/YouTube - New input: Their network signs up from seeing the demo - *Key: This only works because the product experience is genuinely "lovable" - marketing can't fake this* **Lovable's Founder Social Loop** - Input: Anton posts about what they're building on X/LinkedIn - Action: Post shows velocity/vision/behind-the-scenes - Output: Reaches millions of impressions organically, humanizes the brand - New input: Developers sign up to try what they saw - *Went from 0 followers to 2000+ reactions per post in 10 months - zero paid marketing* **What's BFL's equivalent?** - What happens when someone generates an incredible image with FLUX? - Where do they naturally want to share it? - How does that bring new users back to us? ## **2026 Bets ** ### 1.Figure out what our destination is - We are dev first product but our end product is visual and creation - Turn Playground into a **studio / creative platform** that’s a true destination (people stay, create, and share). - Build enough surface area (features, integrations, UX) to 15–20x current Playground revenue - or tank it - Build for agent first world ### 2. Video & Generative Media Bet - **Ship a strong video model** and ride the video/generative media adoption wave instead of sitting it out. - Use video as the “mega hit” growth story that underpins the 30M+ revenue narrative. ### 3. Community & Education Bet - Treat **DevRel + educational content** as the core marketing engine: - Deep how‑tos on open weights, auras, training, etc. - Multi‑format content (3 / 10 / 30 min; X, LinkedIn, YouTube). - Become the **source of truth** on visual/open‑weights workflows instead of outsourcing this to others. ### 4. Creator & Influencer Bet - Double down on **creatives and influencers** to compensate for slow internal hiring: - Creators show what the models can do (images + video, reels/TikTok/YouTube). - Influencer distribution into creator communities that you can’t staff fast enough internally. ### 5. Segment Focus & Differentiation Bet - Move away from “horizontal image model” and **pick segments where you win** (e.g. specific creator verticals, regulated industries, or workflows). - Clarify why someone picks BFL over: - Google (better models, more \$\$) - Chinese open‑weights players (cheaper, less censored) - 11Labs/other creative platforms. ### 6. Partner Ecosystem Bet - Use **partners as distribution**, not just logos: - Deep integrations with tools like Comfy, NVIDIA, Adobe, Figma-type players, “next Replicate/File.” - Co‑marketing, co‑education, and embedded usage that drives recurring revenue. ### 7. Process & Team Bet - Build a real **growth/marketing org**: - Foundational marketer, growth engineer, technical content generalist, brand/motion, plus someone like Aitana for social/creatives. - Standardize **launch and campaign processes ** - Hires - ~~Growth: PMM ~~ - Growth: marketing (field, SEO, self serve, pricing) - Events/ experiences & brand, social - Growth Eng ## **Action Items & Owners** ### **IMMEDIATE (Dec 2025)** - **~~Finalize Owais (Growth Marketer/ PMM) hire** → Sarah → 🟡 In Progress~~ - **Finalize Marketing Lead (Brand, Content & Community) hire** → Sarah/Mira → 🔴 Dec-Jan - **~~Write Aetana JD** (Generalist Marketer) → Sarah → DONE~~ - **Write DevRel #2 JD** → Stephen → 🔴 This week - **Align with Dave on marketing budget** → Sarah → 🔴 By Dec 20 - **Reach out to Lovable's agency** → Sarah → 🔴 This week - **Source Motion Designer freelancers** → Stephen → 🔴 This week - **Define content formats & Q1 calendar** → Stephen → 🔴 By Dec 20 - **~~Implement launch tracker** → Sarah → Done? ~~ - **Document cross-functional launch requirements** → Sarah → Launch framework done? ### **Q1 2026 (Jan-Mar)** - **Hire Website Designer/Builder** → Sarah → 🔴 Jan - **Go live with marty Scorsese **→ Sarah → 🔴 Jan - **Source Growth Engineer (Frontend)** → Stephen/Growth Marketer → 🔴 Jan-Feb - **Leverage a16z media team** - define asks → Stephen → 🔴 Jan - **Create launch template** (assets + copy + why) → Stephen + PMM → 🔴 Jan - **Identify 20-30 YouTube creator targets** → Stephen → 🔴 Jan - **Launch first influencer pilot** (5 creators) → Stephen → 🔴 Jan - **Develop founder marketing strategy** → Sarah + Stephen → 🔴 Jan - **Define low/medium/high shipping velocity scenarios** → Sarah + Product → 🔴 Jan - **Create bottom-up revenue forecast** → Sarah + Growth Marketer → 🔴 Jan - **Document "What Marketing Does/Doesn't Do"** → Mira + Stephen → 🔴 Jan - **Systematize Nvidia/Comfy approach** → Stephen → 🔴 Feb - **Identify "next Fal" partnerships** → Stephen + Partnerships → 🔴 Q1 - **Plan SF/London/NYC/LA experiences** (execute Q2) → Stephen + Aetana → 🔴 Jan-Mar --- ## **Key Insights from Session** ### **What We're NOT Doing** - Elaborate onboarding flow optimization (no product surface yet) - Paid acquisition campaigns at scale - Email marketing programs (audience too small) - Traditional demand gen (waiting for sales clarity) - Billboards/mass brand advertising **Why:** Limited bandwidth, no Studio product, unclear ICP, need foundations first. Focus is on high-impact brand-building that makes us appear as category leader, not incremental acquisition tactics. ### **2026 Failure Modes to Avoid** If BFL struggles in Dec 2026, it will be because we: 1. **Didn't build community** - highest leverage for developer-focused company 2. **Kept dropping weights without context** - no education on how/when/why to use 3. **Didn't penetrate creative world** - still seen as researchers, not creative tool 4. **Failed to nail positioning** - still known only in niche circles 5. **No application layer** - still just models, we arent a destination 6. **Too horizontal** - didn't define what we win at 7. **Video didn't ship** - biggest gap vs market expectations 8. **Ignored agent wave** - didn't ride adoption curve 9. **Launches stayed broken** - treated as code drops, not products 10. **Safety too strict** - limited growth potential 11. **Didn't create perception of scale and leadership** - still feel like scrappy research lab, not visual AI category leader competing with Google/OpenAI ### **Truths We're Facing** **Product reality:** - Playground isn't a destination - people come and go - Value prop not strong enough to retain - "Not a destination" problem unsolved - Models sitting between Google (quality) and China (cheap, open weights) **Brand reality:** - Not as strong as we think - known in niche only - Losing mindshare to competitors despite technical excellence - Need faces/personalities, not just corporate account ### **What's Working ** - Nvidia/Comfy weight optimization content - Technical deep-dives (when we do them) - Research transparency resonates with developers - High-quality creative outputs when we do them - need to systematize this into brand perception strategy - Research credibility - translate this into "we're the leaders who invented this field" narrative --- ## **Next Strategy Review** **When:** End of January 2026 **Topics to Cover:** - Progress on Q1 hires - Content velocity achieved - Influencer pilot results - Budget alignment outcome - Studio timeline update - Shipping velocity scenarios validated - Video model progress "}

*Shortcuts:* Adobe Brain & Custom Models Meeting Notes 📄 [Adobe Documents](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1LjOpv-ozkMrvnInI_cJwdRPhE_bplEvZ?usp=drive_link) 📝 [Brand Context Protoco](/2f1c370222d58076927fe31a078c871b?pvs=25)l 📝 [Latest Agreement](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1MVnf-QwUHl0Z2ViKldcC3vZ-iJGo-Ods/view?usp=sharing)
📦 [Adobe Product List](/27ac370222d580c6b018eaa04ea2b29c?pvs=25) ## Partner Overview ---
**Company Overview** ### Adobe’s Lines of Business --- Adobe is fundamentally a SaaS company, and the bulk of Adobe’s revenue comes from recurring subscriptions (creative, document, experience). Adobe increasingly sells bundled or integrated deals combining creative tools, document workflows, and experience/marketing stacks for enterprises.

Multiple VPs including Hannah Elsakr (3rd party model strategy). From BFL: Sumith, Matt, Amanda, Dustin, Scott. ### Agenda 1. BFL backstory & team intro 2. Model capabilities vs. competitors 3. Demo of Flux Kontext (Context) 4. Tease Flux.2 and early Flux Video --- ### Key Discussion Points **BFL Overview** - Founded last year, 48 people across SF and Freiburg. - Core team behind latent diffusion, Stable Diffusion, SDXL, SD3, Stable Video Diffusion. - Backed by A16Z, GC, Adobe Ventures. - Current models: Flux (fast text-to-image, strong text rendering), Flux Ultra (4MP hi-res), Kontext (image generation + editing). **Flux Kontext Demo** - Showcased character consistency, style transfer, and iterative editing. - Highlight: Strong performance on text rendering and reference preservation. - Adobe attendees interested in: - Multi-character + multi-image support. - Masking & region-based editing for Photoshop. - Workflow for storytelling / sequential consistency (comics, film). - Progressive edit quality (avoiding degradation). **Flux.2 Preview** - Currently training; interchangeable with Flux.1 endpoints. - Major improvements: - Photorealism + fantasy generation. - Stronger world knowledge & multilingual prompting. - JSON/structured prompting. - Better per-pixel detail, highly accurate reflections, text rendering. - Expected release: \~weeks, potentially available for early integration before Adobe Max. - Likely strictly superior to Flux.1 (except possibly speed). **Flux Video Early Research** - Goal: fast iteration + precise controls, not just “one-shot” text-to-video. - Workflow demos: storyboard with Kontext edits → video interpolation. - Still training; targeting medium-res now, higher res + HDR/10bit longer term. - Adobe Premiere team requested: 4K output, alpha channel support, HDR color spaces. - Specific requirements from Premier team: Premiere Pro customers would expect: - 4K resolution (that could be 1080 upscaled to 4K) - From a bit-depth standpoint, usually 10 or 12 bit (because they might want to take elements and composite them). So if you could generate elements with alpha channels, it's even better. - Color space standpoint: anything HDR is is going to be good for them - Acc to Dustin: For HDR in Kino, the best first solution will to include it in the upscale pipeline if we go that route. So there is resolution upscaling but there is also color upscaling, going from 8bit color (our current) to higher depth color, ideally 16 being the target. For native integration that would be very tough (will need an HDR vae and tbh I am not sure this is 100% needed if we can downscale/upscale the color space and maintain the info, for high high high end customers it would be needed but generally the quality of models needs to go up a lot in other factors till that is really needed) **Adobe Feedback & Interests** - Strong appetite to test Flux.2 early, even in unfinished form, to build presets ahead of Adobe Max. - Clear interest in: - Photoshop (masks, selections, region edits). - Firefly Boards (preset-based workflows). - GenStudio (ads/marketing). - Express. - Premiere (video integration). - Teams want deeper “bespoke” model work: partner with BFL to “deep tune” models for Adobe-specific workflows (beyond generic API use). - Adobe happy to act as exclusive early tester for Flux.2 pre-release. - Adobe suggested joint evaluation cycles (using their large internal eval teams). --- ### Outcomes & Action Items - **Flux.2 Testing:** Deliver early endpoints within \~2 weeks; coordinate with Sam on which Adobe teams (Photoshop, Firefly, Boards, GenStudio, Express) need access. - **Adobe Max Launch:** Explore positioning Adobe as launch partner for Flux.2 (Photoshop GA + GenStudio potential). - **Deep Partnership:** Begin scoping process for co-developed model fine-tuning (requirements gathering across Adobe teams → feasibility discussion with BFL). - **Flux Video:** Continue R&D; align specs with Adobe Premiere team (4K, HDR, alpha). Not ready for Max, but Adobe sees future opportunity. - **Masks & Controls:** Prioritize mask-based editing and multi-image references in Flux.2 to align with Photoshop workflows. - **Follow-up Sessions:** Plan deeper dives with product leads at Adobe to gather workflow-specific requirements.
**Sam / Amanda Catch-up** **Topics:** - Adobe Roadshow - More finalized list of attendees? - - Photoshop GTM: - BFL will send blog post submission + socials by EOD today - Adobe Max - Will keep Sam posted on Flux.2 release timing in case it’s possible to be included in GA
**EXT Meeting w/ Photoshop (launch & co-marketing)** Topics: Photoshop launch, Marketing items Attendees: Sam Branson, Olivia Morad (Director of Product Marketing, Photoshop) - Launch is still 9/25 - Public beta, will include Flux Kontext and another model (Nano banana?) - What Adobe’s planing on their end for the launch - Key takeaways: - **First time bringing 3rd party models into Photoshop; **big mental shift for users and some reservations around using different models, but Adobe knows that users are using different models and want to offer flexibility - **For gen-fill 3P models will only be available on desktop, with plan for mobile and web as fast follow** - had some ‘sneak peeks’ into Nano Banana w/ some influencers —\> something for us to consider in the future - Adobe positioning: giving user choice and flexiblity PLUS the power of photoshop (stay in their workflows) - **For September 25th Public Beta: **Tier 1 / L1 marketing motion and activation next Thursday (25th) - **Planned activities:** - Press release / blog post (***when can we get access to this?***) - Channels: Social, community, Customer Support engaged, Community ambassadors that will be briefed (they will share w/ their networks) - Paid Media - Email - Making updates on Adobe.com - Promo: 1 month promo to standard and premium plan users to try models for free within photoshop (credits are automatically allocated to users, for all standard units folks will get 100 credits per model and 500 credits per model on the premium plan), but the burn down of the credits is influenced by the model inference - **Access to the beta experience:** - This will be in the beta app (800K users), so you have to sign up for the trial, find the beta app, then find the introductory modal - beta app is a totally separate build, but accessible to everyone who has photoshop - same location as where you get updates for GA app in Creative Cloud home - They released gen-fill in beta and had no discovery issues - The experience will be released in the GA app by Adobe Max (Oct 28th), which is all users - **BFL planned activities:** - Video (for socials) - content will be photoshop and gen-fill focused - provide a quote from Robin for PR/blog?? - Blog post on our end w/ a customer or use story - **Adobe’s Planned Activities For GA at Adobe Max - OCt 28th** - Photoshop is one of the leading stories, and 3P will be featured in some way (not sure yet) - options are keynote and the blog - maybe BFL can wrap in Flux.2 or tease it at the very least? - Maybe we can announce day 0 support for FLUX.2? - **Follow-ups:** - ~~Sam: Add Olivia to BFL Slack channel~~ - ~~Olivia: Share messaging guidelines~~ and UI assets today - ~~Olivia: Add Adobe social/comms team to Slack~~ - BFL: Share quote from Robin for Adobe’s blog post or PR if needed - ~~Stephen: Brief editors with Adobe assets for video production~~ - ~~BFL: Draft blog post proposal using Adobe messaging framework~~ - All: Coordinate approval processes (Adobe needs max advance notice) - Monitor Flux 2 timeline - potential Max tie-in if ready by late October
**INT Recap Discussion** **Internal:** Sanjana, Matt, Andi, and Amanda **Topics: **Discussed latest effort w/ Adobe, upcoming roadshow, and Adobe Max **Next Steps** - Finalize for Roadshow (week of Sept 22nd) - Ask Sumith about evaluations for Flux2 to show at roadshow - Sam to confirm attendees for roadshow - Ask Photoshop team (interested in Beta late Sept) if they already have customers requesting - could meet w/ these customers at Adobe Max? - Kiosk at Adobe Max as part of Ventures sponsorship (Oct 28-30th) - Who will man the kiosk at Adobe Max? Zion could be good to send (based in LA) - Andi and Robin chat on whether they want to attend
**EXT Meeting w/ Sam B. (Photoshop, Adobe Max, & Demo Day)** **External:** Sam/Sanjana **Topics:** Photoshop status, Max info., and Teams at the demo day - Photoshop - likely launching nano banana with us, want best possible version of our models - current plan is to launch both models at the same time - “name recognition is a thing” but dont want to roll out as a king maker, same is true Adobe wide - end of September still the timeline - public beta. out of the gate prob represents much higher Day 1 usage. - part of Gen-Fill capability - 40K total users in beta pool, when gen-fill was launched in beta, the beta pool grew to 1.2M. - ping Adobe in Slack about date to prepare Eng - Demo Day - Hannah Elsker(?) leading Strategic Initiatives and 3P model strategy, important to be involved. she’ll be in San Jose for all of next week but is confirming the availability - he’ll be sending some slots over via Slack to hold - Sam will prob be traveling there to host - theyve done one of these so far, relatively well-attended, and will be recorded to be shared (under NDA, only internal) - 90 min window - **Teams may include AI Product leadership, Firefly, Firefly Boards, Photoshop, Express, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, GenStudio** - about 50 ppl being invited - **image to video workflow will be important as well** - Max - some general msg back to his personal invite by EOW - invitation for 2, paid Max passes - can get a discount - cc Sam on the email to Ventures team for the passes -
