content:
{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"Adobe Pro Proposal","url":"https://www.notion.so/2bcc370222d5805d869be207d7bbd022","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/2bcc370222d5805d869be207d7bbd022 as of 2026-04-17T13:55:58.070Z: {"title":"Adobe Pro Proposal"} --- **Context:** A summary of a deal for Adobe to license our Flex model (external proposal linked below) specifically for use with Enterprise customers within Foundry. 💡***What has been added: non-negotiables and commercial tiers based on their desired terms.*** ## **A. Overall Value & Risks**
Opportunities Risks
BFL • Adobe is one of a small handful of companies where BFL can strike a large closed-weights deal.
• There is strong product-market fit between Flux models and Adobe's product surfaces, and given industry trends Adobe is in a highly likely position to pay a substantial fee for frontier model weights.
• BFL cannot efficiently serve Adobe's end-customer base directly at scale, so a single high-value agreement with Adobe allows BFL to capture that market through one commercial relationship rather than fragmenting across thousands of ENT accounts.		 • Adobe products still hold significant market share in creative tooling. While usage of traditional creative software is at risk as image and video models get better, there is a substantial lag in market adoption of models that could give Adobe a durable advantage if allowed to distribute fine-tuned versions of our models.
• Given Adobe's penetration of the ENT customer segment (some that directly overlap with BFL's current and target base) allowing broad distribution of Pro model derivates could cut off a large portion of both BFL's commercial licensing and API business).
• The scope restrictions in this deal exist specifically to prevent this outcome.
Adobe • Allows Adobe to fine-tune a SOTA model on ENT customer data to deliver on key Foundry workflows.
• Adobe already has existing ENT customers and relationships, and this deal allows them to deliver: 1) a differentiated, brand-safe generative capability on top of those accounts, 2) post-training and fine-tuning flexibility that no API-only arrangement provides, and 3) ENT customer brand customization at scale, which is the core commercial promise of Foundry.		 • Dependence on a 3P model for a flagship ENT product surface creates continuity and roadmap risk.
• Adobe also needs attribution flexibility to market Foundry as a proprietary product, which creates tension with our interest in brand visibility.
• And the scope of what Adobe can do with distribution, derivatives, white-labeling needs to be permissive enough for Adobe to build and market a real product.
## **B. Adobe’s Feedback & Our Recommendations** **Current Status:** They have continued to stress the urgency of the deal, although we’re not sure what is driving this (e.g., turning our draft in a matter of days, which is unusual). They have positioned this deal as a "Strategic Partnership" designation alongside Google, Runway, Microsoft, and OpenAI, but this is not reflected in their changes to the agreement. ***⚠️ The latest from my call w/ Ersin last night (April 9th)*** ---
**Deal-blockers** ** • White-labeling: **Despite Adobe legal scrapping all co-marketing commitments, he said he'll do joint PR, publicly position Foundry as collaborating with Black Forest Labs, and even offer BFL-labeled base models alongside white-labeled derivatives for customers who want them. ***He specifically wants fine-tuned models built on customer data to be white-labeled, ***since he views those as containing Adobe and customer IP, not just BFL's.

** • Distribution: **Adobe legal removed our language limiting distribution, and Ersin himself admitted that “Foundry” is just a construct. **"Foundry-only" is enterprise-private, not product-surface-limited.** Ersin's understanding of Foundry scope = private to specific enterprise customers, not accessible to the general subscriber base. But ***he can't commit to limiting which Adobe application surfaces an enterprise customer uses to access their endpoint*** (e.g., a Photoshop panel for that specific enterprise). Amanda pushed back that powering multiple workflows across multiple products for a single customer is still distribution — even at 50 seats. Ersin acknowledged the distinction and agreed to tier that separately.
***Nice-to-haves*** ** • Beyond Foundry Distribution & Internal Use: He proactively proposed a second tier for GA consumer surfaces.** Without much prompting, Ersin suggested structuring the agreement with a base enterprise tier (Foundry/derivatives, white-label + co-marketing) and an optional second tier that kicks in if any Adobe product team wants to deploy a derivative in consumer-facing GA products (CC apps, Firefly subscriber base, etc.). He acknowledged this would reach hundreds of millions of users and warrants meaningfully higher commercials. He even suggested measuring it by number of deployed model instances as a scale limiter.
**Other clarifications** ** • He's only interested in derivatives for Foundry, not hosted-as-is.** Ersin confirmed he will not host \[Flex\] as-is, whether labeled or white-labeled. This agreement is exclusively about creating and deploying fine-tuned derivatives for ENT Foundry customers.

• **Derivative destruction is solvable.** Despite Adobe legal adding more favorable terms around their control, distribution, and post-expiry rights for derivatives, Ersin confirmed Adobe would destroy derivatives at end of term with documentation. His ask is a wind-down/cool-down period so existing enterprise customer agreements can run out naturally, he doesn't want to pull back a live deployment from a paying customer mid-term. He framed this as a legal timing issue, not ownership.		 • The derivative wind-down period should be added as a standard term across all tiers (something like a 12-month cool-down where no new customer agreements can be signed post-expiry, but existing live deployments can run to their natural end) - Ersin signaled he's ready to agree to this.
## Our Recommendation --- ### Non-Negotiables
Term Status
On-prem deployment for their customers ❌ Not permitted
Distillation / Reverse-engineering ❌ Not permitted
Using models for AI-training workflows ❌ Not permitted
Standalone APIs ❌ Not permitted
Less than \$8M in Year 1 for white-labeling and distribution ❌ Not permitted
LoRAs / Fine-tunes ✅ Permitted (expire when contract expires)
Derivatives ✅ Permitted (expire when contract expires)
### Commercial Tiers & Our Recommendation The current tiers need to shift, because the call fundamentally changed two things: (1) white-labeling is no longer a premium add-on, and (2) the distribution distinction is now enterprise-private-multi-surface vs. GA consumer, not Foundry vs. everything else.
Commercial Tier Terms Internal Comments
**(Current Adobe anchor - what we proposed)**
\$4M / year		 Flex only · Foundry surface only · No white-labeling · No internal Adobe use · Models labeled "Flux" ***None-starter for Adobe***
**Tier 1 (Floor): Enterprise Foundry with white-labeling + co-marketing**

**\$8M in year 1, \$16M in year 2**
\*Alternative is \$4M trial for 6 months

OR

\$XM floor + variable (options: #images, #derivatives instances per customer)

*\*\*At \$500K selling price to their customers they will break even at 16 ENT customers in year 1.*
 • Flex only
• Private end-points exposed in Adobe ecosystem/products for ENT Foundry customers only
• NO standalone end-points
• White-labeling
• No internal Adobe services use		 • This captures table-stakes distribution and white-labeling
• ENT Foundry customers access their derivative model through multiple Adobe product surfaces (a Photoshop panel, a GenStudio workflow, etc.) rather than a single private API endpoint.
• Premium for removing BFL attribution; enables Adobe to sell \[Flex\] as proprietary. The co-marketing commitments should be explicitly baked in as conditions of this tier, not optionals (joint press release, Foundry x BFL public positioning, BFL-labeled base models available alongside derivatives).
**Tier 2: Broader Distribution** + **White-Labeling **
\$20M in year 1; \$30M year 2

*\*\* They could see it as a 8% R&D cost on what we believe is \$120M in annual ENT Firefly revenue.
This would cannibalize the current API spend of \$1.2M per year (primarily driven by Photoshop and Firefly), and also allow Adobe to use Flux for Brand-Brain (their B2B tool for Marketers to create on brand assets).
*		 Tier 1
+ distribution across other Adobe Customer segments (not just ENT Foundry)
+ use of Flex across Adobe internal services		 • This becomes pan-Adobe deal, and reflects platform-level embed in an \$18B+ product ecosystem (across DME + DX).
• This is what Ersin proactively proposed for CC apps, Firefly subscriber base, general public-facing products. Frame it as an option that can be exercised during the license term (his suggestion), not something Adobe has to commit to upfront.
• For this type of deal we would need to involve **Ely Greenfield** (CTO, Digital Media) and **Varun Parmar** (GM for ENT Firefly and Gen Studio).
## Recommendation w/ Variable Components {toggle="true"} ## Final Proposal for Adobe: ***Non-negotiables:*** - No on-prem deployment on behalf of clients - No distillation / reverse-engineering - No using models for AI-training workflows - No standalone APIs; however, derivatives can be integrated into Adobe products - \$8M flat fee per year - Some co-marketing commitments (PR, Placement, etc.) **Year 1** - \$8M flat fee **Year 2** Full sensitivity analysis [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/10bjVD05MliEiEmKo4y9XbyrtO9Z_3X80/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=100040495989598506312&rtpof=true&sd=true). - \$8M flat fee continues - **Foundry Customers:** - Variable per instance cost at waterfall per customer, and potentially waterfall per instance - If 1-2 instance on avg. per customer then pricing would be: - \$100K per instance for 1-10 customers - \$75K per instance for 11-20 customers (\$50K backup) - \$50K per instance beyond 20 customers (\$10K backup) - Renegotiation cap at 200 absolute instances - *Anchored in both our per image list price and ENT licensing fees since this is our opportunity cost - both the per image is below our average list price and the total per customer amount is below our ENT ACV.* - \*The per-image equivalent of the \$100K instance fee ***~~at 70% utilization~~*** works out to \$0.068/image, above our \$0.06 list price. The total \$100K is also below our annual ENT contract value for open weights licensing, which are \[dev\] / less good models. - GA / Consumer Customers: - Variable per image cost \$0.062 (list price would be \$0.09) up to 200M images per year, then it goes down to \$***0.038 ***per image after that ## Path 1: Lower cost on Foundry, and pricing GA/other segments for scale {toggle="true"} --- ***BFL Fee Assumptions*** - Fixed: \$8M /year - Variable (Foundry): Each P5 instance setup fee per customer is \$20K (first 10 customers), then \$15K (customers 11-50), and \$10K (51+ customers). - Variable (GA/Consumer Segment): Waterfall pricing, \$0.062 per image up to 200M images/year, then as low as \$0.038 per image ### 1. Conservative Case ***Only 10 Foundry customers in both years, and 20M images across their consumer segment (cannibilizing all direct API spend from Adobe today).***
Year 1 Year 2 2-Year Total
Adobe Deal \$8.0M \$9.44M **\$17.44M**
Direct API (same demand @ \$0.09) \$3.12M \$3.12M **\$6.25M**
Open Weights (\$10K/customer/month) \$1.2M \$1.2M **\$2.4M**
**Our POV: **This is a very good deal for us. Over two years, we earn \$17–17.4M versus \$6.25M if we'd served the same demand through direct API; roughly a **\$10.7–11.2M premium**. - Open weights at this scale isn't scaling fully; the deal earns 7× what we'd make on OW licenses alone (assuming each customer won’t go over 2M images per year). The \$8M flat fee is driving most of our value. - We would need to charge \$0.062 per image for their consumer segments for up to 20M images to safe-guard the current API revenue we get from them. We would also recommend to start waterfall pricing at 200M images per year and above. **Adobe's POV:** Potentially comfortable. They're paying \$8M to access FLUX derivatives across their Foundry platform, white-labeled and distribution-ready. On the GA images they process, they're paying \$0.038–\$0.062 versus the \$0.09 they'd pay BFL directly, saving them **\$560K at the high price** in Year 2 versus equivalent direct access. The deal saves them money relative to every alternative. --- ### 2. Realistic Case: ***20 Foundry customers Year 2, and doubling current image count to 40M GA/Consumer images***
Year 1 Year 2 2-Year Total
Adobe Deal \$8.0M \$10.83M **\$18.83M**
Direct API (same demand @ \$0.09) \$3.12M \$6.25M **\$9.37M**
Open Weights (\$10K/cust/month) \$1.2M \$2.4M **\$3.6M**
**BFL's POV:** Still a strong deal at **\$8.5–9.5M premium over direct API** across two years. - The Foundry per instance component starts to become a bit more meaningful (\$350K at 20 customers), though it's still modest. - The GA/Consumer per image side at 40M images looks good: net GA contribution of **\$1.28M **after cannibalization of \$1.2M. **Adobe's POV:** - 20 Foundry customers is a natural growth trajectory. For them, the deal at 40M GA images (doubling their current # images via direct API) costs \$10.83M vs. \$11.95M if they paid BFL's direct fine-tuned rate for everything (\$0.09). They're **saving \$1.12M**. That saving grows as volume grows, so Adobe is incentivized to push more volume through the licensed model rather than through direct API calls. It’s the cost we pay for distribution, even if we have to sell it to them at a discount. --- ## Breakevens 1. **ENT customers: Scenario 1 (no GA variable):** The deal beats direct API up to approximately **68 Foundry customers**. Below 68, the flat fee structure wins decisively. Above 68, BFL would have earned more serving those customers directly at \$0.09/image. In practice, whether BFL could realistically service 68+ enterprise Foundry customers directly is a different question — the distribution value of the Adobe deal is real even above the breakeven. 2. **GA image volume:** At a **lower per-image price (\$0.038):** direct API becomes more valuable once GA images exceed **\~132M per year**. That's a 6.6× multiple on current baseline demand, plausible if Firefly consumer usage scales meaningfully, but not a near-term concern if we believe they will run 20–40M images. At a **higher per-image price (recommendation is \$0.062):** the breakeven pushes all the way to **\~246M images**. At 100M images, the deal at high price still outperforms direct API by about \$4M. Again, we would have to believe that we could achieve that scale on our own, which isn’t necessarily as feasible. The only way this becomes unfavorable for us is if Foundry scales to 70+ enterprise customers *and* GA volumes cross 130–250M images *simultaneously*. ## Path 2: Higher cost on Foundry, and pricing GA/other segments for scale {toggle="true"} --- ***BFL Fee Assumptions*** - Fixed: \$8M /year - Variable (Foundry): Each P5 instance setup fee per customer is \$100K (first 10 customers), then \$90K (customers 11-50), and \$80K (51+ customers). - Variable (GA/Consumer Segment): Waterfall pricing, \$0.062 per image up to 200M images/year, then as low as \$0.038 per image ### 1. Conservative Case: ***Only 10 Foundry customers in both years, and 20M images across their consumer segment (cannibilizing all direct API spend from Adobe today).***
Year 1 Year 2 2-Year Total
Adobe Deal \$8.0M \$10.24M **\$18.24M**
Direct API (same demand @ \$0.09) \$3.12M \$3.12M **\$6.25M**
Open Weights (\$10K/cust/month) \$1.2M \$1.2M **\$2.4M**
**BFL's POV:** Over two years we earn \$17.76–18.24M versus \$6.25M if we were to serve customers directly via our API(a **\$11.5–12M premium)**. \$1M of the Year 2 revenue is coming from 10 instance fees. Infinite Canvas as AIs True Creative Interface Picture the scene: You are art directing a brand pitch. Two monitors. On the left, you are generating images on the playground. On the right: Claude for prompt refinement, Figma for layout, a browser tab running an upscaler. Four tools. One brain. Zero flow state.
Then it happens! After fourteen attempts, finally - the first decent image. Exact mood, exact light. You push your luck and try one more seed. Version 15 is a miss. Version 16 is worse. You want to go back, but the playground doesnt keep history - every session starts blank, and anything you didnt manually save is simply gone in a endless long history.
Ten minutes of reconstructing prompts from memory later or ten minutes of scrolling down the playground until you find the image - your momentum is ***dead.***
This is where professional AI design actually lives right now. The models themselves are extraordinary with photorealistic output in seconds. But the (most) interfaces wrapping them.. They are chat windows. Support ticket boxes basically. We accepted the chatbox because the models were new and the outputs were miraculous enough that the interface didnt matter. That period is over since last year. The models are now amazing and the prompt box has become the bottleneck it always was. Designing complex layered visual work through a chat window is the wrong tool for the job - in the same way a telephone is the wrong tool for architecture. *You can communicate ideas through it. You cannot build in it.* Designing visually complex, multi-layered work through a single text prompt in a chatbox is the wrong tool for the job and the infinite canvas is the only one that makes sense (right now). ## **The Problem Space** The productivity wall isnt coming from the models. Flux and other Models have never been more capable. The wall is coming from the medium and the medium right now is fundamentally broken for visual work. ### **The Linear Trap of Chatbots and Historys** The most glaring flaw of traditional LLM interfaces and image generation tools (like Midjourney, our Playground or other Examples) is that they operate on a strictly chronological, linear timeline. You input a prompt at the bottom, the output appears, and the entire conversation shifts upward. But design doesnt work that way. Design is spatial. It branches. It is an iterative spatial and branching process. A real creative process looks nothing like a chat thread. You generate a baseline, then split into three color directions. You take the second direction and explore four different compositional approaches. Then you pull back and hold the result next to the original to feel the distance traveled. That back and forth that simultaneous comparison thats where the actual thinking happens. A chat thread and our playground do not support this. In a chat interface, previous iterations are buried under the weight of new ones. In the Playground, the history disappears after a page reload, and bugs in the history feature prevent you from finding it again. This creates a severe psychological friction known as **Scroll Fatigue**. I find myself constantly scrolling up and down, trying to mentally hold the context of "Version 4" while looking at "Version 47." The interface treats every generation as a disposable, isolated transaction rather than a piece of a larger, evolving puzzle. ### **Context Switching and the Fragmented Mind** Because the chatbox cannot serve as a workspace and professionals are forced into what we call the "Frankenstein Workflow." You use a textbased AI to brainstorm the brief. You use a linear Chatbot to generate the raw imagery. You use a web-based Upscale. You use a heavy desktop software to composite the image. you use Slack to share the Images. This forces the brain to endure the **Context Switch Penalty**. Every time a professional switches between different software environments, it takes an average of 23 minutes to regain deep focus. you are moving your brain between entirely different modes of interaction from creative prompting to spatial layout, to technical file management. Furthermore - all systems loses context at every step. When you drag an image out of Playground into Figma (or whatever space we use to save and share images), the image becomes "dumb." Figma doesnt know what prompt generated it. If you need to make a slight adjustment to the lighting or change something else, you have to jump back into Playground and hope the UI lets you scroll to the missing Prompt. The bridge between generation and execution is completely broken. ![A recent FLUX Project I worked on - impossible to do in the Playground](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/dcb297f8-3a9b-48e6-9823-1f2e77449001/Bildschirmfoto_2026-04-15_um_09.54.54.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4663XEIS66G%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151917Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJGMEQCIB2MS73WIK7RgJMhrpEwm0dfUUgt%2Bf2bIdl3rcxqxmdCAiAgR7FKDqvoTwngRCVA5q7EPQFb9%2Bk0rlb3cE1U4sZbmCr%2FAwgIEAAaDDYzNzQyMzE4MzgwNSIMl1bhDnnTjwjObtcaKtwDu7ufhf2%2B4f4oKJcP6UQ554HU5UouSIG2qJg9YJ8l6N1ogmW3fJTOa2Rgf0doYThXdljMdP35ui9LzDzSymMDZm8OvXpE2d09MZeU3KYrVqOZrGL2m%2BpLRZpnRlpNaINEqbLDqQzgXZl7%2BajGbZ8GTGyygP%2B1tqTkr3XBrc%2BO71AmuURWpoX%2BKpTs863pp0FsqLgCbDLvJBGQx4C49GcZdVUXfUDsFdPaNp4Hn11mcoWUFVBHZ5CD34FQ3hWPtRQNQ5l9X8xOha1jkFiRc%2BEMierrvNILLmVxEdO%2BzP66cdjWQvzBolN3AYhyRcBklONSmdBMy3vMgd0svqRi4wgou0tfAKVY0tXfRQy3D0D0FioULpk6dNGpPqhlC6d2SwduHfBeEQdU8jgD%2FDbtP4Pazp9pC8jASzuBME%2B%2FgFiQ8%2Bw2Uz1RPCnMnhyWIf5st%2F1XJPHU3F1UnRl7uDBfMSvzW74x4v8VApK8ONGfy2smr%2FX1dl2ANTp2YUv5csylNZmN%2FS9dmVfRHGtOknkpQJTEp%2BHBG2SBu5%2BZb0H5TiIbvYkBgWEbMF%2FeyAcdPJEIiHDMO0qyVBaMoh3B5xDp8gDuk9cqFZJMaUUz4GfnK4zkbqPNENy9jjznnpXfqmgw49OTzwY6pgGhDDzte4aq7LnDBS5iSVsDu56Byw01sTWqj0laQ94PVd1M7rQoD4EBmihdmyAyNiMdbwVYluJpQOf5zB0CBRDzU829Bm9CNQI8gj0200o%2Bir43gTddct9x50M9vVb6AjN3%2BAK6RK02tsuBrl8LQ9yo09crlThuas1SUJwGv1Oi9gtRia83wWVHes%2FL7xxs8L7D%2BIBvqJh4W3A%2BIdV4HF0ilVQWOegB&X-Amz-Signature=4dea8a6b36db6eabeb34726b14d790a59d5bb3df5f947894666e9e972308426b&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) ## **Part 2: The First Principles of Visual Ideation ** If the chatbox is the wrong answer what does the right one look like? To get there we have to stop thinking about "talking to an agent" and start thinking about how creative thinking actually works. before software, before ai, before screens, before any of this. So if the chatbox fails - what replaces(d) it? The answer isnt found in better software or agents. Its found by stepping back further than that. Before the interface debate, before AI, before screens entirely and asking a simpler question: *how does creative thinking actually work?* ### **The Architecture of the Human Moodboard** Long before digital design tools existed creative professionals used physical space to think. They pinned images on the wall with polaroid photographs into massive corkboards. ![A oldschool in(finite) cana](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/d7437879-1a0c-4a1f-8430-c6b13a43aa72/1_ia4Z2bQWOTD_Ri14eXlrIg.webp?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4663XEIS66G%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151917Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJGMEQCIB2MS73WIK7RgJMhrpEwm0dfUUgt%2Bf2bIdl3rcxqxmdCAiAgR7FKDqvoTwngRCVA5q7EPQFb9%2Bk0rlb3cE1U4sZbmCr%2FAwgIEAAaDDYzNzQyMzE4MzgwNSIMl1bhDnnTjwjObtcaKtwDu7ufhf2%2B4f4oKJcP6UQ554HU5UouSIG2qJg9YJ8l6N1ogmW3fJTOa2Rgf0doYThXdljMdP35ui9LzDzSymMDZm8OvXpE2d09MZeU3KYrVqOZrGL2m%2BpLRZpnRlpNaINEqbLDqQzgXZl7%2BajGbZ8GTGyygP%2B1tqTkr3XBrc%2BO71AmuURWpoX%2BKpTs863pp0FsqLgCbDLvJBGQx4C49GcZdVUXfUDsFdPaNp4Hn11mcoWUFVBHZ5CD34FQ3hWPtRQNQ5l9X8xOha1jkFiRc%2BEMierrvNILLmVxEdO%2BzP66cdjWQvzBolN3AYhyRcBklONSmdBMy3vMgd0svqRi4wgou0tfAKVY0tXfRQy3D0D0FioULpk6dNGpPqhlC6d2SwduHfBeEQdU8jgD%2FDbtP4Pazp9pC8jASzuBME%2B%2FgFiQ8%2Bw2Uz1RPCnMnhyWIf5st%2F1XJPHU3F1UnRl7uDBfMSvzW74x4v8VApK8ONGfy2smr%2FX1dl2ANTp2YUv5csylNZmN%2FS9dmVfRHGtOknkpQJTEp%2BHBG2SBu5%2BZb0H5TiIbvYkBgWEbMF%2FeyAcdPJEIiHDMO0qyVBaMoh3B5xDp8gDuk9cqFZJMaUUz4GfnK4zkbqPNENy9jjznnpXfqmgw49OTzwY6pgGhDDzte4aq7LnDBS5iSVsDu56Byw01sTWqj0laQ94PVd1M7rQoD4EBmihdmyAyNiMdbwVYluJpQOf5zB0CBRDzU829Bm9CNQI8gj0200o%2Bir43gTddct9x50M9vVb6AjN3%2BAK6RK02tsuBrl8LQ9yo09crlThuas1SUJwGv1Oi9gtRia83wWVHes%2FL7xxs8L7D%2BIBvqJh4W3A%2BIdV4HF0ilVQWOegB&X-Amz-Signature=294c2a9ae623caee38b21fc9352a9ae1f1fb56ada05834ffd6b1c17a5a9b800b&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) This is a cognitive necessity based on the theory of the **Extended Mind**. The human brain struggles to hold multiple complex visual images in its shortterm memory simultaneously. By placing items in physical space we offload that cognitive burden onto our environment. We use spatial juxtaposition and placing a harsh brutalist font directly next to a soft organic photo to instantly gauge harmony or tension. ### **Jobs to Be Done (JTBD) in Creative Collaboration** When we apply the "Jobs to Be Done" framework to enterprise design the inadequacy of the chat interface becomes even more clearer When a Marketing Director sits down to work, their JTBD is almost never "I want to generate a single, isolated 1024x1024 PNG of a dog riding a skateboard." Their JTBD is: "I need to orchestrate a marketing campaign with 40 different Flux Images. I need a primary hero image for the website, three vertical video variations for TikTok, a 3D product mockup for our investor deck, and a consistent color palette that ties them all together." A chatbox cannot deliver this. It delivers isolated assets and not a visual world. ### The “Flow” in Workflow As I already said: When I use the Playground or our API im stuck in a one-at-a-time mode: Input prompt, wait for result, and if I want to try something different, start a whole new process. Its typical of many AI design tools and it breaks my focus. Almost exactly one year ago something changed. Weavy and Flora were launched. Two Infinite Canvas UI - both have grown incredibly fast. Weavy has since been acquired by Figma. Flora recently closed its Series B round with \$45 million in new funding. With these infinite canvas I can run several ideas at once and see them develop side by side. This matches how I actually think when designing or protoyping - considering multiple options simultaneously rather than one after another. ![*A demo of Flora*](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/2eb9a63b-f8d6-4a17-98cd-58f751eb2b3c/optimized_Screenshot_2025-03-14_at_10.45.04_AM.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4663XEIS66G%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151917Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJGMEQCIB2MS73WIK7RgJMhrpEwm0dfUUgt%2Bf2bIdl3rcxqxmdCAiAgR7FKDqvoTwngRCVA5q7EPQFb9%2Bk0rlb3cE1U4sZbmCr%2FAwgIEAAaDDYzNzQyMzE4MzgwNSIMl1bhDnnTjwjObtcaKtwDu7ufhf2%2B4f4oKJcP6UQ554HU5UouSIG2qJg9YJ8l6N1ogmW3fJTOa2Rgf0doYThXdljMdP35ui9LzDzSymMDZm8OvXpE2d09MZeU3KYrVqOZrGL2m%2BpLRZpnRlpNaINEqbLDqQzgXZl7%2BajGbZ8GTGyygP%2B1tqTkr3XBrc%2BO71AmuURWpoX%2BKpTs863pp0FsqLgCbDLvJBGQx4C49GcZdVUXfUDsFdPaNp4Hn11mcoWUFVBHZ5CD34FQ3hWPtRQNQ5l9X8xOha1jkFiRc%2BEMierrvNILLmVxEdO%2BzP66cdjWQvzBolN3AYhyRcBklONSmdBMy3vMgd0svqRi4wgou0tfAKVY0tXfRQy3D0D0FioULpk6dNGpPqhlC6d2SwduHfBeEQdU8jgD%2FDbtP4Pazp9pC8jASzuBME%2B%2FgFiQ8%2Bw2Uz1RPCnMnhyWIf5st%2F1XJPHU3F1UnRl7uDBfMSvzW74x4v8VApK8ONGfy2smr%2FX1dl2ANTp2YUv5csylNZmN%2FS9dmVfRHGtOknkpQJTEp%2BHBG2SBu5%2BZb0H5TiIbvYkBgWEbMF%2FeyAcdPJEIiHDMO0qyVBaMoh3B5xDp8gDuk9cqFZJMaUUz4GfnK4zkbqPNENy9jjznnpXfqmgw49OTzwY6pgGhDDzte4aq7LnDBS5iSVsDu56Byw01sTWqj0laQ94PVd1M7rQoD4EBmihdmyAyNiMdbwVYluJpQOf5zB0CBRDzU829Bm9CNQI8gj0200o%2Bir43gTddct9x50M9vVb6AjN3%2BAK6RK02tsuBrl8LQ9yo09crlThuas1SUJwGv1Oi9gtRia83wWVHes%2FL7xxs8L7D%2BIBvqJh4W3A%2BIdV4HF0ilVQWOegB&X-Amz-Signature=dcf930a55bb3679712b6166b134ef8ca6af836c0c5038e29bc0fa3d80ebf836b&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) The sauce is in how closely the Flora team worked with actual creative professionals to understand their workflow. They collaborated with New York Universitys Tisch School of the Arts, designfirm Pentagram, and other major creative institutions and agencies across the US. They are building it for real creative workflows because they are embedded in those communities. You can feel that closeness to the end user when you are using the product. It just makes sense. The lesson im taking away: In the world of AI powered tools, understanding your users deeply is (slowly) becoming more important than the underlaying models. Its not just about the Models anymore. Users dont care about the technical details of how the model works. Users care about whether it helps us create better work more efficiently. Thats it. Can "}

content: {"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"👋 AI Solutions Onboarding","url":"https://www.notion.so/2b4c370222d58085b88adf9d67fc9756","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/2b4c370222d58085b88adf9d67fc9756 as of 2026-03-11T13:22:12.226Z: {"Verification":"verified","title":"AI Solutions Onboarding"} # GTM Context - - - - - recent company update & strategy [https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/13mr7svxqVu6ygmxgdPbSPBLGswNPaaVeChd-rBLBSfI/edit?usp=sharing](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/13mr7svxqVu6ygmxgdPbSPBLGswNPaaVeChd-rBLBSfI/edit?usp=sharing) - - Make sure you’re part of the [GTM Google Group](https://groups.google.com/a/blackforestlabs.ai/g/sales/members), if not yet ask to add # Solutions Vision & Goals: - Read & comment your thoughts on AI Solutions Strategy: ### **Question to brainstorm on & discuss with team:** - How can / should we customize BFL tech to certain customers? - What could be the customized products & services to offer in the Applied AI context? - How do we experiment faster with what & how to offer customizations? # BFL Tech Context - - [Playground](https://playground.bfl.ai/image/generate) - [Prompting Guide - FLUX.2 - Black Forest Labs](https://docs.bfl.ai/guides/prompting_guide_flux2) - In our API ([Hoellental](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/hoellental)), the accessible Endpoints vary based on the organization ID linked to your token. Add your Organization Id to the internal org whitelisting to get access to more endpoints: [https://github.com/black-forest-labs/hoellental/pull/3087](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/hoellental/pull/3087) # Tool Access Checklist - [ ] slack - [ ] notion - [ ] attio - [ ] github - [ ] claude - [ ] claude code - [ ] cursor (?) - [ ] azure - [ ] vercel - [ ] linear - [ ] discord - [ ] signoz - [ ] training cluster - [ ] granola # Organizing & Documenting SE & FDE Work Let’s minimize meeting time by maximizing async visibility of all progress & resources ## Knowledge Collection & Documentation - Notion is our core knowledge base & internal documentation tool - Best way to find answers to your questions is using [Claude with “Ask BFL”](/28ec370222d58076a535d4c9a11bf63f?pvs=25) ## Customization Project Progress Tracking - Single point of access for customer resources & notes: - We track progress of customization project progress in Attio (CRM): [app.attio.com](https://app.attio.com/black-forest-labs/custom/customizations/) - Customer Drives are spread between Partnership & Sales Drives - Sales: [drive.google.com](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1NzWdEBycyBh-hVf7qdnv4AtjCkb40sdP?usp=drive_link) - Partnerships: [drive.google.com](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A3-13caXR5nJYVwpiN5chpm9mTQHDOob?usp=drive_link) - To store any customer assets, or resources created by you please create a “Customizations” folder in the respective account drive. - Please create a “Customization” object in Attio for every engagement you’re working on. - Every Customization needs to be pointed to a Notion page that tracks resources. Ideally this is a page for the specific project you’re working on including created assets, prompts, challenges, solution architectures etc. ([see this example](/2e0c370222d58084b2b4c0251fd9ed66?pvs=25)) - Alternatively link to account page in , please create one if not existing - Every customization needs to be tied to a Deal object. If that one doesn’t exist yet, please reach out to the sales or partnership colleague to create it. - The Customization view will be used as basis for our weekly FDE progress sync ## Other important tools: AI Meeting Notes: Human Evals for generations: [https://eval.bfl.ai/user-guide](https://eval.bfl.ai/user-guide) Logs, traces & more: Signoz # Onboarding Challenges ## BFL admin Grant yourself 100,000,000 credits on the playground. Check whether you find how to raise your API quota. Use Claude to help you how to do it: ## Generate your Slack profile picture with FLUX - Use our BFL [playground](https://playground.bfl.ai/image/generate) to generate your profile picture - Explore Model variants and their strengths and weaknesses ## Warming up with FLUX - Generate 5-10 Mini Countryman Campaign Resources, make sure always assure absolute car consistency and to follow visual language of the MINI campaigns - - [Der MINI Countryman: Mit Platz für Familie und Freunde](https://www.mini.de/de_DE/home/range/mini-countryman.html) - - How could we automate this & build a workflow around the generation process? *Design a high level workflow architecture.* ## Deploy your first customized endpoint - Read through the [README for the ](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/hoellental/blob/gtm-master/api/core/gtm/README.md)[`gtm-master`](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/hoellental/blob/gtm-master/api/core/gtm/README.md)[ branch](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/hoellental/blob/gtm-master/api/core/gtm/README.md) in our api monorepo hoellental - Deploy a customized endpoint with a behavior of your choice to the `internal_bfl` partner org - for example you could build a pipeline with customized prompt upsampling to only use shades of your favorite color - Open a PR, get it reviewed & deploy your custom endpoint to a gtm labs endpoint - Make some api calls and post the results + instructions to call your endpoint in the #tischler Slack channel Additional context and instructions for the customized endpoint - Check out [this PR ](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/hoellental/pull/3094)on how an custom endpoint could look like - Feature branch from (and merging to) the gtm-master branch in Hoellental - Once you have done your change and created a PR, add the review and a region tag (where the deployment should be spun up) to the PR - Deployment takes around 15mins - To test your endpoint, make sure you have a **Staging BFL API Key **- this is different from your regular BFL API Key for prod. Follow [this video](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C074J2C10BA/1766143740.810639/1766094284.804429) to create your API Key "}

### Upcoming Events {toggle="true"} New database ### Contracts / Agreements {toggle="true"} View of Contract Database ### Key People {toggle="true"} View of Key People Database ### Docs/Resources {toggle="true"} :gdrive:[ Shared Folder with Assets ](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1pe4SSCoWSCFypvoJLl-7uUjV6uzIijTe) \[Internal Strategy\] Amazon Pricing Proposal - [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BXpjOREAm0sxfm1OP3qkyjvPheF2yxYfeXyKaCINUg4/edit?gid=1486453055#gid=1486453055](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BXpjOREAm0sxfm1OP3qkyjvPheF2yxYfeXyKaCINUg4/edit?gid=1486453055#gid=1486453055) Review: Amazon Vendor Security Policy [https://drive.google.com/file/d/17ugAExjz7h5Q4WjAzNJ5cnalCZ5gKSZV/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/17ugAExjz7h5Q4WjAzNJ5cnalCZ5gKSZV/view?usp=drive_link) :pdf: → Bedrock Opportunity Bedrock [https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1ciB82e-OzolxgVeIguBCdDVGzoV25XuNpDYXyXoR3CU/edit?slide=id.g383ce4fab86_0_286#slide=id.g383ce4fab86_0_286](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1ciB82e-OzolxgVeIguBCdDVGzoV25XuNpDYXyXoR3CU/edit?slide=id.g383ce4fab86_0_286#slide=id.g383ce4fab86_0_286) ### Competitive Dynamics {toggle="true"} [Amazon Nova](/273c370222d580bd9a8df94aff7a534c?pvs=25) → Amazon’s LLM + Image Model ### News {toggle="true"} - 12/29/2025 - [Prime Video NBA Schedule](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/entertainment/stream-nba-prime-video) - 11/11/2025 - [Transform campaign and asset development with Creative Agent](https://advertising.amazon.com/resources/whats-new/unboxed-2025-creative-agent?ref_=a20m_us_wn_ftrd3_btn_111125_wn_ca) - 09/17/2025 - [Amazon Ads launches new agentic AI creative tool](https://advertising.amazon.com/library/news/amazon-ads-agentic-ai-creative-tool) ### Use Cases {toggle="true"} **Amazon Ads / Creative X** - [Creative Studio - Enhance Campaigns with AI from Amazon Ads](https://aistudio.amazon.com/) - Create and build campaigns with AI. This is where FLUX is integrated. - [How Amazon is using AI to dominate streaming TV ads - Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91435813/amazon-dominating-streaming-tv-ads-ai) - [How Amazon is using AI to dominate streaming TV ads - Fast Company](https://archive.ph/20251111151129/https://www.fastcompany.com/91435813/amazon-dominating-streaming-tv-ads-ai) - [Amazon is about to be flooded with AI-generated video ads](https://www.theverge.com/news/685160/amazon-ads-ai-video-generator-us-launch-availability) - [Amazon has a new creative agent to help your business build its own ads](https://www.techradar.com/pro/amazon-has-a-new-creative-agent-to-help-your-business-build-its-own-ads) - [AWS re:Invent 2025 - Amazon Ads Creative Agent uses AWS to democratize ad creation (IND3335)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EPRE8_FHGdQ) **Alexa+ ** - [Introducing Alexa.com, a completely new way to interact with Alexa+](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/devices/alexa-plus-web-ai-assistant) > You can use [Alexa.com](http://alexa.com/) to get quick answers, explore complex topics, create content, plan trip itineraries, and get help with homework. But Alexa+ doesn't just provide information, it’s designed to take action. It can help you complete countless tasks: managing your to-do list, updating your family calendar, controlling your smart home, making reservations, and so much more. It also provides persistent context and continuity, allowing you to access Alexa on whichever device or interface best serves the task at hand, with all previous chats, preferences, and personalization seamlessly carrying over. - [Expedia, Yelp, Angi, and Square to build new agentic experiences for Alexa+](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/devices/alexa-plus-voice-booking-integrations) **Prime Video** **Amazon MGM Studios** - [Exclusive: Amazon plans to use AI to speed up TV and film production](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/amazon-plans-use-ai-speed-up-tv-film-production-2026-02-04/) ### Customizations {toggle="true"} Amazon Product Photo Dataset \[EXT SVEN\] Product Photography Alexa Deal — Pending Items ## Meeting Notes --- ### \| Matt / Augustine {toggle="true"} **Attendees:** - BFL: Matt - Amazon: Augustine ### Call Prep ### Opening (2 min) "Hey Augustine, appreciate the time. I read through your latest draft and your comments. I want to use this call to understand what's actually blocking us, not to negotiate, because I think Monday will be more productive if we go in knowing where the real gaps are." "Augustine, I appreciate the time. I want to be direct with you before Monday.
We've now moved our positions twice in your favor. On SLAs, on commercial terms, on structure. Your latest draft came back more complex and more restrictive than the one before it. That's not the direction we need to be moving.
We have a shared goal of launching to customers in 10 days. That means a signed contract by next Friday. I want to hit that. But the way we get there isn't another round of redlines. It's getting the right people in a room early next week who can actually make decisions.
So here's what I need from this call. One, who on your technical team is driving the SLA requirements? I want them on a call with Ian before Monday. Two, who has the authority on your side to close on training restrictions and the minimum commit? Those are the two issues where we're genuinely stuck, and I haven't been able to get resolution through you. That's not a criticism, it's just a recognition that we probably need to escalate on both sides to get this done.
If we can get the right people in the room Monday with a mandate to close, I'm confident we can get there. If we go into Monday the same way we've gone into the last few calls, we're going to miss the launch window. I don't think either of us wants that." --- ### Signal 1: Who's Driving the SLA Complexity? (8 min) "Your team came back with more metrics, not fewer. P50, P90, a separate uptime SLA. Help me understand, is that coming from your engineering team, legal, or somewhere else?" *What you're listening for: does he name someone, or deflect?* If he names an engineer: "Great. Can we get that person on a call with Ian today or tomorrow? I think there's a genuine technical misunderstanding here that a 30-minute conversation can resolve." If he says "I'm not technical": "I know, so who are you relying on for the technical input? I want to connect them with Ian directly before Monday so we're not debating this in a big room." If he deflects entirely: he either doesn't have engineering backing or is being told to hold the line regardless of technical merit. {"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"🌲 An Introduction to Generative Models via the BFL API, our Playground and forestlabs.black","url":"https://www.notion.so/16fc370222d5801eade4cb0ceee1caa8","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/16fc370222d5801eade4cb0ceee1caa8 as of 2026-04-10T17:57:44.876Z: {"title":"An Introduction to Generative Models via the BFL API, our Playground and forestlabs.black"} ✨ 🌲 ## Intro The goal of generative modeling is to learn the underlying structure of a given data distribution, and to sample from it. If this learning process was successful, a generative model can be used to create entirely new, unseen samples from that distribution. This can, for example, be used to create new images from textual descriptions or “prompts”, or other images (think “img2video”). The following tasks aim to teach about generative model capabilities that are currently available via the [BFL API](https://docs.bfl.ml/). ## What is an API? An API (Application Programming Interface) functions like a universal translator and a delivery system for software. When two programs need to communicate with each other, the API provides a standardized way to package and exchange data between them. Each request usually comprises three key elements:
- **Endpoint**: the destination address to which the request is sent.
- **Proper formatting**: Using standardized data formats to ensure that both programs understand the data being exchanged.
- **Authentication**: Verifying that you have authorization to access the API, often through methods such as API keys or OAuth tokens. For example, for a text-to-image API: - **Request**: you send a text description such as “sunset over the mountains” along with your API key to the API endpoint. - **Validation**: The API checks your API key to confirm that you are authorized to use the service. - **Processing**: The request is processed by the image generation model, which creates an image based on your description. - **Response**: The API returns the generated image or an error message if something went wrong, e.g. an invalid API key or an unclear description.

## Inpainting with FLUX Fill An additional feature we released via FLUX.1 Fill as part of the “FLUX.1 Tools” was inpainting (Fill) and outpainting (Expand). We see three major use cases for this tool:
- i) Object insertion. For the image with the two glasses below, first try to insert a third one. Next, try to fill both of them with any liquid of your liking. Finally, try to remove one of the glasses.
- ii) Object removal. Now, try to remove one of the glasses (don’t worry if it does not work, models fail consistently at this task)
- iii) Outpainting: Currently only supported via the “Mask” upload in forestlabs.black, we can skip it for now. Good for extending images on any side. To use FLUX.1 Fill we can go back to the playground and select \`Fill\` on the left sidebar. You can then upload an image and select the area you'd like to change (see screenshot). To use Expand, simply select the expand mode below the Fill mode in the sidebar. ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/252b401c-d798-48b5-a5f6-cd7c6cae0daa/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466ZJCKGI4H%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151922Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJIMEYCIQD0VbvbO8djOeW0rThx8glcgP3AmXue4GEnVZu17R8CygIhAIwrQP7OuPMdgSkYaZo9mjM4HSR5rCKYxmhlcBidpBHvKv8DCAgQABoMNjM3NDIzMTgzODA1IgyrIp5Z1aE3M51liKwq3APeK7c%2BwtY3roJIYc6OGODXVcSsE3YWp6traQGILUz3Q2ZLSltzcjO93PW11HlFWvhqf2UwxNxvNcXwaoG%2BoE0CZ9k%2BCPnAbL5hDzc4UGvEDsDL8huunJrQ9TKQZhnxMenm%2FAUGRHarVaNP%2Bpyuw8MBPUJLOIMUBBNu4X2OLCDVAFm49kP9MvBOQK%2FZLTgkEI%2BIg1DyLCkWAxVd9KKYlrjoZzOqF%2F%2BRcFbyL0Usd5UKKemSmNdNVqX4sR0XNEms1X5mmLPps77keSgB3R20SVTCtQ55TCw5%2BuvhkO5xgCmMOVgGGfS6%2BOBLC%2BRtnuh46%2BieKGOInlrLgzQmD0BOsuvHLBtrXvWFE6D5WXKg7C9at9FXuD5BtHXX5SzNPZekVSFJtxvGK3y3T9YZwfkxt2x2cnXiGIpz1J5kAn2EWu9sMXByJr4AOH1iTxbiJKpEhPwbtXi9wEqz5XN1S8%2BI4OFeFHjwmuxIookUECCcwpPjHLjN%2F9PGIQwnKMXIMXzt6mbP%2BN8Bj%2BZU9g71k0yO%2B0MciJS02rlWpZz7BjYcwDOkl54tzGHAr%2BRzd8nsdecmiyBUn8IA9116535COMeu7pKWQecjNVafHHBtgUJrlkHhcRX5ZR0hkampvQkPrzDuzpPPBjqkAfRpe94uZy7MtsZ2y0vUYkssoTvR9%2FFG4b53%2Fg8WtEdFbr2kkAcaEj4fAojxeELMU6OKBepQfW%2F3tqOqlyrpB8EU846wXV%2F%2F39xENMboxtUo4HbWztG%2Fii3y50hiho%2BovH37s7E%2Fo4%2BDnCCLwtuJvPLIVJSJ3g66djbgod4ocdmhNut2ObfjJyd3mM83BNDs0eQGFbG%2FVwLiP4dsDpv2YxJGxHvS&X-Amz-Signature=db52f100b7529c4d766c03e76c865b5d0fba1732c915a1212d6d64d28af8e3ec&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) ## Finetuning Now we will use our finetuning endpoint `/v1/finetune` via our [Forestlabs tool](forestlabs.black) to create a
finetuned model of a character or object via the LoRA algorithm, that enables to finetune our model
with as few as 5-10 examples that all show the same character or object. Feel free to train a LoRA of yourself :) ### Training a customized model ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/eab02b86-598f-4c20-9a30-044e86231111/forestlabs_finetune_training.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466ZJCKGI4H%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151922Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJIMEYCIQD0VbvbO8djOeW0rThx8glcgP3AmXue4GEnVZu17R8CygIhAIwrQP7OuPMdgSkYaZo9mjM4HSR5rCKYxmhlcBidpBHvKv8DCAgQABoMNjM3NDIzMTgzODA1IgyrIp5Z1aE3M51liKwq3APeK7c%2BwtY3roJIYc6OGODXVcSsE3YWp6traQGILUz3Q2ZLSltzcjO93PW11HlFWvhqf2UwxNxvNcXwaoG%2BoE0CZ9k%2BCPnAbL5hDzc4UGvEDsDL8huunJrQ9TKQZhnxMenm%2FAUGRHarVaNP%2Bpyuw8MBPUJLOIMUBBNu4X2OLCDVAFm49kP9MvBOQK%2FZLTgkEI%2BIg1DyLCkWAxVd9KKYlrjoZzOqF%2F%2BRcFbyL0Usd5UKKemSmNdNVqX4sR0XNEms1X5mmLPps77keSgB3R20SVTCtQ55TCw5%2BuvhkO5xgCmMOVgGGfS6%2BOBLC%2BRtnuh46%2BieKGOInlrLgzQmD0BOsuvHLBtrXvWFE6D5WXKg7C9at9FXuD5BtHXX5SzNPZekVSFJtxvGK3y3T9YZwfkxt2x2cnXiGIpz1J5kAn2EWu9sMXByJr4AOH1iTxbiJKpEhPwbtXi9wEqz5XN1S8%2BI4OFeFHjwmuxIookUECCcwpPjHLjN%2F9PGIQwnKMXIMXzt6mbP%2BN8Bj%2BZU9g71k0yO%2B0MciJS02rlWpZz7BjYcwDOkl54tzGHAr%2BRzd8nsdecmiyBUn8IA9116535COMeu7pKWQecjNVafHHBtgUJrlkHhcRX5ZR0hkampvQkPrzDuzpPPBjqkAfRpe94uZy7MtsZ2y0vUYkssoTvR9%2FFG4b53%2Fg8WtEdFbr2kkAcaEj4fAojxeELMU6OKBepQfW%2F3tqOqlyrpB8EU846wXV%2F%2F39xENMboxtUo4HbWztG%2Fii3y50hiho%2BovH37s7E%2Fo4%2BDnCCLwtuJvPLIVJSJ3g66djbgod4ocdmhNut2ObfjJyd3mM83BNDs0eQGFbG%2FVwLiP4dsDpv2YxJGxHvS&X-Amz-Signature=54534b2e61b43f05baa1b24868a1858df89c6532ba38d2b39990a630b4b4570b&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) To enable the training, follow these steps: - select the endpoint `finetune [production]` - select a name for your customized finetune (here ‘bfl-test’) - define a trigger word (here ANDI). Using this work in a prompt for the finetuned model will trigger the finetuned model to generate an images depicting the character or object it was finetuned on. - change the learning rate to 0.00001 - The remaining parameters can be kept as they are by default. - Upload a .zip folder containing images of an object / character that you would like to teach the model about. Try to use at least 10-20 different images. - start the training by clicking the generate button at the top - wait a bit until the training has finished - using `my_finetunes [production]` you can check if the training has already ended. If so then you should see your finetune (the name you selected plus some number indicating the timestamp of creation) appear at the end of the list that’s displyed when clicking the `Generate` button. You can vary the `Mode`parameter. Available options are `general`, `character`, `style` and `object`. Do so and create one finetune for each of them for the same set of images. Compare the different finetunes with each other after that. Additionally you can vary the `Quality Mode` parameter. Available options are `maximum_speed`, `balanced` and `maximum_quality` . ### Sample with your Finetuned Model ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/406e2a06-70e8-4f8d-83ea-44a91f65904e/forestlabs_finetune_inference.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466ZJCKGI4H%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151922Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJIMEYCIQD0VbvbO8djOeW0rThx8glcgP3AmXue4GEnVZu17R8CygIhAIwrQP7OuPMdgSkYaZo9mjM4HSR5rCKYxmhlcBidpBHvKv8DCAgQABoMNjM3NDIzMTgzODA1IgyrIp5Z1aE3M51liKwq3APeK7c%2BwtY3roJIYc6OGODXVcSsE3YWp6traQGILUz3Q2ZLSltzcjO93PW11HlFWvhqf2UwxNxvNcXwaoG%2BoE0CZ9k%2BCPnAbL5hDzc4UGvEDsDL8huunJrQ9TKQZhnxMenm%2FAUGRHarVaNP%2Bpyuw8MBPUJLOIMUBBNu4X2OLCDVAFm49kP9MvBOQK%2FZLTgkEI%2BIg1DyLCkWAxVd9KKYlrjoZzOqF%2F%2BRcFbyL0Usd5UKKemSmNdNVqX4sR0XNEms1X5mmLPps77keSgB3R20SVTCtQ55TCw5%2BuvhkO5xgCmMOVgGGfS6%2BOBLC%2BRtnuh46%2BieKGOInlrLgzQmD0BOsuvHLBtrXvWFE6D5WXKg7C9at9FXuD5BtHXX5SzNPZekVSFJtxvGK3y3T9YZwfkxt2x2cnXiGIpz1J5kAn2EWu9sMXByJr4AOH1iTxbiJKpEhPwbtXi9wEqz5XN1S8%2BI4OFeFHjwmuxIookUECCcwpPjHLjN%2F9PGIQwnKMXIMXzt6mbP%2BN8Bj%2BZU9g71k0yO%2B0MciJS02rlWpZz7BjYcwDOkl54tzGHAr%2BRzd8nsdecmiyBUn8IA9116535COMeu7pKWQecjNVafHHBtgUJrlkHhcRX5ZR0hkampvQkPrzDuzpPPBjqkAfRpe94uZy7MtsZ2y0vUYkssoTvR9%2FFG4b53%2Fg8WtEdFbr2kkAcaEj4fAojxeELMU6OKBepQfW%2F3tqOqlyrpB8EU846wXV%2F%2F39xENMboxtUo4HbWztG%2Fii3y50hiho%2BovH37s7E%2Fo4%2BDnCCLwtuJvPLIVJSJ3g66djbgod4ocdmhNut2ObfjJyd3mM83BNDs0eQGFbG%2FVwLiP4dsDpv2YxJGxHvS&X-Amz-Signature=fe6659ac2787c45bfc9f11ed8d15f3e08ab2b4ca2559113d336f0dbde736969e&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) Once the finetuning is finished: - switch to the endpoint `flux-pro-1.1-finetuned [production]` - select the name you’ve given to your finetune - start sampling. Remember to use the trigger word in the prompt if you want to generate the character or object it’s been trained on ## Fast Editing via FLUX.1 Kontext \[pro\] and \[max\] FLUX.1 Kontext is a game changer for the image editing due to its great character consistency and speed. In the last task you might’ve might’ve noticed that it’s pretty effortful to create a model that can preserve a character only with text-to-image. Now we’re using Kontext for the same task than in the last task. ie for generating multiple different images that consistently show the same object or character in different contexts/environment. etc. So we go back to the playground and select the \`Edit\`mode, upload an image and just leave the rest up to FLUX.1 Kontext (see example below) 😉 ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/4d03ce34-2247-4358-bbe1-df11d7c1c3d5/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466ZJCKGI4H%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151922Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJIMEYCIQD0VbvbO8djOeW0rThx8glcgP3AmXue4GEnVZu17R8CygIhAIwrQP7OuPMdgSkYaZo9mjM4HSR5rCKYxmhlcBidpBHvKv8DCAgQABoMNjM3NDIzMTgzODA1IgyrIp5Z1aE3M51liKwq3APeK7c%2BwtY3roJIYc6OGODXVcSsE3YWp6traQGILUz3Q2ZLSltzcjO93PW11HlFWvhqf2UwxNxvNcXwaoG%2BoE0CZ9k%2BCPnAbL5hDzc4UGvEDsDL8huunJrQ9TKQZhnxMenm%2FAUGRHarVaNP%2Bpyuw8MBPUJLOIMUBBNu4X2OLCDVAFm49kP9MvBOQK%2FZLTgkEI%2BIg1DyLCkWAxVd9KKYlrjoZzOqF%2F%2BRcFbyL0Usd5UKKemSmNdNVqX4sR0XNEms1X5mmLPps77keSgB3R20SVTCtQ55TCw5%2BuvhkO5xgCmMOVgGGfS6%2BOBLC%2BRtnuh46%2BieKGOInlrLgzQmD0BOsuvHLBtrXvWFE6D5WXKg7C9at9FXuD5BtHXX5SzNPZekVSFJtxvGK3y3T9YZwfkxt2x2cnXiGIpz1J5kAn2EWu9sMXByJr4AOH1iTxbiJKpEhPwbtXi9wEqz5XN1S8%2BI4OFeFHjwmuxIookUECCcwpPjHLjN%2F9PGIQwnKMXIMXzt6mbP%2BN8Bj%2BZU9g71k0yO%2B0MciJS02rlWpZz7BjYcwDOkl54tzGHAr%2BRzd8nsdecmiyBUn8IA9116535COMeu7pKWQecjNVafHHBtgUJrlkHhcRX5ZR0hkampvQkPrzDuzpPPBjqkAfRpe94uZy7MtsZ2y0vUYkssoTvR9%2FFG4b53%2Fg8WtEdFbr2kkAcaEj4fAojxeELMU6OKBepQfW%2F3tqOqlyrpB8EU846wXV%2F%2F39xENMboxtUo4HbWztG%2Fii3y50hiho%2BovH37s7E%2Fo4%2BDnCCLwtuJvPLIVJSJ3g66djbgod4ocdmhNut2ObfjJyd3mM83BNDs0eQGFbG%2FVwLiP4dsDpv2YxJGxHvS&X-Amz-Signature=0e6d5d075cb15596e3f40451649b7792a965b216103d3dda22c93e766794f918&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) ## Putting it all together The final task is to create a small photo story using all the endpoints together as needed. The story should be about 15-20 images. To be able to show
a consistent main character, it’s useful to use FLUX.1 Kontext. Lastly write a small report about this project. State which models and endpoints you were glad and which ones you had issues with both from a performance perspective (for the respective model) and from a usage perspective (how easy/intuitive was it to use it). {"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"API Customers with special data handling","url":"https://www.notion.so/26fc370222d580beb7a0db2115860fc5","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/26fc370222d580beb7a0db2115860fc5 as of 2025-10-10T15:19:40.670Z: {"title":"API Customers with special data handling"} Learn more about our default policies on handling personal customer data [here](/26fc370222d580e9bca6dd04bb91ba5d?pvs=25) With some customers we have zero data retention and no training clauses in place. This page is a tracker shared between Legal, Engineering and GTM to track these cases and make sure we implement special data privacy policies for customers with whom we have contractually agreed to it. In our default API contract templates we keep the flexibility to both save personal customer data, use it for analytics (e.g. for improving our services), and also to train AI models on it. However, **in reality we don’t train on any user input or output data so far (as of Sept. 2025)** so we can principally agree to not training on customer data if one really wants (we can use this to trade against other things in deals). Some customer even require stricter privacy policies and want us to **delete input text data directly when generating the result.** We refer to this as **zero data retention policy. ** > \[[This agreement overview](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1_EM_z6LHWPMwibWFDGbeZX2PFYaDSh-x/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117009868738180578161&rtpof=true&sd=true) maintained by the legal team also contains information on data handling.\] ## List of customers with special data handling To be maintained by (Legal), (GTM), and (Eng). Where we're going ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/906aee77-a843-43f8-82fb-fd7845b07616/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466T4YB26F6%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151937Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJHMEUCICNbwXh0aW9j98TinV0dtmAAn1BNLhp8%2BRfEi2lbTsPcAiEAh9ujqp%2FGiHZi1rZWVF9ASiEH5ObwG8DjEykVj77ZWVAq%2FwMICBAAGgw2Mzc0MjMxODM4MDUiDNKpXuCSLUQ%2FfMkrvCrcA57MHcOalb9myLRgaMibNiiELAkvcjk3INMBhk%2BGiMn4Evbhs0dNEXKdBQx5jGg8UttZuR8v5q5rCDMj4gzjjnAQS2utT9xBr92jf6U4j%2F6Q1RVVxTTTTdwofv3yUjUECewcpvRjgeYLSIoGxYZDG4%2FQu6ju5QEhfVAGd8rMP%2Bp%2BgiHUPZH%2FYJ8U9IeySIWgkrf%2FcxTc8R2gmMXTi0i7tpLk%2FXlT8emj2OTJz1oHwdZDMwLwHFbIIMP1toaWdgiarkHMKCL%2BWwQrz%2B8540b8vFI%2B%2FvbvPPbK0S4uk%2BeEEe1bSvU%2B1q1vvyK%2FWAa%2BiZaKl2dxCU3WprVJZrBOgWYj3UwL7%2FyFymM4apCpm7boRPvtuIHOAjRe2GDhB%2BsXzK5TquPRQv7XSGYndAowNuFtvFfqGF9EB1C6QtIYZ9i35zXigcPlX8Je4vJqrUQaGnVk03LFzq5bHOPh2iM8zCCjvfpww%2FhWVuldt0kVMn1cChrZK2Cgru5%2BmMQXymW3QPuGCHDU9zJ5S6LbRDGu4a1Or5jc6O9VkKmJQXkUPwZNXriGaQqF6q8A6%2BEIbSsNifzsaEND61cql9wNIXJen27WhE%2BFIhFVhN67uCwX63AIHKebdM1ZTe9nWFCL9QpOMNfPk88GOqUBG%2BVShPJIagUI7qsSCJKDXzCcQPlU2t4K2r0Q7dAM92RjDXKAQANFiOxmvnslORI%2BKiBphtmXBdOUIuAQDXNIg3z1aemtf5h31DqnhH9KOQvf5bMgWv6ifoU%2FkqGDUnG%2Bw7utR7QqKgj2q5H1%2FflLSdlVpCij3elmGVLE%2FoigdHAwYA6ZfyoIeXV3mU0PlBQhmN7bSKqpLPsu3AnWizYBj03wppQW&X-Amz-Signature=68e9c9d42aa2671f0d6313342c6b93b49dcc21e6c80b72ec05959c50126844e0&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) We're not an image gen company. We're the frontier AI research lab powering visual intelligence and we need the world to understand that. By end of 2026 we want people to know three things about BFL: - We ship world-class research at commercial speed - We're the default for frontier devs and creatives because we’re uniquely suited to their needs (best models, open weights, open source, customization tools like LoRas, API is world class, FLUX Agent, multi-cloud, no lock-in) - We're the foundational AI lab building the future of visual intelligence (why it’s important, what it unlocks, why we’re uniquely positioned to do it, launch of FLUX.3) We are not "the open-source Midjourney." We’re not the cheaper Google alternative. We are not the sovereign alternative. --- # What changed at the offsite We agreed to stop being reactive and start being intentional. That means: - Quality awareness over quantity - More voices from the team (more BFL faces and not only Robin & Andi) - Becoming more visual - More visible to the people who matter - Consistent presence on our own social channels, and leaning into the angles that make us unique: strength of the research team, open research / tech, 70 people vs big tech. ![](file://%7B%22source%22%3A%22attachment%3Af51fbf4c-118c-43a4-a3f8-5fd2f4f64ff7%3Aimage_(37).png%22%2C%22permissionRecord%22%3A%7B%22table%22%3A%22block%22%2C%22id%22%3A%2231ec3702-22d5-80c0-9b24-d224eb5d369f%22%2C%22spaceId%22%3A%22d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6%22%7D%7D) It's not just one person doing comms and marketing at the same time. We can move to a marketing-led comms strategy. Not top-down, old-school PR - marketing drives the narrative, the positioning, the story. **We need to clearly articulate why visual intelligence matters **and we need to do that before FLUX.3 lands, because FLUX.3 is when we can actually demonstrate the expanded scope. --- # What we're shipping in the next weeks The goal is to build momentum and shift the narrative before FLUX.3 **KV Cache launch (next week):** Klein 9B, 1.4–2x faster for image editing. NVIDIA co-launch confirmed, they're including us in their press release and channels. **"How BFL approaches research":** A blog about our open research philosophy. Show that we ship research and share it, when people join BFL, they can continue shipping research. Follows Self-Flow and the new research setup that encourages open publication. **FDE work showcase:** The solutions team builds custom LoRAs (Amazon Ads) that beats NB pro. Show to the world that BFL is also more than just a research lab and we can help companies deliver real values. **BFL Vision: Why Visual Intelligence Matters:** Builds on Robin's North Star doc. Visual models are getting dramatically more general, agentic applications are exploding, and we're defining what visual intelligence looks like. This reframes us from "image gen" to "visual intelligence infrastructure." Needs to land big before FLUX.3 **Scorsese campaign: **Top-of-funnel branding. Expands our reach beyond the early adopter crowd. **These need to be sequenced together, not run independently.** See --- # Goal and metrics **Our focus for H1 2026 is to build quality awareness to increase model usage.** Win the position as the leader of building frontier models that are SOTA for quality and uniquely good for creative control at speed. We should be perceived as the “premium” brand that augments the human creator and honors the craft of making things — from movies and graphic design, to simulated worlds for robotics and games. We are anti-slop and anti-human replacement. We’ll measure this by increases in impressions, website visits, and models usage (via API or licensing) from current baselines.
**Metric** **Total Impressions (Social + Brand (Media, OOH)
**
**37M cumulative impressions
**
previous: \~6M last 6 months		 **Monthly Website Visitors**

**550K-1M per month
**
previous: \~420K per month for the last 6 months		 **Model Usage
**
**10K unique users retaining 30 days
**8K current unique users so far
2M developers using Fal
**
200M requests per month
**150-180M requests per month from Oct 25 -Jan 26
--- # The workstreams ## 1. Narrative & brand awareness Why visual AI matters. Tier 1 press profiles (Economist, Fortune (✅), Bloomberg). AI Podcasts (Dwarkesh, Latent.Space) **We build visual AI, our brand should feel like it. **We need more of our own tech in everything we put out. Show the work, show what FLUX can do, stop writing paragraphs when an image would say it better. *We need to inspire the world with our visuals* ## 2. Content & social Post more on socials and focus on artistic creation, ads/typography, product UI. Also highlight work from the community, specially around Open Source → Content from engineers and creative technologists. → Early influencer/creator program with 20 creatives that already have a large audience ## 3. Case studies 3–5 enterprise case studies. Hugo Boss, VSCO, Envato are contenders. These are the proof points for the narrative shift. --- ## 4. DevRel as a growth lever Educational content and developer partnerships → organic growth engine. If frontier developers default to FLUX, everything else follows. Deep technical blog posts, cookbooks, video walkthroughs. Not only "how to call the API" but "how to build production visual AI workflows." Developer experience: World class docs, SDKs, and starter templates. Community: hackathon with LTX in May, podcast appearances, strategic partnerships to investigate (Vercel/HF/Replicate(Cloudlfare)). Early access program for high-signal developers. Why now: every developer who builds something real with FLUX before FLUX.3 becomes a multiplier at launch. --- ## 5. Co-marketing & partnerships 2–3 marquee partners by Q2. We need to distinguish distribution partners ("use FLUX here" - Adobe, Canva) from narrative partners ("here's the change we enable"). Right now all our partners are distribution. We need narrative partners too. **More visible to the people who matter: **We're too invisible right now. The people building with FLUX and the ones that should do need to about us. More presence, more touchpoints, the right partnerships to put us in front of the right people. Not hanging out everywhere, it's about making sure BFL is impossible to miss if you're in our space. ## 6. Growth infrastructure **Website**: models page, enterprise use cases, social proof (400M+ downloads, customer testimonials), solutions pages by use case (marketing content, product design, web dev, productivity), logos. The website doesn't reflect where we are right now. **Email**: onboarding sequences (prompting guide, use cases, API key setup), usage-triggered emails (playground → API nudges), monthly product updates. Blocked on Segment fix. Separate initiative to optimise activation flow with [customer.io](http://customer.io/) (at risk, needs to move to growth team). **Growth partnerships**: test and trial high-quality partnerships driving traffic to our models, products, and brand. --- # How we're prioritizing Impact (does it reach frontier devs or pro creatives?), cost (time + money), confidence (will it actually work?). - Nail the "Why Visual AI Matters" narrative - everything else depends on this - Social media consistency - visible, compounds over time - Enterprise case studies - proof points for the narrative shift - DevRel + developer experience - builders who adopt pre-F3 become launch-day multipliers - Co-marketing partnerships - Q2 ramp, needs partner alignment --- # Read more "}

The URL might have already expired (it was set to expire at 07:59:23Z... actually wait, that might be 7:59 AM UTC. Let me check the current time. The file is 21 bytes which is definitely not an image. The URL may have expired already or the download failed silently. Let me check what's in the file. Check file contents bash cat /home/claude/dog_banana.jpg Output Host not in allowlist Ah — the egress proxy is blocking the blob.core.windows.net domain. The network configuration only allows specific domains: api.anthropic.com, archive.ubuntu.com, crates.io, files.pythonhosted.org, github.com, index.crates.io, npmjs.com, npmjs.org, pypi.org, pythonhosted.org, registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com, security.ubuntu.com, static.crates.io, www.npmjs.com, www.npmjs.org, yarnpkg.com. Since the Azure blob storage domain isn't whitelisted, I can't download the FLUX-generated images to disk — they're only accessible through those temporary URLs. I need to be upfront about this limitation and explain that the network policy blocks the bfldeliveryprodeu*.blob.core.windows.net domain where the results are stored. ```
- [ ] Stephen: I find the viewer for now more annoying than anything else, it breaks my flow as my cursor is usually going through it and then i zoom out all the time - [ ] It also makes it impossible to save the image actually - [ ] when you ask for more complicated workflows, Claude is telling us to download and re-upload because it can’t store it at the moment (in this case I had asked to generate a 4K image) ```markdown From Claude Plan Generate at 2048×2048 PNG (max API res) with FLUX Max You download it from the widget Upload it back here I run Real-ESRGAN locally to upscale 2x → 4096×4096 (true 4K+) ``` ## Decisions / follow-ups - "}
