{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"BFL Narrative ","url":"https://www.notion.so/27ec370222d5802eacd7d29555096d46","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/27ec370222d5802eacd7d29555096d46 as of 2026-02-14T13:20:43.569Z: {"title":"BFL Narrative"} # 1. Our role in the world {toggle="true"} A clear definition of our role in the world, our vision and mission. Mainly for top-level communication when explaining the company. **Vision – What is our impact on the world**

Powering visual intelligence everywhere. **Mission – How we get there (new)


MAIN
**Deeply rooted in foundational research, we continually build state of the art technology **to redefine **the visual understanding of the world.
**Past - What we have done

**Building structure from chaos: Our team pioneered Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX.1 – milestones in the evolution of generative AI – making text to image generation accessible to everyone. **Present - What we are doing

**From imagination to reality:** **We are building powerful, controllable, and composable tools empowering millions of people fulfill their creative potential and enterprises to create, scale, and govern visual content. **Future - Where we are going

**From outputs to actions: Creating multimodal models as the foundational pillar of visual intelligence, across products, platforms, and realities. # 2. How we express it {toggle="true"} **First: **The descriptive expression of our positioning. Used primarily for outward-facing communication (e.g., website, decks).
 **About – A brief copy of who we are and what we do

Option 1:** We’re the leading frontier AI research lab, continuously building the most advanced technology that shapes** **the visual understanding of the world. Our most recent models power a wide range of products – turning imagination into reality with precision, speed, and creative control. Follow us into the new. **About Short - Company one-liner

**Black Forest Labs – The frontier AI research lab for visual intelligence. **About Long – A longer format copy of who we are and what we do (e.g. Website)
** **Vision** We exist to power visual intelligence everywhere. **
Mission** Rooted in foundational research, we continually build state-of-the-art technology that advances how the world is seen and understood. We’re a frontier AI research lab focused on shaping visual understanding – so powerful applications become possible, deployable, and genuinely useful.

Our latest models already power products across industries, turning imagination into reality with precision, speed, and creative control. **
The Journey

Our Past – Where we come from** Our team brought structure to chaos: pioneering **Latent Diffusion**, **Stable Diffusion**, and **FLUX.1**—milestones that made text-to-image generation accessible to millions and set a new standard. **
Our Present – What we’re doing now** From imagination to reality: we’re building powerful, controllable, composable tools. They help people fulfill their creative potential—and help enterprises **create, scale, and govern** visual outputs with confidence and consistency. **
Our Future – Where we’re headed** From outputs to actions: We are creating multimodal models that unify perception, generation, memory, and planning—becoming a foundational pillar of visual intelligence across products, platforms, and realities. Interactions will shift from human-led, AI-assisted to AI-led, human-assisted, with intent as the interface. **
Strong beliefs, weakly held – How we work ** We ship technology, not demos. We bias toward precision, speed, and control, treat governance as a feature, and design for usefulness today and compounding value tomorrow.

We believe foundational research becomes durable infrastructure, platform beats point tool, and small, exceptional teams move the frontier. Above all, we are bound not just by talent, but by relentless curiosity and a hunger for what’s next – because the next decade won’t be won by faster tools alone, but by foundational innovation and the teams that turn it into applied technology.

From our labs in Freiburg and San Francisco, we’re pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. Never staying in the now.

**Follow us into the new.** **Second: **The creative translation of our positioning into feeling. It explains what it means to be a research lab, what drives us emotionally, and how we show up in the world—our voice, symbols, and rituals. It turns purpose into story and gives marketing, the website, and decks a coherent tone, so people don’t just understand us—they sense us.
**Brand Manifesto
** We don’t believe in done,
in final or finished. We believe
the only thing that matters
is what’s next. So we keep moving.
Keep making. Keep going. To leave behind what is
and imagine what if. Pulled forward by the new,
we are not here just to stay here. So if you are searching
for the finish line,
you won't find it here.
You won’t find us there. Because we are already off INTO THE NEW **Brand Message

INTO THE NEW.
** It’s a universal truth
Every great leap starts with a step into the unknown. It’s a mindset
We don’t cling to what is, we reach for what could be.
Exploration isn’t a phase. It’s our way forward. It’s a call to action
The next idea won’t come from the past. It waits in the new. **The Narrative’s Cosmos** Theme:
Imagination → Exploration → Transformation Speaks to:
Forward movement, curiosity, research mindset Function:
The invitation towards all to go beyond what's known and seen. A never ending leap toward what’s next. **Audience Talk Tracks** These are time-bound as the company evolves and advances its offering. For example, new products require tailored messages to communicate their advantages, and new technology calls for updated pitches to investors. Please treat them as valid, but limited in time.**

The Communication Approach
**Lead with inspiration. Convince with explanation.
### Customers {toggle="true"} **Who we are talking to:**
Enterprises and creators looking to create visual media with AI. **The goal:**
Own the category and further establish yourself as the recognized leader in generative media AI. **The approach:**
Put the product front and center, communicating features in ways that excite, inspire, and spark curiosity. **Headlines:** - Forget what is. Imagine what if. - Own every pixel. - Create the uncreated. - Don’t iterate the past. Create the future. - Model the new. - Play. Create. Manipulate. - There’s nothing you can’t change. - Grow a world. Out of your mind. - What hasn’t been can now be. - Unleash your Vorstellungskraft. - Reality is a spoon. Bend it. - Grow a world. Out of your mind. - Words change worlds. - How you say it is how you see it. - In the beginning was the word. - From imagination to image. - Nothing that you can’t rewrite. - Context is everything. Control it. - Think it. Type it. See it. ### Talent {toggle="true"} **Who we are talking to:** The current team and top talent open to new opportunities. **The goal:** Attract and retain a diverse group of highly ambitious and skilled people who share our drive and values. **The approach:** We stay true to our roots as researchers, carrying the same drive and curiosity into every part of the company, from product to sales. We welcome those who share this mindset to help shape the future of generative AI with us. - Welcome to the forest. - Not here to stay. - There is no final version. - Searching for researchers. - Let’s push boundaries not just pixels. - Build the features of the future. - Change the world by creating new ones. - Wanted: Frontier Developers (M/W/D) - If you can think it, you can make it.
### PR & Public {toggle="true"} **Who we are talking to:**
Publications that shape industry narratives and public opinion. **The goal:**
Establish Black Forest Labs as a leading voice in generative AI (while preserving a sense of mystery). **The approach:**
Further embrace our role as a European role model for innovation and leadership, while making our product announcements the benchmark for where the industry is heading and what comes next. **
Headlines (less sticky, more journalistic)**: - Neuropa now: BFL leads the wave of visual AI. - German imagineering. - New in Europe: AI market leadership. - Freiburg – the unlikely capital of visual AI. - At the frontier of imagination. - A company built on Vorstellungskraft. - For this company today is already too late. - From research to reality: How a group of scientists became a market leader. - How BFL became a European role model by building cutting edge models. - Why AI is about asking the right questions. ### Investors {toggle="true"} **Who we are talking to:**
Current and potential future investors. **The goal:**
Secure long-term commitment and continue attracting high-profile investors who want to back the best team in the game. **The approach:
**Keep the momentum by continuously demonstrating our ambition as the European category leader building the infrastructure for the next era of media creation.
- Leading Europe into the new. - Based in research. Built for reality. - Power every pixel, everywhere. - Let’s own every pixel. - Generating media – and returns. - From the Black Forest into the world. # 3. How we live it {toggle="true"} **Beliefs & Behaviors** Into the New means:
**Beliefs** **Behaviors**
**Curiosity is key** We are driven by the question of “what if?”. Curiosity shapes the way we think, build, and collaborate, helping us push boundaries together.
**Science not fiction** Our work is deeply rooted in research. We stick to the facts, challenge assumptions, and embrace consistent iteration.
**Nothing is permanent** We know there’s nothing that can’t be changed for the better and embrace the consistent evolution of ideas. Change is not a challenge, but a constant.
**Tonality
**
**Optimistic** We speak with clarity and optimism, reflecting our belief in progress and a mindset that embraces possibility over permanence.
**Inspiring** We aim to spark curiosity and imagination, expressing ourselves in a way that invites exploration and encourages experimentation with the tools we create.
**Ambitious** We speak boldly, with the conviction of knowing who we are, and the drive to redefine what’s believed to be possible.
## Additions {toggle="true"} Black Forest Labs is a pioneering developer of frontier AI for pixels, transforming how we shape and experience the visual world. A \[European / independent\] lab with global impact, our technology enables creators, developers, and enterprises to bring unimaginable ideas to life. **1. Why it matters** AI is transforming how we experience, interact with, and contribute to the visual world. Our technology communicates the ideas that cameras can’t capture. There’s a blockbuster film, video game, graphic novel, couture dress, soaring cathedral, and creative campaign in everyone—we help them realize it. - **Proof point: partnerships. In just over a year since founding, our models power everything from creative tools (e.g. Adobe) to design software (e.g. architecture / gaming firm) and social media experiences (e.g. Meta).** **2. Why we’ll win** **We’re frontier. **Black Forest Labs is building the foundational infrastructure for visual intelligence. Blending European research with American dynamism, we develop powerful, extensible, and global technology that pushes the capability frontier. - **Proof point: performance. Upon release, our models top public benchmarks for quality, control, and efficiency (e.g. ImgSys). Demand for these models and services is generating sustainable revenue to support our frontier research.** **We’re pioneers. **Our founding team includes pioneers of powerful (latent diffusion), accessible (Stable Diffusion), and controllable (FLUX.1) visual AI. With a track record of breakthrough research, our small but exceptional team of \~50 rivals some of the largest companies in history. - **Proof point: market share. By user (e.g. Poe) and deployer (e.g. Artificial Analysis) share, we compete with Google and OpenAI, and surpass Alibaba, Tencent, and Bytedance.** **We’re open. **We are deeply committed to open innovation. By sharing open technology, we enable researchers and developers around the world to build, test, and deploy new tools that we can scarcely imagine today. We apply layers of mitigation before, during, and after every release to combat the misuse of AI. - **Proof point: community. In the global AI race, our open models are the only open American or European models to rival DeepSeek for popularity (e.g. HF likes). Our founding team has contributed open generative models that total over 400M downloads—more than Google and Microsoft combined (e.g. HF total downloads).** **3. Where we’re going. **We are developing multimodal models that unify perception, generation, memory, and reasoning- laying the foundations for visual intelligence that responds to human intent. Series B funding will accelerate our research and development, unlocking compute, talent, and data to help us make imagination reality. "}

title: BFL Operating Model
content:
{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"BFL Operating Model","url":"https://www.notion.so/2c3c370222d58037b54fd3eda2b939d9","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/2c3c370222d58037b54fd3eda2b939d9 as of 2026-04-01T14:53:08.905Z: {"title":"BFL Operating Model"} # Role of Operations at BFL {toggle="true"} **Why now? **At 20 people, the CEO *is* the operating system. At 70+, that breaks. You're in every room, every decision, every hire conversation. This doc is the plan to get you out of the bottleneck so you can focus on what only you can do. - operations at BFL means turning our money in the bank into \$XM ARR by managing the **company's three biggest cost centers (compute and people, followed by data)**…while building the systems that let X people ship faster with x less headcount than incumbents - It’s operating system that governs how compute, people, data and risk are converted into frontier progress - If compute is our factory, Ops runs the factory: deciding what gets built, when, at what cost, and under what rules - **(1) The 3 main spend items** - Compute and infra: largest burn, the finance component. Compute is not a fixed cost, it's a strategic weapon to us. Ops owns provider strategy, training vs. inference allocation, and capacity planning tied to the model roadmap. Every dollar misallocated here is a model that ships late or ships worse. - People (second largest, fastest growing cost). the people we're hiring, frontier ML researchers are the scarcest talent pool. We're competing against orgs with 100x our headcount and 10x our compensation budgets for the same \~200 people who can push the frontier. Ops ensures every hire is strategic, not reactive, and that we build comp and talent systems that let us win despite the asymmetry. - Data (third largest, most underleveraged cost): training data is the “raw material” of the factory. Today we procure it reactively, without taxonomy, without feedback loops, and without a sourcing strategy beyond a handful of large providers. The wrong dataset costs model performance and release cadence. The right dataset at the right time is a competitive moat - **(2) The operational system layer = what makes spend productive** - **Compute governance.** Provider strategy, training vs. inference allocation, capacity planning tied to the FLUX 3 schedule. Compute is our single largest line item and every allocation decision is a bet on what ships next. Ops ensures those bets are deliberate, tracked, and tied to the model roadmap rather than made ad hoc - **Capital & talent deployment =** **Raise, allocate and track. **Fundraising and strategic finance - investor pipeline, fundraise execution, due diligence, strategic partnerships. Hiring strategy, comp systems, resource allocation, budget pacing, forecast accuracy, board reporting. The full lifecycle of capital operationalised: bring it in, deploy it across compute, people, and data, report on it. Essentially turning CEO decisions into tracked, measurable execution - **Research reality translation.** The specific interfaces that turn research breakthroughs into shippable products: the Research to Product bridge meeting, launch coordination, and the customer feedback → research loop. This includes the data pipeline (procurement → sourcing → evaluation → feedback to research) and the infrastructure that lets BFL expand into new modalities without reinventing the process each time. Today this is ad hoc and person-dependent. The ops job is to make it a repeatable pipeline in 2026. - **Cross-functional coherence & velocity.** The function-by-function interface model: Ops ↔ Finance, Ops ↔ People, Ops ↔ GTM, Ops ↔ Product/Eng. Launch coordination, bottleneck removal, decision rights. The reason models ship in weeks after completion, not months. - **Decision architecture & operating model.** The weekly/monthly/quarterly cadence that operationalises strategy: frequent leadership sync, monthly strategy day, monthly finance review, quarterly OKR cycle to see if we are off or on track. The infrastructure that lets people operate as one company without the CEO in every room. - **Corporate operations.** Legal, IT/security, compliance, external comms and employer brand. The "keep the lights on" layer that scales us quietly or breaks loudly. **
Ops doesn't do any function's job. Ops makes every function's job possible, measurable, and coordinated so BFL operates as one company, not \~7 teams that share a Slack workspace** The job is ensuring: **Inputs are strong **→ **Engine runs fast **→ **Outputs improve**
Layer Metric Category
Inputs compute, people, data, capital
Engine research velocity, execution speed
Outputs model progress, adoption, revenue
How this maps to people and headcount What Great looks like Signals our Operating model is working Operating clarity: Accountability vs Enablement ## Key Metrics Framework {toggle="true"} **The system in one line:** **Inputs → Engine → Outputs** Operations owns the inputs and the engine. The company measures the outputs. ### 1. Core Inputs These are the three production inputs for a frontier AI lab. Operations is accountable for all three.
⚡ Compute — Do we have enough, and are we using it efficiently? **Metrics**
Metric Why it matters
GPU capacity available Are we under-resourced before a training window opens?
GPU utilisation % Are we wasting what we have?
Training cost per run Are we improving efficiency run over run?
Inference cost per request Does our margin hold as usage scales?
Compute runway (months) How long can we run the current roadmap?
**Strategic signals** - Compute secured vs. roadmap needs — never reactive, always ahead - Compute concentration risk — provider dependency Compute is not a fixed cost. It is a strategic weapon. Every dollar misallocated is a model that ships late or ships worse.
👥 People — Are we deploying talent where it matters most? **Metrics**
Metric Why it matters
Headcount vs. plan Are we executing the hiring strategy?
Hiring velocity Are we moving fast enough to win talent wars?
Critical role fill rate Are the right seats filled before they become blockers?
Researcher-to-engineer ratio Is the technical mix right for the roadmap?
Retention of top 15 superstars Zero unplanned departures is the target
**Strategic signals** - Time to hire for frontier ML roles - Top contributor output and satisfaction For frontier labs, talent density matters more than raw headcount. We are competing against orgs with 100x our headcount for the same \~200 people who can push the frontier.
📦 Data — Do researchers have what they need to improve models? **Metrics**
Metric Why it matters
New datasets acquired Are we building the right raw material pipeline?
Dataset throughput How fast is data moving from procurement to training?
Labeling throughput Are we creating bottlenecks downstream?
Time: acquisition → training The hidden latency that delays model releases
Data pipeline reliability Is this a single point of failure?
**Strategic signals** - Dataset diversity across modalities - Training data freshness at time of run Data is the quiet bottleneck. Today we procure reactively, without taxonomy or feedback loops. The ops job is to make this a repeatable pipeline in 2026.
### 2. Strategic input = Capital Operations also owns the capital layer: fundraising infrastructure, deployment, and efficiency.
💰 Capital / Fundraising — Do we have enough runway to execute the roadmap? **Metrics**
Metric Why it matters
Cash runway (months) How long can we operate without a new raise?
Capital raised vs. plan Are we on track with the fundraising strategy?
Investor pipeline health Are we always fundraise-ready?
Burn multiple How efficiently are we converting capital into ARR?
Capital efficiency Revenue generated per dollar deployed
**Strategic signals** - Ability to finance the next compute generation - Investor demand and narrative strength The \$300M raised is not a buffer. It is the fuel for Lift 1. Operations owns how it is deployed across compute, people, and data — and reports on whether each allocation is producing the intended output.
### 3. The Engine (Operations) Operations converts inputs into outputs through five systems:
System What it does
**Compute governance** *(Finance ↔ Research interface — not a standalone system at this headcount)* Compute cost & capacity: Finance. Compute allocation (what trains when): Research. No dedicated system until there is a dedicated owner.
**Capital & talent deployment** Fundraising execution and investor pipeline (Ops). Budget pacing, resource allocation, board reporting (Finance — not duplicated in Ops). Headcount plan (Ops). Comp architecture and org design (People — not duplicated in Ops).
**Research → reality translation** Research-to-Product bridge, launch coordination, customer feedback → research loop
**Cross-functional coherence & decision architecture** *(one BizOps mandate — Nicholas)* Operating cadence, function interface model (Ops ↔ Finance, People, GTM, Product/Eng), bottleneck removal, decision rights, OKR cycle. Not three separate systems — one job.
### 4. Outputs (What the company measures) Operations does not own these directly — but if the engine is broken, these break.
Output Signal
Model capability progress Benchmark improvements, new capabilities unlocked, performance vs. competitors
Training efficiency Performance per GPU, training cost per run, scaling efficiency
Research velocity Iteration speed, research-to-production time, time from idea → experiment → model change
Product / developer adoption API usage growth, active users, applications built on FLUX
Revenue per compute Revenue per GPU, inference margin, revenue growth vs. compute growth
> **If compute → capability → adoption → revenue is flowing, the engine is working. If it breaks anywhere, Operations finds it first.** Cadence ### Weekly rhythm proposal
Day Forum Who What happens
Monday Leadership sync Robin + all functional leads Each lead: top priority, blocked, at risk. **Ops drives decisions, assigns owners, closes open items in the room.** Decisions made here are final unless explicitly escalated. Robin gives strategic guidance, not approval.
Tuesday ~~Cross-functional intersections~~ — **ad hoc only** Ops + relevant leads Called when needed: active launch sync, live blockers, a specific cross-functional decision. Not a weekly default. Research → Product bridge runs monthly on its own cadence.
Wednesday 1:1s with function leads Ops + each lead Deeper dives on blockers, people issues, strategic questions. Where Ops learns what’s actually happening vs. what’s reported. Coach, unblock, escalate to Robin when needed.
Thursday ~~Cross-functional initiative work~~ — **ad hoc only** Ops + task force Called for live launches or sprint coordination (e.g. FLUX 3 launch task force). Not a standing weekly slot. Tuesday and Thursday serve the same purpose — no need for both as defaults.
Friday Strategic work Ops only — no meetings Planning, documentation, analysis. Board materials, resource models, compute and capital allocation modelling.
### Quarterly rhythm - **Month 1:** Strategic planning - **Month 2:** Mid-quarter check — on track? Need to adjust? - **Month 3:** Quarter close + retrospective — what shipped, what didn't, why ### New forums to introduce
Forum Who Cadence Purpose
Revenue forecasting call Head of Sales + Finance + Robin + Ops Weekly Pipeline visibility, churn signals, forecast accuracy. Ops owns the cadence; GTM and Finance own the inputs.
Strategic planning session Ops + Finance + Robin only Quarterly (half-day) Recalibrate priorities, review resource allocation against actuals, set next quarter goals. Tight group, not a forum of 10.
Board prep working session Ops + Robin 2 weeks before each board Align on narrative and materials before the room. No surprises at the board.
Post-board debrief Ops authors, shared with all leads After each board Translate board feedback into action items. Close the loop so board output reaches the team.
**Product ↔ Research ↔ GTM bridge** Morgan (Product) + Axel/Robin (Research) + Anthony (GTM) + Ops Monthly The most critical missing forum at BFL. Three things happen here: (1) Customer and market signal flows GTM → Research systematically, not ad hoc. Anthony's team surfaces what customers need; Research hears it directly. (2) Research shares what's coming in the next model cycle so Product and GTM can plan against it — no more 120-day gap between model completion and launch. (3) Product flags what it needs from Research to ship the roadmap. Ops runs the meeting, owns the agenda, and closes action items. Not a status update — a decision and alignment forum.
## How Ops works with each function {toggle="true"} ### Ops ↔ Finance (Dave)
Owns
**Finance** Revenue accounting, cash management, AP/AR, audit, tax, treasury, FP&A, budget pacing, resource allocation models, capital deployment decisions, board reporting, forecast accuracy. One team — no Finance/FP&A split at this headcount.
**Ops** Consumes Finance outputs for operational decisions. Sets operating rhythm that makes forecasting possible.
**The interface:** Finance owns the full capital picture (actuals and forward deployment). Ops is a consumer of Finance outputs, not a parallel producer of allocation models. > At 70–100 FTE there is no meaningful distinction between "what we spent" and "what we should spend next." That's one financial brain. Ops does not duplicate it. ### Ops ↔ People (Kaylee)
Owns
**People** Hiring strategy, recruiting execution, offer management, onboarding, benefits, employee experience, performance systems, comp bands & leveling, equity philosophy, org design, performance review design
**Ops** Headcount plan & hiring budget
**The interface:** Ops sets the headcount plan and budget → People owns everything else end-to-end. - Ops builds the hiring plan — "Head of Product by Q1, 3 SEs by Q2, 5 researchers by Q3." People builds sourcing pipelines, manages interview loops, closes candidates. - People owns comp architecture, leveling, equity philosophy, and org design. Ops does not co-own these at this scale. - Together: bi-weekly talent planning (Robin, Ops, recruiting leads, hiring managers rotating). ### Ops ↔ Research (Axel + Robin)
Owns
**Research** Model development, training, benchmarks, paper publication, technical direction
**Ops** Compute procurement, data pipeline readiness, research hiring on schedule, launch coordination when models are ready
**The interface:** - Monthly: **Product ↔ Research ↔ GTM bridge** — the three-way forum that replaces ad hoc signal routing. GTM brings customer needs, Research brings what’s coming in the next model cycle, Product surfaces roadmap requirements. Ops runs it and closes action items. - Quarterly: Research capacity planning — what compute does FLUX 3 need, when, which provider? Ops translates into procurement and budget decisions. - Launch coordination: Research says “model is ready.” Ops ensures Product, Eng, GTM, Comms are simultaneously ready so the 120+ day gap disappears. > Research, Product, and GTM have operated in silos. The monthly bridge forum is the structural fix. Ops is the convener — not the owner of any function’s agenda. ### Ops ↔ GTM
Owns
**GTM** Selling, customer relationships, deal execution, pipeline management, SE engagements, RevOps system operation (pipeline stages, CRM hygiene, forecasting cadence, quota and comp design)
**Ops** RevOps system design (one-time setup, quarterly audit). Customer feedback → research loop. GTM hiring plan.
**The interface:** Ops designs the RevOps system once (pipeline stages, CRM hygiene standards, quota logic), then ownership transfers to GTM. Anthony’s team runs it day-to-day. Ops audits quarterly and owns the customer feedback → research routing. - Ops designs the FDE motion economics, then GTM executes it and owns it. - GTM surfaces customer feedback signal; Ops routes it to Research on a defined cadence — this is the one RevOps interface that stays with Ops. ### Ops ↔ Product (Morgan) & Engineering (Tim / Sandeep / Kyle)
Owns
**Product / Eng** What gets built, how it gets built, technical architecture, API reliability
**Ops** Resource allocation across product bets, cross-functional launch coordination, prioritisation frameworks when teams compete for eng time
**The interface:** Ops doesn't set the product roadmap. Ops ensures the roadmap is resourced and that tradeoffs are explicit. - When Product wants Studio AND FDE AND video launch in Q1, Ops is the one who says: "you can't do all three with current headcount — here are the options, pick two." - Monthly Engineering Architecture Review: align infrastructure investments with research needs and business scalability. ### Function interface summary
Function Ops provides Function provides back
Finance Operating rhythm, fundraising execution, investor pipeline Actuals, cash position, budget pacing, resource allocation models, board reporting, audit readiness
People Headcount plan & hiring budget Recruiting execution, candidate pipeline, employee experience, comp philosophy, org design, performance systems
Research Compute procurement, data pipeline, launch coordination, hiring Model readiness signals, compute requirements, technical direction
GTM RevOps systems, channel strategy, customer feedback loop, growth loop design Pipeline data, customer feedback, market signal
Product / Eng Prioritisation frameworks, resource tradeoff analysis, launch coordination Roadmap, technical constraints, capacity estimates
## Operating Principles # ***New*** [Our board philosophy and operating cadence](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gn_Pr-HzewxIF1CnzBAB69dkPxj4mImdHarZl0SjIMc/edit?tab=t.628ucaub9qbt) Product ↔ Research ↔ GTM Bridge "}

<content>
## **Bi-annual feedback coupled with salary review**
- BFL has two structured feedback sessions per year, one from mid March to early April and the other from mid September to early October. Both be coupled with a formal salary review (the process for salary reviews are covered in a separate document).
- The feedback format for these is more structured than in the moment/real time feedback. This is to enable reflection of impact and performance over the last 6 months.
- If an employee has been with BFL for 3 full months by the time the performance review, they should have a review but it’s highly unlikely it will result in a salary increase
- The process will consist of the following elements:
	- Self review
	- Functional lead review
	- Review meeting to discuss feedback
	- Calibration (Leadership and Functional Leads)
	- Comp review
- The different reviews and the calibration cover similar areas and should focus on the last 6 months
- Reviews are based on impact and impact potential rather than experience/performance and will hopefully drive both individuals and leads to focus on the work that has had the most impact on the business and team.
- **Use this levelling **[guide](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11cFz0x9HfIvfT2aV7KhT7wG7yR5yyMQES7fzSUY2QaI/edit?gid=405978997#gid=405978997) **for reference**
**Process**
1. [**Self review**](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1B_9uFlSAIMAcl3Jib3pyUBQ1TIGK4z8XE2ELREqnuRQ/edit)
- Each employee completes a brief self-reflection along with career aspirations
- The self review will be shared with the reviewer ahead of the review date
1. **Lead assessment**
- Lead assesses their team member using:
	- Levelling [guide](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11cFz0x9HfIvfT2aV7KhT7wG7yR5yyMQES7fzSUY2QaI/edit?gid=405978997#gid=405978997), own feedback and peer feedback (if needed for blind spots)
	- The purpose of the Lead review is to evaluate impact and impact trajectory, not effort or intent.
	- [Feedback pointers](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1vx4Fs2xfLCCDiRJS-_XsnjWYN-JBdDA8r_dFO8HU5OA/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.i1aeisrgt138)
1. **Peer feedback optional**
- It’s the responsibility of each Lead to ensure they give well-rounded feedback to whoever they are reviewing. That most likely means they need to get input from a range of team members. 
1. **Review meeting**
- After the self and reviews are done and any potential peer feedback has been collected, the Lead books a meeting with their direct report to go through the feedback.
1. **Calibration (Leadership, Lead + People)**
- In the calibration session, Leads discuss each team members ratings. 
- The goals of calibration is to align on
	- Impact
	- Trajectory
	- Relative performance
- The session is NOT for storytelling instead:
	- Ensuring rating are consistent
	- Evidence-based
	- Consistent across teams
**Useful tips**
- Collect notes/examples in whatever way works for you throughout the 6 months just after one review and before the next.
- The notes can be super simple and should really just act as prompts for you. This will enable you to compile your review (whether self, lead or inner circle) quicker when you get to it and also avoid just giving examples of things that happened in the last few weeks (recency effect)
</content>
</page>"}

📇 Room Directory **Phonebooth (1 Person, ideal for virtual meetings)** - Herzogenhorn - Teufelsmühle - Roßkopf **Small Office (2-3 People, all with whiteboards)** - Spießhorn (cozy chairs, great for a 1:1 or interview) - Brend - Seebuck - Blauen **Medium Office/Conference Room (4-6 People, all with whiteboards)** - Belchen (seats 4) - Kandel (Monitor, seats 6) - Schauinsland (Monitor, seats 6) **Large Conference Room (10+ People)** - Feldberg (Whiteboard + Large Monitor, seats 14) **Chill Space** - Kaiserstuhl (need a moment to unwind or a cat nap, catch a breath here or try out the daybed) ## 🛠️ How to Book via Google Calendar 1. Open **Google Calendar** and create a new event (or open an existing one). 2. Click **"Add rooms or location"** under the event details. 3. In the room search, browse or search the available rooms — each listing shows: - **Capacity** (e.g. "Room for 4 people") - **Equipment** (monitor and/or whiteboard, if available) 4. Select the room that best fits your needs and save the event. 5. You'll receive a confirmation if the room is available. If it's already booked, try an alternative. > ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/f113cd05-cadb-4b83-afe3-6c229eae634d/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4662OQBKTTR%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151943Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED0aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJIMEYCIQDHPUViy0C%2B4yPs0P4nHW6t5JZfoCY%2FNCsxJ3vxt4CEpwIhANHt7XRCTZrITa0eE%2FkNyJIPKeWDGDw2lhX5eK8bhncAKv8DCAYQABoMNjM3NDIzMTgzODA1IgyW8XW%2BepB7E1jDLzAq3APAgtUxC%2BR5DJGu4aSAW3qL6L96htJfswSpIj%2BMMjGbB5CXw2b9xq2XCmDL28U668NF%2FS2R8ihVFN01%2FYPUYclUi6zuD2azuBqXLbwmZo2sHWZ9COMZpmNUmE46nUGdjUyLDN%2FZfE962LDKpVJMrsVh2fGsRAtadvohiNpNGM3DYWyUAQgjdOvxaVAHHYw8V2KlTkJ7yWEVAwgUOBiq48Iqj78n6LZWPVZcNO7pZvLnn7JZSc7zmh9Yme5iDEU2QuGliECOciYlyJ%2FM02ik8oYszQ5bwOof6V7mrjjYJTSvxnULqoHGHdEspdr1StMcZ0zDoeikSuZHP%2FlUyRokOhAhbHccGNf0rhUWBgJ3eB4vHOv2RibvhPkm7luhwY5bmamriyo%2F%2F4opukI8YTrEqyXUKZn%2BTuLujcya2D7JCoXFZ3M6IY6CuSX%2BFfsmvJzeaTKThWdlLebj%2FxEXyuyQd4AS9%2BJnbPIMrrbcbKVMwjNbG3QTg26VmUp5Ft3wmQefqmKqV5vxNUJe%2BqgMTMOKl0nhIQrsdx4EPCdKBmTyhmUZTbe3CxVPo%2BCqBrh4PAgDbWv0Pmq7zTxsWJLIYLkir%2BeQvPNMF2l9m0DQDHwmHv%2B9O2HdT29k2y1wfTAOVDCMpJPPBjqkATy9m8CQ5iJ%2FkAdMLdjsOpKwS0qyXMqC6mxWuMmbzrd8lr7oTfjgt%2BobNtsavBt0v9ii0QCM2a%2F5EEeeiAGeJwl0waYbwtSezkXmR%2FpmxvHSLMvEwqg3zyxdLppEyLD95WWodpqNYHj7BwDkiVsAcRAdZN%2FLViAu00cxxxxYmOZNNJysa4b0OjoL5s5ZmRSfb%2BhYYUo8M4G%2B%2F9yOBIIiBQGJ6RIq&X-Amz-Signature=244a38384d2c74b94665feae1ff72f8760b69792c0e7fbf3c7472e42232e2e89&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) > 💡 **Tip:** Book rooms as early as possible for recurring meetings or all-hands sessions. --- ## ✅ Choosing the Right Room
Your group size Recommended room size
1–3 people Telephone Booth (1 person) or Small room (2–3 capacity)
4–6 people Medium room (4–6 capacity - Belchen, Kandel, Schauinsland)
10+ people Check for the largest available space (Feldberg)
**Please avoid** booking a 6-person room for a 1:1 or a solo call, unless all other small rooms are already booked. If the right-sized room isn't available at your preferred time, consider: - Using a slightly larger room only if no other option exists - Taking the call from your desk with headphones --- ## 🖥️ Room Equipment at a Glance Each room in Google Calendar is labelled with its available equipment. Here's what the labels mean:
Label What it means
Screen Screen available for laptop connection or screensharing
Whiteboard Physical whiteboard in the room
*(no label)* No AV equipment — suitable for discussions/virtuals only
--- ## 📋 Booking Etiquette - **Release rooms you no longer need.** If your meeting is cancelled or moves, remove the room from the calendar event so others can use it. - **Don't hold rooms "just in case."** Only book when the meeting is confirmed. - **Arrive on time.** If your meeting ends early, free up the room for the next booking. - **Leave it as you found it.** Clear whiteboards, tidy chairs, toss trash, and take your things (and coffee cups) with you. --- ## ❓ Questions or Issues? If a room is showing as unavailable but appears to be free, or if you have trouble with the booking system, contact Carolyne. "}

content:
{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"Brand Voice Guide [for Claude]","url":"https://www.notion.so/29dc370222d580949e78f41d9e754b74","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/29dc370222d580949e78f41d9e754b74 as of 2025-11-18T16:39:36.545Z: {"title":"Brand Voice Guide \\[for Claude\\]"} ## Ready-to-use narrative snippets *Long form Narrative *[*here*](/27ec370222d5802eacd7d29555096d46?pvs=25) ## Company intro snippets {toggle="true"} **Ultra-short (1 line)** - Black Forest Labs – the frontier AI research lab for visual intelligence - We exist to power visual intelligence everywhere. - From Freiburg and San Francisco, we're redefining how the world is seen and understood **Short (2-3 lines)** - Black Forest Labs is a frontier AI research lab focused on visual intelligence. Our team pioneered Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX.1 – Today, these foundations power millions of creations worldwide, from individual artists to enterprise applications. - From our labs in Freiburg and San Francisco, we're building the foundational technology for the next era of creativity and visual understanding. **Medium (paragraph)** - Black Forest Labs is a frontier AI research lab building the foundational technology for visual intelligence. Our team pioneered breakthrough innovations including Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX.1 – models that now power products used by millions across creative tools, enterprise platforms, and social media. Rooted in foundational research and driven by relentless curiosity, we're not here to iterate on what exists – we're here to build what's next. ## What we do snippets {toggle="true"} **Product-focused** - We build AI models that turn imagination into reality – with precision, speed, and creative control - Our technology powers everything from creative tools to enterprise platforms, enabling anyone to create, scale, and govern visual content **Technology-focused** - We build multimodal foundation models that unify perception, generation, memory, and reasoning - Our research advances visual understanding – making powerful, controllable, and composable AI genuinely useful **Impact-focused** - We're making the visual world programmable – turning ideas that cameras can't capture into images, videos, and experiences - Our technology enables millions of people to fulfill their creative potential and enterprises to scale visual content with confidence ## Why it matters {toggle="true"} AI is transforming how we experience, interact with, and contribute to the visual world. Our technology communicates the ideas that cameras can’t capture. There’s a blockbuster film, video game, graphic novel, couture dress, soaring cathedral, and creative campaign in everyone - we help them realize it.
**Proof point:** partnerships. In just over a year since founding, our models power everything from creative tools (e.g. Adobe) to design software (e.g. architecture / gaming firm) and social media experiences (e.g. Meta).  ## Why we will win {toggle="true"} **We’re frontier. **Black Forest Labs is building the foundational infrastructure for visual intelligence. Blending European research with American dynamism, we develop powerful, extensible, and global technology that pushes the capability frontier. - **Proof point: performance. Upon release, our models top public benchmarks for quality, control, and efficiency (e.g. ImgSys). Demand for these models and services is generating sustainable revenue to support our frontier research.
** **We’re pioneers. **Our founding team includes pioneers of powerful (latent diffusion), accessible (Stable Diffusion), and controllable (FLUX.1) visual AI. With a track record of breakthrough research, our small but exceptional team of \~50 rivals some of the largest companies in history. - **Proof point: market share. By user (e.g. Poe) and deployer (e.g. Artificial Analysis) share, we compete with Google and OpenAI, and surpass Alibaba, Tencent, and Bytedance.
** **We’re open. **We are deeply committed to open innovation. By sharing open technology, we enable researchers and developers around the world to build, test, and deploy new tools that we can scarcely imagine today. We apply layers of mitigation before, during, and after every release to combat the misuse of AI. - **Proof point: community. In the global AI race, our open models are the only open American or European models to rival DeepSeek for popularity (e.g. HF likes). Our founding team has contributed open generative models that total over 400M downloads—more than Google and Microsoft combined (e.g. HF total downloads).** ## Where we are going {toggle="true"} We are developing multimodal models that unify perception, generation, memory, and reasoning - laying the foundations for visual intelligence that responds to human intent. ### **Use this as foundation for all writing tasks:** `You are writing for Black Forest Labs (BFL), a frontier AI research lab building foundational visual intelligence infrastructure. We merge European research excellence with American dynamism to create powerful, extensible, and global technology.

BRAND FOUNDATION:
- We're frontier: Building state-of-the-art visual AI models that top public benchmarks
- We're pioneers: Our founding team created latent diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX.1 and Flux.2
- We're open: Deeply committed to open innovation while applying rigorous safety mitigations
- We're competitive: By market share, we rival Google and OpenAI

VOICE PRINCIPLES:
1. Forward Over Backward - Frame as possibility, not achievement
2. Active Over Passive - Use dynamic verbs that convey motion
3. Precise Yet Profound - Make every word count
4. Questions Over Answers - Pose provocations, not proclamations

PERSONALITY TRAITS:
- Relentlessly Curious (ask questions others haven't thought of)
- Pioneer Mindset (model the unmodeled)
- Technically Poetic (precision doesn't mean boring)
- European Champion (confident without arrogance)

AVOID: "Revolutionary," "unleash creativity," "solution," "final," "simply," corporate jargon
EMBRACE: Explore, discover, forge, build, next, beyond, curious, frontier, forest` ## 📱 Social Media Prompts ### For Technical/Research Announcements (Twitter/X, LinkedIn) `Write a social media post announcing [TOPIC] for Black Forest Labs.

TONE: Authentic, enthusiastic, unvarnished - the public craves genuine interactions from founders/researchers

STRUCTURE:
- Open with a provocative "what if" or forward-looking statement
- Share the technical advancement in precise but accessible terms
- Frame impact as possibility, not achievement
- End with invitation to explore, not a call-to-action

STYLE:
- Mix short punches with longer thoughts
- Use fragments for emphasis. Like this.
- Avoid excessive exclamation points
- Embrace playfulness - put the magic back in AI
- Feel human, not corporate

EXAMPLE OPENING PATTERNS:
- "What if [impossible thing] became routine?"
- "The next frontier in visual AI: [advancement]"
- "Here's what we're exploring: [technical detail]"

Remember: These are early days in uncharted territory. We offer building blocks, not final solutions.` ### For Product Launch Posts `Write a social media announcement for [PRODUCT/MODEL].

CONTEXT: Visual AI is magical, and we were there from the beginning. But these are still early days - like digital cameras or personal computers, we're laying foundations for transformation we can scarcely imagine.

KEY MESSAGES:
- We build for creators (there's a blockbuster film in everyone)
- We realize the impossible (making real the unreal)
- We push the frontier (supporting demanding creative tasks)
- We lay foundations (enabling tools we can't yet imagine)

TONE: Put the magic back in AI. Embrace playfulness, not skepticism.

AVOID:
- Overclaiming ("best ever," "revolutionary")
- Category clichés ("unleash your creativity")
- Corporate speak ("industry-leading solution")

INCLUDE:
- What makes this technically significant
- What it enables creators to explore
- What questions it opens, not answers it provides` ### For Community Engagement `Respond to [COMMUNITY POST/QUESTION] as Black Forest Labs.

TONE: Unvarnished, authentic, relatable. Avoid micromanaged corporate communication.

PRINCIPLES:
- Be genuinely enthusiastic about what the community creates
- Ask "what if" questions that invite further exploration
- Share technical precision without being dry
- Acknowledge uncertainty - we're in early days of this technology

STRUCTURE:
- Acknowledge what they've built/asked
- Add technical insight or forward-looking context
- Pose a question or possibility to explore further

Remember: The public punishes micromanaged communication and craves authentic researcher/founder voices.` ## 🤝 Partnership & B2B Communications ### Customers **Who we are talking to:**
Enterprises and creators looking to create visual media with AI. **The goal:**
Own the category and further establish yourself as the recognized leader in generative media AI. **The approach:**
Put the product front and center, communicating features in ways that excite, inspire, and spark curiosity. **Headlines:** - Forget what is. Imagine what if. - Own every pixel. - Create the uncreated. - Don’t iterate the past. Create the future. - Model the new. - Play. Create. Manipulate. - There’s nothing you can’t change. - Grow a world. Out of your mind. - What hasn’t been can now be. - Unleash your Vorstellungskraft. - Reality is a spoon. Bend it. - Grow a world. Out of your mind. - Words change worlds. - How you say it is how you see it. - In the beginning was the word. - From imagination to image. - Nothing that you can’t rewrite. - Context is everything. Control it. - Think it. Type it. See it. ### For Partnership Announcements `Write partnership announcement copy for [PARTNER NAME] integrating [PRODUCT/MODEL].

CONTEXT: Our models power creative tools (Adobe), design software (architecture/gaming), and social platforms (Meta). This proves market demand and validates our frontier technology.

STRUCTURE:
1. Lead with forward-looking impact, not the partnership itself
2. Explain what this enables (not just what it is)
3. Include precise technical capabilities that matter
4. Frame as foundation for future innovation

TONE:
- Confident without arrogance
- Technically precise yet accessible
- Focus on possibility, not completion

PROOF POINTS TO CONSIDER:
- Performance benchmarks (quality, control, efficiency)
- Sustainable revenue supporting frontier research
- Global reach and multilingual capabilities
- Community adoption metrics

AVOID:
- "We're excited to announce..." (passive, backward-looking)
- "Game-changing" or "revolutionary" (overused)
- Dwelling on past achievements

PREFERRED PATTERNS:
- "What if [industry] could [new possibility]?"
- "[Partner] is now exploring [capability] with FLUX..."
- "The next frontier for [use case]: [technical advancement]"` ### For Enterprise/API Documentation Copy `Write [DOCUMENTATION TYPE] for [PRODUCT/FEATURE].

PURPOSE: Help enterprise developers build powerful applications with our models.

TONE:
- Technically precise (this is infrastructure, not a toy)
- Pragmatic and actionable
- Confident in capabilities, honest about limitations

STRUCTURE:
- Start with what's possible, not what exists
- Provide exact technical specifications
- Include realistic use cases, not aspirational marketing
- Frame as building blocks for innovation

AVOID:
- Marketing fluff in technical docs
- Overclaiming model capabilities
- Corporate buzzwords
- Passive voice

INCLUDE:
- Precise metrics (latency, throughput, quality benchmarks)
- Control mechanisms available
- Integration possibilities
- Clear limitations and constraints` --- ## 💼 Careers & Talent Communications ### For Job Descriptions `Write a job description for [ROLE] at Black Forest Labs.

WHO WE ARE:
``We're a ~50-person team that rivals some of the largest companies in history. Our founding team pioneered latent diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX.1 - contributing models with 400M+ downloads (more than Google and Microsoft combined).
``
TONE:
- Relentlessly curious and forward-looking
- Honest about challenges (we're building at the frontier)
- Inspiring without being grandiose
- European sensibility (confident, not brash)

STRUCTURE:
1. Open with provocative question about the frontier we're exploring
2. What this role will pioneer (not "responsibilities")
3. What questions you'll help us answer
4. Who thrives here (not "requirements")

AVOID:
- Corporate HR speak ("rock star," "ninja," "10x engineer")
- Lists of requirements that read like checkbox compliance
- Claiming we have all the answers

EMBRACE:
- "What if" framing
- Honest technical challenges
- Emphasis on exploration and discovery
- Questions we're asking, not answers we have

EXAMPLE OPENING:
"What if visual AI could understand intent as naturally as it generates pixels? That's the frontier we're exploring - and we need someone who..."` ### For Employer Brand Content `Write [BLOG POST/ARTICLE] about working at Black Forest Labs on [TOPIC].

CONTEXT: We're European champions showing what's possible outside Silicon Valley. Small team, exceptional impact, frontier research with sustainable revenue model.

TONE:
- Authentic and unvarnished
- Proud of European roots without being defensive
- Curious about what's possible
- Honest about being in early days

THEMES TO EXPLORE:
- Building from the forests of Germany for global impact
- Merging research rigor with rapid iteration
- Open innovation with responsible guardrails
- Small team tackling questions others haven't asked

AVOID:
- Startup clichés ("move fast and break things")
- Defensiveness about European vs American AI
- Claiming we're "done" or have it "figured out"

STRUCTURE:
- Open with a question about the frontier
- Share what we're exploring (not what we've achieved)
- Include specific technical challenges
- Frame as invitation to join the exploration` --- ## 🚀 Product Launch Communications ### For Launch Announcements (Blog/Press) `Write a launch announcement for [PRODUCT] for [AUDIENCE: technical community/general press/partners].

NARRATIVE FRAMEWORK:
1. WHY IT MATTERS: AI transforms how we experience and contribute to the visual world. Our technology helps visionaries communicate ideas cameras can't capture. (There's a blockbuster film, couture dress, soaring cathedral in everyone)

2. WHY WE'LL WIN:
- Frontier: Building foundational infrastructure for visual intelligence
- Pioneers: Track record of breakthrough research (latent diffusion → Stable Diffusion → FLUX)
- Open: Committed to open innovation with rigorous safety

3. WHERE WE'RE GOING: Multimodal models unifying perception, generation, memory, and reasoning

TONE FOR EACH AUDIENCE:
- Technical: Precise, benchmark-focused, capability-oriented
- Press: Vision-forward, impact-focused, accessible
- Partners: Integration-ready, production-proven, extensible

STRUCTURE:
1. Open with what this unlocks (not what it is)
2. Technical capabilities that matter (benchmarks, novel controls)
3. What's now explorable (not "possible" - that implies it wasn't before)
4. Where this frontier leads next

PROOF POINTS TO INCLUDE:
- Performance metrics (top ImgSys benchmarks)
- Novel capabilities (e.g., multi-language support, precision control)
- Community/market validation
- Sustainable model (revenue supports research)

AVOID:
- "We're excited to announce" (start with impact)
- Excessive superlatives ("best ever")
- Claiming completion ("final," "perfect")` ### For Product Positioning Docs `Create positioning document for [PRODUCT] for [AUDIENCE/USE CASE].

FRAMEWORK - THREE PILLARS:

1. WHY IT MATTERS
Frame the transformation, not the feature:
- What creative possibility does this unlock?
- What was impossible that's now explorable?
- Who benefits and how? (specific, not generic)

Proof point: [Partnership/adoption example]

2. WHY WE'LL WIN
Technical differentiation:
- Performance benchmarks (be specific)
- Novel capabilities (what others can't do)
- Production readiness (sustainable revenue)

Proof point: [Market share/adoption metric]

3. WHERE WE'RE GOING
Research trajectory:
- What frontier are we pushing toward?
- What questions are we asking next?
- How does this fit the bigger vision?

TONE:
- Lead with vision, back with metrics
- Confidence rooted in performance, not hype
- Forward momentum, not achievement celebration

COMPETITIVE POSITIONING:
- Frame against capability gaps, not competitors
- Highlight unique advantages (open weights, multilingual, precision control)
- Acknowledge tradeoffs honestly` --- ## 📊 Investor & Stakeholder Communications ### For Board Updates / Investor Memos `Write [UPDATE TYPE] for [AUDIENCE: board/investors/stakeholders] on [TOPIC].

TONE:
- Confident, data-driven, forward-looking
- Honest about challenges and tradeoffs
- European sensibility (substance over style)

STRUCTURE:
1. **Bottom Line Up Front**: Key insight/decision/milestone in 1-2 sentences
2. **Context**: Why this matters for our frontier position
3. **Data**: Specific metrics, benchmarks, market validation
4. **Trajectory**: Where this leads, what it enables
5. **Ask/Next Steps**: Clear, actionable

PROOF POINTS TO LEVERAGE:
- Benchmark performance (ImgSys rankings)
- Market share (user/deployer metrics vs Google, OpenAI)
- Community validation (HuggingFace downloads, model usage)
- Revenue growth (sustainable model, not just hype)
- Partnership momentum (Adobe, Meta, enterprise adoption)

FRAMING:
- Position as frontier infrastructure play, not feature development
- Emphasize sustainable revenue supporting research
- Show competitive position through capability, not marketing
- Frame challenges as opportunities at the frontier

AVOID:
- Burying key points in paragraphs
- Over-optimism without data
- Ignoring competitive realities
- Vague next steps` --- ## 🎬 Video Scripts & Multimedia ### For Product Demo Scripts `Write script for [VIDEO TYPE: demo/tutorial/announcement] about [PRODUCT/FEATURE].

OPENING HOOK (first 10 seconds):
Start with a provocation or impossible-seeming result, not an introduction.

Example patterns:
- "What if you could [impossible thing]?"
- Show before/after or transformation immediately
- "Here's something that shouldn't be possible yet..."

STRUCTURE:
1. Hook: Show the magic first
2. Context: Brief setup of the challenge/frontier (15-30 sec)
3. Demo: Show capability with precision (60-120 sec)
4. Technical insight: What makes this work (30-45 sec)
5. Invitation: What to explore next (15-30 sec)

TONE:
- Genuinely enthusiastic (not performative)
- Technically precise (show don't tell)
- Unscripted feel (authentic, not polished corporate)
- Focus on exploration, not completion

VISUAL DIRECTION:
- Start with output, work backward to process
- Show real use cases, not abstract demos
- Include UI/parameter details for technical audience
- Keep text minimal, let visuals carry meaning

AVOID:
- Long intros explaining who we are
- Corporate presentation style
- Over-produced polish (be authentic)
- Claims without showing` ## 📝 Quick Reference: Voice Patterns ### SAY THIS, NOT THAT:
❌ Avoid ✅ Use Instead
"Our solution helps you..." "Explore what's possible with..."
"Industry-leading performance" "Tops ImgSys benchmarks for..."
"We've completed the development of..." "We're now exploring..."
"Revolutionary new feature" "What if you could \[specific capability\]"
"Unleash your creativity" "Model what you imagine" / "Build what cameras can't capture"
"Easy-to-use interface" "Precision control for..."
"We're excited to announce" "What's now possible: \[specific advancement\]"
"Final version" "Latest frontier: \[model name\]"
"State-of-the-art" \[Cite specific benchmark: "Top ImgSys quality score"\]
### POWER VERBS: Explore • Discover • Pioneer • Model • Forge • Build • Push • Extend • Enable • Unlock ### AVOID VERBS: Complete • Finalize • Perfect • Revolutionize • Transform (overused) ### SENTENCE STARTERS: - "What if..." - "Here's what we're exploring..." - "The next frontier in..." - "From our forests in Germany..." - "What cameras can't capture..." - "What's now explorable..." ## 🎯 Audience-Specific Quick Prompts ### Developers / Technical Community `Write for developers who want precision, benchmarks, and extensibility.
- Lead with technical capabilities
- Include specific metrics
- Frame as building blocks
- Be honest about limitations
- Focus on what they can build` ### Creators / Artists `Write for creators who want magical results with real control.
- Lead with creative possibility
- Show don't tell (use examples)
- Balance magic with precision
- Frame as tools for ideas cameras can't capture
- Acknowledge craft and skill` ### Enterprise / Decision Makers `Write for buyers who need production-ready infrastructure.
- Lead with business impact
- Include performance/cost metrics
- Emphasize reliability and scale
- Frame as sustainable, frontier technology
- Show proof points (partnerships, adoption)` ### Press / General Audience `Write for readers who want to understand impact without jargon.
- Lead with transformation, not technology
- Use accessible metaphors
- Show real-world applications
- Frame as early days of major shift
- Balance magic with responsibility` ### Investors / Board `Write for stakeholders who need strategic context.
- Bottom-line up front
- Data-driven insights
- Competitive positioning
- Clear trajectory and milestones
- Honest about challenges` --- ## 🚦 Final Checklist Before publishing any content, verify: - [ ] Opens with forward-looking statement, not achievement - [ ] Uses active voice and dynamic verbs - [ ] Includes specific proof point (benchmark, metric, partnership) - [ ] Frames as exploration/possibility, not completion - [ ] Avoids category clichés and corporate speak - [ ] Appropriate for audience (technical precision vs accessibility) - [ ] Maintains European confidence (not Silicon Valley bravado) - [ ] Reflects honest uncertainty about early-stage technology - [ ] Product names follow guidelines (FLUX.2 \[pro\] format) - [ ] Company name correct (Black Forest Labs, not "FLUX") "}

We intend to automate this eventually. Does this workflow work for Cloudflare? **
Technical & Support** ***Benchmarking/Testing:*** Our models are available now for your team to start testing and running evals. Just note they can't be used commercially until we have a signed contract in place. ***SLAs & Support:* **This is a new motion for us with hosted dev models, so a few questions to understand your needs better: - What's been your experience with SLAs from other model providers? - How have you typically used/required support in the past - break/fix only, or ongoing optimization? - Are you primarily looking for engineering support during initial implementation, or is ongoing partnership support important? - What metrics matter most to Cloudflare? On our call, I heard response times mentioned. Happy to jump on a call if it's easier to discuss any of this live. ### \| Matt / Nikhil (in-person) {toggle="true"} **Attendees:** - BFL: Matt - Matt joining BFL 5 weeks ago (partnerships role) - Mutual connection via Lisa Campbell (Nikhil and Lisa were at Dropbox together with Sanjana) - Cloudflare: Nikhil Kothari (Partnerships) - Nikhil at Cloudflare 2 years, product partnerships focus - Developer platform partnerships (not networking/security sides) - Background in B2B/enterprise cloud infrastructure **Agenda** - Intros - Feedback on Contract **Summary** ### Cloudflare Platform Overview {toggle="true"} **Infrastructure & Scale** - Serverless platform competing with hyperscalers for new application workloads - Own infrastructure: 330+ cities globally (including China) - mini data centers - Serves 20% of all websites, 40% of top 1M sites - Abstracts scaling and latency complexity - users don't need to worry about geographic distribution - **Value proposition:** Different architecture from hyperscalers - Not competing on training clusters (not good at giant clusters) - Competing for net-new app workloads where latency/global distribution matters - Example: User in US → user in Asia → user in Brazil all get optimal experience automatically **Customer Segments** - Full spectrum: students → startups → Fortune 10 - **SMB:** Self-serve model - **Mid-market:** Sales team coverage (rough definition: \~3K employees, \<\$500M revenue) - **Enterprise:** Dedicated sales for larger accounts - **Digital natives:** Strong position - Cloudflare is default for networking/security (historically Akamai) **Strategic Positioning** - Full-stack development platform (front-end, back-end services + inference) - Not a pure-play inference provider like Fal/Replicate - **AI as expansion play:** Upsell opportunity into large existing installed base - Customers choosing between: AWS/Vercel vs Cloudflare as complete platform - Use cases where latency matters: voice AI, interactive apps, image generation ### AI Inference Platform Strategy {toggle="true"} **Platform History** - Launched serverless inference \~2 years ago - Phase 1: Open-source models (including Flux Schnell) to build efficiency and stand up program - Phase 2: Proprietary models via revenue share (\~1 month ago) - Also supporting enterprise private deployments **Model Curation Approach** - Curated catalog: handful of models per category - Not comprehensive marketplace (not taking "Kaiber's approach") - **Current image models:** Leonardo (one other proprietary partner) - Expanding into: voice AI (strong demand), eventually video (too early) **Platform Differentiation** - Squeezing maximum efficiency from infrastructure (cost-effective inference) - All supporting services for full applications - Voice AI example: Not just inference, but all complementary real-time components needed ### GTM & Sales Motion {toggle="true"} **Customer Engagement** - Sales team NOT prescriptive on model selection - lack expertise - Expect partners (BFL) to provide: - Prescriptive guidance on use cases - Examples: "For realism, use X" or "For logos, use Y" - Enablement materials for sellers **Go-to-Market Motions** 1. **Pay-as-you-go:** Marketing + awareness campaigns 2. **Direct sales (enterprise):** Focus on ISVs/platforms where image gen is native capability - Website builders, creative apps, social media platforms - Sell-through model - volume grows as their users grow - Even large enterprises often have scoped/contained projects (not massive usage yet) - Exception: AI-native experiences with large user base = high volume **Expansion Opportunity** - 20% of internet, 40% of top 1M sites already on Cloudflare - Large installed base = expansion/upsell opportunity - Challenge: How do existing customers learn about new models? - Solution pending: Concrete GTM plan after user conference (more from leadership) ### Marketing & Developer Relations {toggle="true"} **Conference Context** - Cloudflare user conference: Next week in Vegas - Team consumed with conference prep - affects timing **Cloudflare Marketing Approach & Ethos** - **Open ecosystem:** Developer-friendly, no lock-in, free where possible - **Technical content only:** No fluffy partnership announcements - Popular blog posts: Technical details, how it's built, how it works - **Case studies:** - Not business impact/CFO-focused - Technical: How developers built it, decisions made, trade-offs, considerations - Audience: Engineering managers, CTOs **Flexibility** - Can get creative with unique approaches per partner - Not predefined molds (unlike hyperscalers) - Part of company culture - less structured than hyperscalers - DevRel investment available (Craig mentioned) **FLUX.2 Launch Partnership (November target)** - Strong interest from Cloudflare to be launch partner - Joint marketing/DevRel collaboration - Need to complete agreement before launch - Both teams can move fast (small/nimble) ### Commercial Structure {toggle="true"} **Revenue Share Model** - **Base:** 30% revenue share to BFL - **Proposed tiered structure:** - Aggregate \$2M total sales → 25% - Aggregate \$5M total sales → 20% (they don’t go below this to give partners margin protection) - Floor: 20% minimum - **Rationale:** Cloudflare is public company, reports gross margin (30% is below target but acceptable to start) **Deployment Model** - Cloudflare takes ALL capacity/region risk - Serverless, usage-based pricing (no dedicated instances) - Global deployment - Cloudflare figures out GPU allocation across regions - NOT like hyperscaler model (no committed capacity from BFL) - Enterprise customers: Can commit for volume discounts **Contract Scope** - **Initial models:** FLUX \[dev\] and Kontext \[dev\] - **Flux tools:** Default to include (Fill, Canny, Depth, Redux) - need product team confirmation - These are specialized/fine-tuned for specific use cases - Available via API - **New versions:** Mutual agreement process (ideally via email, avoid paperwork) - Video would require separate agreement (different cost structure) - Image model updates should work with simple mutual agreement ### Technical & Operational Requirements {toggle="true"} **Benchmarking & Access** - **Cloudflare needs:** Evaluation access for cost profiling - **Process:** Engineering team must run benchmarks (not happening during conference week) - **License question:** Dev is permissive for non-production use (need to confirm if Kontext is same) - If can't test internally → need BFL to provide access for benchmarking - **Expectation:** Dev models are distilled and efficient relative to competitors. Expect Cloudflare benchmarks to go well. - BFL can help if Cloudflare's numbers seem off **Reporting & Metering** - Need documentation on BFL's license server setup - Cloudflare has unique architecture - need to understand compatibility - Will review docs and come back with specific questions **Support Structure** - **Cloudflare stance:** Acknowledges need for reasonable support - **Proposed:** Priority/severity levels (P1/P2) with response time SLAs - Response time commitment (not necessarily remediation time) - For model issues beyond hosting (dependencies from BFL) - **Cloudflare responsibility:** Anything related to how model is served **Model Lifecycle Management** *New Models/Versions:* - **Cloudflare preference:** Be launch partner (day-one availability, not playing catch up) - Launch partner notification/heads-up on new releases *Deprecation:* - Notice required (BFL developing deprecation policy) - Maintain license entitlement for existing customers during wind-down - Can't abruptly pull the plug on customers *Termination Scenario:* - Propose wind-down period (figure out appropriate timeline). Give existing customers time to migrate/ramp off. - Fees would continue during wind-down - Stop onboarding new customers **Contract Clarifications** *Section 4(a)(i) - Restrictions:* - **Issue:** Need to allow resale/distribution for Cloudflare's channel partners - Channel partners should be able to sell "Flux on Workers AI" (not selling Flux directly) - Language needs adjustment *Legal Review:* - BFL legal review: Expected Friday/Monday - Nikhil reviewed in parallel with legal team - Expected comments from Cloudflare legal: Indemnities and liabilities - Overall assessment: Nothing majorly problematic ### Next Steps & Timeline {toggle="true"} **Immediate Actions:** - [ ] Cloudflare legal review: Friday/Monday expected - [ ] BFL: Define evaluation access and benchmarking plan - Cloudflare engineering team to run cost benchmarks (after conference week of Oct 20) - Provide evaluation access if needed - [ ] BFL to share licensing server/metering documentation - How usage is reported back to BFL - Cloudflare to review and return with specific questions - [ ] Align on deprecation notice/wind-down approach - [ ] Define support SLAs (priority levels, response times) - [ ] Clarify restrictions language (4(a)(i)) for channel partner resale - [ ] Address legal comments on indemnities/liabilities - [ ] Finalize commercial terms (including tiered revenue share thresholds) - [ ] Develop GTM plan (after conference - more concrete in couple weeks Oct 20+) - Enablement materials, use cases, customer profiles, etc. ### Summary for Slack :slack: {toggle="true"} **\[Cloudflare\] Contract Discussion Update** Had a productive meeting with Cloudflare yesterday on hosting our models via their serverless platform. No redlines yet, but got verbal feedback on key terms. Their legal review expected early/mid next week. **CONTRACT FEEDBACK** **Commercial Terms** - **Revenue share tiers:** Proposed scaling structure based on aggregate sales - \$0-\$2M = 30% - \$2M-\$5M = 25% - \$5M+ = 20% - Rationale: Public company gross margin targets (30% is below their threshold) - Question: Would we be open this? Where would we like to negotiate (\$ thresholds or %) - **Benchmarking:** Need to run evals to finalize price floors - Timing: After their user conference (Oct 20+) - Question: What's our process for providing eval access? **Operational Terms** - **Support \[2(h)\]:** Requesting response time SLAs for model-specific issues (not hosting) - Standard for them: Priority/sev levels with response commitments - Question: Are we open to this? - **Model lifecycle:** - New releases: Want day-one availability with advance notification - Deprecation: Requesting reasonable notice period - **Termination \[7(c)\]:** Want wind-down period for customer transitions - BFL fees continue during wind-down - New sales stop - Existing customers get time to migrate - **Reporting \[6(b)\]:** How do they report usage back to us? - Question: Do we have documentation to share? - **Legal:** Expect comments on indemnification/liabilities (no specifics yet) **GTM OPPORTUNITIES** - Strong interest in being a FLUX.2 launch partner 🎉 - Focus has been open-source models. We would be their second proprietary model (other is Leonardo) - Flexible approach, no rigid playbook - Focus on developer/technical content and case studies (not fluff) - DevRel team (Craig Dennis) potentially interested in collaboration (cc: @Stephen Batifol) **NEXT STEPS** - [ ] **Cloudflare:** Redline agreement (early/mid next week) - [ ] **BFL:** Share benchmarking/eval process documentation - [ ] **BFL:** Share reporting requirements documentation - [ ] **Both:** Complete contracting + deployment before FLUX.2 launch (November) **Questions for the team:** 1. Where would we like to negotiate on rev share (\$ thresholds or %)? 2. Eval access process for their benchmarking? 3. Support SLA commitment - are we open to this? 4. Do we have reporting documentation to share? ### Feedback on Contract ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/935ee964-a25b-4be5-a9db-4389f140c3d7/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466VWZORQSV%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T151950Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJGMEQCIGqqwzYsmYu4DObUWn%2F1J3DsL9DB6KPlchxz3cX7ZgkrAiAfGyV4LbTPjEv4yqJmJrkt7naXYrz2dmMzWLD9cc2lQir%2FAwgIEAAaDDYzNzQyMzE4MzgwNSIMOx%2BF9x%2FvYqM2QH9XKtwDIrEmBun2jnReF0PAYYCD6V%2FQJzI7EdjLeUPbGd5KVOjHqe8jVW16wJdLF70vBNigWUUrXy3RFYLeov3tl6bU9EfqC1mOwEyHsLQcfysx7h4v13jC3voZg07b5CNKMK4vObN7WYpsmmUtuUTF5grLxCRYISPILmhx%2FPUOv2SWOuu4eVBxnKFhu%2B7iotZ9NRz3podoYa6DLZh64%2BAtBz9%2FX11cjcab%2FxmC%2FGugApU3XLuhZXLCa3TPsbooyNvecNvzCHAnkPXMDRUtuD2rxcXtls5rnALx3FYhFOMqhDHPtocryK%2FpkCwWD6GO7%2FrEGGlglcBa9O96CHbIcVAh2nj3QVNS6zM8bvuiqdYAbCRiZnrnWkWAKEygH1quDqNjJA1UA%2FN7rGJO6KzuYPofK3Rv7%2Bje%2FsCOFA2RMU%2BrnjtBzOhR4hZ7aEpSU1OFL6bJbFklnSWt%2FTxE8T7oJUXA7HSPfliZvtSDy6G0GSJmRaWowrr%2BMcQL4eKSS8DlZguAKaiAtSRDvOGCifsTusjZcwHf2mWl2GbEF0t11dqaOCthrca1gZ5Rf98yrKpJO5%2FgUQ3HA%2BTgt6C9khZuHaRLiibVaKwHDqL1tsPQtGHX1qFVY9tGg8jUToqSJPRgPZIwidWTzwY6pgHniKBOA9t1j144wWEhWzlmmN9XiM2qln59iC1Q5I%2BsYcsQRtsxxLROsXvlBCD2MnqK%2F1P1xqfbpcpUbjbs5x%2FyiD9qzxDc0X5alSs04ZF144njvEZ8M4VtgYxCVAQnG3bzdqPI%2FwMi65fnRd4YEv3qdR6LlZjjZjiJxI5QUl6GjTyyc89SHoNIlxcUKz0F3QCbNeJg9MNFHQSYySLAXau19vjDNK6P&X-Amz-Signature=ac3b4527c60fd354904a4a96e8c2ebc9b1db30df2985489ebf0ecc143d7e4930&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) [**Responses from Slack**](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C07FKH3C36Y/1759984114.981149/1759984114.981149)** :slack:** - <content>
## Purpose
Evaluate practical coding ability + systems thinking in a data / infrastructure context.
This is NOT a pure LeetCode interview.
Focus on:
- Writing clean, correct code
- Reasoning about constraints (memory, I/O, scale)
- Ability to evolve a naive solution into a production-ready one
## Problem Options (Pick ONE per interview)
Interviewers should choose ONE problem based on candidate background.
### Option 1: Duplicate File Detection
Best for: Data systems, storage, I/O-heavy candidates
Focus:
- File I/O patterns
- Memory constraints
- Multi-stage filtering (size → partial hash → full hash)
- Scaling to large datasets
Reference: : [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1BculOrdJpFwSJ-2YDv_PuRfvQyJoaDgLkE5O5oiJg6w/edit?usp=sharing](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1BculOrdJpFwSJ-2YDv_PuRfvQyJoaDgLkE5O5oiJg6w/edit?usp=sharing)
### Option 2: Container Distribution
Best for: Infra / distributed systems candidates
Focus:
- Bottlenecks (registry bandwidth)
- Distributed coordination
- Peer-to-peer / tree distribution
- Failure handling
Reference: : [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DKVWkG0ANemMbnI-gPpZeJcwmU5JJBoHkWf8iV2G0lo/edit?usp=sharing](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DKVWkG0ANemMbnI-gPpZeJcwmU5JJBoHkWf8iV2G0lo/edit?usp=sharing)
### Option 3: AllReduce
Best for: ML infra / training systems candidates
Focus:
- Distributed communication patterns
- Tradeoffs (latency vs bandwidth)
- Correctness + deadlock awareness
Reference: : [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1L21_Lvx9crh5yZeHDnZXnTyrMKzk5yFysVj56k2_EZU/edit?usp=sharing](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1L21_Lvx9crh5yZeHDnZXnTyrMKzk5yFysVj56k2_EZU/edit?usp=sharing)
### Option 4: Streaming Data Pipeline
Best for: Data infra + ML pipeline candidates
Focus:
- Streaming vs batch
- Memory + chunking
- GPU starvation / pipeline design
- Reliability + checkpointing
Reference: : [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Sy1TZEK_8iipxo-FL0jbKu_oOdrh-EoF9ovbdVXQYOM/edit?usp=sharing](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Sy1TZEK_8iipxo-FL0jbKu_oOdrh-EoF9ovbdVXQYOM/edit?usp=sharing)
### Option 5: Pipeline Scheduling (1F1B)
Best for: deeper ML systems / parallelism candidates
Focus:
- Scheduling + dependencies
- Resource utilization (bubbles)
- System-level reasoning
Reference: : [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1irVX3XhsM1zT_IFE4O1bIH-dY_77r-jayGmVzPUO8IM/edit?usp=sharing](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1irVX3XhsM1zT_IFE4O1bIH-dY_77r-jayGmVzPUO8IM/edit?usp=sharing)
## Evaluation Criteria
Strong Yes:
- Writes clean, correct code quickly
- Identifies constraints (memory, I/O, scale) early
- Evolves solution into production-ready design
- Strong communication throughout
Yes:
- Correct solution with some guidance
- Understands tradeoffs but may miss depth
- Minor gaps but solid fundamentals
No:
- Struggles to produce working solution
- Cannot reason about constraints or scaling
- Weak communication or unclear thinking
</content>
</page>"}

<callout icon="🚫" color="gray_bg">
	The current program is on pause - Stay tuned for the updated tool for our coffee chat
</callout>
The coffee chat is a 30mins meeting each week with a randomly selected team mate that you will find automatically in your calendar in the weeks where you’re not off. 
Here’s a quick summary on how it works/why we have it:
- coffee chats are meant to be 30mins chats to mix up members of different teams on a regular basis as we grow - just to get to know each other.
- Chat about whatever you want (doesn't have to be work-related)
- based on your cal availability you will find a meeting slot with another BFL member in your cal in each week
- If the slot doesn't work (can be based on large timezone differences and packed calendars) simply check in with the team member you will meet and reschedule to a date that works for both
- if there's an uneven number of employees available in a week, one person has no meeting for that week. But feel free to simply reach out to someone else if you still want to participate and should be that person.
Happy ☕ -chatting!
