title: Engineering Dev Setup
content: {"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"🚢 Engineering Dev Setup","url":"https://www.notion.so/263c370222d580ab861efc5b0ae49f50","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/263c370222d580ab861efc5b0ae49f50 as of 2025-10-03T06:00:13.014Z: {"title":"Engineering Dev Setup"} This is a perpetually WIP doc. As a new hire it is your sacred duty to pay it forward by adding any undocumented tribal knowledge you uncover during your onboarding. # Codebase and Dev Cluster 1. Clone the [https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/) repo into your local workspace 1. If you can’t open this link, ask to add your github to the BFL org 2. Ask to add you to the cluster 1. Read through the documentation about this here: [https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/blob/main/docs/cluster.md](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/blob/main/docs/cluster.md) 3. Follow the schwarzwald [readme](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/blob/main/README.md) to set up your python virtual environment 4. If you’re working on Backend, clone the [https://github.com/black-forest-labs/hoellental](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/hoellental) repo as well and read through it’s readme # Development Patterns ### IDE and Remote Dev Use whatever IDE you’d like, but we do have company Cursor plan. If you’re a Claude Code enjoyer that’s also supported. The recommended coding practice is to code on your local machine, use `rsync` to push changes to the GPU cluster, then execute code on the GPU node. There is a custom script that executes `rsync` specifically for this: [https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/blob/31c2d7063336b8408798f976349e13d772e8ffce/sync.sh](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/blob/31c2d7063336b8408798f976349e13d772e8ffce/sync.sh). This has a couple benefits: - If you want to install a system-level package (e.g. node.js for Claude Code or oh-my-zsh) it’s a bit of a headache on the GPU cluster. Instead, you can do this on your local machine and get your dev setup exactly how you want it without having to configure the GPU cluster. - You’re decoupled from network issues. You only need good enough internet to `rsync`, ssh, and kick off the script. ### Long-Running Jobs on the Cluster If you need to execute a long-running job on the GPU cluster, we recommend using tmux as follows: 1. ssh into a login node 2. Start a new tmux session 3. Run `./schwarzwald/scripts/getgpu_gb200.sh` to grab a GPU node 4. Kick off your script 5. Detach and reattach to/from your tmux session at will! This is needed because we don’t ssh directly into GPU nodes, and instead they are managed and cleaned up by some otherworldly process. Running `getgpu_gb200.sh` in a tmux session persists your connection to the GPU node, else the node will be cleaned up. "}

title: FDE - Hiring process
content:
{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"FDE - Hiring process","url":"https://www.notion.so/29bc370222d580c3bd0fddf80d1aaeb9","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/29bc370222d580c3bd0fddf80d1aaeb9 as of 2026-03-23T14:00:40.920Z: {"title":"FDE - Hiring process"} # Process Overview
**Round** **Facilitators** **Duration** **Notes / Resources**
Screening Recruiter 30 min
Experience & Behavioral 45 min
Sales Collab
(Senior Only)		 Sales / Partnership 45 min Senior candidates should go through an additional round with sales/partnership to confirm confidence with owning customer relationships & collaboration with sales
Technical Case & Problem Solving 45 min scenario based exercise, debugging an issue a customer may face
FDE Interviewing - Technical Cases
Onsite Freiburg / SF including culture fit with founder Full Day
# Round Details ## Interview #1: Pre-Screening **Culture based questions:
**Adaptability around high pressure situations.
Environment that you thrive in. **Technical knowledge:
**High level overview of their knowledge of deploying and finetuning GenAi Models.
Solving customer technical problems with examples. ## Interview #2: Peer Interview - Experience & Behavioral This round asks the candidate to present a recent technical project they're proud of, in significant detail. The goal is to assess technical depth, ownership, decision-making quality, and genuine engagement with their work.
**Opening prompt to candidate:** *"Tell me about your favourite recent technical project you worked on and are proud of. Walk me through the problem you were solving, the architecture of your solution, and the key decisions you made along the way. Go as deep as you can — we love details."*
Allow the candidate to present for \~5-10 minutes before steering with questions. Take notes on claims you want to probe later. Your aim as interviewer should be to: - Understand the problem and solution they are presenting in as much detail as possible (be curious!) - Test the candidates understanding for the technologies and design decisions involved in the solution they are presenting - Be the devils advocate and ask the most critical and “dumb” questions about the project the candidate is presenting Assess for the following: - How much did this person actually do versus observe or coordinate? - Can they explain implementation details, not just architecture diagrams? - Do they say "I" vs. "we" appropriately — taking credit where earned but acknowledging collaborators honestly? - Can they describe dead ends they personally hit and how they worked through them? - Do they know the gnarly edge cases and why certain parts were harder than expected? - Do they light up when describing the problem or the elegant parts of the solution? - Do they show curiosity about their own work — things they'd still like to explore or improve?

**Red flags:** Only able to describe the system at a high level. Can't answer "what was the hardest part for you personally?" with specifics. Attributes all key decisions to others when pressed.**
** Directions of questions you could ask: - Why did you take design decision x? - What tradeoffs did you have to make in y? - What would you do different when taking this decision next time? - How did you measure success of z? ## Interview #3: BFL Technical Scenario Goal: probe their problem-solving capabilities and domain expertise + working with clients Prismo Aspect Ratio Challenge FDE Interviewing - Technical Cases ## Onsite ### Onsite Technical Challenge Challenge repo: [https://github.com/black-forest-labs/mle-onsite](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/mle-onsite) **Requirements for challenge discussion:** *Good candidates should…* - … explain sampling pipeline fixes - … explain finetuning config changes (specifically in connected to the customer requirements described) - High res - Learning rate - … explain fine tuning data handling - did they add new synthetic data (e.g. for additional car colors)? - how did they label the data? - … be able to discuss REST API hosting challenges - what might be different challenges at larger scale & in prod? - … reason over agent architecture choice - Which tools are available to the agent & why? - Which agentic patterns ([e.g. loop, vs, sequential)](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents) & why? - … formulate a solid product vision for a conversational interface for image gen & edit ### Sales / Partnership Interview (during onsite) Your aim as interviewer should be to: - Understand the candidate's natural instinct for navigating customer relationships — even if they haven't formally done it before - Probe whether they can think commercially: understanding deal dynamics, stakeholder mapping, and what makes a customer successful (not just technically unblocked) - Test their ability to translate technical work into business value and communicate it to non-technical stakeholders - Gauge how quickly they could be trusted to represent BFL in a customer-facing context without heavy supervision Questions to ask: - "Walk me through a time you had to convince someone — a colleague, a manager, a user — to adopt a technical approach or tool you believed in. How did you frame the value?" - "A customer you own has gone quiet after a successful POC — they haven't expanded usage or responded to your last two messages. What do you do?" - "You're on a call with a customer who asks for a feature we don't have and won't build in the near term. How do you handle that conversation without losing the deal?" Assess for the following: - Can they think in terms of outcomes for the customer, not just tasks they completed? Do they naturally frame things around value and impact? - Do they show comfort with ambiguity and incomplete information — or do they freeze without a clear technical spec? - Can they read a room? Do they demonstrate awareness of different stakeholder motivations (technical buyer vs. economic buyer vs. end user)? - Do they show a bias toward action and ownership — "I would do X" rather than "I would escalate to someone"? - Are they coachable? When pushed back on an answer, do they adapt their thinking or get defensive? - Do they demonstrate genuine curiosity about the business side — or does commercial thinking feel foreign and uncomfortable? **Red flags:** Frames every answer purely in technical terms with no awareness of the business context. Can't articulate why a customer would care. Defaults to "I'd ask my manager" for any customer-facing scenario. Shows no curiosity about deal dynamics or partnership strategy. # Resources **Black Forest Labs🌲— Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) & Solutions Engineer Interview Preparation Guide** "}

title: FDE Workflow Productisation
content:
{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"FDE Workflow Productisation","url":"https://www.notion.so/33cc370222d5807e9d7fed8e43bf58fd","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/33cc370222d5807e9d7fed8e43bf58fd as of 2026-04-08T10:49:21.333Z:
<page url="https://www.notion.so/33cc370222d5807e9d7fed8e43bf58fd">
<ancestor-path></ancestor-path>
<properties>
{"title":"FDE Workflow Productisation"}
</properties>
<content>
**Why?**
There is nothing more "customer-validated" than workflows developed by FDEs upon customer requests. In a world of unlimited opportunities, this signal is extremely valuable to figure out what our customers find valuable.
**What?**
We need a process that makes the best of this signal and of our FDEs' expertise and creativity. We want FDEs to invest extra effort in workflows they believe could have broader commercial appeal beyond a single customer, and have a way for some of them to graduate to the product so they can be used by all our customers.
---
## Process
1. **Alignment**: The Product & FDE teams build alignment on customer needs, vision and strategy via the existing weekly meeting.
2. **Exploration**: Based on this knowledge and customer interactions, FDEs should consider putting extra effort into the development of workflows, and possibly showcases (demo UIs or playground templates) that meet the needs of customers. Jakob is responsible for the investment put into exploring these opportunities.
3. **Early Product involvement**: As FDEs progress on a workflow and gain confidence in its value, they should seek input from engineers in the Product team to build it in a way that would require minimal re-work if it graduates.
4. **Graduation proposal**: When the FDE team believes a workflow is worth productising, they submit a proposal to the Product team. The proposal should include:
	- A description of the workflow and the customer problem it solves
	- Which customers are running it in production today and the revenue/usage data
	- A working demo or link to the customer deployment
	- A first-pass self-assessment against the evaluation criteria below
5. **Evaluation**: The Product team assesses the opportunity using the criteria below. This is a cross-functional effort involving Creative Technologists, Legal, Product Marketing, DevRel, and Engineering. Evaluation happens on an ad hoc basis for now — we will revisit whether a dedicated monthly or quarterly cadence is needed.
6. **Decision**: Morgan makes the final decision to graduate or not, based on the assessment and the current roadmap and Product team capacity.
7. **Non-graduation path**: Workflows that don't graduate can still be included in showcases so customers and prospects understand what's possible, but they continue being maintained as custom developments by the FDE team.
---
## Evaluation Criteria
- **Strategic alignment**
	- Is it aligned with the vision and product strategy?
	- Is it an activation, retention or revenue play?
- **Reach**
	- How easy is it to demonstrate the workflow?
	- How easy is it for customers to test the workflow?
	- What is the expected number of customers adopting it in the 6 months following launch, and the expected revenue?
- **Impact**
	- What share of the customer's generations is the workflow used for, for the customers using it in production today?
	- Is the workflow improving something customers can already do, or enabling them to do something novel?
	- How much of a difference does the workflow make to their business?
- **Confidence**
	- What is the number of customers running it live in production today, the revenue generated and margin?
	- What are the alternatives to this workflow?
	- Are competitors offering something similar?
- **Effort**
	- How much effort is required (across all functions) to productise it?
	- How much effort is required (across all functions) to maintain it?
	- How future-proof is the workflow — i.e. how likely is it to still be valuable after the launch of our next foundation model and derivatives?
---
## Success Metrics
We will evaluate whether this process is working using the following indicators:
- Number of workflows explored by the FDE team
- Number of workflows graduated to product
- Number of active customers per graduated workflow 30 and 90 days after launch
- Average time from proposal to launch
</content>
</page>"}

title: Feedback and review cycles at BFL - Primer for Leads
content:
{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"Feedback and review cycles at BFL - Primer for Leads","url":"https://www.notion.so/250c370222d5807686bdee75a7d70b56","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/250c370222d5807686bdee75a7d70b56 as of 2026-04-09T16:15:13.554Z: {"title":"Feedback and review cycles at BFL - Primer for Leads"} ### **Feedback culture** Performance at BFL is linked to the delivery of high impact work. We value hard work in general and specifically hard work that generates a huge level of impact for the business (regardless of function). Our review structure and ultimately also our reward strategy is to recognise high impact work. Giving and receiving feedback is a natural and essential part of how you continuously improve performance and productivity. Feedback should ideally be real time and given continuously throughout a working relationship and project. There is also benefit in more structured feedback milestones throughout the team member’s journey with BFL and the below covers this. ### **Probation/”First few months”** Probation is a statutory requirement in most countries with an exception for the US. The probation periods tend to last 3-6 months and in some countries there is an opportunity to extend if deemed necessary. In countries where probation is a legal requirement permanent employment needs to be actively confirmed. Whether you legally have to include it or not, the first few months of someone’s employment are incredibly key. This is when you learn about the company and the work and it’s an opportunity to decide from both sides if there is a good fit. It’s good practice to have a proactive conversation at the start of someone’s employment to ensure everyone is on the same page in terms of expectations. Maybe there are some specific goals but even if there aren’t, there will be project and collaboration expectations that would be great to clarify. On a monthly basis, for the first three months, schedule a meeting/coffee chat/”walk and talk” and check in how the person is performing, if they feel they have the right support and provide development guidance. This doesn’t have to be super formal but it needs to be “labelled” as a check-in so that everyone is on the same page. Prompts but really shouldn’t be too scripted: - How have things been going - anything you're especially proud of or finding tough? - Do you feel clear on what’s expected of you day-to-day? - Are there any blockers or challenges where I can help or step in? - Is there anything I or the team can do differently to make your work easier or more effective? - How are you finding collaboration with the team? There is no need to specifically follow up with the person if things are going to plan. If you think you need to have a bit more of a serious conversation because something isn’t going exactly to plan, make sure you’re able to sit down somewhere face to face and have a more structured meeting. In this situation, follow up on Slack or email afterwards to make sure there is some documentation. All feedback, but particularly feedback about something that isn’t going so well, should have examples and follow up. If you’re the manager of someone who does have a** statutory probation period**, schedule a meeting at the end of this period to cover similar topics as above. Two possible outcomes: - All is going well and according to plan: - Confirm that to the person and the People team - Things are not going to plan: - You think it’s fixable, so you extend the probation for a set period of time. Just make sure to check with the People team first. Probation can’t be extended indefinitely, and the rules vary by country. - You don’t think it’s fixable, for example, they might not have the right experience or may not be the right cultural fit. In this case, you end the probation. Make sure to involve the People team as this is a legal process and requires proper documentation. You’ll also need to align on company communications, so ensure everyone is on the same page. - Remember, you don’t have to wait until the end of the probation period if it’s clear earlier on that the person isn’t going to be the right fit. Whether there’s a formal probation period or not, the longer someone stays, the harder the decision can become. They get embedded in projects and build relationships. That’s why it’s important to use the first few months to really assess whether it’s likely to work out. If there’s a statutory probation period and you decide to part ways, it’s generally much simpler from a legal perspective to do so during probation than after. ### **Continuous 1:1s** - We strongly encourage you to keep up frequent check-ins and feedback beyond the initial onboarding phase. - Use 1:1s to do a quick temperature check and surface any specific topics. - Set a regular cadence — ideally at least once a month, but more frequent is often better. Set whatever cadence works for you. - 1:1s can be casual — a walk, coffee, or short chat — as long as they happen regularly. - Use similar informal prompts as above to guide the conversation, allowing space for openness and feedback. - Avoid ad hoc scheduling — it’s easy for 1:1s to slip unless they’re booked in advance. ## **Feedback calendar**
**Month** **Activity**
January–December (all year) In-the-moment feedback (ongoing)
Individual based on start-date Probation feedback
March Structured feedback cycle opens (Spring)
Mid-April Salary review decisions complete
September Structured feedback cycle opens (Autumn)
Mid-October Salary review decisions complete
## **Bi-annual feedback coupled with salary review** - BFL has two structured feedback sessions per year, one from mid March to early April and the other from mid September to early October. Both are coupled with a formal comp review (the process for salary reviews are covered in a separate document). - The feedback format for these is more structured than in the moment/real time feedback. This is to enable reflection of impact and performance over the last 6 months. - If an employee has been with BFL for 3 full months by the time the performance review, they should have a review but it’s highly unlikely it will result in a salary increase - The process will consist of the following elements: - Self review - Manager review - Upward review - Peer feedback (optional) - Review meeting between manager and direct report to discuss feedback - Calibration - Comp review - Reviews are done in Rippling. This ensures that everything is in one place and saved centrally. - The different reviews and the calibration cover similar areas and should focus on the last 6 months - Reviews are based on impact and impact potential rather than experience/performance and will hopefully drive both individuals and leads to focus on the work that has had the most impact on the business and team. **Useful tips** - Collect notes/examples in whatever way works for you throughout the 6 months just after one review and before the next. - The notes can be super simple and should really just act as prompts for you. This will enable you to compile your review (whether self, lead or inner circle) quicker when you get to it and also avoid just giving examples of things that happened in the last few weeks (recency effect) [**You’ll find more details here**](/285c370222d58022bd06fc738013f47f?pvs=25)**
**[**Levelling guide**](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11cFz0x9HfIvfT2aV7KhT7wG7yR5yyMQES7fzSUY2QaI/edit?gid=405978997#gid=405978997) ## **Serious performance concerns (after probation)** The rationale for doing ongoing feedback throughout the year is so that you spot lower performance or any other issues outside of the structured reviews. A few key things to keep in mind: - As a Lead/Leadership, be vigilant if you see any drop in performance or productivity. - Address it straight away and find out why i.e. is there a real performance issue or is something (company or personal) affecting the person’s ability to perform. - Give the right support or course correction and if serious, document it. For example give the feedback in writing or if verbal feedback do a written follow up. - If there is no change, depending on where the person is located, it could lead to: - Immediate termination - Need to initiate a performance improvement plan - Need to a settlement agreement - Speak to the People team as early as possible if you see these signs. ### "}

# **Head of Finance MOC**
### **Mission**
- Build and scale a world-class finance function to support Black Forest Labs' rapid growth to 100m ARR+
- Drive strategic financial planning and controls across our global operations while preparing the company for future growth milestones: we always want to be fundraising ready
- Partner with leadership to optimise our dual revenue streams from API and licensing models, cash flow planning/compute/ fundraising planning
In a nutshell, we are looking for a generalist who is hungry:
-
	![]()
	Strategic financial planning /FP&A who can go deep on financial modeling, build our budget, track metrics
-
	![]()
	(Up) Scaling financial processes and systems
-
	![]()
	Accounting DNA for managing accounting operations and monthly bookkeeping with external accounting firm
-
	![]()
	Liquidity and cash flow management
-
	![]()
	Can work independently without a large team around them
-
	![]()
	Maintains agility needed for continued growth: international expansion, sophisticated financial planning
-
	![]()
	Can run EY finance ops workstreams
### **Outcomes (Next 12-18 Months)**
### Financial Planning & Strategy
- Develop and maintain comprehensive financial models and rolling forecasts aligned with company strategy
- Lead consolidated reporting and financial planning across international entities
- Drive strategic initiatives including pricing strategies and long-term financial planning
- Partner with leadership to provide actionable financial insights for decision-making
### Operations & Infrastructure
- Design and implement scalable financial controls and accounting infrastructure
- Oversee core financial operations (AR/AP, bookkeeping, reconciliation)
- Manage cash flow optimization and treasury operations
- Establish efficient, scalable finance ops processes for BFL's continued growth
### Compliance & External Relations
- Lead tax strategy and compliance efforts with EY and other partners
- Oversee global IP structure and transfer pricing implementation
- Ensure regulatory compliance across all jurisdictions
- Manage relationships with key financial partners and vendors
### Team Building & Leadership
- Work independently for 6-12 months and collaborate with external accounting and tax advisory firms
- Create effective working relationships with CEO, Chief of Staff, Sales
- Establish finance as a trusted strategic partner to the business
### **Core Competencies**
### Technical Excellence
- Deep expertise in SaaS/AI finance, particularly with usage-based, API and software licensing models
- Strong foundation in GAAP/IFRS with international accounting experience
- Proven ability to build financial systems and controls from the ground up
- Experience with modern finance tech stack implementation
### Strategic Leadership
- Track record of being a strategic partner to CEOs/founders in high-growth technology companies
- Ability to translate financial concepts for technical and non-technical stakeholders
- Experience in scaling finance operations internationally
- Strong analytical skills with focus on business impact and actionable insights
### Cultural Fit & Working Style
- Comfort with ambiguity and rapid change typical of AI/ML technology companies
- Hands-on leader willing to both set strategy and execute on tactical needs
- Interest in AI/ML technology and BFL position in the market
### Must-Have Qualifications
- 5-10 years of relevant FP&A experience in B2B software/technology companies
- Experience managing international financial operations and entities
- Professional accounting qualification (CPA, ACCA, or equivalent)
- Track record implementing financial systems and controls
- Experience with both API and software licensing revenue models
### Nice-to-Have Qualifications
- German language proficiency
- Prior experience in AI/ML companies
- Background in venture-backed startups
### **Success Metrics (First Year)**
1. Implementation of scalable financial planning and reporting processes
2. Establishment of international entity / IP structure with EY and controls
3. Runs monthly closing bookkeeping independently
4. Revamp Financial systems like ERP
### Resources Required
- Systems implementation budget
- Travel budget for time at international offices
- Professional services budget (audit, tax, advisory)
### Reporting & Relationships
- Reports to: CEO
- Key Relationships: Chief of Staff, Legal, Sales
- Not expected to build a large team around them for a while
</content>

### Overview
**One-line description:** We’re making our models friendly to use (don’t need to be an prompt expert to get photorealistic results), while still being powerful (with new features like web/image search and transparent backgrounds).
A major upgrade to FLUX 2 Pro, Flex, and Max with improved prompt upsampling, auto aspect ratio inference, visual grounding, and transparent backgrounds — making our FLUX 2 models higher quality, easier to prompt, and more intelligent.
**Launch date:** April 28th, 2026 or May 2nd, 2026
**People involved:** Maxim, Scott, Alex, Owais, Stefan, Robin, Nihanth
## What problem we’re solving?
<callout icon="/icons/star_red.svg" color="red_bg">
	**Developers building on our models struggle to build useful product experiences that creators actually retain on.** 
	- Getting images that look photo-realistic and not AI slop requires expert prompting and alot of manual steps.
		*Amazon Alexa flagged a "baked" look that isn't professional-grade, VSCO reported color shifts ruining their filters, and Canva saw quality degrade over iterative edits. *
	- Images aren’t configurable or usable in a real workflow because models don’t remove backgrounds or give you the exact aspect ratio you need to post on social, edit in Figma etc.
		*Amazon Ads and Alexa both found that basic prompts produce unusable output, and Alexa asked how to generate clean transparent-background stickers for overlaying on photos. *
	- Model can’t search the web for real world references to create with (current events, specific locations, products)
</callout>
## Who are we building for
<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**P0: **Developers with end users that aren’t prompt experts, but still need high fidelity outputs and more control (eg Krea, Freepik, Lovart, Figma, Adobe).
</callout>
<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**P1: **Professional creatives that don’t use tools like ComfyUI, but can use tools like Figma, Weavy, and Krea. They need ease-of-use and the ability to create usable outputs for e-commerce, brand design, and advertising use cases. 
</callout>
## Messaging
<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	### **High quality images with simple prompts. **
	FLUX 2.1 gives you photorealistic images by default, even if you use simple prompts.
	Users can also now control the generation to get the exact image they need: 
	- Remove backgrounds: create logos, graphic designs, character photos without a background. Add to an existing design file in Adobe, Figma, etc without needing to make manual edits.
	- Web and image search: refer to logos/characters/places directly in your prompt and the model will search the web for images of that thing to use as a reference image during generation. 
	- Get images in the exact aspect ratio you need (just specify “16:9” or “Instagram”)
</callout>
## What we're launching
We’re releasing upgraded 2.1 versions of **Pro, Flex, and Max**. Here’s what’s shipping:
**Web search and image search for recent things** (aka Visual Grounding): you don’t need to manually upload reference images of publicly known things anymore. Just refer to logos/characters/places directly in your prompt and the model will search the web for images of that thing to use them as a reference images during generation.

				### Why Launch FLUX 2.1
				- Image generation is moving from "cool toy" to "default way to create" for professional workflows
				- Current customers like Amazon, Canva, Snap, and e-commerce companies still rely on manual methods because outputs aren't reliable enough
				- Every time the model produces unusable results, users revert to traditional methods
				- 2.1 makes the model smarter and less reliant on expert prompting to close the quality gap
				### Core Problems Being Solved
				- **Requires expert prompting**: Basic prompts produce unusable output; 2.1 adds better prompt upsampling, auto aspect ratio, grounding, and background removal
				- **AI-generated look**: Outputs have a "baked" appearance; new PUP produces more natural, photorealistic results
				- **Inaccurate representations**: Model mixes up product colors, proportions, and details; visual grounding searches the web so the model actually "sees" what it's generating
				### What's Shipping in 2.1
				- Upgraded versions of Pro, Flex, and Max simultaneously (models stay the same, logic changes)
				- New prompt upsampling for more realistic images and better character reference/text editing
				- Automatic aspect ratio inference from prompt content
				- Visual grounding that searches the web for reference images of named people, logos, characters, and places
				- Transparent background removal capability
				- API parameter alignment with Google and OpenAI standards
				### Technical and Legal Discussions
				- **Visual grounding risks**: Can directly copy watermarked images from web search and recreate people/IP with high accuracy; risk elevated because users may not understand images come from web, not model
				- **Moderation approach**: Output moderation still in place but input-side blocklist may need enhancement; LLMs can help with IP filtering in the prompt upsampling layer
				- **NSFW testing**: Still needed to identify edge cases in image search
				- **Communication strategy**: May need to manage risk through marketing/comms and FAQs explaining how visual grounding works
				### Evaluations and Testing
				- Amazon load tests scheduled for April 2-3
				- LM Arena whitelist ready; can submit immediately for weekend results
				- Playground Arena available but has UI issue to resolve
				- Endpoint improvements include GPT 5.4 swap (faster, same quality) and prompt tweaks to avoid copying reference images
				### Open Questions Discussed
				- **API parameters**: Whether to expose quality parameter (like GPT image) and grounding default on/off
				- **Image search API**: Currently using Serper API on ramp card (not production-ready); need to evaluate Google API for cost and reliability
				- **Pricing model**: Flat fee vs additional charges for grounding; need to decide across Pro/Flex/Max and implement pricing functions
				- **Demo experience**: Critical dependency for launch success; exploring chat UI for natural iteration and discovery (Prompt Party model)
				### Launch Timeline and Dependencies
				- Original target: April 14, 2026
				- Revised target: April 21, 2026 (still optimistic)
				- Key dependencies: safety testing with Bender (\~8 day SLA), legal/moderation decisions, demo experience, pricing implementation, Flex and Max variants
				- Easter holiday may impact European team availability
				- Alexa team expecting early access regardless of public launch date

	## Why ship FLUX 2.1?
	Image generation is at an inflection point where it's slowly moving from "cool toy" to "default way to create" for professional workflows. But that transition only happens when the output is good enough that people stop going back to manual methods like photoshoots, design agencies, and hand editing. Today, our biggest customers still do things manually:
	- Amazon runs millions of ad creatives across languages and can't afford a prompting expert for each one
	- Canva and Snap need to serve non-technical end users who will abandon the feature if results look fake
	- E-commerce companies need product images that are accurate enough to actually sell things. 
	Every time the model garbles a product, shifts a color, or requires five prompt rewrites to get something usable, it pushes users back to the old way of doing things. 2.1 closes that gap by making the model smarter to handle the basics on its own so image generation is not just an experiment people try and give up on.
	#### **New prompt upsampling (PUP)**
	#### Higher realism
	Reduced bake and more photorealistic outputs across the board. Example: T2I reduced bake using the same prompt.
	<columns>
		<column>
			<empty-block/>

	#### Aspect ratio inference from the prompt
	Greatly improving quality of life and arena scores. It will be possible to prompt specific aspect ratio, i.e. “16:9” or “landscape”. If those are not present, the model will guess based on the prompt content i.e. it will guess 9:16 for a prompt “instagram screenshot”
	#### Visual grounding (aka Web Search)
	Model will identify named people/logos/characters/places in the prompt and will look online for the images of those to use them as a reference images during generation, i.e. for prompt “Robin Rombach holds the flag of Black Forest Labs”, model will find images of Robin and BFL’s logo and generate an image:
	<empty-block/>
	#### **Transparent background.**
	Background removal capability, allowing users to generate images with transparent backgrounds via a `background` parameter (`auto | transparent | opaque`).
	#### **API parameter alignment.** 
	Parameters aligned with Google and OpenAI standards for easier integration.

		- [ ] Team to decide on Max scoring improvements (vision generation loop vs replacing Pro with Flex) [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5801f9e01dbb08758de17]
		### FLUX 2.1 Launch Timeline
		- **This week**: Send Pro endpoint to Elena Marina for evaluation, finalize feature set and pricing [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Next week**: Polish and ensure everything is ready [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Target launch**: April 14th (approximately 2 weeks out) [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- Timeline may shift depending on Elena Marina evaluation results [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		### What's Launching with FLUX 2.1
		Releasing upgraded versions of Pro, Flex, and Max models simultaneously with: [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Improved prompt upsampling**: More realistic images, better character reference and text editing [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		- **Auto aspect ratio inference**: From prompt content (e.g., "16:9" or "landscape") [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Visual grounding**: Web search for named entities in prompts [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Transparent background**: Background removal capability [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Better quality and latency** compared to current models [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- API parameter alignment with Google and OpenAI standards [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		### Technical Decisions & Discussion
		- **GPT model choice**: Need to test GPT-5.4 mini vs current 5.1 for latency before sending to Elena Marina [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		- Partnership allows for re-evaluation if needed, relatively low cost concern [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		- **Endpoint design**: New endpoints for each model (not drop-in replacement), users opt-in by choice [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580be812de011d15d6489][^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d58047ae07ef18d2841be1]
		- **Upsampling latency**: OpenAI upsampling takes \~5 seconds (majority of request time in best case), compared to 1.85s generation [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5801f9e01dbb08758de17]
		- **Max scoring**: Considering improved scoring with custom prompts per generation and tournament-style comparison [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5801f9e01dbb08758de17]
		### Pricing Complexity Concerns
		- Team pushing to simplify pricing model rather than adding complexity [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5803b84c5c8ba2f4ae35d]
		- Grounding can be expensive (\~1.5 cents for 3 images) and should have separate pricing toggle [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5808bbf37de2bc474d8ef]
		- Transparent background also incurs GPU costs that need margin calculation [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5808bbf37de2bc474d8ef]
		- Proposal: Average out costs into simplified per-megapixel pricing rather than exposing all feature complexity [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5808bbf37de2bc474d8ef]
		- Stefan emphasized avoiding more pricing variables and keeping it simple for customers [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		### Amazon/Alexa Partnership
		- Alexa wants access to new prompt upsampling, originally planned to launch tomorrow but delayed due to backend issues [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- Likely don't need grounding for Alexa use cases (more world knowledge focused) [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- Decision needed on custom endpoint vs standard 2.1 endpoint with parameters [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- Pricing needs to be locked in; need to clarify existing agreement with Alexa team [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- Team leaning toward single endpoint with parameters rather than managing two separate endpoints [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		### GTM & Marketing Perspective
		- Owais noted this feels like a substantial launch, not just a small release [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580fb9b08f5c8d109bf16]
		- Multiple compelling use cases to showcase [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580fb9b08f5c8d109bf16]
		- Core value: Makes models easier to use, less reliant on expert prompting [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5806b99a5e8558da1c90f]
		- Quality of life improvements (auto aspect ratio, grounding) reduce user effort while improving results [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5806b99a5e8558da1c90f]
		- USP for customers: Higher realism, more smart features via prompting, better product consistency [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5803b84c5c8ba2f4ae35d]
	</summary>

title: FLUX 3 - Nailing Hero Use Cases
content:
{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"FLUX 3 - Nailing Hero Use Cases","url":"https://www.notion.so/33ac370222d58006842adc3f7e38f039","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/33ac370222d58006842adc3f7e38f039 as of 2026-04-07T19:44:09.329Z: {"title":"FLUX 3 - Nailing Hero Use Cases"} The purpose of this doc is to align on the use cases that we must nail with FLUX 3 to be competitive and get commercial success. ## What are the Priority Capabilities for FLUX 3? {toggle="true"} Tier 1 - Image to Video - Text to Image - Image to Image - Video to Video Tier 2 - Text to Video ## What are the Priority High Level Use Cases for FLUX 3? {toggle="true"} Tier 1 - Ecommerce - Advertising / MKG Tier 2 - Social Media ## What are the Priority Low Level Use Cases for Video? {toggle="true"} Tier 1
Photorealism The bar is "brand manager approves for a paid campaign without caveats" — not "impressive for AI." Audiences reject anything that looks synthetic.
Reference Object Fidelity Exact reproduction of labels, textures, colors, and proportions from the input image. Zero hallucination — a distorted logo on a product spin is a launch blocker.
Cross-Clip Consistency Same product or character looks identical across every clip in a campaign. 20 ad variants = pixel-consistent appearance in all 20.
Deterministic Camera Control Specifiable orbits, pans, zooms, tracking shots. E-commerce: smooth 360° with consistent lighting. Advertising: dolly, crane, rack focus.
Surgical Video Edits Swap backgrounds, product variants, or text overlays while everything else stays pixel-identical. Key constraint: fidelity preservation across multiple edit rounds with no drift. Video Kontext — unchanged regions are untouched, not re-generated.
Instant Edit Turnaround Edits like swapping a background or updating text should return in seconds, not trigger full video regeneration. Architecturally, edits must operate on existing latent representations, not re-run the full pipeline.
Video Style Transfer Apply color grading, stylistic filters, or brand aesthetics to existing footage without regenerating content.
Tier 2
Multi-Keyframe Generation Provide N keyframes (not just start or start+end) and the model generates coherent motion between all of them. Multi-keyframe unlocks precise narrative control — specify exact moments and the model fills transitions faithfully.
Typography & Animated Text Deterministic font, color, size, and animation style across campaign variants — variant #1's headline treatment = variant #20's. Text that appears, animates, and exits with transitions (fade, slide-in, typewriter, kinetic). Likely requires style-reference conditioning.
Motion Graphics & Animation Transitions (wipes, dissolves, geometric reveals), logo animations (scale up, particle assembly, draw-on), animated data (charts that build, counters, process flows), and kinetic effects on static assets (Ken Burns, parallax, dynamic cropping). Collapses post-production workflows into single generation calls.
Layer Compositing Semi-transparent overlays, lower thirds, badges, and UI elements composited into the scene. Most ad and social content is layered, not a single shot.
Tier 3
Custom Font Rendering Render specific brand fonts accurately. Likely requires font-conditioning input (upload font file) rather than prompt-based inference.
Multi-Angle Scene Generation Same scene from 3–5 camera positions for editorial cutting.
Useful references: - ## What are the Hard Constraints? {toggle="true"} - **Duration:** 45–60 seconds minimum. - **Resolution:** 1080p minimum. - **Aspect Ratios:** at least 9:16, 16:9, 1:1, 4:5. - **Speed:** Generation at least competitive with leading models, without being at the expense of quality. Editing near-real-time. ## What Good looks like for our Hero Use Cases? {toggle="true"}
Product 360° Spin (Ecommerce) A product (e.g., sneaker, handbag, electronics device) on a clean background does a smooth, complete 360° rotation. Logo, material details, and geometry stay pixel-perfect throughout. \~10 seconds.
**Maps to:** Reference Object Fidelity, Deterministic Camera Control
**Customer signal:** Photoroom (#1 pain point: product accuracy degrades during rotation), Walmart (abandoned 360° spins due to hallucination), Envato (product showcase is 83% of volume)
Fashion Virtual Model Walk (Ecommerce) An AI-generated model wearing a user's garment walks toward camera, pauses, turns, walks away. Garment drape, texture, and brand details stay consistent. 1:1 or 9:16 aspect ratio, \~8 seconds.
**Maps to:** Reference Object Fidelity, Cross-Clip Consistency, Photorealism
**Customer signal:** Photoroom (virtual model animation is #1 use case), Envato (bring-image-to-life is #2 use case)
Automotive Hero Shot (Advertising) A luxury car drives through a mountain road — tracking shot that follows the car laterally (Russian arm style). Reflections, paint finish, and wheel geometry stay accurate. \~10 seconds.
**Maps to:** Deterministic Camera Control, Reference Object Fidelity, Photorealism
**Customer signal:** Omnicom (#2 and #7 use cases — automotive key visuals and TVC motion; Russian arm specifically flagged as missing from all models)
Product in Lifestyle Context (Advertising) A warehouse product photo of a kitchen appliance is transformed into a lifestyle scene — the appliance sits on a counter, steam rises, hands interact with it. Natural, subtle movement — not exaggerated. \~15 seconds.
**Maps to:** Photorealism, Reference Object Fidelity, Surgical Video Edits
**Customer signal:** Walmart (#1 use case: raw warehouse images → lifestyle marketing video), Photoroom (unnatural/exaggerated movement is pain point #2).
Designed Social Ad from Product Image (Advertising / Social) From one product photo, generate a 15-second social-ready ad with motion graphics, animated headline, price badge, and CTA. Designed compositions with text and graphic overlays, not just camera shots. 9:16 primary, \~15 seconds.
**Maps to:** Motion Graphics & Animation, Typography & Animated Text, Multi-Keyframe Generation
**Customer signal:** Canva (#1 ask: coherent multi-shot generation), Walmart (promotional videos). Distinct from "Product in Lifestyle" — this is *designed* ad creative, not photorealistic footage.
Background Swap on Existing Video (V2V Editing) A product demo video where the background environment changes from a studio to a beach to a kitchen — while the foreground product and hand motion stay pixel-identical. \~10 seconds showing 3 variants.
**Maps to:** Surgical Video Edits, Instant Edit Turnaround
**Customer signal:** Omnicom (V2V localization: UK kitchen → Spanish kitchen), our V2V editing research (background swap is #1 editing use case)
Text & CTA Overlay Swap (V2V Editing) A promotional video where the headline text, price tag, and CTA button change between variants — "Save 20%" → "Spare 20%" → "Ahorre 20%" — while the video footage stays identical. Animated text elements (fade-in headlines, sliding price tags, pulsing CTA buttons) should render with typographic precision across all variants. \~6 seconds × 3 variants.
**Maps to:** Surgical Video Edits, Instant Edit Turnaround, Typography & Animated Text
**Customer signal:** Walmart (near-zero hallucination on text is #1 capability ask), Omnicom (screen content localization for Apple is #1 use case)
Style Transfer on Existing Footage (V2V Editing) Take raw footage of a product unboxing and apply a warm, cinematic color grade that matches a brand's visual identity. Same footage, 3 style variants side-by-side. \~8 seconds.
**Maps to:** Video Style Transfer
**Customer signal:** Omnicom (style transfer is a production need), our V2V research (style transfer & color grading is #3 editing use case)
"}

title: FLUX.2 [klein] - Private API integration
content:
{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"FLUX.2 [klein] - Private API integration","url":"https://www.notion.so/2e9c370222d5805abe1ff9955ca9a94e","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/2e9c370222d5805abe1ff9955ca9a94e as of 2026-03-19T14:14:45.724Z: {"title":"FLUX.2 \\[klein\\] - Private API integration"} # Image Generation with FLUX.2 \[klein\] **UNMODERATED ENDPOINT** — The `-private` endpoints documented on this page are **unmoderated**. They do not apply content moderation or safety filtering to generated images. Using these endpoints is subject to the specific terms agreed between Black Forest Labs and whitelisted partners (which can stipulate that Partners deploying these endpoints are fully responsible for implementing their own content moderation and ensuring compliance with applicable laws and regulations). FLUX.2 \[klein\] is our fastest and most cost-effective model family, optimized for high-throughput use cases while maintaining excellent quality. Available in two variants: **Klein 4B**, **Klein 9B.** This is a guide for private, extremely fast endpoints we offer to trusted partners. ## API Endpoints **Global Endpoint (Recommended):** - [`api.bfl.ai`](http://api.bfl.ai) - Automatic failover between clusters for enhanced uptime **Regional Options:** - [`api.eu.bfl.ai`](http://api.eu.bfl.ai) - European Multi-cluster - [`api.us.bfl.ai`](http://api.us.bfl.ai) - US Multi-cluster routing ## Available Models
Endpoint Description
`/flux-2-klein-4b-private` Fastest model, 4B parameters, **unmoderated**
`/flux-2-klein-9b-private` Higher quality, 9B parameters, **unmoderated**
--- ## Basic Text-to-Image Generation The API uses an asynchronous workflow: 1. **Submit** a generation request 2. **Poll** for results using the returned `polling_url` ### Python Example ```python import os import requests import time # Step 1: Submit generation request response = requests.post( 'https://api.bfl.ai/v1/flux-2-klein-9b-private', headers={ 'accept': 'application/json', 'x-key': os.environ.get("BFL_API_KEY"), 'Content-Type': 'application/json', }, json={ 'prompt': 'A serene mountain landscape at sunset with golden light', 'width': 1024, 'height': 1024, }, ).json() print(f"Task ID: {response['id']}") polling_url = response['polling_url'] # Step 2: Poll for results while True: result = requests.get( polling_url, headers={ 'accept': 'application/json', 'x-key': os.environ.get("BFL_API_KEY"), }, ).json() if result['status'] == 'Ready': print(f"Image URL: {result['result']['sample']}") break elif result['status'] == 'Error': print(f"Error: {result.get('error')}") break time.sleep(0.5) ``` --- ## Generation with Reference Images FLUX.2 \[klein\] supports up to **4 reference images** for style guidance and context. Images can be provided as URLs or base64-encoded data. ### Python Example with Reference Images ```python import os import requests import time import base64 from PIL import Image from io import BytesIO # Prepare reference images (can be URLs or base64) # Submit generation with reference images response = requests.post( 'https://api.bfl.ai/v1/flux-2-klein-9b-private', headers={ 'accept': 'application/json', 'x-key': os.environ.get("BFL_API_KEY"), 'Content-Type': 'application/json', }, json={ 'prompt': 'A cozy coffee shop interior, warm lighting, photorealistic', 'input_image': '', 'input_image_2': '', 'input_image_3': '', 'width': 1024, 'height': 1024, }, ).json() polling_url = response['polling_url'] # Poll for results while True: result = requests.get( polling_url, headers={ 'accept': 'application/json', 'x-key': os.environ.get("BFL_API_KEY"), }, ).json() if result['status'] == 'Ready': print(f"Image URL: {result['result']['sample']}") break elif result['status'] == 'Error': print(f"Error: {result.get('error')}") break time.sleep(0.5) ``` --- ## Request Parameters
Parameter Type Required Description
`prompt` string Yes Text description of the image to generate
`width` integer No Output width (default: 1024, max total: 4MP)
`height` integer No Output height (default: 1024, max total: 4MP)
`input_image` string No First reference image (URL or base64)
`input_image_2` string No Second reference image (URL or base64)
`input_image_3` string No Third reference image (URL or base64)
`input_image_4` string No Fourth reference image (URL or base64)
`seed` integer No Random seed for reproducibility
`output_format` string No `"jpeg"` or `"png"` (default: jpeg)
**Note:** The `safety_tolerance` parameter is not applicable to these `-private` endpoints as they are **unmoderated**. No content filtering is applied to generated outputs. --- ## Response Format ### Initial Response ```json { "id": "task-uuid-here", "polling_url": "" } ``` ### Polling Response (Success) ```json { "id": "task-uuid-here", "status": "Ready", "result": { "sample": "https://delivery.bfl.ai/..." } } ``` > **Important:** The signed URL in `result.sample` expires after **10 minutes**. Download the image immediately rather than storing the URL. --- ## Rate Limits - **Standard limit:** 24 concurrent active tasks - HTTP 429 indicates rate limit exceeded --- ## Model Comparison
Model Speed Quality Best For
Klein 4B Fastest Good High-throughput applications, rapid prototyping
Klein 9B Fastest Better Balance of speed and quality
--- ## cURL Example ```bash # Submit request curl -X POST 'https://api.bfl.ai/v1/flux-2-klein-4b-private' \ -H 'accept: application/json' \ -H 'x-key: YOUR_API_KEY' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "prompt": "A futuristic city skyline at night", "width": 1024, "height": 768 }' # Poll for result (use the polling_url from response) curl -X GET 'https://api.bfl.ai/v1/get_result?id=YOUR_TASK_ID' \ -H 'accept: application/json' \ -H 'x-key: YOUR_API_KEY' ``` "}

It delivers *state-of-the-art* image generation and advanced image editing with exceptional realism, precision, and consistency. Built for professional use, **FLUX.2 \[max\]** produces production-ready outputs for marketing teams, creatives, filmmakers, and creators around the world. # API Integration **FLUX.2 \[max\]:** `POST`[https://api.bfl.ai/v1/flux-2-max](https://api.bfl.ai/v1/flux-2-max)
**API Parameters** **Required Parameters** `prompt` (string) - Text description of the image to generate **Optional Parameters** `input_image` (string) - Base64 encoded or URL of the image `input_image_2` (string) - Base64 encoded or URL of the image `input_image_3` (string) - Base64 encoded or URL of the image `input_image_4` (string) - Base64 encoded or URL of the image `input_image_5` (string) - Base64 encoded or URL of the image `input_image_6` (string) - Base64 encoded or URL of the image `input_image_7` (string) - Base64 encoded or URL of the image `input_image_8` (string) - Base64 encoded or URL of the image `width` (integer) - Width of the image, default `1024` Range: 256-2048 `height` (integer) - Height of the image, default `1024` Range: 256-2048. `seed` (integer) - Seed for reproducibility `output_format` (string) - Output format for the generated image. Default: `jpeg`. Valid values: `jpeg`, `png` `safety_tolerance` (integer) - Range 0-5, default 2. Moderation tolerance level.
**Example Request** ***Python*** ```javascript import requests import os import time api_key = os.environ.get("BFL_API_KEY") # Submit generation request response = requests.post( "https://api.bfl.ai/v1/flux-2-max" headers={"x-key": api_key}, json={ "prompt": "A mountain landscape at sunset", "width": 1440, "height": 1440, "output_format": "jpeg" } ) print(request) request_id = request["id"] polling_url = request["polling_url"] print(f"Request ID: {request_id}") print(f"Polling URL: {polling_url}") ``` ***Repsonse *** ```javascript Request ID: Polling URL: ```
**Polling** A successful response will be a JSON object containing the result, where **`result['sample']`** is a signed URL for retrieval. Our signed URLs are only valid for 10 minutes. Please retrieve your result within this timeframe. ***Python*** ```python # This assumes request_id and polling_url are set from the previous step import time while True: time.sleep(0.5) result = requests.get( polling_url, headers={ 'accept': 'application/json', 'x-key': os.environ.get("BFL_API_KEY"), }, params={ 'id': request_id, }, ).json() status = result["status"] print(f"Status: {status}") if status == "Ready": print(f"Result: {result['result']['sample']}") break elif status in ["Error", "Failed"]: print(f"Generation failed: {result}") break ``` ***Response *** ```python Request ID: ```
# Why it matters - **Highest precision image editing. **FLUX.2 **\[max\]** achieves the highest consistency in image editing across the FLUX.2 model family. It preserves colors, lighting, faces, written characters, and objects with all their details making it the ideal choice for high-quality **use cases** like **product marketing, e-commerce, product variations, interior design, 3D reconstruction, filmmaking **and more… - **Generate images grounded in real-time information.** FLUX.2 **\[max\]** searches the web when needed, you can create visuals of yesterday’s football game, the weather in real-time of any cities or re-create historical events. - **Maximum Prompt Adherence. **FLUX.2 **\[max\]** follows prompts with greater accuracy than previous FLUX models. It handles both concise and detailed instructions with improved precision, translating text input into visual output that aligns more closely with user intent. - **Multi-reference editing with state-of-the-art character consistency.** FLUX.2 **\[max\] **will keep identities, products and styles consistent. Built your projects with maximal coherence. - up to 8 reference images possible on API - up to 10 reference images on the Playground - **FLUX.2 \[max\] is our most creative model to date. **Built for creators, artists, filmmakers, and creatives around the world who want to bring their visions to life with maximum creative freedom. # FLUX.2 **\[max\] Use-cases** ## Product Marketing > Create highest-quality, marketplace-ready product photos that look polished, consistent, and professional - content: {"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"FLUX.3 Midtraining Goals","url":"https://www.notion.so/314c370222d580419c94f6900de02437","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/314c370222d580419c94f6900de02437 as of 2026-03-30T15:51:19.056Z: {"title":"FLUX.3 Midtraining Goals"} # General questions - [ ] Multi-task training: - [ ] how are we balancing the tasks vs each other, i.e how much image editing, how much image to video, how much text to video? - [ ] what does more conditioning (image(s), camera, video) beyond text mean for noise schedule? - [ ] already start building specialized models? - [ ] Which discriminative tasks can we add? - [ ] Which tasks to add? - t2i: ✅ - i2i single: ✅ - i2i multi: ✅ - t2v: ✅ - i2v: ✅  - specific frames → video 🚧 - reference editing (if time) - single ref ❌ - multi ref ❌ - t2v+a: ✅ - i2v+a: ✅ - v2v: 🚧 - camera control (can be used for basic action prediction conditioning) - discriminative outputs - masks - bounding boxes - more explicit action conditioning? (What exactly?) - [ ] Evaluation pipeline : - [ ] build extensive evaluation for each task, which methods to use for*:* - [ ] t2i: - [ ] human ✅: /blob/eval/maksim/benchmarks/t2i_bench_2026-02-13/ - [ ] i2i single: - [ ] human ✅ : /blob/eval/maksim/benchmarks/i2i_bench_2026-03-30 - [ ] i2i multi: - [ ] human ✅ (old) - [ ] t2v: → Vbench2.0 - [ ] human ✅: /blob/eval/maksim/vbench2_results/eval_site/prompts/ - [ ] auto: pending - [ ] i2v: → Vbench2.0 - [ ] human ✅: /blob/eval/maksim/benchmarks/i2v_bench_2026-03-30 - [ ] auto: pending - [ ] t2v+a: → VAbench - [ ] human ✅: /blob/eval/maksim/benchmarks/t2av_bench_2026-03-30 - [ ] auto: pending - [ ] i2v+a: → VAbench - [ ] human ✅ (needs to be copied though): /blob/eval/maksim/benchmarks/i2av_bench_2026-03-30 - [ ] auto: pending - [ ] v2v: - [ ] camera control: - [ ] discriminative outputs - [ ] masks - [ ] bounding boxes - [ ] action prediction/conditioning - [ ] prompt upsampling (initial variant should be ready by then): different prompt upsamplers, task dependent? ## Steps to take (during pretraining) We already want to be evaluating during pretraining to assess if continued pretraining gives us further improvements after adding all the new tasks - [ ] set up evaluation pipeline - [ ] set up midtraining config with all the tasks mentioned above - [ ] consistent finetuning using that config to see if we gain more performance through further pretraining (can be lower res than the actual pretraining but should contain all the tasks # Data ## Video **Goal:** - Increase length of generation (5s, 10s, 15s) - Increase resolution (from 190p/360p in pretraining to 360p+ in midtraining) - Build path for interactive prompting. - interactive prompting needs specific captions - some of the caption pairs should be in instruct/change format instead of t2v - Frame(s) conditioning/image to video - Camera control - video-to-video - Precise time control - e.g. timestamped captions (for the above) - camera trajectories - cut conditioning? **Compared to FLUX.2: **new modality **What we need:** - **General video data** - [ ] more filtering needed? - possibilities: - better watermark detection - higher motion filtering (available on the fly, decide based on pretraining performance) - [ ] video resolution? - [ ] going beyond 360p? - **general** - [ ] *captions: determine captioning ratio between 5s, 10s, 15s *(Owner ) - [ ] Answer question ‘Does training on longer captions improve motion understanding in general’? → ablation - [ ] get training speed perspective on this - **prompting interactivity (Owner + to conduct experiments)** - [ ] * identify switch between actions / semantic difference (switching captions)* - option: check for consecutive frames with low motion - option: check for frames with high difference to the start in some similarity space - option: base it on cuts - option: literature review - **procedure:** collect data for each options and ablate - [ ] *conduct captioning* - [ ] *transform captions into “instruct style”* - **frame conditioning (Owner since captions similar to interactive prompting)** - [ ] *get frame-aware captions* - conditioning formats: - start, - mid - end - start + end - alternative: random frame at t for combination with precise time control - [ ] *reference image(s) to video* - [ ] single ref: - [ ] multi ref: - **Camera control (Owner **❌) - [ ] *input format: *decide whether to - “distill” camera positions into prompt - leave as coord - do both - [ ] *combine with time* —\> camera trajectories - **Time control (Owner **❌) - [ ] *discuss options* - timed cut conditioning - timed captions → yes for interactivity of prompting - timed camera coordinates → yes for precise camera control and trajectories 🤖 - **Discriminative Tasks (Owner **❌) ## Image **Goal:** - Improve common weak points with target datasets - Improve instruction-alignment - Lay the foundation for specific product features - Final Resolution **Compared to FLUX.2: **bigger focus on typography, maybe some different product focus, better captions **What we need:** - Large scale, general image data with hierarchical captions - Base pumpkin - Status: ongoing - improved captions - … ## Image Editing **Goal:** - Introduce Editing as a task - Build strong general capability for referencing & local editing **Compared to FLUX.2: **better scaled datasets, local editing focus **What we need:** - local editing - inpainting dataset including captions (up to 200M): Ready to run, needs gpus - Referencing - products (60M) + posts (40M): ready to train - sstk-ref - TODO: May need stronger filters → only keep if faces are sufficiently large - inat: should be fine to train - \[likely out-of-scope/time\] video → editing pairs - \[likely out-of-scope\] pumpkin pairs - TODO make the pipeline work well - local + Referencing: - inpainting on posts → estimated at least 6M suitable samples - TODO needs finalization - TODO running it - discriminative tasks: - image to mask - image to bounding box ## Video Editing # Audio - # Open Questions: - Should we try to include “control-net” tasks either as a general helper, or as a potential to flywheel with tighter control? - Should we try to bring in explicit cut conditioning here? This has the risk, that our cut detection method might be flawed and provide a bad signal to the model. But is the chance for a good feature in general and a contender for a strong timestamp signal. Also a native starting point for mid generation prompt change - Exact captioning scheme and timestamps for captions? We want interactive prompting so need to annotate time segments of a video clip with captions. - Do we want to create explicit negations in prompts? E.g. “The man isn’t wearing a hat”. Can mostly be solved already by prompt rewriting, but might be awkward “The man has a bald head”. Interesting for “there are no cuts” - Will we have enough high quality data to include video editing - how about audio? - Do hierarchical captions help us? - Do we want to add some additional quality filtering for videos and if so what? - Do we want to invest more on color-ref? Likely needs bigger scale, maybe some changed approach - Can we do explicit camera position conditioning in a sensible way? - Do we want to include 15s clips as well? - make ablation - How much compute do we need? - work back from 1 month midtraining with the decided # Out of Scope "}

title: Global Expense & Travel Policy
content:
{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"💸 Global Expense & Travel Policy","url":"https://www.notion.so/fe9db70444c745039151b879bb1db603","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/fe9db70444c745039151b879bb1db603 as of 2026-04-15T10:03:34.036Z: {"title":"Global Expense & Travel Policy"} ### Welcome to BFL's expense policy We've designed these guidelines to make your work-related spending easy and hassle-free. General rule is: **Act in BFL’s best interests.** **Your Ramp card will be your primary method for handling business expenses and travel, reimbursements where needed and will be issued during your onboarding process.**
Remember, the key is to book early (min. 14 days in advance where possible) and spend wisely to avoid unnecessarily high costs and stretching to upper limit or beyond. If you need an exception, just chat with Sarah before booking. Flights and hotels tend to be more expensive on Ramp platform, please use your Ramp card on alternative booking sites. **Ramp = Primary payment method for all business expenses** - Software subscriptions and licenses - Office supplies and equipment (out of your \$2.5k allowance when you start) - Conference tickets and professional development - Business meetings and team events - Data roaming charges for business travel - Travel expenses - Accommodation - Meals while traveling (conferences, customer meetings, Freiburg trips) - Local transportation (taxis, ride-shares) during work trips - Any other business-related purchases **What the card should not be used for ** - Non-business streaming services or subscriptions like Home Wifi or Netflix, Spotify - Wifi at home - Personal purchases of any kind - Cash withdrawals or cash advances - Gift cards or prepaid cards - Political contributions - Splitting purchases to circumvent spending limits - Entertainment venues (clubs, bars) without clear business purpose - Cryptocurrency or gambling - Fuel for personal vehicles (use mileage reimbursement instead) - Family member travel or meals **All expenses \>\$75 require a receipt and memo. Ramp fetches receipts from your email.** *Note: Ramp doesn’t allow country or city specific policies.* **Hotels** {color="green_bg"} **Europe 🇪🇺& UK 🇬🇧** - Germany 🇩🇪 generally half the price of US rates - Major Business hubs (Berlin, Munich, Frankfurt) up to 250€ per night. - Secondary cities (such as Freiburg) up to €200 per night - **For Freiburg specifically, reasonable rooms for 125-150€ per night if you book on time, ****some suggestions**** below:** - Black F Tower or Black F House (use the code “CORP” during the booking process for a discount) - Aparthotel Adagio - The Cloud Suite Apartments - Hampton by Hilton Freiburg - Apartments for longer stays: - *Black F apartments & Black F House* - *Wohnen auf Zeit - Innenstadt-Appartements* - *Freiburg Apartments Friedrichring* - *Friedrich Boutique-Apartments* ***Your accommodation budget during onboarding is €2,000.*** ***For offsites, we encourage extending your stay by one week (before or after) and join us in Freiburg. Accommodation budget: €1,200. *** **Major 🇪🇺hubs:** - London, Paris and Amsterdam, the upper limit is €350/£300 per night **USA 🇺🇸** - Major Business hubs (NYC, SF/Palo Alto, LA, Miami) upper limit is \$350 per night - SF recommendations [here](/384da917594344d2bd0af44efd47e01f?pvs=25#e819cf489c6544eba5c8718abac75169)
BFL Corporate Pricing Options: - [**Luma Hotel **](https://be.synxis.com/?adult=1&arrive=2026-04-07&chain=19010&child=0¤cy=USD&depart=2026-04-08&hotel=35419&level=hotel&locale=en-US&productcurrency=USD&promo=FORESTB&rooms=1)15% off Best Available Rate. (10 min. walk from office) Contact: Jacques Rachal call/email if there is no availability and he will work to get you taken care of. [jacques.rachal@lumahotelsf.com](mailto:jacques.rachal@lumahotelsf.com) Direct 415-757-1437 - **Hotel Via** (Note this is directly across from the professional baseball park, so check the SF Giant’s schedule before booking here) - Use code: BFLABS when searching room availability to get the rates - Contact Brandi Rivera: [brandie@hotelviasf.com](mailto:brandie@hotelviasf.com) Direct: 415- 200-4979 - Negotiated rates: - **RATE: January 1, 2026 – March 31, 2026, April 1, 2026 – November 16, 2026** - South Beach King/Queen/Two Queen Beds: \$269.00 per night plus tax - Park View King/Queen/Two Queen Beds: \$289.00 per night plus tax - **RATE: April 1, 2026 – November 16, 2026** - South Beach King/Queen/Two Queen Beds: \$315.00 per night plus tax - Park View King/Queen/Two Queen Beds: \$389.00 per night plus tax - **Hyatt **- SF recommendations in the Welcome to SF [Notion page](https://www.notion.so/Welcome-to-San-Francisco-384da917594344d2bd0af44efd47e01f?source=copy_link#e819cf489c6544eba5c8718abac75169), but this link is good for any Hyatt properties not just SF - You need to link your BFL email to your Hyatt profile or create a new one - This is the link to use to get our corporate pricing: - [Black Forest Labs - Be More Here with Hyatt Leverage](https://www.hyatt.com/loyalty/en-US?corp_id=238828) - **Marriott **- SF recommendations in the Welcome to SF [Notion page](https://www.notion.so/Welcome-to-San-Francisco-384da917594344d2bd0af44efd47e01f?source=copy_link#e819cf489c6544eba5c8718abac75169), but this link is good for any Marriott properties not just SF - You will be getting an invite via your BFL email address to [Business access by Marriott Bonvoy](https://businessaccess.marriott.com/hotels)
- For secondary cities the upper limit for reimbursement is \$300 per night. *Need an exception? Just ask – we understand last minute travel for customers and conferences can get pricey.* **Travel** {color="green_bg"} - Plane ✈️ - Economy for short flights; Price guideline within Europe: \< \$350 return - Economy Premium for \> 4h trips - Long-haul flights should be booked as early as possible, ask for approval \> \$2,500 - Please always book return flights as they are significantly cheaper than individual flights - Car 🚗 - For group trips only. - Train 🚆: First choice for intra-Germany and Europe travel: book via Deutsche Bahn for travel within Germany. - First-class tickets for \>2 hour trips **Food & third party entertainment** {color="green_bg"} - Business related dinners & drinks with third parties or occasionally within the team should not exceed \> €/\$50 per head, otherwise ask for approval before. While this guideline aims to promote cost consciousness, we recognize that reasonable exceptions may arise based on business context, location, and circumstances. Use professional judgment and ensure expenses align with business objectives. - All attendees & purpose of the expense should be mentioned when submitting the receipt. **Workplace equipment** {color="green_bg"} - Your current laptop & mobile phone allowance stands at €2.5k (\$2.7k) including office equipment related expenses if you’re working out of SF or Freiburg office and is \$4k (€3.5k) if you’re remote. **Reimbursements** {color="green_bg"} All out of pocket expenses will be reimbursed via Ramp, linked to your bank account (which needs to be added in the system). Open the App, click + and select “new reimbursement” and upload the receipt to initiate the process. Happy smart spending! "}
