{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"🚀 GTM Team Meeting Notes","url":"https://www.notion.so/311c370222d581fab2cbcc446435cdad","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/311c370222d581fab2cbcc446435cdad as of 2026-04-14T15:57:53.742Z: {"title":"GTM Team Meeting Notes"} **👤 Owner:** @Anthony Charbonnier - - Opens - Product update - - Deal updates - Hiring update --- # **April 7, 2026** {toggle="true"} *(Summary)* **👥 Present:** Anthony Charbonnier · Jakob Pörschmann · Stephan Lachmann · Alexander Thebelt · Owais Khan · Gigi Henze · Stephen Batifol · Aitana Giebels van Bekestein · Morgan ## 🏆 Team Recognition Alex: product photography breakthrough + Snap deal leadership. API team: 99%+ success rate on Amazon load test after an intensive week — benefits all customers. Isabella: strong AE candidate pipeline. Amanda: open weight license work flagged as critical for Q2. Sarah Cyro (product): unblocked LoRa functionality. ## 🧪 LoRa / Object Removal Demo LoRa trained on FLUX client 9B for Samsung + Runway use cases. Input: image + binary mask → seamless background replacement. 56% win rate vs Runway in human evals (200 images, 50 evaluators) — competitive with NanaBanana 2, faster and cheaper. Prompt inpainting also built for Wix partnership. All endpoints documented in Notion and ready. > **Gap:** Needs website integration for customer visibility and lead generation — Slack follow-up assigned. ## 🤝 Reseller Strategy Runway pushing daily for object removal endpoint access. Current handshake agreements lack structure and pricing discipline. Decision meeting tonight (Anthony, Amanda, Matt) to formalize the framework. > **Decision:** Deliver the endpoint but build proper commercial terms around it. Transparent communication with Runway while protecting BFL interests. ## 🛒 Amazon Load test: passed ✅. API performance significantly improved. Contract stuck on Amazon's side — service order sent 2 weeks ago, no redlines back. Aggressive SLA requirements received Friday (non-standard — won't become BFL standard). Training component still under negotiation. **Tomorrow's launch not happening** due to Amazon delays. SLA learnings will inform future enterprise deals. ## 📣 Marketing & Hiring Aitana joined as BFL's first dedicated marketing hire — seeking customer use case stories for website. Hugo Boss and Dutch Telecom already identified as candidates. New AE expected to sign within days. Owais newsletter content flagged as strong — should expand frequency + audience segmentation. ## Next Steps - [ ] LoRa website integration — Slack follow-up - [ ] Reseller strategy decision tonight (Anthony, Amanda, Matt) - [ ] Zalando legal call tomorrow 4 PM — Gigi joining for technical topics - [ ] Amazon: respond to SLA requirements + escalate training component - [ ] Customer story development with Aitana (Hugo Boss, Dutch Telecom) --- # **March 31, 2026** {toggle="true"} *(Summary)* *(Q1 closed — missed targets but strong foundation building for Q2. Major deals in motion across Amazon, Disney, Adobe, and Snap.)* ## 🏆 Team Recognition Gigi for exceptional Zalando demo and customer engagement. Stephan for enabling GTM to move faster on infra and teaching rather than just solving. Amanda for nailing the first GTM demo day presentation to Samsung. Sam for the Disney mega-proposal built in 2–3 days. Matt, Jakob, Ian, Alex for relentless work on Amazon. LD team for raw output volume and quality of customer feedback generated. ## 📊 Q1 Revenue & Pipeline ARR declined MoM: \~\$46M (Jan) → \~\$38M (Mar). Net new ARR: \$164K actual vs \$3M target — only 2 new logos (Runway, Forks). ByteDance collapsed \$6M → \$450K. License revenue flat since Aug 2025 — Chinese OS model competition increasing. > **Q2 churn incoming:** PhotoRoom (\$50K/mo) + Lightricks (\$80K/mo) turning off Flux 1 dev licenses. > **Root causes:** Team too small to cover existing accounts + inbound significantly lower post-Flux 1 era + Q1 deals (Amazon) slipped out of team's control. ## 🔥 Major Deal Updates **Amazon Alexa** — Beta ongoing; GA blocked by load test failures (timeout \>20s vs 20s threshold). SOF #5 pending legal review; sticking point: training on BFL data. Custom product photography endpoint delivering tomorrow. New opportunity: Amazon Kids (early conversations). Target: load test run Friday. **Disney** — Engagement across all BUs. 3-tier proposal sent: Tier 1 current dev models \~\$8M ACV; Tier 2 all dev models over 3yr \$18M→\$35M; Tier 3 Pro models on-prem (OpenAI-level partnership) — primary target. Robin met Disney head of BD in LA as first touchpoint. **Snap** — Actively reinventing pricing model with auto-encoders during live negotiations. **Adobe** — IP/legal complexity flagged: Adobe suggesting Flux derivatives via Foundry may not need "powered by Flux" branding — technically inaccurate. Mohan + Amanda working on a one-pager tying technical, legal, and commercial frameworks together. ## 👗 Virtual Try-On (Gigi) End-to-end LoRA solution built for Zalando: sub-1s, strong character + garment consistency. No competitor exists at this spec over API. Zalando: 5–20M daily page viewers — massive volume opportunity. Building public BFL shop demo for broader rollout. Next: explore public launch with a fashion brand partner (e.g. Freepik). ## 🏗️ Account Tiering Framework (Sam) New framework to protect SE time and maximize impact. P0 (e.g. Meta): 9-figure TCV, dedicated owners + founder sponsor. P1 (Adobe, Amazon, Snap): \$1M+ ARR / 8-figure TCV, dedicated SE + research POC. P2–P3: mid-range ARR, Slack channel + launch-time intensity. P4 long tail: reactivation only, no dedicated SE. SE engagement decisions based on use case impact × deal size. Note: SE co-creation can create IP/ownership complications — loop in Mohan or Amanda if in doubt. ## 🔓 Open Weights Initiative (Amanda) Launch delayed April 1 → \~April 6. New SKU structure: **Builder** (10K image limit, Klein models only, restricted use cases — automated flow replacing self-serve) + **Enterprise** (\$10K+/mo minimum, full model flexibility, SLA). Website updates, migration comms, and Builder flow all in progress. ## 🚀 FLUX 2.1 Launch Anticipated \~2 weeks from March 31. Improvements: better human rendering, less baking, easier prompting, better low-light, auto-resolution. Pricing still being worked out. GPT-4o image release adding urgency to evals. > **Request from Amanda:** Updated ELO scores + before/after examples needed for sales materials at launch. ## Next Steps - [ ] Amazon: Run load test Friday; resolve SOF #5 legal redlines; deliver product photography endpoint - [ ] Disney: Continue BU engagement; progress partnership proposal - [ ] Snap: Finalize pricing model and close - [ ] Virtual Try-On: Build public BFL shop demo; identify fashion brand for public launch; loop in Owais on marketing - [ ] Open Weights: Complete website updates, Builder SKU automation, migration comms by \~April 6 - [ ] FLUX 2.1: Resolve backend + pricing; prepare updated ELOs and sales materials - [ ] GTM: Begin Q2 vertical strategy — Media & Entertainment as first motion; outbound push into e-commerce/retail - [ ] Account framework: Publish tiering doc; align new AE hires on SE engagement rules # **March 24, 2026** {toggle="true"} ## 👋 New Team Member **Huachun j**oined as forward deployed ML engineer in SF ! ## 🏆 Team Recognition Ian: Amazon partnership setup and infra support. Gigi: major progress on try-on. Freddie: volunteered research support for Snap technical requirements. Isabella: hiring process improvements already visible. lex + Stephan: strong collaboration on Adobe Brand Brain — third Adobe project underway, new open source protocol for B2B marketing use case, endpoint delivered for POC testing. ## 🛠️ Infrastructure Update (Ian) GPU availability challenges: review deploys compete with prod — check utilization dashboard and use Kubernetes tools to monitor without waiting for full rollout. Simplified worker deployment system in development (template-based, automated logging, cleaner folder structure). DB querying limitations due to rapid growth — BigQuery too expensive, seeking alternatives. API architecture: Azure API cluster + separate worker clusters; long-term target is unified clusters to cut latency. ## 🤝 Amazon Alexa Load test delayed by 1 day (infra issues). Beta launch this week, GA 1 week after. Order form finalizing: 30% minimum commitment of max TPS, quarterly commits with 30-day notice for increases — risk-sharing model to protect against volume uncertainty. Technical: 20s timeout issue resolved (graceful error handling). Latency optimization ongoing, 2 PRs in progress. > **Key learning:** Educate customers on technical specs upfront. Product teams often lack deep knowledge — proactive guidance prevents model evaluation mistakes. ## 📊 Revenue & Pipeline March: \~\$500K shortfall expected. Gamma trending negative (capacity blocking testing). Client still not live. Upsides: ByteDance usage spike, TikTok US meeting Thursday; Samsung subsidiary (Shell) new lead identified. Adobe + resellers still on legacy endpoints — need marketing push + deprecation timeline clarity. > **Proposed:** Office hours for tier 1 strategic accounts to drive endpoint migration and prevent churn. ## ⚙️ Ops & Account Ownership Amber (RevOps) starts mid-April. [Excel-based account ownership audit in progress](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-nolfQ5Sr0P9wsEURJOCGFXZrz8TsQ76/edit?gid=1219653003#gid=1219653003) — moving from deal-level to account-level ownership. Sales team to review and claim accounts. Clean handoff planned for Amber. ## Next Steps - [ ] Finalize Amazon order form (minimum commitment structure) - [ ] Complete account ownership audit before Amber's start (mid-April) - [ ] Drive legacy endpoint migration — marketing push + deprecation timeline - [ ] Resolve fal / Klein 9B commercial use questions (OF requirement, LoRA rights, strategic stance) --- # **March 17, 2026** {toggle="true"} *(Summary)* ## 🏆 Team Recognition Alex delivered a strong Adobe demo in his 3rd week — challenging use cases, solid execution. Gigi's Zalando meeting went exceptionally well, partnership continuing with a case study in progress. Review cycles completed; open feedback from the team was noted as valuable. ## 🔥 Amazon Deal In intensive sprint mode — Matt, Jakob, Mohan, Adam, Dave running daily updates. Deal looking close to completion. ## 📊 Revenue & Pipeline March at \$443K ARR, 30% down vs February with 16 days in. Single biggest account holds the key to closing the gap to the \$43M ARR target — they're still on the old quantized model; switching them to client would hit the number exactly. Adobe traffic still on legacy endpoints. Canvas, FAT, Runway same. Kontext 9B KV cache launched with no meaningful traction yet. New adds in pipeline: Disney (strong interest), Coca-Cola HBCAG (Swiss subsidiary, using FLUX for global marketing image generation — reliability and scalability are their main concerns). > **Key watch:** One account switch = \$43M ARR target hit. This is a sprint priority. ## 🤝 Recruitment Israel now onboard as internal GTM recruiter (London-based). US pipeline improving — AE onsite candidates in motion, AE role progressing well. Ho Chin starts Monday in SF; Stephan buddying for onboarding. Currently planning 2 FTEs, evaluating demand for a third. ## 🛠️ Enterprise Playground Demo (Deutsche Telekom) Stephan demoed the custom enterprise playground. Stand-out moment: color correction feature that isolates and corrects only the Deutsche Telekom magenta hex across generated images — replacing an expensive internal tool DT currently uses. Client reaction: "jaws dropped." Feature is framed as white-label licensing, not custom development. 70-80% complete; base features ready within 2 weeks of contract signature. > **Key decision:** Pricing model set at €20K/month licensing fee + API consumption. ## Next Steps - [ ] Monitor Amazon deal sprint — target close - [ ] Stephan to finalize Enterprise PG base features (2-week target post-signature) --- # March 10, 2026 {toggle="true"} Agenda - Opens - 5 mins - Update on FLUX.2 Pro update launch + new launch (Seb) - Update on numbers (Seb) - Salesforce Ventures request (Matt ) - FDE named accounts (Jakob) - CEO engagement process (Anthony) - Freiburg presence sync (Summary) **👥 Present:** Anthony Charbonnier · Sebastian Bresser · Sam Thompson · Matt Smallwood · Jakob Pörschmann · Stephan Lachmann · Alexander Thebelt · Gigi Henze · Owais Khan ## 📊 Revenue & Launch Impact New model launches are not bringing new users — a recurring issue. Need to ensure launches land with more impact. Revenue remains highly volatile: generic API endpoints can be switched off easily by customers, whereas custom endpoints create much stronger stickiness. > **Key decision:** Shift focus and effort toward customer-specific endpoints. Make them more visible, publicly recognized, and a clear GTM priority. FDE team will take on significantly more custom endpoint work. ## ⚠️ Embedded Client Pricing Issue (Envato) (Seb) One embedded customer received an unexpected \~\$800K bill (expected it to be \~10x less). They responded by dropping FLUX Pro and moving to Max only. Seb is preparing a revised commercial offer to bring Pro back. Highlights the volatility risk of usage-based revenue without clear customer cost visibility. ## 🤝 Salesforce Outbound (Matt + Sam) Sam has been running a targeted outbound strategy for \~2 months with a prioritized account list. Proposal: align as a sales team on which accounts to route through Salesforce to maximize hit rate. Sam to sync with Matt on target account list and ensure outreach quality stays high. ## 🔧 FDE Named Accounts (Jakob) Jakob presented the FDE named account model — modeled after AWS's account manager + solutions architect pairing for large accounts. Engineering-side trust is key to long-term deal stickiness. Team to be more proactive in reaching out to customers (e.g., via dedicated Slack channels) rather than waiting for support requests. Snap deal cited as a cautionary example of reactive-only engagement. > **Key decision:** FDE team to proactively reach out to named accounts, introduce themselves as technical points of contact, and offer to co-build. Reactive-only posture to be avoided. ## 🛠️ Demo PG for Enterprise (Stephan) Demo deferred. Stephan to present next week. ## 👔 CEO Engagement Framework (Anthony) Draft framework shared for when to include Robin (or Andy) in customer meetings. Robin has been explicit: he wants to engage when it genuinely moves a deal, not as standard process. Framework covers: for whom, for what, and when. Kept deliberately light — no 2-page briefing doc. Andy can be looped in via the same process. > **Key decision:** Framework to be finalized based on team feedback this week, then validated with Robin next week. ## 🏢 Freiburg Presence Sync Goal to coordinate overlapping weeks in Freiburg for the European team. Simple coordination via Slack or a Notion page for date proposals. Separate from a broader GTM team offsite (still to be planned by Anthony over next couple of months). ## Next steps - [ ] Seb to finalize revised commercial offer for embedded client (bring back Pro) - [ ] Sam + Matt to align on Salesforce target account list - [ ] Jakob to formalize FDE named account proactive outreach approach - [ ] Stephan to present enterprise PG demo next week - [ ] Anthony to collect CEO engagement framework feedback and validate with Robin - [ ] Anthony to set up Freiburg presence coordination (Slack or Notion) --- # March 3, 2026 {toggle="true"} (Summary) ## Pipeline & Revenue API ARR trending down, March pipeline unlikely to close in-month. Runway and Mercado Libre signed but not yet ramping. Net new revenue urgency is high. Key deals active: Snap (\$3.99M renewal at risk from March 8), Amazon (launch March 24, SSO \~2 weeks), Disney (multi-studio proposal, dozens of millions), Adobe (\$4M closed weight deal + Brand Brain), Samsung (Fold 8 + foundational license), Microsoft (PowerPoint live, April GTM). ## FLUX.2 Pro — Speed Update FLUX.2 Pro now 2x faster. Endpoint change required — not automatic for existing customers. Targeted outreach list created. Matt coordinating reseller notification. > **Key decision:** Speed improvements do not trigger price changes. Communicate value, not infrastructure savings. ## Custom Endpoints () - Jakob Transparent background generation live with Gamma — first customer-specific endpoint operational. \~5s latency. Requires separate API key (sales engagement opportunity). Notion doc ready to share with customers. Enterprise Studio on the roadmap. ## Open Weights License Restructuring (doc ) - Amanda Moving from model-focused to workflow-focused tiers: **Builder / Platform / Professional / Enterprise**. Legal framework 95% complete. Eliminates previous self-serve confusion and gives reps a consistent starting point. > **Key decision:** Amanda to send pricing survey to finalize tier pricing before legal terms are locked. ## FLUX.3 Video Customer Research ( Andy's framework adopted for structured [customer interviews](/317c370222d581819b87f70eb21df4cf?pvs=25) on video use cases. Critical to distinguish use cases vs model capabilities. Always request visual input/output examples. Results posted in a dedicated Slack thread for data team visibility. ## Next steps - [ ] Customer research interviews to kick off — include FTE team members for technical depth - [ ] Amanda to send open weights pricing survey - [ ] Legal to finalize license terms immediately to avoid backlog for Open Weight --- --- # February 24, 2026 {toggle="true"} (Summary) **👥 Present:** Anthony Charbonnier · Can Ergin · Jakob Pörschmann · Ansh Gupta · Stephan Lachmann · Sebastian Bresser · Amanda Botha · Sam Thompson · Matt Smallwood · Sebastian Schröder · Mohan Nadig

Video here : [https://drive.google.com/file/d/1gUFhMhaHveEBScRUolMZITrtRok0SM9Z/view](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1gUFhMhaHveEBScRUolMZITrtRok0SM9Z/view) ## 📣 Model Launch Comms & Pricing New optimized models **(Klein 9B, FLUX.2 pro) **are dropping on . Agreed that incremental model updates (speed improvements, minor optimizations) get an email update only — no full launch treatment. On pricing: no price decreases for faster models. Adobe's Flex discount didn't move the needle on volume, so we're sticking with value-based pricing. Speed = more value, not lower cost. > 💡 **Key decision:** No price decreases for speed updates. Communicate value, not GPU savings. ## ⚖️ Open Weight Licensing & Pricing Sales is getting flooded with open weight license requests across all customer sizes. Sam and Amanda will deliver a first draft of a structured pricing framework (platform fee + per-model + per-image charges, tiered) in Notion by Thursday. Sebastian Bresser will share the legal terms (5 tiers, from simple to bespoke enterprise) on the same timeline. Goal: give every rep a consistent starting point. ## 🎯 Prioritization With reduced headcount , we're going into ruthless prioritization mode. De-prioritizing time-intensive, low-revenue enterprise prospects (Mercedes, BMW) for now. Focus shifts to scaling existing customers (e.g. Envato) and retention via QBRs. > ⚠️ **Qualification bar ? :** If an account doesn't project \$100K ARR, we qualify it out. 10-15% of team time to go toward automating operational work (discounts, pricing calculators) to free up capacity. ## 🐋 Whale Deal Updates ### Disney High interest across multiple groups. Preparing a company-wide agreement with 4 options (dev license through bespoke). +\$10M **3yr deal**, offer going out end of week. ### Adobe \~\$1.1B run rate customer. Two new opportunities: Adobe Brandin integration (April target) and closed weight models for Foundry (internal fine-tuning). Countered their proposal at **\$4M minimum**, could elevate to strategic partner status. ### Microsoft Flux launching in Foundry today. PowerPoint integration live for a small cohort, full rollout in \~1 month. Targeting **GTC week** for the announcement. ### Amazon (Ads + Alexa) Ads transitioning from dev license to API by early April. Alexa wants Flux in their chat interface with \~2.5M images/day potential. > 🚨 **Critical blocker:** SSO is required for both Amazon deals — needs to be a sprint priority. ## Next steps - [ ] **Sam + Amanda + Seb b** open weight pricing draft in Notion by Thursday --- "}

content: {"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"Head of Revenue","url":"https://www.notion.so/313c370222d580e9aefbeb22524aa031","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/313c370222d580e9aefbeb22524aa031 as of 2026-03-16T12:01:57.810Z: {"title":"Head of Revenue"} We're looking for a VP of GTM to build and lead the commercial function as we buildscale from strong early revenue traction into a true global enterprise business. We have real customers, real revenue, and real momentum, and we're looking for the right person who will take that foundation and build something exceptional on top of it. This is not a role for someone who wants to apply a standard SaaS sales playbook. We are defining the frontier of visual intelligence and rewriting playbooks on how to grow with our customers and partners. You'll own the full commercial arc: pipeline strategy, revenue execution, customer acquisition and growth, partnership strategy withacross the world's largest companiesa wide range of players, and run and manage the team that delivers all of it. You'll report directly to the CEO and work as a member of the leadership team with the access, context, and influence that comes with that to influence both the GTM motions and the company in general. --- **What You'll Own** *Revenue & Execution* - Own the revenue operating model across all sales- and partner-led channels, defining targets, forecasting, and the accountability frameworks that drive consistent execution - Drive both net new logo acquisition and expansion within existing accounts. ~~— ~~~~understanding that these are not typical hunter/farmer divides but require the same commercial acumen applied to different moments in the customer relationship~~ - ~~Manage a team that has close partnership to existing customers to catch inflection points in both directions: accounts ready to scale significantly as new capabilities land, and accounts that may be re-evaluating as their own product or the model landscape shifts~~ - Treat ongoing productPMF validation as a commercial function — feeding structured customer signal back into product and research, and using that loop to sharpen both the expansion motion and the net new pitch. In the visual AI space, PMF is both defined by competitive model releases but also unlocking new capabilities rather than just better solutions to existing problems - Manage the inherent forecasting complexity of an API-first, consumption-led business — where revenue is driven by usage rather than seat count, committed contract value is only part of the picture, and actual consumption can diverge significantly from expectation based on model releases, customer product cycles, or shifts in the competitive landscape - ~~Build and continuously refine forecasting processes that account for this volatility across both new and existing revenue — developing leading indicators, consumption signals, and customer engagement data as proxies for pipeline health where traditional SaaS metrics don't apply~~ *Team Building & Organisation Design* - BuildInherit a growingnascent commercial function with strong players and build it iinto a world-class global sales and partnership organisation. PutThis is a genuine greenfield opportunity for someone who wants to put yourtheir stamp on how a category-defining frontier AI labcompany goes to market. - ~~Identify, recruit, and develop the lieutenants who will run key functions and geographies. Build the GTM leadership layer that will define the quality and culture of the team at scale~~ - Design a deliveratethe organisational structure deliberately: establishing the right balance between direct sales, FDE solutions, ongoing customer relationships, and partner-led and managed revenue. Ensureing the team is structured to cover new business and existing accounts without sacrificing depth in either - Understand and actively influence product-led growth motions — the self-serve and developer-led pipeline is a meaningful part of the business, and the GTM organisation needs to work with it intelligently rather than around it - ~~Build a team capable of managing a genuinely global business, with the commercial fluency to operate effectively across North American and European markets without requiring separate playbooks for each~~ *Revenue Operations* - Own the operational infrastructure underpinning the commercial team: CRM, pipeline analytics, compensation design, and territory planning - Build forecasting frameworks suited to a consumption model. Recognising that standard SaaS tooling and methodology will need to be adapted or replaced, and that the forecasting process itself needs to evolve continuously as the business scales and the revenue mix shifts - Create visibility into consumption trends at the account level that allows the team to act proactively — identifying accounts building toward significant scale, accounts showing signs of reduced engagement, and the leading indicators that distinguish the two - Partner closely with Finance to ensure revenue recognition and forecasting align across the business, and that the commercial team's view of pipeline translates into reliable financial planning inputs *ICP Definition & Segmentation* - Work with research, product and marketing leadership to define and continually refine our ideal customer profile — the market for foundational image models is evolving fast, and new use cases, buyer profiles, and competitive dynamics emerge regularly - Build segment-specific approaches that reflect actual buying behavior across agrentic, developer, mid-market, and enterprise customers - Help the team stay oriented around the right customers as the landscape shifts *Enterprise & Strategic Customer Engagement* - Lead executive-level relationships with our largest and most strategic customers, acting as a genuine partner to their technology and product leadership - Understand customer roadmaps deeply enough to surface where FLUX creates compounding value — not as a point vendor but as long-term infrastructure partner - Manage the complexity of accounts where consumption can shift rapidly based on model releases or changes in the customer's own product direction *Partnerships* - Define and evolve a partnership strategy that spans the full ecosystem: resellers and distributors, inference providers, creative platforms, and other strategic integrations - Recognise that each partnership type requires a different commercial and operational model. An inference provider relationship looks nothing like a creative platform integration or a consulting resale arrangement, and the team needs to be able to manage that complexity - Build frameworks from first principles in a space where standard playbooks don't yet exist, and iterate as the ecosystem matures - Ensure partnerships are structured to deliver pipeline and revenue, not just brand presence or distribution reach *GTM Collaboration* - Work in close partnership with Product and Marketing — a relationship that looks fundamentally different at a foundational model company than in SaaS - Product decisions have deep technical and research dimensions; the VP of GTM needs to be embedded in the capability development cycle, not a downstream consumer of release notes - Marketing sits close to the developer and research community; commercial and marketing motions need to be tightly coordinated around model moments, not just pipeline stages - Each model release changes what's possible for customers, which changes the commercial conversation, the GTM team needs to move with that, not behind it --- **What We're Looking For** - Proven experience building and leading commercial teams through meaningful scale, with a track record of defining the motion, not just executing a predefined one - Demonstrated ability to identify and develop sales leadership. Building the layer of people beneath you who can run geographies, functions, and customer segments with genuine autonomy - Genuine understanding of the developer and creative infrastructure space. able to speak credibly with technical buyers and understand how models are evaluated, procured, and integrated - Experience operating across North American and European team, with an appreciation for the structural and cultural differences in not just how enterprise deals get done in each but how teams need to be run across continents/ - Familiarity with API-led or consumption-based commercial models, and the forecasting, compensation, and operational challenges that come with them. On top of enterprise driven motions, capability of scaling an organic growth from long taile customers will be key. - Able to engage authentically with a research-led product organisation — not as a translator between technical and commercial, but as someone who genuinely finds the technical work interesting and can participate meaningfully in conversations about capability, differentiation, and where the model is heading. Understands that in a foundational model company the product roadmap is partly a commercial input, not just a commercial output and brings customer and market perspective into those conversations with the same rigour they'd bring to a pipeline review - Leads with high standards and low ego. Able to attract strong people, give them real ownership, and hold them accountable without creating the internal friction that slows a scaling organisation down. Knows the difference between a team that hits a number and a team that builds something durable, and builds toward the latter even when near-term pressure points toward the former - A builder first. Process design, early hires, and getting the structure right matters more than inheriting a finished machine --- **What Makes This Role Unusual** - This is a rare opportunity to define how one of the most innovative companies in the current AI landscape builds its commercial function — the decisions made in the next 12-18 months will shape how BFL goes to market for years - Product-market fit isn't established once. It's actively re-established with each model release and each shift in what customers can do with visual intelligence - The expansion and net new motions require the same depth of commercial thinking applied to different customer moments, not separate teams with separate orientations - You'll be helping define the commercial surface area of the product, not just selling against a fixed one, while simultaneously executing against near-term revenue targets - The team you build spans direct sales, FDEs, and partner motions in a space that is evolving rapidly. Designing how those functions work together is as important as hiring well into each of them - Managing the tension between near-term execution and longer-term organisational and market development is a core part of the job - This represents a frontier approach in GTM. A new space that is evolving more rapidly than any before. It is an opportunity to redefine how GTM operates in a the fastest growing segment that has ever existed. Questions still to answer - *What does good look like? Do we look at someone who has managed a large team of direct sales folk or someone who has built a smaller function? What about their overall ownership of partners? Would a person with strong partner experience but less direct make sense?* - *How relevant is industry background? Do we need to have someone who has had a background of selling into creatives (eg sr sales at Figma, Adobe or Canva be relevant?)? What about someone who has sold to dev;s but not necessarily in a visual space (eg databases or tooling)* - *How do we rank skills of running teams which sell into a a large number of customers at a smaller deal size vs one who has experience with \$10m+ deals count? Does where they come from differ - eg selling large Oracle or Azure deployments given years of PMF vs someone who has needed to do something at a scrappy start-up* - *Where do they sit in overall US management? Are we looking for someone to be de facto country manager? * - *How do they sit in the broader company management framework? Do they influence or own marketing? How do we feel about the interaction with product - if there are inherent disagreements in direction on product vs sales-led GTM (eg focus on PLG vs SLG) how do we resolve and how do they sit hierarchically with Morgan?* - *How much do they have autonomy to reverse previous decisions? For example if they wanted to do a territory based hiring or disagreed with the FDE motion, how much authority do they have to do this and who would they need to ask permission from?* - What are the spikes we actually want this person to have and how do we rank them? For example: (1) exceptional enterprise closer and relationship builder, landed and grew \$10m+ accounts at technical infra company. Someone who has sold into technical buyers at companies building products on top of a model, not someone who has sold SaaS to a procurement team. The evaluation process for a foundational model is fundamentally different. (2) partner ecosystem specialist: someone who genuinely understands how to build and manage revenue through infrastructure-layer relationships, inference providers, hyperscalers, platform integrations. *(3) Org Builder: scaled teams, have leadership depth, can juggle moody sales team* - Are we looking for: - A revenue leader owns pipeline, sales, and partnerships. They're measured on ARR. Marketing is a peer function they collaborate with and influence but don't control. This is a VP Sales or CRO profile. - A full GTM leader owns revenue *and* marketing, brand, demand gen, developer relations, content, the lot… They're measured on both pipeline and market presence. This is closer to a CCO or President of GTM profile, and it's a materially harder search. Given we have no Marketing leader to navigate around, no existing structure to protect, and no political complexity in the handoff. The incoming person gets a clean slate to design how commercial and marketing functions relate to each other from the start "}

Enterprise/ABM ✗ No experience ✓✓✓ Core strength ✓✓ B2B product launches
Field Marketing ✗ Not her background ✓✓✓ Extensive ✓ Event/conference experience
Partnership Marketing ✗ Limited ✓✓✓ Distributor/channel experience ✓✓✓ Multi-stakeholder coordination
Product Marketing ✓✓ PMM at product-led companies ✓✓ Cross-functional ✓✓✓ Core role at Meta
**REVENUE STREAM FIT**
**Playground** (\$10M target, \$3M current) ✓✓✓ **PRIMARY** - PLG, viral, consumer acquisition ✗ Enterprise focus ✓✓ Performance optimization
**Open Weights** (\$25M target, \$20M current) ✓✓✓ **PRIMARY** - Community, creator, developer adoption ✗ Not her world ✓ Developer platform experience
**Standard API Self-Serve** (\$40M target, \$30M current) ✓✓✓ **PRIMARY** - PLG mechanics, activation ✓✓ Demand gen ✓✓✓ Performance/conversion focus
**Open Weights + FDE + Support** (\$20M) ✓✓ **SUPPORT** - Marketing air cover for consultative sales ✓✓✓ Solutions marketing ✓✓ Product solutions background
**Playground as a Service** (\$10M) ✓✓ **SUPPORT** - Case studies, content ✓✓✓ Enterprise solutions ✓✓ B2B product marketing
**Closed Weights** (\$10M) ✓ **SUPPORT** - Security/enterprise messaging ✓✓✓ Enterprise positioning ✓✓ Enterprise product launches
**Whale** (\$65M) ✗ No enterprise deal experience ✓✓✓ ABM/field programs ✓✓ Multi-stakeholder coordination
**Meta Licensing** (\$105M from \$35M) ✗ **NOT MARKETING** - BD/Legal ✗ **NOT MARKETING** - BD/Legal ✗ **NOT MARKETING** - BD/Legal (insider knowledge not applicable)
**Marketing-Addressable Revenue Potential** **\~\$52M** (Primary: \$42M + Support: \$10M) **\~\$65M** (Whale programs) **\~\$42M** (Performance optimization focus)
**WORKING STYLE**
Experimentation vs Playbooks ✓✓✓ Experimentation, fast testing ✓✓✓ Playbooks, repeatable systems ✓✓ Data-driven iteration
Hands-On vs Strategic ✓✓✓ Very hands-on, scrappy ✓✓ Builds teams/systems ✓✓ Mix of strategic + execution
Builder vs Scaler ✓✓✓ Builder (0→1 DNA) ✓✓✓ Scaler (process-oriented) ✓✓ Scaler with product sense
Creative vs Analytical ✓✓✓ Creative distribution, viral thinking ✓✓ Analytical, systematic ✓✓✓ Analytical, data-driven
**CULTURAL FIT**
Research/Developer-First Culture ✓✓✓ Product-led, technical fluency ✓ Enterprise-first mindset ✓✓ Platform/technical background
Startup Agility ✓✓✓ Thrives in ambiguity ✓✓ Process builder ✓ Scale-up experience
AI Creative Tools Market ✓✓✓ Native understanding ✗ Learning curve ✓✓ Adjacent (AI, not creative tools)
**BEST FOR BFL IF...** **You need PLG/community growth for product-led revenue streams** **You need enterprise marketing machinery for Whale deals** **You need performance optimization + partnership coordination**
**RISKS** • No enterprise ABM experience• Limited partnership marketing• Single market focus (creative tools) • Doesn't know AI creative space• May be overbuilt for current needs• Enterprise focus doesn't match revenue mix • Not a PLG/community builder• Meta knowledge less relevant for licensing• More tactical than strategic
**IDEAL COMPLEMENT** **+ Growth Engineer(s)** for conversion/activation infrastructure **+ Growth Marketer** for self-serve/PLG motion **+ Creative/Community Marketer** for top-of-funnel
## Bottom Line Recommendation: **Hire Marta + 1-2 Growth Engineers** **Why Marta wins:** 1. **Highest revenue addressability for marketing-driven streams**: \$52M (\$42M primary + \$10M support) 2. **Native market knowledge**: Only one with direct AI creative tools experience 3. **Right skill mix**: PLG + community + experimentation matches your actual needs 4. **Cultural fit**: Product-led, developer-first, research DNA alignment 5. **Stage fit**: 0→1 builder who scaled through hypergrowth (your exact transition) 6. **Complements Owais perfectly**: He does positioning/messaging, she does distribution/growth 7. **Maternity-ready**: Builds compounding systems (content, campaigns, community) not people-dependent processes **Why not Natalie:** - She's built for enterprise revenue (\$65M Whale) but that's a smaller opportunity than your PLG streams (\$52M) - Most of your revenue isn't marketing-addressable anyway (\$150M+ is BD/Sales/Licensing) - You'd be paying for ABM/field/enterprise infrastructure you don't need yet **Why not Iva:** - Her Meta insider knowledge doesn't apply to licensing deals - Her performance marketing strength overlaps with Growth Engineering needs - She's not a community/PLG builder, which is your actual gap //// BUT - **Playground/Studio is untested** (not proven \$3M→\$10M path) - **FDE is the priority** (consultative, high-touch solutions) - **Enterprise is actually driving revenue** (not pure PLG) - **But you don't want "boring enterprise marketing"** (no generic ABM/field programs) **We want ** - **Showcase-first marketing**: Demos, examples, "wow" moments that sell themselves - **Creator partnerships** but for B2B use cases - **Product-led enterprise**: Self-serve entry → high-touch expansion - **Technical content that's beautiful**: Developer docs that feel like brand experiences - **Use case storytelling**: Customer stories that show "what's possible" not "we help enterprises transform" If **FDE + Open Weights + Solutions** are driving revenue (consultative, enterprise-influenced), we need: ### Marketing that enables high-ACV, technical sales WITHOUT being boring: **Priority 1: Technical Solutions Marketing** - Showcase what's possible with FDE (example galleries, case studies with actual output) - Integration guides and reference architectures - "How we solved X for Y" content that's visually compelling - Demo environment that sales can customize per prospect **Priority 2: Developer Marketing → Enterprise Conversion** - Technical content that attracts developers who work at target enterprises - Open source examples, benchmarks, comparisons - Community that surfaces enterprise buyers (like Vercel, Hugging Face model) **Priority 3: Creative Brand that Sells Enterprise** - Visual excellence that differentiates from OpenAI/Google/Runway - Product launches that create buzz (not press releases, but "events") - Executive thought leadership that's actually interesting ## We DON'T need: - Pure PLG/growth marketer (Marta's core strength) - Demand gen for outbound motions - Traditional enterprise marketing (Natalie's strength) ### We DO need: **Technical Product Marketer with Creative Sensibility** Someone who can: 1. **Translate technical capability into compelling use cases** (FDE solutions marketing) 2. **Create showcase content** that makes complex tech feel magical (11Labs model) 3. **Enable sales without owning sales** (materials, demos, customer stories) 4. **Build developer → enterprise funnel** (technical content that attracts enterprise developers) 5. **Make enterprise buyers feel cool** (not corporate) ### Marta (Mirage → Captions): **Strengths reconsidered:** - ✅ Visual AI creative storytelling - ✅ Can make technical products feel exciting - ✅ Creator partnerships could work for B2B (game studios, production companies using FLUX) **New concerns:** - ❌ Her 90-day plan is consumer/creator-focused, not FDE-enablement - ❌ No solutions marketing or technical sales support experience - ❌ Playground/Studio focus when that's unproven ROI **Could work IF**: We redirect her from consumer creator marketing → B2B creative partnerships (agencies, studios, production companies as showcase customers) ### Natalie (Enterprise SaaS): **Strengths reconsidered:** - ✅ Solutions marketing for enterprise - ✅ Enables sales without boring corporate marketing - ✅ Multi-stakeholder technical products **Concerns remain:** - ❌ Doesn't know visual AI / creative space - ❌ Track record is more traditional B2B, not "cool enterprise" ### Iva (Meta → Aleph Alpha): **Strengths reconsidered:** - ✅ **B2B product marketing at scale** (Meta ads platform) - ✅ **Technical solutions** (retail, conversion data products) - ✅ **Developer → enterprise motion** (Meta's model) - ✅ **Currently at AI company** (Aleph Alpha = enterprise AI) **New appreciation:** - Meta ads platform = technical product sold to enterprises through self-serve → high-touch - Product marketing for conversion data = solutions marketing for technical use cases - Central Europe lead = multi-stakeholder, complex sales support **Reevaluated fit:** - ✅ Can do FDE solutions marketing (has technical product marketing background) - ✅ Understands developer → enterprise funnel (Meta's core motion) - ✅ Won't do boring enterprise marketing (came from product-led culture) - ❓ Unknown: Can she make it feel "cool" or will it be technical but corporate? ### Marta: 70% "Engine" fit, 20% Enterprise/Partner fit - **Nails:** Inbound, lifecycle, PLG infrastructure - **Weak:** Outbound, demand gen, enterprise, partners - **Would need:** Someone else to eventually own enterprise/partner marketing ### Natalie: 40% "Engine" fit, 80% Enterprise/Partner fit - **Nails:** Outbound, demand gen, enterprise, partners - **Weak:** PLG/growth infrastructure, inbound (in self-serve context) - **Would need:** Growth engineers to own PLG infrastructure ### Iva: 60% "Engine" fit, 60% Enterprise/Partner fit - **Covers:** Inbound (performance), lifecycle (funnels), enterprise (B2B product mktg), partners (platform experience) - **Weaker:** Pure PLG creativity, but has technical chops - **Most balanced** but not exceptional at either "}

title: How marketing is prioritizing
content:
{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"How marketing is prioritizing","url":"https://www.notion.so/30bc370222d580c6887afc9eec5bec26","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/30bc370222d580c6887afc9eec5bec26 as of 2026-03-04T11:40:28.293Z: {"title":"How marketing is prioritizing"} **Our focus for H1 2026 is to build quality awareness to increase model usage.** Win the position as the leader of building frontier models that are SOTA for quality and uniquely good for creative control at speed. We should be perceived as the “premium” brand that augments the human creator and honors the craft of making things — from movies and graphic design, to simulated worlds for robotics and games. We are anti-slop and anti-human replacement. We’ll measure this by increases in impressions, website visits, and models usage (via API or licensing) from current baselines. ---
Criterion Questions to ask Score (1–3)
**Goal alignment** Does it build awareness with frontier devs or pro creatives? Does the partner/channel have wide distribution or tight network effects? 1 = weak fit / 3 = strong fit
**Investment required** Can we run a lightweight test before committing? Does it match where our team has depth? 1 = high cost, unproven / 3 = low cost, testable
**Execution confidence** Do we have the experience and bandwidth to deliver a clean test? 1 = needs heavy external support / 3 = within team strengths
Any opportunity scoring 7–9 total: pursue. 4–6: deprioritize or redesign. 1–3: decline. # Prioritization framework ### Alignment with our goals Does it build awareness with frontier developers and professional creatives at scale? - Does the opportunity have wide distribution? Working with a partner like Krea has large distribution on social vs. a B2B enterprise company with very minimal reach. The difference between reaching hundreds of target users vs. thousands to millions. - Is a given community tightly networked and lead to a multiplier word-of-mouth effect that reaches thousands. eg community hosted events with 50 AI artists in SF leads to 100X reach via word-of-mouth or quality leads. - Weird cool ideas like a theater pop-up where people can stop by and watch a short AI film made by a creator in a cozy setting “BFL drive in theater”. Has potential to get shared heavily via word of mouth. --- ### Investment required Prioritize opportunities that allow us to test with lower spend instead of ones that require a large investment from day one. - We’d prioritize things like social, enterprise sales enablement, customer stories, working with a small group of influencers, supporting the community because they allow us to test raising awareness at scale quickly. - Investing \$100K in paid ads at this stage doesn’t make sense without having a destination product and a clear understanding of our customer acquisition cost + payback period --- ### Confidence level Are we confident in our ability to deliver a clean test given team’s experience and internal resourcing bandwidth. - Marketing/Growth team today has deeper experience in product/growth marketing, developer experience, brand, and supporting enterprise sales. We should lean into those strengths! Prioritize channels like social, brand campaigns, sales enablement, developer relations etc. - Channels like demand gen conferences/events, paid ads and SEO can be figured out, but would likely need the support of externals in a large way. --- ### Example scenario Nebius (one of BFL’s compute providers) has requested working on co-marketing and events with them for NVIDIA’s GTC conference. Their target audience is other research labs/researchers and their reach/distribution on social platforms is low (500 average views on YouTube). They don’t align with our goal of quality awareness with frontier developers and professional creatives at scale. So we’ll de-prioritize and turn down this opportunity. --- ### Other variables to think about - Do they fit with our brand values of SOTA models, augmenting humans, and leading with openness? Higgsfield is an anti-brand and we should avoid working with them. ### Exception cases - High-impact conferences where speaking gives us consistent credibility within the research community without paying large amounts for sponsorships or co-hosting. "}

{"title":"How to create review Deployments in Hoellental?"}
</properties>
<content>
If you want to change something of the pipeline of our Models, you will need to create your own Deployment. Luckily we have a very easy way on how to do that. 
### Step 1 
Change the Code in the Hoellental the way you need it
### Step 2 
Open a new PR (first-name/topic e.g. gianluca/size-adjustments). Push your local changes.
### Step 3 
Add Labels: Region (e.g. EU4) + Review 
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	This deployment may take between 15-20 mins
</callout>
### Step 4 
Call the API with the these two changes
```javascript
default: https://api.bfl.ai/
```
**How to adjust:** 
```javascript
https://review-[Your PR Number which can be found in PR-Url].[Region you chose as a label].bfl.ai
```
```javascript
example: https://review-3019.eu4.bfl.ai/
```
### Step 5 
Get a Review Deployment Key ([BFL Review Key](https://share.1password.com/s#jcvIJUtGe_lVg0wcVvZOYWV5ELmEJsPVdY4SgSae610) in 1Password if link doesn’t work) and make sure not to leak it (pls)
### Step 6 
Work with your new created endpoint just like you would with BFL
</content>
</page>"}

The Idea Modern diffusion transformers perform well, but they rely on full attention layers whose cost grows quadratically with sequence length. That becomes a problem as token counts rise with image resolution, video length, and world-model context. This project tests a
simple alternative: replace most attention layers with cheaper directional scan blocks, and keep only occasional attention layers for global mixing. The core hypothesis is that image tokens do not need full global attention at every layer. Vision data lives on a 2D grid with strong spatial structure, so structured row and column scans may be enough to move information across the image if they are combined with
periodic attention. If that works, we get a model that keeps much of the quality of a DiT while using a more scalable mixing mechanism. We already have early signs that this is plausible. In partial runs, several DeltaDiT variants are outperforming the DiT baseline at the same scale, although it is still unclear whether that gap will hold through a full 1M-step training run. The purpose of this
project is to turn that early signal into a clean result by measuring both absolute quality and FLOP-adjusted quality across a focused architecture sweep. # Why This Matters ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/d7efbebe-39c2-4070-9690-131a6e2494e3/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466TNFUTTVN%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T152058Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJHMEUCIFg7HfTQa1rgfUBIWH2kdaSgt0FJQTndiqVuthfnljElAiEAoT2rZPPU%2BQKvDOTE6dcCHh3B4YecrHZay%2F0HrCLo%2FyAq%2FwMICBAAGgw2Mzc0MjMxODM4MDUiDHnxyW43ii%2FLm19yMSrcA3VR%2F9mgr%2FhfeDzvgfym9%2FVEhRrCtQSQBfvwsnKPKytWncdtbR%2BHhL1FAUPK37%2FSjHwAn6XUmbDhMhcXMN%2BAAVLTtnz%2BC2SgmyuotcL3rteFNhRBvdVQeed7Dv%2BNKgdg%2B1gtk99fqwFTFSrriNGd4DYNcabsdAqF6YoYr3Z5ggiKmg9Jv8cNv1vab5Poy%2Bjo2BW0fjtu6mhcZxZ64S2IkSSaLNLDmxT7riusITuXvrLMEEOiFSwVCAQG98kJwjqIiQQJdj08LxPATjoEdGZVaqLsxJ0kb90MHzF4RCWnxav9SSW%2BQ%2BTu%2FSeLENQLyzgQNPoa%2BlC1qzaa0bt6yseIlQIehra1x8TYyDUai978qSV4rK5GoJ76NaJyokS2pfYAG5PlIu13pnqiJW3vWmhtjqBVRLynxt1dhk%2FaySR376bWJFO07y%2BcFMvbEGr9zML%2FK9%2FcQ%2BRe2ONWDvHAK3DBArypfznDXGa6vUrYZ4kFMCXycrfpqd7A5vK6V5hTV0zsBpMV84gwzZe%2Bj1VUmwL6RBQcWtTALbE%2FbLrDAXKSx9Z%2BeV7KL%2BEolSaHCifVKWNwTzVBBTy2w8U4ck4Jo0KbsqofgYoJVgCnrstmI1NvoIvwezJu0WfbyVMX89wsMKTOk88GOqUBSQn1EoqVZ%2Fnw52qdr3A37BiHusPePSqUya9Z836sbf9R4%2F5ipNa6IZ7qwOyiUlkN52WHxVmeDTkDY7emeXbeV0h5CrHzbags%2FlUlBgMpPj%2BLSPEhk%2B4M%2B1jWecqX8Z7M0%2B0sIlHj%2F2eE0lb9WHWBgu%2BMydMGfRLTwGUM7BqZQ4BXkhrTg5heQS9mIiAK1%2Bp2GBQqKtqdb1R2FxrBunNQuWf5iloN&X-Amz-Signature=b860ce6978a405bb030d980906ea03b6a09ea3b039d7c3f243cd932fa0add180&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) Quadratic attention is manageable for moderate image sizes, but it becomes a real bottleneck once token counts grow. That matters for higher-resolution image generation, and it matters even more for video and world models, where sequence length grows across both space
and time. In those settings, the choice of token mixer starts to determine what scale is even practical. This project is interesting because it is not just trying to make DiT cheaper in an ad hoc way. It is testing whether full attention is the wrong default primitive for visual generative models. If structured directional mixing can handle most of the local and medium-
range communication, then attention may only be needed intermittently as a global synchronization mechanism. That is a useful result even if it only holds partially. A clear compute-quality tradeoff would already be valuable for potential distillation targets, or consumer models. A stronger result would be showing that a hybrid scan-plus-attention architecture matches or beats a standard DiT while scaling more gracefully. # What We Would Build We start from an XL-sized DiT-style model and replace most transformer attention blocks with DeltaDiT directional scan blocks based on Gated DeltaNet. Attention is retained periodically so the model still has access to global mixing. The main comparison is between three classes of models. 1. Single-scan models use one directional pass per scan block and are the cheapest option, but they impose a strong directional bias. 2. Multi-scan models use multiple passes within each block, such as row, column, and
reversed orders, which improves symmetry and coverage but increases compute substantially. 3. The most promising idea here is a “4:1 scheduled variant”:** instead of making each scan block heavier, it**** alternates scan direction across depth**** and**** inserts attention
periodically**. **The goal is to ****recover the representational benefits of multi-directional mixing**** while staying *close to single-scan cost*.** This gives a clean ablation ladder. The fixed 1-scan, 2-scan, and 4-scan models tell us what we gain by adding more directional coverage within a block. The 4:1 scheduled model tells us whether distributing directional diversity across layers is a better use of
compute than packing multiple scans into every layer. # Experimental Plan The experiments compare a standard DiT baseline against several DeltaDiT variants on 256px ImageNet with matched XL-style capacity. We measure standard training behavior and downstream sample quality, but we also measure empirical forward-plus-backward FLOPs per token
and use that to track total training compute. That allows us to report both raw performance and compute-normalized performance. The central questions are straightforward. First, can DeltaDiT variants match or beat the DiT baseline in quality? Second, which scan strategy gives the best quality-compute tradeoff? Third, does the 4:1 scheduled architecture capture most of the benefit of richer
multi-scan models while staying near the cost of a single-scan model? Early systems results are already informative. The 4:1 architecture seems to beat or match the DiT baseline in FID, while retaining the best attributes of a single and 4 scan model variant. The remaining work is to determine whether these early pointers hold over the full length of training. # Why This Is Interesting If this works, it suggests a different way to build visual generative transformers: use structured sequential mixers for most layers and reserve attention for periodic global coordination. It creates a cleaner path to scaling. If the model can move away from relying on dense attention everywhere, then larger spatial and temporal contexts become more realistic without a proportional explosion in compute. That is exactly the regime that matters for
high-resolution generation, long video, and world models. The most important thing to prove out is not just that scans are cheaper. It is that there is a regime where directional scan blocks are a better allocation of compute than full attention at every layer. If that result holds, it would justify a broader shift in how we
design generative vision backbones. # Measuring Success **(NOTE! this is not an actual chart, just illustrating how an ideal outcome may look)** ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/8204aff4-9a03-4df0-ad10-a0259a7f0ec5/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466TNFUTTVN%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T152058Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJHMEUCIFg7HfTQa1rgfUBIWH2kdaSgt0FJQTndiqVuthfnljElAiEAoT2rZPPU%2BQKvDOTE6dcCHh3B4YecrHZay%2F0HrCLo%2FyAq%2FwMICBAAGgw2Mzc0MjMxODM4MDUiDHnxyW43ii%2FLm19yMSrcA3VR%2F9mgr%2FhfeDzvgfym9%2FVEhRrCtQSQBfvwsnKPKytWncdtbR%2BHhL1FAUPK37%2FSjHwAn6XUmbDhMhcXMN%2BAAVLTtnz%2BC2SgmyuotcL3rteFNhRBvdVQeed7Dv%2BNKgdg%2B1gtk99fqwFTFSrriNGd4DYNcabsdAqF6YoYr3Z5ggiKmg9Jv8cNv1vab5Poy%2Bjo2BW0fjtu6mhcZxZ64S2IkSSaLNLDmxT7riusITuXvrLMEEOiFSwVCAQG98kJwjqIiQQJdj08LxPATjoEdGZVaqLsxJ0kb90MHzF4RCWnxav9SSW%2BQ%2BTu%2FSeLENQLyzgQNPoa%2BlC1qzaa0bt6yseIlQIehra1x8TYyDUai978qSV4rK5GoJ76NaJyokS2pfYAG5PlIu13pnqiJW3vWmhtjqBVRLynxt1dhk%2FaySR376bWJFO07y%2BcFMvbEGr9zML%2FK9%2FcQ%2BRe2ONWDvHAK3DBArypfznDXGa6vUrYZ4kFMCXycrfpqd7A5vK6V5hTV0zsBpMV84gwzZe%2Bj1VUmwL6RBQcWtTALbE%2FbLrDAXKSx9Z%2BeV7KL%2BEolSaHCifVKWNwTzVBBTy2w8U4ck4Jo0KbsqofgYoJVgCnrstmI1NvoIvwezJu0WfbyVMX89wsMKTOk88GOqUBSQn1EoqVZ%2Fnw52qdr3A37BiHusPePSqUya9Z836sbf9R4%2F5ipNa6IZ7qwOyiUlkN52WHxVmeDTkDY7emeXbeV0h5CrHzbags%2FlUlBgMpPj%2BLSPEhk%2B4M%2B1jWecqX8Z7M0%2B0sIlHj%2F2eE0lb9WHWBgu%2BMydMGfRLTwGUM7BqZQ4BXkhrTg5heQS9mIiAK1%2Bp2GBQqKtqdb1R2FxrBunNQuWf5iloN&X-Amz-Signature=b010b1f3acf47e322d9f03454fc29c98f3e9a6cadbf355828b0fba0896e9c6de&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) Basic success - Show that one or more DeltaDiT variants match or exceed the DiT baseline on image generation quality. - Show that reducing attention-block frequency does not materially degrade performance. - Identify which scan pattern gives the best quality-compute tradeoff. Stronger success - Show that the 4:1 scheduled model outperforms heavier multi-scan alternatives on a FLOP-adjusted basis. - Show that the advantage persists over full training rather than only in early steps. - Establish a clear recipe for combining directional scan blocks and periodic attention in diffusion transformers. # Compute Needs Minimum: 32 GPUs
Ideal: 128 GPUs The main cost comes from running a clean architectural sweep with enough scale and duration to separate real effects from early-training noise. # Who Should Work On This This project fits a small team of 1 to 3 researchers with experience in diffusion models, efficient sequence modeling, and large-scale training. The work is part architecture design, part systems measurement, and part careful ablation. # References - DiT - Gated DeltaNet - Mamba and related state-space models - Vision Transformers "}

Write down here. Linking here the [customer/partner FAQs](/270c370222d580a8a921f19dfb3800ea?v=287c370222d580ad92ed000cb906fd28&p=291c370222d580b38987c1dffa971a4e&pm=s&pvs=25)
**Motion** **Description** **Example Customer** **Use Case** **Comment**
Direct
Distributor A company that makes money by selling access to our model (amongst other models). Possibly adds workflows on top. FAL, LMArena Allows for direct access to our model. Their customers either use them because credits they buy allow them to use other companies models or they add value with workflows. Often people will combine models - for example use us for an image and another technology for conversion of that to a video Often price sensitive as their margin is determined between what they buy from us and what they can charge to their end user
Tech partnership/marketplace A broader technology platform that offers multiple offerings - some own brand others 3rd party. Tends to manage a whole ecosystem and tries to keep customers within that ecosystem. Our models can often be bought via credits on their platform Azure, Adobe Firefly Expansion of the ecosystem - by offering the model they can keep users within their environment. May require hosting of the model themselves so they can profit from the inference. May offer discounts based on the amount of committed spend a customer has Often the tech partner will have sales teams incentivised to have customers spend/commit more on their platform. They will get commission on sales from our models and so a way to GTM is to partner with their sales teams to work out how we can make money for them, which will drive more sales for us
Embedded/OEM Where our model is hosted within another application and exposed to an end user as an option within that application - either explicitly or white labeled. The model itself is not sold directly but is used within the application Adobe Photoshop, Canva, Microsoft Powerpoint Adds incremental functionality into the application for users. Keeps them within the application.
Advertising Agency Will perform creative work for their clients/brands. This will include graphic design, branding, website design, copy/content writing, video, marketing and more. Make money through chargeable time, project based pricing and retainers None as of yet Will utilise models to help with pitches, ideation and eventual production material. Will possibly be operating on tight margins and tight deadlines so speed of ideation and cost efficiency will be high. Will be looking to ‘do more with AI’ given the changing trends but unlikely to be tied to a single model or supplier. Value capture vs value add can be hard as issuance of an image in a campaign could result in low fees for us but high charge to client. Still likely to be high use case given multiple ideation in the creative process or need to continually produce imagery. Make money outside of graphic design so this is just part of the services they offer. One to many client option could lead to different ways of pricing. May also want to be able to align costs (spend with us) to projects. Likely an FDE candidate for larger agencies as custom workflows, deep integration and bespoke features could well be where we can impart move value
Consultancy Accenture
- Direct distribution via resellers (FAL, LMArena, Replicate) - expand distribution of the model through popular creative sites. Leverage their marketing and pull to efficiently reach larger B2B and B2C audience - Tech partnerships (Azure, AWS) - MaaS allows us to expand our reach through Azure network, draw down of committed spend against our models - Embedded technology - (Adobe, Canva, Microsoft) - our model directly available in creative products such as Photoshop and Powerpoint - Agencies - use of Forward Deployed Engineers within creative/advertising agencies to maximise use of our models for delivery to clients - Consultancies (Accenture, CapGemini etc) - to be used as part of AI transformation within large organisations and embed models into workflows **Below is a view of initial customers** Initial view of customers (Claude research)

API-first platforms serving developers - Usage-based pricing models - Multi-tenant SaaS architectures - High-volume, low-latency requirements **Use Case for FLUX:** - Core product offering (primary revenue driver) - Real-time image generation at scale - Custom model hosting and optimization - White-label AI services **Key Value Drivers:** - **Performance:** Sub-second inference times critical - **Scale:** Handle millions of requests per day - **Reliability:** 99.9%+ uptime requirements - **Cost Efficiency:** Margin optimization essential --- ### 🎨 **Secondary ICP: Creative Software & Design Tools** **Customer Examples:** Canva, Gamma, Freepik, Snap Inc. **Company Characteristics:** - **Size:** 100-7,500 employees - **Revenue:** \$100M-\$2.7B - **Location:** Global (US, Europe, Australia) - **Stage:** Late-stage private or public - **Industry:** Creative Software, Social Media, Design Tools **Business Model:** - AI-powered content creation tools - Template and asset generation - User experience differentiation **Key Value Drivers:** - **Quality:** Professional-grade outputs - **Integration:** Easy API integration - **Customization:** Brand-specific capabilities - **User Experience:** Seamless creative workflows --- ### ⚡ **Tertiary ICP: Cloud Infrastructure & Enterprise** **Customer Examples:** Amazon Services, DataCrunch, Mistral AI **Company Characteristics:** - **Size:** 500-10,000+ employees - **Revenue:** \$500M-\$500B+ - **Location:** Global presence - **Stage:** Mature/Public companies - **Industry:** Cloud Computing, Enterprise Software **Business Model:** - Infrastructure as a Service - Enterprise licensing - Platform integrations - B2B focused **Use Case for FLUX:** - Managed AI services offering - Enterprise feature addition - Platform ecosystem expansion - White-label solutions **Key Value Drivers:** - **Enterprise Features:** Security, compliance, SLAs - **Scalability:** Global deployment capabilities - **Support:** Dedicated account management - **Integration:** Enterprise system compatibility Review of prosposects/inbound ## Sub-tasks - {"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"Inference optimisation - Hiring process","url":"https://www.notion.so/29bc370222d5809e9377c476d48b9269","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/29bc370222d5809e9377c476d48b9269 as of 2026-03-06T08:16:22.885Z: {"title":"Inference optimisation - Hiring process"} 1. 15 mins call with Tim 2. 45 mins non coding with Cheng This will be a QA style interview around training large transformer models on large GPU clusters. Things that we might talk about:
- Parallelization strategies such as DP (also HSDP / FSDP), TP, PP
- GPU compute hierarchies
- Efficient attention implementations 1. 45 mins coding with Tim  In this interview we will debug some Triton code together. If you are new to Triton, it might be helpful to take a look at the tutorials ([https://triton-lang.org/main/getting-started/tutorials/](https://triton-lang.org/main/getting-started/tutorials/)). That being said, I am happy to help you with the syntax. We mostly want to see that you understand the fundamentals of GPU compute hierarchies and are comfortable using them in practice. Specifically we will look at a part of FLUX1 inference ([https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux)), though it’s not required to review the architecture beforehand. 1. Onsite Inference/Optimisation Job Description "}
