{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"🔎 Legal Wiki","url":"https://www.notion.so/2c7c370222d580a59133c8e324b67b20","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/2c7c370222d580a59133c8e324b67b20 as of 2026-04-17T09:31:40.725Z: {"title":"Legal Wiki"} *Privileged & Confidential * ### **Commercial** Topics {toggle="true"} Fundamentally, there are 3 revenue sources for BFL *(simplified!)*: 1. **API Services Agreement **(We host the model and incur inference compute costs to provide an API that our customers use to integrate our models into their own products) 2. **Commercial License Agreement (”CLA”) **for our Open Weights models (our customers download the Open Weights-Versions of our models and then self-host (i.e. they incur inference compute costs) 3. **Playground** Customers purchase credits to use our Customer-facing interface called “Playground” (this is essentially a front-end to our API) *\[Additionally, there are various **bespoke agreements** with larger strategic customers and, if unavoidable, we sometimes enter into **Reseller** or **Evaluation** agreements.\] * 1. **GoogleForm:** Our GTM-team uses [this Form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeBRq2a78VNqxJF6W92E-fseetbUz39HXgRccbvfeYgoCKgvg/viewform) to generate new drafts for agreements. The questions in the Form give you a good sense of the main issues that are usually considered as part of the negotiation. The Form is meant to speed up drafting and to make it easier for non-legal team members to assess legal implications of certain contractual provisions. 2. **Overview**: The below decision-tree shows the logic behind the Form and illustrates which documents will be drafted based on the answers provided. EU and Non-EU documents were forked *\[we work with boutique law firm *[*Aitava*](https://www.aitava.com/en/)* for Germany/EU-specific questions\]*. Page 2 illustrates the flow from initial Customer contact to executed agreement and how the legal team interacts with GTM.

*\*You’ll note that this does not contain the option of binding CLA and API Services together in one agreement - this option is currently being drafted. * 3. **Negotiation** 1. If legal help is required for negotiation, GTM creates a ticket in . 2. If we need to clarify technical questions (e.g., certain cybersecurity requests from customers) we tap Workstreet’s knowledge bank through [https://black-forest-labs.slack.com/archives/C09J2DGC43T](https://black-forest-labs.slack.com/archives/C09J2DGC43T) to avoid asking internal team members repetitive questions. 3. You can leverage your [Legora Account](https://app.eu.legora.com/) to help review and draft clauses and we might automate the redlining process further with Legora playbooks. 4. We use DocuSign to execute agreements 5. An overview of all executed agreements can be found here: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1_EM_z6LHWPMwibWFDGbeZX2PFYaDSh-x/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117009868738180578161&rtpof=true&sd=true](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1_EM_z6LHWPMwibWFDGbeZX2PFYaDSh-x/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117009868738180578161&rtpof=true&sd=true) 4. **Template vs. Master Documents: **For each possible document, there is a “Template Version” and a “Master Version”. 1. The **Template Version** is a customer-ready, clean document that only contains placeholders that are filled based on the answers provided in the Form (see above). Any edits to these documents will immediately go live. 2. The **Master Version** serves as the internal legal team clause bank. It contains 1. fallback options for some clauses, 2. Document comments and edits in tracked changes, or 3. footnotes with additional information that might be relevant for negotiation. The Master Version is meant as a living document. If you learn anything new in a negotiation, read case law, learn about changes in law or if there is anything else that might come in handy for our commercial templates, please drop it in here as a comment, suggestion or footnote. 3. Links to documents (do** ****NOT**** **edit templates): 1. Commercial License Agreement: 1. Inc.: Order Form ([Template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EiqB-a2_AxPefCuvKR47SjoLPQv-LGOYZsXyZZlvcy8/edit?usp=drive_link), [Master](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19wqAzgoTsRW38lHTSQuzR5Kdjuy0tOnaAjyuZR2c8ew/edit?usp=drive_link)); CLA ([Template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uaqAxkXiEWDobKhLjOubIis07vPPoGQhsePzx7fiwns/edit?usp=drive_link), [Master](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1KE4Q4oSk-KJXuR_ZXROkMKcBpzhT5uDIo4K9poBbTOc/edit?usp=drive_link)) 2. GmbH: Order Form ([Template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1iE1_RyT3kAH_oumr9ozK8moJuuRcPbfE2Y7fSAux3Ck/edit?usp=drive_link), [Master](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OsuRj1j3dqiCC5L9dFR6AT0ZFW6Eya-sG257oRatIFE/edit?usp=drive_link)); CLA ([Template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1iE1_RyT3kAH_oumr9ozK8moJuuRcPbfE2Y7fSAux3Ck/edit?usp=drive_link), [Master](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uNDqNA5K_xtoVqkgkCVRHNokldke8sbeBXYRq5KS3Kw/edit?usp=drive_link)) 1. *\[Some sections of the GmbH CLA are currently under review in this working document: *[*20251120_Germany_GmbH_Dev_Agreement*](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Cdfgf9ZVs1Uw2HNyAr0k4Dry-r44uwPeEQHmVOeKnSQ/edit?tab=t.0)*\]* 2. API Services Agreement: 1. Inc.: Order Form ([Template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/18ObYfwN69R_XEDCGclksVDAFqENzcJfRIUs1c3egv6M/edit?usp=drive_link), [Master](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1lIWNyYzHo_Yc31GPVznzgwZmzBJjzNIpT8VoKb3PR-Q/edit?usp=drive_link)); API Services Agreement ([Template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GicU9C6DpJUX9vwXhkT4xxx3lqTSmNlJzX9Lak2nKAI/edit?usp=drive_link), [Master](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NfovCW_BJPew5wJpoIFRM9dcC1pA_VCtOLlgxA6Xu4k/edit?usp=drive_link)); Data Processing Addendum ([Template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OZf287iP8t7djis4N7CdJVc4gh0muNti0N9kQU6BzT8/edit?usp=drive_link), [Master](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X31KJ7RvQFOtLl2_Zaho_hb7atq-sEVNf7I3TYQxPdQ/edit?usp=drive_link)) 2. GmbH: Order Form ([Template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1D_GEXSh00Tu5KIjgj9QQMSwPWDjCiNuGW5CuUpVQBKc/edit?usp=drive_link), [Master](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Gfgc3QDbm1AoDNny2uUdkJOIjQWCFvJCEjNLoF1XuG4/edit?usp=drive_link)); API Services Agreement ([Template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1etMohHDgqhtOrbsLAuw6urlpzFs-QIxBBIS2ri99EoU/edit?usp=drive_link), [Master](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1di1uGYh7CawbXdtXMdnRbzbo8elQZcfz5cqiGiy5Mas/edit?usp=drive_link)); Data Processing Addendum ([Template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qFQMr0OtWzo-nbrbyYfrBZax-ijRPZVLBxkkuE_GcC4/edit?usp=drive_link), [Master](https://docs.google.com/document/d/17Vndwl8djMJZykQtRBIbBHurHZ_h9NDqC_mcXsoEnRI/edit?usp=drive_link)); Data Act Addendum ([Template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1l8wtobnJFhRiBBlR74JRj8Iya1kIaAYiGWGS1oao1AU/edit?usp=drive_link), [Master](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1w2_TiVAQB4NvDaDgKPLhijNHAbHnXKA--3OSkGx5qnc/edit?usp=drive_link)) 5. **Terms and Conditions** 1. Overview** ** b. EU Refresh 1. As part of an effort to make contracting with EU customers easier (see long-form agreements above) we are in the process of updating our publicly available Terms and Conditions and Policies to EU-ready-versions (also in light of GDPR / AI Act requirements): 1. Terms and Conditions (versions with further information can be found [here](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1z5_4K3i8GWBEoGiPGwOj0GyLBmIsC1Je?usp=drive_link)) 1. [BFL_Website and FLUX Terms of Service.docx](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xY6r3Me_Zty6cMk93LQiZ_wGV2pckiqG?rtpof=true&usp=drive_fs) 2. [BFL_FLUX API Service Terms.docx](https://docs.google.com/document/d/16btxSU--l0POfzv0jBJ9E77JXV8q-O6A?rtpof=true&usp=drive_fs) 3. [BFL_Developer Terms of Service.docx](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1C6XKW7xmO433OV1yhv7p0v3vvSUtilqq?rtpof=true&usp=drive_fs) 4. [BFL_Self-Hosted Commercial License Terms.docx](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19mjNOYVckd7zxuCJ_GkTjhSjS30Yo0jh?rtpof=true&usp=drive_fs) 2. Policies 1. [BFL_Usage Policy](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OVYfVO3MX6SgW5OZaj8nTxFqh0LHIwnQAfqum19yLgw?usp=drive_fs) 2. [BFL_Privacy Policy_WIP.docx](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-h5oymNVU53VQkPVhi-stZZwDEpSfNWz?rtpof=true&usp=drive_fs) ![]() ![]() ![]() ![]() ### GDPR / Privacy / Data Act Compliance {toggle="true"} 1. Terms & Conditions and Policy Refresh (see above) 1. Main topic currently under review: Usage of EU Data from Playground for training purposes, as part of our Privacy Policy (see also: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZNv3qJ1ZhkU1zhGS_gfkpiCkQm8BBs3B1pvEcA4RWu4/edit?tab=t.0](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZNv3qJ1ZhkU1zhGS_gfkpiCkQm8BBs3B1pvEcA4RWu4/edit?tab=t.0), [drive.google.com](https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1g6iRdLk2cDgM4KbgWJta9p1g9iU2q3qH) and [https://black-forest-labs.slack.com/archives/C087CHPV0ET/p1763114700444979](https://black-forest-labs.slack.com/archives/C087CHPV0ET/p1763114700444979)). An Opt-Out option for training is currently being implemented by Cyril+team (see [https://black-forest-labs.slack.com/archives/C087CHPV0ET/p1763114700444979](https://black-forest-labs.slack.com/archives/C087CHPV0ET/p1763114700444979)). 2. GDPR Self-Attestation 1. We use [Vanta](https://app.vanta.com/c/blackforestlabs.ai/documents?framework=gdpr) to track our GDPR compliance status 2. Daniel June (DPO) from Workstreet manages the tracking in the Vanta tool and sometimes helps with frameworks or with information available off-the-shelf through our ISO/SOCII compliance efforts. Below are topics that are currently work-in-progress and under review: 1. [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1066tMU62v6-WBk8NP8RGQIyDgrRvomyQXe6JdUo0y_s/edit?usp=drive_link](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1066tMU62v6-WBk8NP8RGQIyDgrRvomyQXe6JdUo0y_s/edit?usp=drive_link) 2. [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1JbJsiv0ueq2IgyOYxZEHlH_Nxo8SMK7E/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117009868738180578161&rtpof=true&sd=true](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1JbJsiv0ueq2IgyOYxZEHlH_Nxo8SMK7E/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117009868738180578161&rtpof=true&sd=true) 3. [https://docs.google.com/document/d/15wDv47rJhDaDYMasvH9_B7YNA-BvjxmZ/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117009868738180578161&rtpof=true&sd=true](https://docs.google.com/document/d/15wDv47rJhDaDYMasvH9_B7YNA-BvjxmZ/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117009868738180578161&rtpof=true&sd=true) 4. **Cookie Policy** (part of [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-h5oymNVU53VQkPVhi-stZZwDEpSfNWz/edit](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-h5oymNVU53VQkPVhi-stZZwDEpSfNWz/edit)), a Cookie Banner has already been implemented 5. There’s an outdated action plan that Latham&Watkins provided before GDPR efforts were integrated in Workstreet’s scope of work: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1JgMA3nB_rqwF_PT4X3CgT0xdkjcasEM6/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117009868738180578161&rtpof=true&sd=true](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1JgMA3nB_rqwF_PT4X3CgT0xdkjcasEM6/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117009868738180578161&rtpof=true&sd=true) 6. [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LSNqdIemUX0FZPv1Im4NhrmUNvPYeHd-/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117009868738180578161&rtpof=true&sd=true](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LSNqdIemUX0FZPv1Im4NhrmUNvPYeHd-/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117009868738180578161&rtpof=true&sd=true) 7. [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eaJDk-VZDGOaq5ru-xWiLAkJprX-yQIF/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117009868738180578161&rtpof=true&sd=true](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eaJDk-VZDGOaq5ru-xWiLAkJprX-yQIF/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117009868738180578161&rtpof=true&sd=true) 8. **Intra-Group Data Transfer Agreement **(incl. Addendum) [drive.google.com](https://drive.google.com/open?id=1MwgBfs1mQsdq6ICL2Jt-Kr7RmpUV39r_&usp=drive_fs) — already executed (Black Forest Labs Inc. and BFL GmbH) 9. **\[Black Forest Labs\] GDPR Policies**[drive.google.com](https://drive.google.com/open?id=1grus2BTuwQfdBZbefweEKMbVCDeWo5ts&usp=drive_fs) — Daniel’s working docs 3. EU Data Act 1. The Data Act could require us to enable deletion or export of the entire history in Playground (as we could be considered a cloud storage provider for the images stored there). This feature has been deployed by Cyril (but tbc if it needs to become more visible). 2. We’ve created a new EU Data Act Addendum (see above) to our long-form agreements in case it gets requested by customers ### Data Strategy {toggle="true"} 1. A while back, we started to draft a slide deck that could be used to start talks with rightsholders for data access: [https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1jA54avyj70GQpEppgmQvyGVy3t4Awj_twvOXxMX_tVk/edit?slide=id.g38c11631ef4_0_328#slide=id.g38c11631ef4_0_328](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1jA54avyj70GQpEppgmQvyGVy3t4Awj_twvOXxMX_tVk/edit?slide=id.g38c11631ef4_0_328#slide=id.g38c11631ef4_0_328) 2. We’re in the process of sourcing ### Takedown Requests {toggle="true"} 1. An overview of current Takedown Requests can be found here: [drive.google.com](https://drive.google.com/open?id=1BxvlzlT6Y_uPkDEb7QigelsC5acVBF1P&usp=drive_fs) 2. Templates for Takedown Requests can be found here: [drive.google.com](https://drive.google.com/open?id=1akP4wGzbL3TqmNko4EA0pC2Za9Osvp_f&usp=drive_fs) 3. We’re in the process of defining an escalation strategy in case takedown requests are not complied with (quite common). More strategic cases (e.g. google ranking above our own website) will likely enter Domain Arbitration with support of outside counsel. 4. [Takedown Requests vs. SEO discussion on slack ](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C07ECSTV3SA/1761298091.749819/1761298091.749819) **DMCA Registration Details ** ### Tools {toggle="true"} 1. [Legora](https://app.eu.legora.com/) (LegalTech tool with ability to research legal resources across multiple jurisdictions, draft or review documents, create tabular overviews of multiple documents). There’s also a Plug-In for Microsoft Word that allows you to use the tool directly in Word. 2. [Claude](https://claude.com/de-de/download) (includes “Ask BFL” functionality that you can use to scan our internal communication tools like Slack, Notion, Google if you’re looking for information) 3. Litera Compare (there seems to be a problem setting this up but we do have a license) 4. [Vanta](https://app.vanta.com/c/blackforestlabs.ai/getting-started) (the entire legal team is admin here) 5. [Attio](/2c5c370222d58065bc09d7cf85878c31?pvs=25) (CRM system) 6. [API Revenue Dashboard](https://api-dashboard.internal.bfl.ai/) 7. Margin Calculator (*work-in-progress!*) "}

		**One-line description:** Add LoRA inference to the API
		**Launch date:** April 1st

## What we're launching/what’s changed
**Product/Feature Description**
The API supports LoRA inference. It is able to load a pre-trained LoRA efficiently and serve generations using this LoRA.
## Why it matters
**Who cares**
Our current production models can’t solve all tasks. A lot of value reside in these tasks since most production models can’t solve them yet.
Various teams (FDE, product) have demonstrated the ability to solve some of these tasks by training dedicated LoRAs.
But until this release we can’t use these checkpoints in production, heavily limiting their reach.

<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**Our focus for H1 2026 is to build quality awareness to increase model usage.**
	We’ll measure this by increases in impressions, website visits, and models usage (via API or licensing) from current baselines.
</callout>
# Three goals for marketing in H1 2026:
<callout icon="1️⃣" color="green_bg">
	### Build **quality awareness** for BFL & FLUX 
	**Black Forest Labs as a frontier lab.**
	Core channels: Press, Podcasts, founder socials, Publish research, Website/Blog
	Content: Press articles, vision of “Why visual AI matters”, Research papers
	**FLUX models best for reliable creative control at speed.**
	Core channels: Socials, YouTube, influencers/community, co-marketing w/ partners
	Content: Customer stories, use cases, model launches, Website
</callout>
<callout icon="2️⃣" color="green_bg">
	### Drive usage** & retention** for our models
	Drive conversions and engagement for the API:
	Core channels: Dev focused websites, docs, YouTube, socials, email, sales enablement
	Content: API docs, sales enablement/ABM, Website
</callout>
<callout icon="3️⃣" color="green_bg">
	### Establish foundation of an **enterprise GTM **engine
	Core channels: Sales motion, emails to existing users, enterprise marketing
	Content: Customer Case Studies, sales enablement material on pitch, model battlecards, etc
</callout>
# Who are we building for?
<callout icon="/icons/card_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**Primary: the frontier developers building AI apps**
	The "highest expectation developer" builds visual apps and tools that creatives use directly (directors, creators, enterprises, agents). They need a solid API with special customization features (like LoRA training) that helps them fine-tune their apps while keeping costs low and speed high. Their main goal is creating AI applications that users actually stick with and keep coming back to, and they work at companies like Krea, Flora, Meta, Notion, Adobe, and Figma.
	![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/f6b13b84-9793-4d69-805e-9bbcf6811979/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466RC6POAOO%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T152125Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjED8aCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJHMEUCICAniNLYkDZKHVWJtpV8sS%2FCVOi7d0P1mqZfs2GoKjcDAiEAs9QJqp3jc5z0xoxTCu8U01W6xndYJuwzewb1taEpWskq%2FwMICBAAGgw2Mzc0MjMxODM4MDUiDL25%2BLVwXxMyO4mrGircA3Ni9rwPt1ctMQNTPzbePuOAC%2Fgr%2B32MVawHY%2BXyIGxM9NixHqDTTvC8sfmglTdD81WIWmRfFsD3%2FupyCc%2BQLlb2L%2Fj3JGPbaDE8NQ1bMkJ8%2BApJp4zTAVXBUj65z%2BHb0M7B5CLeLA6NNjUGgzNZFFVWWr3WQfwpdNU7AbkYfyglCFjgdEwEDE81qdqvaT%2FRtsIYhsqWsRYVKpJyxkGdUa3pn6fAbicvgYlnMM70H69esk20xSNhf6Ox61iGraHoh9l4oi4dizKtllPocOaU%2BGn10xBOfe3U5%2BahK4Px8rSrHeNVPf2HXJ4j%2B7vwSyLviJ33hpOaVzOm09La9yRo0nLG1FT7bzl776XrKCrFHB1flhCQbn69LJ7ltxEIJ6CQ2rU2pE%2FAPUkJiKWKFAjml5Ex4d84liLXml1zdGFg2K6f7LyhsRdNz9warwq4qSPx5jICwLFzeDygNBv%2BBT9pQSSejZUk4TxZdAuzJQZpDu%2FJ%2F2xA5cvE2qVfF9038QBOUySboHwid7qx0OFw%2FPoIbwIEaYqCd9Rg%2F82MONxWgPl1hkMTEI2dC5lbMjUeU1HNze%2FrRjNxkjhh3Yp7qcPxnQ6j65f%2FFoYseR4gZzqiEzGnmTUPO1eRsJU0B0AxMP%2FOk88GOqUBbFgN3U9RO6Og1o26WKtMb34nW2Sts1WlDdszy0Ylt%2FUI2%2BSkmSkyLdBs7IxHFAR4S8J1Q8VBtPrFc%2Fmmg%2Bv4CJoMJ%2Fva7E7xVNxBxaBtc%2F6xPkYTX0%2FUzTbKENTHlZAritVMhmGJ%2BWE%2FdypMpXZMzSjuq%2BmIbxgCt81czWBrVakH65LXCheIDbsT3BMm5DyDKU%2BRKSnFi2Up1XAYk0OkNYcdrcI0&X-Amz-Signature=76f4320437a7ad3d710a6e0c15e13784a62f6adf5169ce477020bc12aa64ca7b&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject)

<callout icon="/icons/card_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**Secondary: the advanced creative (developer+)**
	Should consistently choose FLUX models because they offer the best combination of creative control, speed, and quality. They fall into a few key groups: marketing teams (like those at BMW and Notion) creating brand ads and graphics, product designers using AI for prototyping ideas, and AI creators making visuals and videos for consumers (working at places like Disney or AI studios). They typically use professional tools like Adobe, Krea, or Flora at work. Advanced users work with tools like Comfy UI to fine-tune BFL models.
</callout>
**Who we’re not targeting right now: **Non-technical mass market (e.g. users of Canva, Lovable)
# What problems do they face?
<callout icon="/icons/star_red.svg" color="red_bg">
	**For the developer, it’s hard to build creative tools with AI features that users actually retain on.**
	Developers are still figuring out how to build creative AI tools with lasting user engagement. While tools like Gamma, Adobe Firefly, and Krea see high initial use, they're mostly used for one-off tasks like quick presentations or edits. The goal is to be essential for creating final, production-ready work with fast iteration.
</callout>
<callout icon="/icons/star_red.svg" color="red_bg">
	**For the creator, no model or tool has yet given them the quality, control, and speed they need to ship production ready content.**
	“It takes a lot of work to get it right if they’re being used for sequences where there needs to be a lot of consistency/control. It was over a month of work getting a video ad with Lewis Hamilton just right” — Perplexity Creative Director
</callout>
# How does BFL solve these problems?
<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	### **FLUX models are built for creative control. **
	FLUX models deliver consistent, high-fidelity output with reliable creative control. From character consistency across sequences to accurate text rendering and precise camera angles. You can edit and steer results in real-time, and iterate fast without losing quality. Plus, with open weights and LoRA training, you can own your entire pipeline and customize for your use case.
</callout>

# Three Core Narratives (WIP)
### Why does visual intelligence matter and the path to super intelligence. 
Visual intelligence is harder than language: language is an interface, while vision models reality itself: the geometry of objects, how they relate to each other, what happens when they interact, what stays the same over time and what changes. True intelligence requires understanding the physical world. When models learn to simulate reality (eg predicting what happens when objects collide, how shadows move, how scenes unfold) they develop the foundation for actual reasoning. 
Visual intelligence unlocks everything from content creation to generative UIs that render as fast as you think, to simulations that train robots and agents, to systems that can reason by running mental experiments about the physical world. 
Whoever builds the standard for visual intelligence defines the next platform, because it's the path from generation to reasoning to superintelligence. Black Forest is focused on* *building* the standard for visual intelligence. *The standard means high performance and quality, lean, open, fast, affordable, always available. Ridiculously easy to build on and get great results effortlessly.
**Core channels: **Podcasts, Press Coverage, Founder Writing/Blog, Awareness Campaigns

### Black Forest Labs has an insanely good developer experience
Anthropic and Vercel level developer experience that’s loved because it’s optimized for builders creating AI creative apps. BFL API uniquely good for customization, training LoRAs, latency/speed, cost, BFL Skills, Docs, FDEs for custom deployments.
**Core channels:** Developer Experience, Docs, support for agents like Claude Code, Hackathons, Prompt Guides, etc. 
# Core launches in H1 2026
- Major improvements and faster variants of core FLUX.2 image model (eg 4K generation, fast editing)
- API features (out-of-the box customization, latency improvements)
- Martin Scorsese commercial/campaign
- FLUX.3 (Video, Audio, and Image) launch. BFL becomes fully multimodal
## Hiring plan & Sarah thoughts  {toggle="true"}
	<empty-block/>
	We dont have a “destination product” and no PLG motion…
	## 1. No growth loops, everything is a funnel
	Every initiative is linear: spend money/effort → get impressions → hope people convert. **where is the compounding?** Where is the mechanism where a user of FLUX generates the next user of FLUX? Some concrete gaps:
	- **No viral/referral loop.** When a developer builds with FLUX, there's no systematic way that creates more FLUX developers. Think "Powered by FLUX" attribution in outputs, API response headers that credit the model, referral credits for API usage.
	- **No user-generated content loop.** The community is creating incredible FLUX content already, where's the infrastructure to capture that, amplify it, and turn it into acquisition? This should be a self-reinforcing engine, not just "social media 2x a week."
	- **No content loop from product usage.** Every image generated by FLUX is a potential marketing asset. Where's the gallery, the showcase, the share-to-social from playground?
	## 2. Pricing is unowned at bfl 
	for a company at \$100M ARR with usage based revenue, pricing and packaging is probably the single highest leverage growth initiative we could run
	- experimenting with reverse trials; Let developers hit the API with generous free credits, then convert based on experienced value rather than a paywall.
	- What's our expansion revenue playbook? How do you systematically move a developer from \$50/mo to \$500/mo to \$5K/mo? That's not in any initiative.
	- Where's usage-based pricing optimization? Even small changes to per-request pricing tiers can meaningfully shift revenue without any new user acquisition.
	## 3. Activation is under-defined
	We can "Optimize customer activation flow with customer.io" and some email lifecycle campaigns, but there's no clearly defined aha moment. what is the *specific action* that, once a developer takes it, predicts they'll retain at 30 days? Is it first successful API call? First LoRA trained? First production deployment? First 1,000 requests?
	Without that defined, our activation emails are guesswork. we are sending lifecycle campaigns without knowing what lifecycle milestone actually matters.
	## 4. Massive ToF bias
	Looking at our metrics table: 37M impressions, 550K website visitors, media coverage targets. 10K unique users retaining 30 days. We set the stats as reference point to test how hard they are to achieve. We are investing heavily in pouring water in the top while barely measuring or investing in the bucket itself. what we should be doing: 
	- Cohort retention analysis before spending on awareness. What do our 30/60/90 day retention curves actually look like by segment?
	- Activation rate optimization. What % of signups make their first API call? What % make 10 calls? This should be an initiative with a DRI, not a side project on customer.io.
	- Resurrection campaigns. we have \~8K unique users but presumably thousands of churned or dormant accounts. Reactivating existing users is 5-10x cheaper than acquiring new ones.
	## 5. No experimentation framework or growth engineering
	There's no initiative around building a culture of rapid experimentation. 
	- A growth engineering function yet to be build 
	- Weekly experiment velocity targets: how many tests are we running on onboarding, activation, conversion, retention?
	- A clear learning loop: hypothesis → test → measure → iterate
	The Scorsese campaign is a big, slow bet. important but we should pair that with 10-20 smaller, faster experiments running simultaneously.
	## 6. Developer experience as a growth channel, not support
	We talk about Anthropic/Vercel level developer experience as a theme. But the initiatives DB doesn't back it up with real investment. We don’t have initiatives around:
	- **Time-to-first-API-call optimisation: **what's the current time and how do you cut it in half?
	- **SDK quality and docs** as a top-of-funnel magnet 
	- **Template/starter projects** that show up in search and drive organic signups
	- **In-product growth hooks:** smart upsells when developers hit rate limits, usage dashboards that create urgency to upgrade
	## 7. Enterprise GTM has no PLG wedge
	Goal #3 is "establish foundation of an enterprise GTM engine" but<span discussion-urls="discussion://31bc3702-22d5-80f6-a095-001cd95d641d"> every initiative is sales-led (case studies, sales enablement, pitch decks</span>). the best enterprise deals start with a developer inside the company already using the product. Where's the bottom-up motion?
	- Track which companies have individual developers already on the API
	- Build internal sharing mechanics (team workspaces, usage reports that can be forwarded to a manager)
	- Create the "land" content that helps a developer inside an enterprise justify bringing BFL in
	We are building a brand marketing machine but we are not building a growth engine. 
	Brand gets us on the first conversation. PLG compounds it. Right now almost nothing in the our initiatives touches the product itself as a growth lever 
	next hires to push: **(1)** Define and instrument the activation metric, **(2)** Own pricing and run first packaging experiment, **(3)** Build one viral loop, even a simple one like shareable outputs with attribution.

content: {"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"Martin Scorsese launch date decision doc","url":"https://www.notion.so/32fc370222d58095b3fac9f27f6142ee","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/32fc370222d58095b3fac9f27f6142ee as of 2026-03-26T21:40:48.207Z: {"title":"Martin Scorsese launch date decision doc"} ## Context AI for visual creation is still early and there are raging debates on copyright violations (Seedream, Sora), what it means for jobs, human replacement, and more. Generative AI and visual intelligence have not yet been positioned as clearly beneficial to human creators (to be fair Runway has done a good job caring about movie creators). The video Martin Scorsese did with BFL shows how FLUX actually augments his workflow and gives him a new tool to bring more creations to life vs. replacing people. FLUX and BFL are known in the AI creative developer community, but we have less general awareness with the larger creative community, AI engineers, and the general public. We have the opportunity to make a positive impression on the general creative community and public by announcing that Martin Scorsese is an advisor to BFL + release a video of Martin Scorsese using FLUX for storyboarding. We’ve also invested time and \$100K+ in creating this video with Marty. ## Decision we need to make **Decide when to release the video and announcement to maximize quality awareness** with the general public (creatives, press, people interested in AI, tech twitter, etc) for Black Forest Labs as a premium brand used by creators with the highest standards. ## Variables that matter - Maximizing impact of something we’ve invested in - Building quality awareness as a premium brand - Downside of negative perception as “not shipping anything on models or product” - Content in the video becoming stale given it’s focused on image gen/storyboarding - Ideal messaging is “Martin Scorsese is now an advisor to Black Forest Labs” - Converting awareness into model usage (destination experience, etc) - Maximizing success of the future FLUX.3 launch - Marty’s involvement post video launch and after FLUX.3 ## Options #### Option 1: launch at the end of April. Launching earlier builds brand awareness before FLUX 3, so when the big model launch happens, we're not starting from scratch explaining who Black Forest Labs is. The FLUX 3 launch will be so focused on the model itself that it'll be hard to squeeze in brand-building at that point. Getting the Scorsese moment out early creates a "brand step ladder" that makes the FLUX 3 launch stronger. - To keep the launch momentum going ahead of FLUX.3 we can continue staggered content drops — first the vision of visual intelligence, then Marty video, then an earned media piece, then Robin’s “how we do research”, etc. - End of April gives us enough time to activate multiple channels including press, A16Z new media team, etc. - Downside is that we’re not launching any new model or product with this video. Sentiment from AI and technical creative community could be negative. - We’d have to mitigate this with continuing value for the community (FLUX 2.1 etc) - Understand that we’re using this campaign to broader general awareness (it’s not targeted at the community that already knows us). We have to live with some negative sentiment. #### Option 2: launch 2 weeks before the FLUX.3 launch. Launch the Marty Video very close to FLUX.3 as a major model launch a couple weeks later, avoiding the issue amongst the community (that already knows us) of Marty video being perceived as just a brand moment with no real release behind it. - This requires our content drops of “why visual intelligence” and “how we do research, etc. to do alot more work to build brand awareness and impressions ahead of FLUX.3 launch. - Being so close to the FLUX.3 launch (\~2 weeks) could cause press to miss the FLUX.3 launch and cover only the Marty video. - We’re dependent on knowing an exact launch date for FLUX.3. Might be possible by end of April after pre-training, and Marty video launch could get delayed into mid/end of may. #### Option 3: launch after FLUX.3 Connects Martin Scorsese to our video model. Feels like the worst option because the current video is focused on storyboarding images and could actually distract from the FLUX.3 multi-modality narrative. It would be much better to do more with Marty close to or after the FLUX.3 launch (eg another video, co-interview, etc). - If we thought it made sense, and we could not get anything out of Marty after FLUX.3, then saving the Marty video until after FLUX.3 could provide a major post FLUX.3 launch moment that drives more model usage. ## Decision Recommend going with Option 1 to launch the marty video at the end of April. We should be clear that we’re targeting the general public with the Marty video and building our brand awareness to make FLUX.3 successful. We need to invest in content drops before and after the Marty video to sustain momentum and brand building. We should expect negative sentiment from the community that knows us (Reddit, X, etc) and plan to mitigate. We should also be planning to mitigate negative perception of Marty using AI in a Hollywood that is quite resentful of AI. ## Likely outcomes and their probabilities - **65%** **likelihood**: Launch builds large brand awareness with total impressions as 10M+ in 2 weeks via social, press coverage, YouTube, etc. We see sustained increase in website traffic and maybe even new sales leads. We get negative feedback from the engaged community on Reddit, X, and Discord that we didn’t launch anything new with the marty video and have to manage or live with it. Second order impact: we’re known to more people, our follow on content drops see more engagement, and we maximize reach and awareness of FLUX.3 launch. - **35% likelihood**: launch builds large initial awareness but does not lead to sustained website visits or retention on our models given we don’t have a destination product. We get press coverage and our follow on content drops see more engagement. We get negative feedback from the engaged community on Reddit, X, and Discord that we didn’t launch anything new with the marty video and have to manage or live with it. Second order implication: places the onus on us to build a demo app experience that leads to sign ups and usage of our models (atleast as a demo) before the launch. "}

The BFL-specific clauses are on pages 122-124 of the EA Product Terms doc and start on page 89 for the MCA (when you export as PDF from the button at top right). Please be sure you’re using the “Present Day Terms” option when viewing/exporting. Let me know if this isn't what you were looking for.

4/2/2026 - [Today we're announcing 3 new world class MAI models, available in Foundry](https://microsoft.ai/news/today-were-announcing-3-new-world-class-mai-models-available-in-foundry/) **MAI-Image-2** has turbocharged image generation performance and speed on Copilot after debuting as a top 3 model family on the Arena.ai leaderboard. Users experience at least 2x faster generation times on Foundry and Copilot with similar quality, based on real-world production traffic data. Phased rollouts are also underway in Bing and PowerPoint. **MAI-Image-2** was created with photographers, designers, and visual storytellers that demand natural lighting, accurate skin tones and texture, and clear in-image text for diagrams, layouts, and graphics. Once again, speed and quality don’t come at higher costs – **MAI-Image-2** is offered at competitive price-to-performance. Customers are already embracing **MAI-Image-2 **for creative work. WPP, one of the world’s largest marketing and communications groups, is among the first enterprise partners building with **MAI-Image-2** at scale. “**MAI-Image-2** is a genuine game-changer. It’s a platform that not only responds to the intricate nuance of creative direction, but deeply respects the sheer craft involved in generating real-world, campaign-ready images,” said Rob Reilly, Global Chief Creative Officer, WPP. “WPP has some of the best creative talent in the world and **MAI-Image-2** is making them even better.”

### \| \[Internal Sync\] Bulleit (Katie) + Matt + Owais {toggle="true"} **Attendees:** - BFL: Matt, Owais - Bulleit: Katie ### **Microsoft PowerPoint Integration Launch Strategy** - Flux models now :slack: Slack Message {toggle="true"} Hey [@Nadine](slackUser://black-forest-labs.slack.com/U0A1NQX0S79) - Caught up with [@Owais](slackUser://black-forest-labs.slack.com/U0A6T0CGUKU) and [@Katie](slackUser://black-forest-labs.slack.com/U019P7EGL86) last week after we spoke with MSFT.Here's the thinking around GTM for Powerpoint at GTC: - **1. Skipping GTC as our launch moment: **Too much Nvidia noise, involving Nvidia into the story to get amplification via their channels is clunky. More importantly, teasing a preview at GTC would dilute the eventual GA announcement. - **2. Anchoring to Microsoft's PowerPoint GA rollout (currently planned for the week of April 8th) : **We announce when users can **actually access the feature**. GTC falls in the middle of Microsoft's rollout, the call to action would be unclear. Hitchhiking on Microsoft's comms gives us distribution and credibility. - **3. Model picker world. Flux as the default: **Right now customers would be unaware FLUX is powering the features. However, Microsoft is building a model picker that will be announced as part of this GA rollout. When this rolls out, customers can pick their model of choice. Our goal is to be the default pick. Will continue to push Microsoft on this. - **4. PR plan deferred pending Microsoft confirmation: **I'm working on getting clarity from MSFT on what will be included in their launch announcement around April 8th. Both teams are aligned on mentioning FLUX and Black Forest Labs. Our amplification strategy will depend on that. **Next step:** - Get alignment from Microsoft on their announcement plans. **On meetings with Microsoft Execs:** - That's a separate workstream. My counterparts are helping me understand who will be in attendance and then I'll make intros to find some available time. ### \| BFL / Powerpoint - GTM {toggle="true"} **Attendees:** - BFL: Matt, Owais - MSFT: - Matthew Hacker – Account Executive for BFL - Kostas Seleskerov – Group Product Manager, PowerPoint - Shilpi Gupta – Technical Program Manager, PowerPoint - Daniel Epstein – Technical Strategist (global team) - Davide Vanzo – HPC & AI Architect, GTC booth/content lead - Eric Van Aelstyn – Senior Product Marketing Manager, M365 Copilot - Lisa Svensson – Product Marketing, Microsoft 365 Consumer (PowerPoint PMM) ### **PowerPoint Integration Demo** - Three key experiences (all within agent mode): 1. Create presentation - contextual image generation based on slide content 2. Add image experience - generates relevant images without specific prompts 3. Edit image experience - multi-turn editing with natural language prompts - Agent mode is Microsoft’s new standard for PowerPoint creation/editing - Multiple prominent entry points planned - Zero query prompts feature “create presentation” and “create image” as hero prompts - Template picker includes branded templates for commercial users - Model picker coming soon - users will choose between available models - Works on both AI-generated and user-provided images ### **Current Availability & Rollout** - Currently live for Frontier audiences only - March rollout planned: - Gradual deployment starting at 10% across web, Windows, and Mac - Not a flip-switch launch - percentage-based rollout by market ### **Go-to-Market Plans** - Joint BFL + Microsoft narrative needed on Flux in PowerPoint and Agent Mode as the new default creation surface - Early focus on Frontier users as initial CTA during March rollout, then broader GA story once availability is high - GTC (March 16–19) discussed as a possible moment for: - Theater session at Microsoft’s booth (Davide coordinating) - Potential joint BFL/Microsoft presence and Nvidia tie-in if there’s a credible three-way story - Preference from both sides to time bigger public push to when most customers can actually use the feature, to avoid “too-early” announcement with no in-product experience - PR coordination to run through Eric (commercial), Lisa (consumer) and their PR teams, with alignment on: - Whether/when to call out Flux/BFL by name (especially once model picker ships) - How commercial vs consumer narratives differ ### **User Adoption & Use Cases** - Wide variety of users across industries - not niche, mainstream adoption - Highest usage among marketing teams, sales teams, and HR - Popular across commercial and consumer segments - Image generation already popular in Copilot chat surfaces - Document grounding (referencing other workspace files) in internal testing ### **Technical Capabilities & Limitations** - Contextual prompt formation based on slide content - Current limitations with Flux: - No transparency support (needed for icons) - Spelling errors in text-heavy infographics - Flux Pro now available - best model for typography - Faster models coming soon for near real-time editing ### **Next Steps** - Microsoft to provide demo videos via Teams channel - Joint go-to-market planning needed: - Align on public messaging timing - Consider GTC (March 16-19) announcement opportunity - PR coordination between teams required - In summary: There are two groups of tiers: online (hot, cool, and cold), and offline (archive). Cool/cold to hot is instant - moving a blob from the cool/cold tier to the hot tier is just a metadata operation. Since they're all online, there is no "rehydration" delay. When retrieving data from offline (archive) to online, that's when rehydration comes in, and could take up to 15 hours. You have the option of requesting a retrieval with high priority, which may complete in less than one hour. For costs, retrieving data from offline to online, there are early deletion plus data retrieval costs (e.g., standard and high priority). Intro and tell us about your role and the work you do at BFL?		 I lead infrastructure at Black Forest Labs. I joined about a year ago from a startup in the LLM serving and finetuning space which got acquired by AMD. At BFL, I'm responsible for our training infrastructure, API backend, and everything that takes our models from research to production at scale.

Black Forest Labs launched in August 2024. We're a small team, about 40 people split between our Freiburg office in Germany, on the edge of the Black Forest, and San Francisco. Our founding team is responsible for much of the original research that led to diffusion models. Many of them were behind the original Stable Diffusion models at Stability AI.

Since launch, our FLUX family of models has topped benchmarks for text-to-image and image-to-image editing quality. The FLUX family spans from open-weight models for on-premise deployments to high-performance models available via our API. Also these Pro Models are available direct from Azure Foundry. This gives customers flexibility to match their security, cost, and integration needs.
Working with a large cluster of GPUs is not the same as deploying general purpose compute infrastructure, walk us through some of your experiences as the team onboarded to Azure AI Infra cluster and how you scaled up to support training your Flux models? Timeline and journey slide You’re absolutely right. Working with large GPU clusters, bring about stresses the systems to its limits. From networking, to memory, to the compute layer. There are challenges in each of these areas. Azure has been our cloud partner since day 1. From H100s to being the first customer on the GB200 NVL72 cluster, Azure has supported throughout.

A case in point, with the GB200s especially, the rack topology and desnity becomes very important which is an anti-pattern to typical node levelVM allocation.

There was no existing playbook for rack-level allocation. We worked directly with Azure's CycleCloud team to develop a new allocation method they call scale_m1. Instead of requesting individual GPUs, we request complete racks.

The rack-level allocation and packing density was critical for maximizing performance on the NVL72 architecture.
What other considerations you had to make throughout the experience on Azure. Getting the infrastructure and related services right, is more than just the best GPUs. How has Azure’s AI infrastructure helped with your TTM goals. High level architecture slide, data pipeline flow and or other services used e.g. blob. Three things beyond the GPUs themselves: driver maturity, storage architecture, and monitoring.

**On drivers:** GB200 was brand new hardware. The entire Azure team plus NVIDIA worked together on providing new drivers, validation, and finding optimization best practices.

**On storage and networking:** Pre-training is intensive not just on GPUs but on storage and networking. We hit issues like partition thresholds and InfiniBand flapping. We've been working with Azure's Storage team to identify common hotpaths and implement pre-emptive load balancing for multi-node training runs.

**On monitoring, and resiliency: **It’s vital to have monitoring during training runs, especially production runs. Anything can go wrong when running month long training jobs, and figuring out the underlying problem, resolving it, and resuming the runs becomes very important.

One thing that people neglect is maintainence, it’s no secret that GPU servers might face hardware issues in their life-cycle, but with the rack density becoming so important for the NVL72, the removing of 1 node for maintenance, impacts the entire rack performance. Long story short, Azure’s over-allocation strategies allowed us to continue without impacting training speed.
How important to you was the orchestration experience of the large cluster?  Was there a benefit with Azure for the type of work you needed to do? Why did you choose Slurm as the job scheduler vs. some other solutions that we've seen customers use? Describe your experience with running Slurm on Azure with CycleCloud as the orchestration engine. Microsoft can show slide on different deployment options Orchestration was critical for GB200. We evaluated several options and chose to run Slurm on Azure CycleCloud.

The combination works well because Slurm is battle-tested for HPC workloads, and CycleCloud provides the cloud-native integration and understanding of Azure's infrastructure. The key was getting Slurm to understand GB200's rack topology.

Traditional slurm does not have native understanding of “racks”, and Cyclecloud worked with SchedMD to integrate block topology in slurm. Using that we were able to schedule jobs normally with slurm taking care of allocating over racks. Additionally, scaling of nodes happened in a rack-wise fashion using the scale_m1 technology.

We also worked closely with the Cyclecloud team, along with Davide, and Jesse, our dedicated Solutions engineers, to beef up the health agents to capture failures in the application layer too, making it much more reliable.

For a small team, this was much faster than building everything from scratch. We got the benefits of Slurm's mature scheduling plus Azure's infrastructure optimization.”
\[Matt to speak to the pace of silicon innovation these days, from A100s just a few years ago, to already talking about Vera Rubin\]
How has collaborating with Azure enabled you to swiftly access the latest NVIDIA GPUs? For instance, in what ways has being among the first to deploy the GB200 at a large scale boosted your performance and job throughput, and ultimately helped you stay at the leading edge of generative model training?		 BFL to share more about their journey with Flux and how its evolved over different versions I don’t think people really comprehend what a behemoth the GB200s are. 13.TB of HBM, with 576 TeraBYTES/s bandwidth, and double the FLOPs as the H100 gives massive improvement to training runs. Training in general (and this is true for both autoregressive models like LLMs and diffusion models), are compute bound, so with compute improvement, it shifts the training speed up quite a lot. Additionally, the extra HBM opens up the ability to “pack training of bigger models into lesser GPUs”, making it more efficient. Lastly, it allows to train with larger batch sizes, which generally helps with better model performance.


But with the bleeding edge, comes the teething problems, the GB200s are a very new technology, it differs from its predecessors not just due to more integrated rack layout, but also due to it being ARM based, having unified memory, the increased dependence of the NVLINK switches, etc. All this leads to dealing with new problems not present in older generations. Thankfully we have support from both Nvidia and Azure, to work on ironing out these issues.
For some of the Audience out there who are just starting out with AI infra for training, post training or inference workloads, what are your top 3 lessons learnt in this process? don’t save any of the gory details BFL top 3 lessons Three lessons from being first on GB200:

**First: Co-design with your cloud provider, don't just consume services.** When we faced issues with training run stability, we didn't file a support ticket. We sat down with Azure's CycleCloud team and co-developed tests to better capture errors before runs. We obsessed over collecting as much logs, and reporting, to share with Azure, to both understand the system better, and also accelerate them improving of the service. To Azure’s credit, the speed in improvement of the node health/resilience has been amazing. Treat your cloud provider as a true partner, you can get features built that solve your specific problems.

**Second: Budget time for immaturity on bleeding-edge hardware.** GB200 is incredibly powerful, but it was brand new. Drivers needed optimization. Documentation was sparse. We had to work closely with both Azure and NVIDIA teams to get everything production-ready. So if the compute speed up is 2x, factor in a cost for working through the kinks. This is not just in time, but also engineering manpower.

**Third: Optimize the entire system, not just GPU performance.** We initially obsessed over GPU metrics. But our most of our pain points came from networking, and storage. AI training is a system. You need to instrument the full pipeline, identify the true constraint, fix it, and repeat. The GPU is often not your bottleneck.

Based in Seattle) - New org - AI Catalyst Team, working with VCs and enterprise companies to find the right distribution points (e.g Fal, Replicate, A16Z, etc) - connection points. Need steady **working-team cadence** to avoid stalls; MSFT to help “connect the dots” across internal product orgs. - **Clipchamp**: Awareness gap on model access; MSFT to connect the dots so the team can **test BFL models internally**. - **Reseller motion**: Live \~1 month but **little enablement done** yet. Proposed times: Tue 9/30 (8–9am PT), Wed 10/1 (9–11am PT), Thu 10/2 (10–11am PT). ### \| Sumith Summary of Clipchamp Meeting {toggle="true"} - \~5 leadership crew of clipchamp came by the office, we had a kino session w/ [@Axel](slackUser://black-forest-labs.slack.com/U06QDSK6MED) with a lunch follow-up. takeaways: - overall they found kino compelling, they were quite excited for the control/speed parts of it - for an integration with clipchamp (both video / image) – the most important factors & blockers, in order of priority, are i) compliance / safety – getting through msft’s RAI, ii) cost to afford their scale / budget, iii) least is performance / quality / control as long as its way off. don’t need bleeding edge quality. - It would be easiest to get the integration done if the cost can already be justified in the \$30/mo copilot sku - Higher cost can also be done but will take longer, they are considering higher tier skus for copilot where it could be slotted in - (Ask on two separate occasions) ### **Additional **[**Context shared over Slack**](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C07FKH3C36Y/1758177708.103309/1758177708.103309)** ** **Sanjana🌴 **[Thursday at 1:34 AM](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C07FKH3C36Y/1758184480.783209/1758177708.103309) [@Sumith](slackUser://black-forest-labs.slack.com/U06PUJ0BT54) are they aware of our partnership with Foundry (so they can use image today on their own GPUs and pay us 11.2% of list price)? On video, we are contractually obligated to negotiate Foundry to also carry those models, and will hopefully arrive at a cost to them that they can stomach in the \$30/month copilot sku **Sumith **[Thursday at 10:47 AM](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C07FKH3C36Y/1758217661.254099/1758177708.103309) > Nice! How much used is Clipchamp? If it's having decent distribution we can work with them to become a launch partner for the video model I think they are native video editors / video experience across all of msft (shipped in device, video features in copilot etc). I would say distribution would be massive. > @Sumith [@Sanjana](slackUser://black-forest-labs.slack.com/U087P9SULFJ) yes they are! lets connect with their cpo on the best of getting this through, seems just as promising as Designer if not more due to their agility to move fast they have a feature where they automatically create videos by pulling stock assets, adding voiceovers and stitching them together etc. images could be nice addition there as well ### \| Flux in MSFT Discussion Follow-Up {toggle="true"} Deck Shared: :google_slides_logo_-2014-2020-:[https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1NIn4r_Yme0CtN_M66cfl-rezCRwAh5OSzmAIEzxcH-s/edit?slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167#slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1NIn4r_Yme0CtN_M66cfl-rezCRwAh5OSzmAIEzxcH-s/edit?slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167#slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167) - Includes PPT specific use-cases + benchmarks ### Summary - **MSFT is bullish** on Flux for **PowerPoint/Copilot** scenarios, across two goals: - **1) Product Improvement **- Primary Use cases: 1) presentation-level styling, 2) icon generation at scale, 3) agent-generated multi-slide presentations, 4) multi-turn edits - 2) **Latency & cost** (GPU constraints are real at MSFT scale) - **Momentum:** - MSFT seemed really excited and engaged (big smiles throughout meeting). Want to build the best quality product with Flux. - GPU access hiccup (had 500 GPUs that were reassigned to another team). However, building and** testing is unblocked**; will send prototypes this week. - Eager to setup a hackathon between teams to identify what’s possible. Want to this ASAP. - **Immediate Next Steps:** - This Week: - **MSFT Send prioritized scenario list** (PPT restyle, icons, infographics) - **MSFT to share prototype links**. - Work with Asha/Bella on Flux-2 launch in Foundry - Next 30 days: - Host a joint hackathon in Mountain View between teams (target ASAP) - Next Month: - Coordinate onsite late October in Mountain View while Andi is in SF --- ### **What Microsoft said (key signals)** {toggle="true"} - **Goal Prioritization:** - 1) **Quality that improves the product for customers **(PowerPoint/Copilot) - **Priority scenarios (seemed similar to announcements from **[**Gamma 3.0**](https://gamma.app/insights/introducing-gamma-3-0)**):** - **Presentation-level restyle**: Style all slides to a reference image. - **Per-slide icon packs**: Generate **N icons** aligned to bullets based on the content. - **Agent-generation: **Collaborating with an agent to generate a 10-20 slide deck at a time. - **Infographics/diagrams**: Multi-turn editing + text fidelity. → Very important use case for Microsoft that they hope Flux2 can solve. - 2) **Latency & cost** (GPU constraints are real at MSFT scale) - **Momentum:** - Copilot/PowerPoint teams are excited and engaged (big smiles throughout meeting) - Want to build the best quality product with Flux - GPU access hiccup (had 500 GPUs that were reassigned to another team) - However, building and** testing is unblocked**; will send prototypes this week. - Eager to setup a hackathon between teams to identify what’s possible. Want to this ASAP. - **Risks** - **Lack of GPUs:** Internally struggling to secure GPUs. Had 500 secured which were given to another team at the last minute. - **Flux-2 timing:** Risk / concern of shipping Flux-1 right before Flux-2 and having duplicate work. - **Evals:** Our evals vs MSFT Evals - Nidhi mentioned they ran evals and were impressed with our performance. - MSFT is happy to **auto-route to Flux** where evals show clear win on **quality and/or cost/latency**. If results are a tie, they won’t switch as it’s not worth the effort. Need to know when to route to us vs GPT. --- ### **What we shared** {toggle="true"} - **Highlights:** - Playground Demo of Kontext - PowerPoint Specific Examples (All sub-10s operations in demo conditions) - Context-aware image generation/editing from PPTX parsing (text content, color schemes, image content) → prompt sampling (LLM-nano) → Flux prompt → write-back. - Bounding-box and masking options for localized edits - Transparent background pipeline (green-screen trick) - Human-preference evals showing Flux Kontext Pro on-par SOTA with much lower latency. - **Flux-2 preview:** \~2 months out. Focusing on maximizing quality (multi-image editing, stronger world understanding, long text, multilingual text). - We’ll discussed future updates and coordinating launch with Foundry. ### \| Matt / Sanjana Microsoft re: Azure Issue {toggle="true"} ## **People** - **Azure compute:** AM **Matthew Hacker**; BD lead **Mike Gaal**; AI Infra **Nidhi Chappell**. - **MaaS/Product:** **Bella Valentini**, **Rajat Gupta**; PMs **Derek Johnson**, **John Nack**; Strategy **Nanditha Ram**. ## Summary - **(Dave) Azure credits:** Received; no outstanding billing issue. - **(Patrick/Tim) Stability:** Azure infra issues appear **resolved** for now. - Weekly (Monday) acct syncs with Matthew Hacker (AM) exist but often light or cancelled. - **Delivery vs. config:** - GB200 delivery dates slipped (May/Jun) but were accepted by BFL - The **rack/config** delivered didn’t match the “standard” BFL expected, however **not explicitly contracted**. - Early instability expected given **new chips**; BFL didn’t seek 100% credits—argued for **shared risk**. - **SLAs/claims:** - **Not centrally tracked** today. - Need a clear, written SLA map + claims process with MSFT AM. - **Strategic posture / optionality:** - Contract through **end of next year**; shorter than the 3-yr push → preserves **flexibility**. - Switching clouds for **training** is **months of work**; should be pre-planned if pursued. - **GCP** product integrations less viable near-term; **AWS** marketplace strong but listing often tied to AWS compute usage (exceptions exist; bandwidth constrained). - **Product integration (Copilot/Designer/PowerPoint):** - Blocked by **model confidence** + **infra perception** - Continued relationship mgmt needed. - **Ownership shift:** Sanjana plans to step back from weekly infra meetings after transition to Matt. - **MaaS (Model-as-a-Service):** - Deal signed; **unknown performance** post-sign (Sanjana hasn’t been engaged by MSFT sellers yet). - Need to clarify **seller incentives, routing, billing,** and enablement materials. - North-star example: **Anthropic × AWS** marketplace motion. - **Focus areas (near-term):** 1. **Microsoft in-product integration** (Copilot/Designer/PowerPoint) 2. **MaaS performance & scale** (seller motion, listings, regions, billing) 3. **Continued Infra stability** --- ## ### ** \| Microsoft / Clipchamp Prep** {toggle="true"} **Attendees:** , , **Draft Deck:** [https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1ZkvMb_qDBKwV9Xh4RarEo1uVUPXyQqdSNva1AtTVtWk/edit?slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167#slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1ZkvMb_qDBKwV9Xh4RarEo1uVUPXyQqdSNva1AtTVtWk/edit?slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167#slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167) **Context** - Clipchamp (Microsoft’s quick & easy video editor tool) team visiting SF office. - Purpose: Preview of our **video roadmap**, not a formal pitch/demo. - Current status: No integration into MSFT products yet. - Reality: We don’t want this meeting but can’t pass it up → keep it light, don’t overshare. --- ### **Key Points from Discussion** - **Positioning** - Emphasize: we’re working on **foundational models**. - Model is particularly strong for **ideation** (fast iteration, previews). - Our differentiator: workflow speed + professional-grade ideation (generate low-res previews in \<10s → select → upscale). - **Content Strategy** - No need for full company overview. - Use **“cherries” = cherry-picked best content/results**. - Clarify: “Flux Video” (placeholder name) in training now → TBD if this exact model is released. - **Depth / Guardrails** - Important to **decide how much to share** (roadmap vs. technical detail). - Microsoft is contractually entitled to analyze once released, but not guaranteed reseller deal unless financials agreed. - Guidance needed from Axel: how deep to go, what not to reveal. - **Storyline (suggested)** 1. We started with foundation models → image editing → now moving into video. 2. Goal: combine speed + professional workflow → unique differentiation vs. Runway, Sora. 3. Model structure: fast low-res previews → select → upscale. 4. Future potential: combine with kontext / image editing for richer workflows - **Meta** - We’ve often **overestimated MSFT teams’ technical depth** → keep explanations simple, anchor on outcomes. - Opportunity to reuse/adapt this deck for Adobe roadshow next week (likely higher integration potential). ### \| Context from Slack for Designer Team {toggle="true"} :slack: [Slack Link](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C07FKH3C36Y/1757916386.770019/1757916386.770019) **Resources Shared** [Prompting Guide - Image-to-Image - Black Forest Labs](https://docs.bfl.ai/guides/prompting_guide_kontext_i2i) [Prompting Guide - Text to Image - Quick Reference - Black Forest Labs](https://docs.bfl.ai/guides/prompting_summary) 📄** **[**FLUX.1 Kontext: Flow Matching for In-Context Image Generation and Editing in Latent Space**](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.15742) **Context** --- - Microsoft (via John Nack (9/15 is last day at Microsoft)) is running evals of **Flux Kontext** for image editing. - Their early results show mixed performance compared to competitors like **Qwen-Image** and **GPT-4o imagegen**. - Meeting with Microsoft scheduled for **Wednesday**; internal prep ongoing. --- ### **Key Points from Slack (shared by Sanjana)** - **Microsoft eval summary (John Nack via Derek’s team):** - Dataset: 100 prompts (face/product preservation + general edits). - Eval methods: - *Modification fidelity & visual quality* → BinaryEval (LLM-based). - *Preservation* → Segmentation Consistency, DINO similarity, AuraFace. - Results: - Flux Kontext **better than GPT-4o** at preserving non-edited regions. - **Worse than Qwen-Image** on prompt-following & modifications. - Missing real multi-turn (no conversation history support). Needs engineering work. - **Andi’s reaction:** - Need to **educate Microsoft** on our definition of “multiturn” (demo it). - Auto evals miss **image quality/artifacting**, where Flux is stronger. - Suggests **human eval** on Microsoft’s prompts if Flux \> Qwen. - Asked Sumith to confirm if Qwen vs Flux comparison already exists. - **Robin’s input:** - Suggest **deep dive into Microsoft’s actual prompts** (sampling settings may affect results). - Notes AuraFace was in BFL’s own tech report, so careful about contradicting. - **Jakob’s prep plan for Wednesday:** - Demo (PPT, contextual visualizations, transparent BG). - Editing live in PPT. - Benchmark slides (4o vs Flux Kontext Pro). - Add benchmarks vs Qwen using KontextBench + Microsoft’s eval setup. - Possibly share **eval scripts** so MSFT can run them themselves. --- ### **Implications for the Microsoft Relationship** - **Risk:** Microsoft’s evals currently favor Qwen over Flux. - **Opportunity:** Highlight Flux’s superior **quality/artifact handling** and **preservation**, plus human eval wins. - **Action Items:** - Run Qwen vs Flux benchmarks internally (Sumith). - Prepare clear **demo + benchmarks** for Wednesday. - Educate Microsoft on **multiturn editing definition**. - Ask for **Microsoft’s actual prompts** to rerun on Flux. - Package **eval scripts** for them (positions BFL as collaborative partner). ### \| Summary of Azure Issue for Matt {toggle="true"} ## **TL;DR** - **Severe instability + under-spec rack density** since early June led to major downtime and inefficiency. - **Credits/Relief secured:** \$1.8M (7/18), then **\$2.6M** (8/12) for June–mid-July **+ 100% discount on PAYGO GB200 through Sep 30** (RI charges still apply). - **Gaps:** Credits not yet visible in portal; mechanics/appearance unclear. No firm ETA to reach acceptable **rack density (≥16 nodes/rack)** or sustained stability. Open Questions: - Were credits applied? - Are we still having issues? - What is the status of the deployment? - Where can we track SLAs? - What’s the process for future claims? - Are we still meeting weekly? ## **Timeline & Key Events** - **Jun 27:** BFL escalates: delays, NCCL/NVLINK/networking errors; \<50% VMs usable for multi-node; requests compensation. - **Jun 30:** Azure AI Infra lead (Nidhi) engages; proposes **weekly call**; Nvidia’s Ian Buck available. - **Jul 18:** Microsoft offers **\$1.8M Azure credit**; asks about **returning \~1,500 H100s by 7/31** (planning). - **Jul 29:** Nidhi: **NVL72 unhealthy broadly** (not just BFL); owes better timeline. - **Jul 28 → Jul 28 email from Patrick:** BFL calculates **12.5% usable time in June**; billed ≈ **\$5.2M** (Jun–mid-Jul). Credit offered \~⅓ of cost; asks closer to **½**; details **rack density shortfall** and **median \~2h to node failure**; requests plan/commitment on density & reliability. - **Aug 11:** “Today’s cluster upgrade” expected to improve BFL-specific limits (e.g., full memory not usable). - **Aug 12:** Microsoft approves **\$2.6M credit** (June–mid-July) **+ 100% discount on PAYG GB200 usage through Sep 30**; BFL pays only RIs; on-demand GB200s free if MS requires on-demand usage. - **Aug 18:** BFL accepts moving forward with the June–mid-July credit. - **Aug 25:** BFL Finance (Dave) says **no credit visible in portal**; asks for **form/timing** (credit note vs. invoice deduction). **Mike**: Finance/billing (Matthew Beckett, Jordan Philipson) will walk through mechanics. ## **What’s actually broken (technical)** - **Usability:** Only **12.5% usable time in June**; frequent **node failures** (median \~2h to failure), unresponsive nodes. - **Density:** Racks far below **NVL72-like density**; averages around **\~9–10 nodes/rack** vs. target ≥16; efficiency losses confirmed by BFL tests and external validation. - **Stability:** CUDA/NCCL/NVLINK/network issues; large manual redeployments; multi-node training severely limited. ## **Commercial concessions to date** - **\$1.8M** credit (7/18) → superseded by - **\$2.6M** credit for **June–mid-July** (8/12). - **PAYG GB200 at 100% discount through Sep 30** (RIs still billable). - Promise to **guide SLA-bound credit requests** for future instability. ## **Open Items / Risks** - **Credit visibility & accounting:** Not showing in Azure portal yet; unclear **how/when** applied (credit memo vs. invoice deduction). - **Rack density & stability plan:** No **committed ETA** or milestone path to ≥16 nodes/rack and sustained stability. - **Cost leakage risk:** Even with PAYGO relief, **RI charges + inefficiency** could keep TCO elevated if density remains low. - **Relationship risk:** BFL flagged concern about **SOTA engineering support** and long-term partnership confidence. ## **Suggested next steps (owner → ask → outcome)** - **Finance (Dave) ↔ MS Billing (Beckett/Philipson):** Get a **written memo of credit application mechanics**, schedule of postings, and how it will reflect on specific subscription(s)/invoices. Confirm **dates and amounts**, and **evidence in portal**. - **Infra leads (Patrick/Tim) ↔ Nidhi/Kanchan:** Secure a **dated remediation plan** to reach **≥16 nodes/rack** (or agreed alternative) with **weekly milestones** (density, node failure MTBF, pass/fail gates). - **Cost tracking (BFL Finance):** Build a **variance tracker**: RI spend vs. expected, effective utilization, incremental cost due to sub-density. Tie to **make-good triggers**. - **SLA credits playbook:** Pre-agree **SLO/SLA thresholds** (e.g., uptime, node failure rate) that auto-trigger **credit amounts** without re-negotiation. - **H100 return audit:** Close the loop on **whether the 7/31 return** happened (or updated plan) and any downstream billing impacts.
