title: Sales × Partnerships — Definition & Account Ownership Framework
content:
{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"🚀 Sales × Partnerships — Definition & Account Ownership Framework","url":"https://www.notion.so/309c370222d5815bafbbe7d0159b95f5","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/309c370222d5815bafbbe7d0159b95f5 as of 2026-02-18T13:54:22.323Z: {"title":"Sales × Partnerships — Definition & Account Ownership Framework"} BFL \| February 2026 \| DRAFT FOR DISCUSSION --- New version based on feedback: Sales × Partnerships — Definition & Transition Plan (v2) ## Goals This framework defines clear responsibilities between Sales and Partnerships to enable both teams to collaborate effectively, scale independently, and avoid deal-level friction as we grow the GTM team in 2026. - Clear differentiation makes it easier to hire, scope roles, and distribute accounts - Both teams have strong opportunities and room to grow - Exceptions can be made based on capacity, relationships, or strategic importance - This is a living document — we review and adjust as the org evolves - This framework was developed collaboratively with the current GTM team and is intended to evolve as the team grows and new perspectives come in --- ## The Classification Principle > **Account ownership follows the motion, not the size.** > **Orchestration** (multiple integration points, investment, ecosystem positioning, co-selling) → **Partnerships** > **Execution** (procurement, contract, PO, renewal, forecast) → **Sales** > When both motions exist in one account, **Partnerships owns the account, Sales can own specific deals within it** ### The Test For any account, ask: *"Is the primary motion selling to them, or building something together?"* - **Mercedes-Benz** with 4 BUs each buying a license = **Sales** (multiple buyers, same execution motion) - **Amazon** with Ads licensing, Alexa integration, compute purchasing, and co-selling = **Partnerships** (orchestration across fundamentally different motions) - **Samsung** with on-device integration + investment component = **Partnerships** (deep technical + commercial complexity) - **Honor** with a \$200K dev license = **Sales** (uni-directional purchase, despite being a smartphone OEM from China) --- ## Partnerships Scope Partnerships recommends, negotiates, and builds long-term relationships that drive revenue growth, brand recognition, scalability, and strategic positioning. The key differentiator is the bi-directional or multi-dimensional nature of the relationship. ### Workstreams 1. **Strategic multi-product accounts** — Cross-BU coordination where BFL both buys and sells, or where deep product integration is required (Amazon, Microsoft, Adobe, Samsung) 2. **Inference providers / resellers / distribution** — Channel strategy, co-opetition management, potential direct migration (Fal, Replicate, Cloudflare, Runware, Together) 3. **Compute providers** — Azure, GCP, AWS, NVIDIA, Nebius. Strategic distribution + procurement 4. **Agencies / SIs / consultancies** — Accenture, Omnicom, WPP, Monks. Ecosystem enablement 5. **Data acquisition & licensing** — Shutterstock, Getty. Cost/investment category 6. **Deep product partnerships** — Co-releases, co-development, on-device (Krea, Samsung, 11Labs, Mistral). Beyond a custom API and/or license deal --- ## Sales Scope Sales owns pipeline generation, deal execution, forecasting, and revenue accountability for accounts where the primary motion is a commercial transaction — API licensing, dev licensing, or enterprise contracts. ### Workstreams 1. **API & dev licensing** — The core sales motion. Procurement-driven, contract-based, forecastable (Freepik, Photoroom, Picsart, Gamma, Envato, etc.) 2. **Big Tech licensing** — Where the deal is a license/API purchase, not a deeper integration (Snap, eBay, TikTok US, Canva) 3. **Enterprise accounts** — German and international enterprises with standard buying motions (Mercedes, Zalando, Deutsche Telekom, Siemens, Schwarz, Inditex) 4. **Deal execution within Partnerships accounts** — When a specific deal within a strategic account reaches procurement stage, Sales can own the close (e.g., Amazon Ads license, Microsoft PowerPoint deal) 5. **Photo/video/design platforms** — Uni-directional API customers (Lightricks, Leonardo, Photoroom, OpenArt, Higgsfield, etc.) --- ## Lead Qualification & Routing **Sales qualifies every inbound lead and account.** All new inbound requests — whether from the website, API signups, or referrals — are qualified by the Sales team first. Sales then routes the account according to this framework: - If the account fits the Partnerships motion (orchestration, multi-BU, ecosystem, reseller), Sales hands it to Partnerships with context - If it's an execution motion (licensing, API, procurement), Sales owns it - If unclear, Sales and Partnerships align in the weekly call This ensures nothing falls through the cracks, qualification is consistent, and Partnerships can focus on strategic work rather than inbound triage. --- ## How Sales & Partnerships Collaborate on Accounts The framework creates three collaboration models depending on the account type: ### Model 1: Partnerships-Led, Sales Supports *Applies to: Amazon, Microsoft, Adobe, Samsung, Apple* Partnerships owns the overall account relationship and strategy. When a specific deal within the account moves to procurement and execution (e.g., Amazon Ads license, Microsoft PowerPoint integration deal), Sales can take over that deal — owning the close, the forecast, and the quota credit. Partnerships stays involved on the strategic layer (e.g., how the Ads deal connects to the broader Amazon compute and co-selling relationship). For Microsoft specifically, Sales can lead and close individual product deals (PowerPoint/Designer, Foundry) while Matt orchestrates the overall MSFT relationship and cross-BU strategy. ### Model 2: Sales-Led, Partnerships Influences *Applies to: Freepik, Canva, Snap, Photoroom, enterprise accounts, etc.* Sales owns the account end-to-end. If a Partnerships angle emerges (e.g., a Canva deal evolves into a deeper product collaboration), Sales flags it and Partnerships provides support — but ownership stays with Sales unless the motion fundamentally changes. ### Model 3: Founder-Led Accounts *Applies to: Meta, and potentially other founder-led relationships* Founders own the C-level relationship. Sales or Partnerships own specific deal execution underneath. Clear swim lanes: founders handle executive alignment, the assigned team member handles day-to-day deal work. --- ## Whales Initiative Matt leads the Whales initiative with a \$65M target for 2026. This initiative identifies, qualifies, and builds relationships with the largest potential accounts. **How Whales fits this framework:** - Matt sources, identifies, and orchestrates whale accounts — building the strategic relationships and getting the right people in the room - When a whale deal reaches the execution stage (procurement, contract, PO), Sales owns the deal close, forecast, and quota - Matt receives sourced pipeline / influenced revenue credit for whales that convert to deals - This aligns with the overall framework: Partnerships orchestrates, Sales executes For whale accounts that are clearly Partnerships-motion accounts (e.g., a new hyperscaler or major platform integration), the deal may stay fully with Partnerships. The classification principle still applies — ownership follows the motion. --- ## Rules of Engagement 1. **One deal owner, always.** Every deal in the CRM has a single owner responsible for execution, forecast accuracy, and close. 2. **Account ownership follows the motion.** Orchestration = Partnerships. Execution = Sales. The test is the nature of the relationship, not the deal size. 3. **Sales qualifies and routes all inbound.** Every new lead is qualified by Sales and distributed according to this framework. 4. **Partnerships-led accounts can have Sales deal owners.** For strategic accounts (Amazon, Microsoft, etc.), Partnerships owns the relationship and strategy. Sales can own specific deals within the account for execution and quota. This creates productive tension between long-term positioning and revenue velocity. 5. **Head of GTM arbitrates conflicts.** When Sales revenue goals and Partnerships strategic goals conflict on a dual-owned account, head of GTM makes the call. 6. **No mid-deal ownership changes.** Current deals stay with their owner through close. Transitions happen after close or at natural breakpoints. 7. **Review trigger.** If a Partnerships account becomes purely transactional over time (or vice versa), flag it for reassignment in the pipeline call. This is a living framework. --- ## Account Map ### Partnerships Accounts
Account Owner Rationale
Amazon Partnerships (Matt) Multi-BU orchestration (Ads, Prime, Alexa+, compute, co-selling). Sales supports deal execution as team scales.
Microsoft Partnerships (Matt) Multi-product integration (PowerPoint/Designer, Foundry/MaaS, Azure). Deep product + distribution. Sales can lead and close individual product deals.
Adobe Partnerships (Amanda) Deep product integration (Foundry, Brand Brain). Bi-directional.
Samsung Partnerships (Amanda) On-device integration, investment component. Complex product partnership.
Apple Partnerships (Matt) Strategic licensing partnership. Founder relationship, complex negotiation.
Krea Partnerships (Amanda) Co-released FLUX.1 Krea. Product partnership. Review if becomes transactional.
Fal / Replicate / Inference Providers Partnerships (new hire) Reseller/distribution strategy. Long-term goal may be direct migration.
Cloudflare / Runware Partnerships (Amanda/new hire) Inference/distribution channel. Reseller agreements.
Agencies (Accenture, Omnicom, etc.) Partnerships (Amanda) SI/agency relationships. Ecosystem enablement.
### Founder-Led / TBD
Account Owner Rationale
Meta Founders (Robin/Andi) + Sales (Anthony) Founder relationship at C-level. Anthony owns deal execution (Playground UI).
LMArena TBD (currently Sam) Eval platform / ecosystem. Discuss with Sam re: Partnerships fit.
### Sales Accounts *Note: Seb currently owns a large share of Sales accounts simply because he was first around. As we hire additional AEs in 2026, these accounts will be distributed more evenly across the team.*
Account Owner Rationale
Freepik Sales (Seb) API licensing. Procurement-driven. Uni-directional.
Photoroom Sales (Seb) API licensing + dev license. Multiple deals, single buyer.
Canva Sales (Seb) Dev license expansion. Large but uni-directional purchase.
Gamma Sales (Seb) API licensing. Quantized model deal.
Picsart Sales (Seb) API licensing across multiple products. Single buyer.
Snap Sales (Sam) Licensing deal. Uni-directional.
Envato Sales (Anthony) API renewal. Procurement-driven execution.
Wix Sales (Anthony) API/dev license deal.
Deutsche Telekom Sales (Anthony) Enterprise licensing. German enterprise.
Bending Spoons Sales (Anthony) API customer, needs active ownership.
HeyGen Sales (Sam, post-close) API license. Matt finishes current deal, then transitions to Sam.
Mercado Libre, Shopify, NBCU, etc. Sales (Sam) API/licensing deals. Standard sales motion.
Siemens, VSCO, Schwarz Sales (TBD) Transitioning from legacy Partnerships. Enterprise licensing.
--- ## Looking Ahead This framework is designed to scale as we significantly grow the GTM team in 2026. A few considerations for the next phase: - **Revenue accountability:** With this clear split, the natural question is whether Partnerships should carry traditional revenue quota or be measured on strategic KPIs (pipeline sourced, integrations shipped, ecosystem coverage). This separation would enable Partnerships to focus on long-term impact without short-term quota pressure — worth discussing for Q2 planning. - **Hiring scopes:** New Sales AEs can be scoped to verticals or geos with clear account lists. Partnerships hires can be scoped to workstreams (resellers, agencies, strategic accounts). ### Strategic Account Teams (Proposal) For our top 5 strategic accounts (Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Apple, Adobe), we should introduce dedicated account teams: - **Account Lead (Partnerships)** — Relationship, strategy, cross-BU orchestration - **Deal Lead (Sales)** — Deal execution, forecast, close, quota - **Dedicated SE/FDE** — Technical support, integration, POCs (allocation TBD with SE/FDE leadership) **Cadence:** Customer check-ins (bi-weekly/monthly), monthly internal account reviews + founder updates to Andi, quarterly external QBRs with the customer, quarterly internal strategy deep-dives. --- *This is a draft for discussion. Prepared by Seb for review with Matt & Amanda, Sam & Anthony, Feb 2026.* "}

title: Sales × Partnerships — Definition & Transition Plan (v2)
content: {"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"🤝 Sales × Partnerships — Definition & Transition Plan (v2)","url":"https://www.notion.so/30bc370222d581799fe2cd8b15815783","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/30bc370222d581799fe2cd8b15815783 as of 2026-02-19T11:32:07.030Z: {"title":"Sales × Partnerships — Definition & Transition Plan (v2)"} BFL \| February 2026 \| Post first alignment with Matt & Amanda --- ## Executive Summary BFL is entering Q2 with two commercial functions operating without a clear separation of mandate. This doc defines what each function does, establishes rules for Q1 (no ownership changes, introduce routing and single-ownership principles), and sets a North Star for Q2+ where Sales owns all commercial execution and quota, and Partnerships becomes a focused function around ecosystem insights, strategic deal-making, and partner program management. The biggest open questions — who owns strategic accounts and carries quota on them, and how to handle resellers — are flagged explicitly and require a dedicated decision before Q2 launch. Anthony will align with Sanjana on next steps. ## Context This is the second version of the Sales × Partnerships framework, updated after discussion with Matt and Amanda on Feb 17. The first version established the classification principle and account map. This version incorporates their feedback and introduces a two-phase approach: a transition phase for Q1 (no changes to current ownership) and a North Star definition for Q2+ that more clearly separates the two functions. Key inputs from the discussion: - Amanda: Partnerships should be defined by its function (ecosystem insights, strategic deal-making, program management), not by which accounts it "owns." Partnerships teams in mature orgs are small, focused, and don't carry traditional revenue quota. - Matt: Adding multiple people to strategic accounts risks breaking the orchestration advantage we have today. Needs more time to see Amazon and Microsoft generate meaningful revenue before layering in expansion plays. - Shared: No account ownership changes in Q1. Strategic accounts need quota treatment — how quota is structured for these accounts needs to be defined. The sooner we define the target state, the better — hiring, comp, and process decisions compound. --- ## Phase 1: Q1 Transition (Now through end of Q1) No account ownership changes. Current structure stays as-is. The goal for this phase is alignment on definitions and rules, not reshuffling. ### What stays the same - All current deal owners keep their deals through close - Matt continues to lead Amazon, Microsoft, Apple; Amanda continues Adobe, Samsung, Krea, agencies - Sales team (Seb, Sam) continues on current accounts. Anthony is currently interim Head of GTM — his accounts will need to be distributed across the sales team as it grows, likely requiring an additional senior AE in EU - Inference providers / resellers stay with current ownership until the new Partnerships hire is in place ### What we introduce now - **Classification principle:** Account ownership follows the motion, not the size. Orchestration → Partnerships. Execution → Sales. - **One deal owner, always.** Every deal in the CRM has a single owner. - **Sales qualifies and routes all inbound.** Sales qualifies every new lead and routes to Partnerships if the motion fits. - **Weekly alignment in pipeline call** for any unclear account routing - **No mid-deal ownership changes.** Transitions happen after close or at natural breakpoints. - **Review trigger:** If an account's motion changes (partnerships account becomes transactional, or vice versa), flag it for reassignment. ### Account map (Q1 — current state) Partnerships accounts: Amazon (Matt), Microsoft (Matt), Apple (Matt), Adobe (Amanda), Samsung (Amanda), Krea (Amanda), inference providers (current ownership until new hire starts), Cloudflare/Runware (current ownership until new hire starts), agencies (Amanda) Founder-led: Meta (Robin/Andi + Anthony on execution), LMArena (TBD — discuss with Sam) Sales accounts: Freepik, Photoroom, Canva, Gamma, Picsart (Seb — to be distributed as team grows), Snap, Mercado Libre, Shopify, NBCU (Sam), Envato, Wix, Deutsche Telekom, Bending Spoons (Anthony — to be distributed as he focuses on Head of GTM), HeyGen (Sam post-close), Siemens/VSCO/Schwarz (TBD) --- ## Phase 2: North Star (Q2+ target state) This is where we want to get to. The shift is more fundamental: Partnerships becomes a distinct function with its own mandate. Sales owns all commercial execution and quota. ### Partnerships: What it becomes *This is Seb's interpretation of the discussion with Amanda and Matt. This section is up for the Partnerships team to define and refine — they know best what the function should look like.* Partnerships is a small, focused team that drives long-term strategic value. The team is organized around initiatives, not permanent account ownership. **Three pillars:** 1. **Ecosystem insights** — Owns the competitive and partner landscape. Brings market intelligence back to leadership. Understands where BFL sits in the ecosystem and where the opportunities are. 2. **Strategic deal-making** — Negotiates and structures complex, multi-dimensional partnerships. These are deals involving investment, co-development, deep product integration, or ecosystem positioning. Examples: Adobe Foundry, Samsung on-device, Amazon co-selling, Microsoft multi-product. *A tension point: how these deals are reflected in quota (Sales quota, shared credit, or separate treatment) needs to be resolved.* 3. **Program & partnership management** — Manages live partnerships post-launch. Ensures integrations ship, usage grows, and the relationship delivers value over time. As partnerships mature, this becomes program management at scale (developer platforms, reseller programs, etc.). **What Partnerships does NOT do in the North Star:** - Carry traditional quarterly revenue quota - Own deal execution, procurement, or forecasting - Manage transactional API/license customers **Partnerships KPIs (to be defined together with the Partnerships team):** Starting point for discussion — Partnerships should propose what they believe the right metrics are. Some initial ideas: - Pipeline sourced / influenced revenue (with clear definitions of "sourced" vs "influenced") - Integrations shipped and live - Revenue from partner-sourced channels (tracked, not quota'd — noting that for some channels like inference providers, the long-term goal may actually reduce this number) ### Sales: What it becomes Sales owns all commercial execution, pipeline generation, forecasting, and revenue accountability. Sales is organized around verticals or geos with clear account lists. **Sales owns:** - All deal execution, including deals within strategic accounts - Quota for all forecastable revenue (API licensing, dev licensing, enterprise contracts) - Inbound lead qualification and routing - Account management for all non-strategic accounts (see strategic accounts section below for the open question on where those sit) - Expansion within existing accounts (upsell, cross-sell, renewal) **How Sales works with Partnerships on strategic accounts:** Sales carries the quota on strategic accounts. This creates a tension point: having quota on an account you don't own doesn't make much sense. This reinforces the need to define account ownership for strategic accounts (see open question below). Regardless of where ownership lands, Partnerships provides the orchestration layer — relationship context, timing sensitivities, cross-BU strategy, and strategic priorities. On strategic accounts, the account owner checks with Partnerships before making major moves. If there's a conflict between short-term revenue and long-term strategic positioning, it escalates to Head of GTM. ### Strategic accounts: Ownership & structure (open question) *This is the biggest open question in the framework and needs dedicated discussion. Getting this right matters more than getting it fast.* The top strategic accounts (Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Apple, Adobe) are the most complex, highest-value relationships we have. They require both orchestration (Partnerships) and execution (Sales). The question is: who owns them? The logic of this framework points toward Sales ownership — if Sales carries the quota on these accounts, Sales should own them. Splitting ownership from quota accountability creates confusion and conflict. The person who's measured on the number should control the account. More importantly, strategic accounts make up a significant chunk of the company revenue goal. That goal translates into GTM quota, which means these accounts need to be quota'd. The question then becomes: where should these accounts sit organizationally? Options worth exploring: - Directly under Head of GTM, with dedicated account owners - As the org matures, a dedicated strategic accounts team with its own leadership - Within Sales, with Partnerships providing the orchestration layer For now, these accounts stay with their current owners (Q1, no changes). The structure question should be resolved as part of Q2 planning. **Regardless of ownership, strategic accounts should have:** - A single accountable owner - Partnerships support on orchestration, cross-BU strategy, and ecosystem context - Dedicated SE/FDE (allocation TBD with SE/FDE leadership) - **Cadence:** Customer check-ins (bi-weekly/monthly), monthly internal account reviews + founder updates, quarterly external QBRs, quarterly internal strategy deep-dives --- ## Transition plan: Q1 → Q2 **Now (rest of Q1):** - Align on Phase 1 rules (this doc) - No account changes, no quota changes - Start Q2 quota conversation immediately (target: decision by end of Feb) - Matt and Amanda comment on this doc, we iterate **March:** - Finalize Q2 quota structure for Sales and Partnerships — company revenue goal transfers into GTM quota; how quota is allocated across direct revenue vs. channel revenue (e.g., AWS/Azure distribution) within strategic accounts needs to be part of this discussion - Define KPIs for Partnerships (non-quota metrics) - Recommend including strategic accounts in quota — these accounts represent significant revenue and are part of the company target. That target translates into quota, which means strategic accounts need to be quota'd. - Scope new Sales AE hires against the North Star account split **Q2 launch:** - New quota structure live - Strategic account ownership and quota model goes live - Partnerships transitions to North Star definition (ecosystem insights, strategic deals, program management) - Sales owns all execution and forecastable revenue - Account team model goes live for top 5 strategic accounts - Review and adjust after 1 quarter --- ## Open questions for next discussion 1. **Strategic account ownership, quota & revenue structure:** Who owns strategic accounts (Sales, Head of GTM, dedicated team)? How is quota structured for direct revenue (e.g., Amazon API deal, PowerPoint integration) vs. channel revenue (AWS Marketplace, Azure distribution) within these accounts? Both feed into the company revenue goal, which transfers into GTM quota — the allocation model needs to be defined. This is the most consequential decision in the framework. 2. **Q2 quota for Partnerships:** KPIs only, or transitional joint quota on strategic accounts? 3. **Inference providers:** These are channel partners by definition (Partnerships motion), but also our largest API revenue source. The ownership question is tied to a bigger strategic decision: do we want to grow the reseller channel, wind it down in favor of direct, or find a middle ground? This needs to be discussed as part of the overall company strategy before we can assign clear quota ownership. 4. **Founder-owned pipeline:** Andi's deals should be transitioned to team ownership. The question is timing and sequencing — which deals move first, and to whom. --- *Updated by Seb after alignment call with Matt & Amanda, Feb 17 2026. Next step: comments from Matt & Amanda, then finalize Q2 quota discussion.* --- Older version: Sales × Partnerships — Definition & Account Ownership Framework "}

<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Executive Summary
	Three hires addressing three distinct gaps, sequenced by urgency. First priority: Senior AE in the US immediately — Sam is already at capacity covering the full US book, and there is no one else hunting the US enterprise pipeline. Second priority: Senior AE in EU/Freiburg to absorb Anthony's accounts as he transitions into the interim Head of GTM role, and a portion of Seb's accounts so Seb can take on hunting again — without this hire the team cannot operate, making it the highest-risk gap. New enterprise revenue has been slow, and unlocking Seb to hunt is strategically important for the company. Third priority: Mid-Level AE in EU/Freiburg to convert inbound leads and \$3.3M in lost mid-market deals across both EU and US. The EU data shows the most immediate mid-market opportunity but this role covers both geos at first.
</callout>
# Overview
This document outlines the sales hiring plan through mid-2026. Three hires — 1 in Q1, 2 in Q2 — each addressing a distinct, data-backed gap.
**Core principle for H1:** The EU and US markets currently require fundamentally different sales motions. EU has strong inbound demand that needs to be converted — the leads and pipeline are there, we just haven't had the people to work them. US requires more hunting and enterprise pipeline development — the market is there but awareness and inbound volume lag behind. As we continue building out the revenue engine and marketing ramps up, these motions should converge over time. But for now, we're hiring for the reality on the ground in each geo.
# Why These Hires, Why Now
This plan follows a conversation between Seb, Dave, and Andi where we pressure-tested where sales hires should sit geographically. Dave's view — that long-term the split should skew more US-heavy — is correct and the data supports it. The US lead gap (16% of all-time leads vs. EU's 34%) likely reflects a brand awareness and demand gen gap rather than a lack of market. We're aligned on that. The nuance is timing: right now, EU has 1,991 unconverted leads and \$3.3M in lost mid-level deals sitting on the table with nobody working them. The US opportunity is real but requires a more outbound-heavy motion with a senior hire until the marketing engine catches up. The plan below hires for both geos simultaneously, with each role running the motion that fits the market today.
The geo analysis across 5,894 leads, pipeline, lost deals, API revenue, and licensing customers paints a clear picture.
On the EU side, we have a conversion problem, not a demand problem. EU accounts for 34% of all leads (1,991) and that share has been accelerating — recent months show EU climbing to 40% of new leads. DACH alone contributes 530+ leads. Not all of these are premium leads — the volume includes a long tail of smaller inquiries — but even accounting for that, the EU lead pool is significantly larger than any other geo and undertouched. There's \$3.3M in lost mid-level deals across 19 accounts that were never properly worked, and EU mid-market API revenue is nearly zero despite 16 direct licensing customers. That's not a lack of market — it's a lack of coverage. The gap between EU lead volume and EU closed revenue is the single clearest hiring signal we have.
On the US side, the picture is different. Leads are steady at \~16% but the enterprise pipeline is enormous — Gamma (\$5.5M), the studio deals Sam is working, and a hunting list of 30+ prospects (Anthropic, Perplexity, Airbnb, [Booking.com](http://Booking.com), Expedia, Notion, Target, Etsy, Marriott, Spotify, etc.) — though it needs to be determined based on the go-to-market motion whether these are sales accounts or partnerships accounts. The mega-deals (Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple) are mainly partnerships-led right now, but as these progress they'll likely need dedicated senior sales support on deal closing and commercial structuring. All 5 current Sr AE accounts are EU-based, which means we're structurally underweight in the US at the enterprise level. Meanwhile Sam has been focused on big studio deals — once those convert, he'll be fully occupied managing them. This isn't a performance issue; it's a capacity and prioritization question driven by how we allocated resources.
Licensing customers are actually balanced across geos (US 17, EU 16, APAC 9), which reinforces that both markets have real commercial traction — they just need different motions to scale.
# Q1: Senior AE — US-based (ASAP)
**Motion: Hunter — Gamma, AI natives, US enterprises**
We need more US presence. Gamma (\$5.5M) needs to transition to this role. The US hunting list is massive and untouched at the enterprise level. Sam is at capacity with studio deals that will keep him occupied once they convert.
Profile: enterprise hunter, comfortable opening doors with AI-native companies and large US enterprises. Strong new-business orientation.
# Q2: Senior AE — EU / Freiburg HQ + Mid-Level AE — EU / Freiburg HQ
These two hires run in parallel — they address different segments but both solve critical EU coverage gaps.
## Senior AE — EU / Freiburg HQ
**Motion: Hybrid — account absorption + active hunting**
This hire unlocks capacity for both Seb and Anthony and solves the EU Sr AE coverage gap.
**What they absorb:**
Anthony's current sales accounts transfer to this person as he moves into the interim Head of GTM role. A portion of Seb's accounts transfer too — freeing Seb to focus on hunting and org-building rather than farming an existing book. This person becomes the EU account owner for a core set of existing customers while also actively developing new pipeline.
**Why hybrid matters:**
A pure farmer would leave a hunting gap in EU. A pure hunter couldn't absorb the account complexity we're handing over. The right profile is someone who's genuinely comfortable doing both — managing and expanding existing relationships while also opening new doors in the EU market. This is a harder profile to find but it's the right one for where we are.
Profile: enterprise hybrid — relationship-driven enough to own and expand complex accounts, commercially hungry enough to hunt new logos. Technical buyer fluency essential. DACH/EU market familiarity strongly preferred. Freiburg-based for HQ proximity.
## Mid-Level AE — EU / Freiburg HQ
**Motion: Inbound conversion — we have demand here and need this person ASAP!**
Inbound-led, data-driven motion. 1,991 leads to convert, \$3.3M in lost mid-level deals to re-engage. Can stretch to cover Korea/Japan mornings (3 Korean license customers already: D2/Naver, Verda, SNOW).
The gap between EU lead volume (34%) and EU closed revenue is exactly what this role fixes. We need to kick off the search in Q1 so the person can start as early in Q2 as possible.
Profile: data-driven inbound converter, farmer-leaning. DACH market knowledge is a plus.
# Next Steps
Align with overall company hiring goals for Q2.
</content>

content: {"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"⚡ Sales process","url":"https://www.notion.so/1eac370222d5800d8a73f01b9c21e7b3","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/1eac370222d5800d8a73f01b9c21e7b3 as of 2025-11-06T10:27:25.991Z: {"title":"Sales process"} This page visualizes our entire deal - quote - cash process. Please note that the process is currently subject to changes, especially with respect to the following points: - Onboarding - Calculation of fees - Invoicing We are currently working on consolidating and unifying the process between different tiers, since it can be simplified a lot in terms of implementation. ADDING THIS PAGE HERE: - NEED TO FIGURE OUT IF THIS NEEDS TO LIVE SEPARATELY # The BFL Transaction Flow This page maps out the current transaction flow of BFL, ie the entire process from a lead that contacts us (How do leads contact us?), over negotiating and closing a deal to how we track usage and invoice our customers. The goal of the above chart is to give a high level understanding of our process flow. How do Leads contact us? \[WIP\] **Deal Flow - Step by Step** Sam note: some detail here onboarding would be helpful. i.e. how to put in CRM (link), first call vs email response logic, what can we discuss when under NDA. 1. Inbound lead - see Qualifying a Deal tips [here](/1a6c370222d58057aad4db3de8b3e335?pvs=25) 2. Help the lead deciding on what works best for their use case: [API](/297c370222d580b293cde7dcd1dcd254?pvs=25) or weight license 1. put deal in CRM 2. Create a working directory with the company name of the customer on the [Sales Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1NzWdEBycyBh-hVf7qdnv4AtjCkb40sdP) (in case Sales Department) or [Partnerships Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1A3-13caXR5nJYVwpiN5chpm9mTQHDOob) (in case Partnerships Department) 3. Maintaining partner notes in [Notion](/26dc370222d58006b734ff07a00f5d17?pvs=25) 3. Pre-signed NDA can be found in [templates](/181c370222d58060bbfcfcd025443e22?pvs=25) (we prefer to use our paper) 1. Send for review by customer 2. Do review with legal team in case redlines 3. In case of redlines: Send via DocuSign 1. signatory on our end or 4. If using Partner/Customer paper, add to this Slack [workflow](slackChannel://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C08KH2QGF45) 4. Discuss pricing, see Monetization Models for [API](/244c370222d580a29627d2cde6a6c6d2?pvs=25) and [Licensing](/244c370222d5800b88b5d133be6da5d6?pvs=25) 5. Send first agreement draft (use this [Google Form](https://forms.gle/MToCZMnaPy6dQpcF9) to create a first draft) 6. Negotiate agreement terms, 1. mainly around indemnity, liability, etc., see our [current indemnification strategy](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11SIoEauerkX9n7638_0kZqyLcL4qxM2gXRurYokXm18/edit?tab=t.0) that is still WIP with respect to the exact criteria (ToDo: put on notion) 2. Loop in legal for agreement back and forth 3. put deals updates into the CRM/the partnerships folder and copy an updates in slack in case you need other people’s input or have issues with a certain decision. For such updates, use or and for legal requests use [https://black-forest-labs.slack.com/archives/C08KH2QGF45](https://black-forest-labs.slack.com/archives/C08KH2QGF45) 7. Once green send for signature with DocuSign 1. signatory on our end: or 2. enable to send a copy of the signed contract to yourself to access it 3. \[only for GmbH\] Send message to to ensure billing from GmbH 8. Move from [Licensing](https://app.attio.com/black-forest-labs/collection/345044a4-a69b-4eb9-85ff-039f2a1fdaab/view/43ce8ad3-9103-43d7-81af-77ecc98d4190)/[API](https://app.attio.com/black-forest-labs/collection/21049968-370f-4f71-9593-3eb50cefc57b/view/80694135-eb4a-4d7b-b798-c4adec4c3440) deals list to the respective Customer Success List ([Licensing](https://app.attio.com/black-forest-labs/collection/6a27e785-5074-4ca2-809b-c408768e1d67/view/7868f881-ef93-463f-95af-9ce652c4cbed)/[API)](https://app.attio.com/black-forest-labs/collection/4a16dea4-cbce-45e9-89fb-dafcb4cd3ef6/view/15123e0d-aefc-434a-b459-e88b098469e0) in CRM 9. Upload the signed contract to a folder `Contracts` as a subfolder of the the Customer folder created in step 2.b 10. Make a shortcut (i.e. a link to the executed contract doc) from the original document to the legal contracts folder (needed for the legal tool Legora), as described [here](/292c370222d58038874efeb942ced364?pvs=25). 11. Inform once you have signed an enterprise API/API reselling or Licensing deal 1. **for API deals** (we need to manually change the terms in the backend) 1. ask the customer about the email address linked to their API key. We need that one to set up the pricing appropriately in the backend 2. let Kyle (or someone from the eng team) and Andi know if you have in place SLAs in the contract 3. let Kyle (or someone from the eng team) and Andi know if you have special data retention policies in the contract 2. **for Licensing deals:** 1. if you have closed a revenue share deal since we need to add the customer to an email list for self reporting their revenue. 2. if you have closed a deal with a usage based component, with or with base fee since also here wee need to add the respective customers to an email list ***Missing: Enterprise questionnaires*** # Hosting Type BFL currently has two primary monetization mechanisms. 1. **API-only models:** Charging for its API which provides access to various [models](https://docs.bfl.ml/quick_start/introduction). The BFL API was generally made available in October 2024, and prices were set mostly based on comparables, with the goal to be at par or cheaper based on our comparable efficiency. The pricing is based on per image/inference basis. Monetization Models: API 2. **Commercial Weight Licensing:** Licensing the weights and inference code of the \[dev\] models for commercial use. The \[dev\] models are suited for customers that have the ability/desire to customize/fine-tune the models (weights can be downloaded from GitHub/Hugging Face), leverage the large open-source community around AI, and scale efficiently for larger volumes as these models run on a customer’s own infrastructure. For smaller volumes we are offering the self-serve [option](https://bfl.ai/pricing/licensing) (\$1K for up to 100K images/month) to suit SMB use-cases, but in the Enterprise (or other customers who don’t want to accept our click-through terms) there is the challenge of trying to weigh volume vs. value based on a customer’s specific use case. We are currently discussing how we may scale this option. 1. Considerations when pricing the \[dev\] model: 1. Pricing can be based on the list price on our [self serve portal](https://bfl.ai/licensing): Can be used for providing i) the rationale for a flat fee (based on estimated volume numbers of the customer) or ii) as a basis for offering a more customized combination of base fee and per-image fees for usage based contracts. **Note: volume based pricing really only works for high volume use cases. For low-volume use cases, where the customer extracts a lot of value from the model, we should not use volume as a pricing rationale. ** 2. Since the customer hosts the model in their own infrastructure (on prem or in a cloud), BFL does not have any production cost for the images the customer generates 3. Additional reasons for justifying cost: 1. **BFL’s training cost** for the \[dev\] model needs to be covered. 2. **Weight access and the associated flexibility** to finetune and optimize 3. **If offered: support**. BFL helps the customer with one or more things of (more things possible ofc, depending on the customer’s needs) 1. hosting 2. finetuning 3. inference optimization 4. prompting/prompt processing 5. Settting up the model UI **Note: **Can ofc only be brought up if actually offered and the customers needs it 4. **Access to the open-source (OS) ecosystem: **When buying a commercial \[dev\] license, the customer gets the right to use all finetunes based on the respective model as well (since they come under the same license). Monetization Models: Licensing \[WIP\] # Contract Type Agreement templates are here [drive.google.com](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1nyW6pUruVWYqBv81Q8wfxN6P4n2qMyN0) ## API ## Commercial Weight license Monetization Models: Commercial Weight License ## Contract variation In general we offer two types of fees - with a monthly minimum commit, which is usually a monthly base-fee, or without. We implement a monthly base fee when a customer wants to secure better per image rates. ### API While we should always try to lock-in future revenue, for some customers setting up a base fee for the API is not feasible, e.g. wix or PropTexx. With PropTexx we’ve found a solution to make BFL the only provider for image editing tasks, see . Especially when we release new models we need to be fast in winning customers as the market is highly competitive. In case you cannot secure a base-fee you can ask for internal approval to set up an agreement without base-fee. It should still be worse commercial terms than with a base-fee. Prepaid credits are another option we can offer to customers who would not like to commit to a monthly base-fee, mostly because of uncertainty about future volume. These prepaid credits come with a discount compared to credits purchased self-serve. More info here ### Dev license So far we didn’t have a case where a customer got discount rates for dev without a base fee. API discounts are here and dev discounts can be found here . ## Legal variations TO DO: need to create a page guiding through our API Enterprise agreement TO DO: need to create a page guiding through our dev license agreement # Onboarding You’ve closed a deal - congrats! Now we need to onboard the customer to make sure that we are billing them and also apply the agreed pricing. In case a customer is using the self-serve license or our API with online terms and prices there is no need for you to onboard them, it’s automatically in the background. ## API 1. Please launch the deal in our CRM Attio and fill out all the fields in the “API customers” list. 2. Please upload the signed agreement in the “Customers” folder on GDrive [drive.google.com](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1NzWdEBycyBh-hVf7qdnv4AtjCkb40sdP). In case there is no specific folder the customer yet, please create one. The name of the folder is the customers name, e.g. “ByteDance”. In case there are different entities within a customer, create a sub-folder, e.g. “TikTok US”. Within this folder, create another folder called “contracts”. Upload the agreement here. Our accountants Attivo have access to this folder and will use it for billing. 3. In case there are different rates compared to the public rates give a ping. He will then update the pricing in the API backend for the customer. 4. Legal & commercial Ops 1. WIP: In case the customer has a DPA, add them to the DPA list (which is still WIP and needs to be created). 2. WIP: In case the customer opted out of training, add them to the no-training-list (which is still WIP and needs to be created). 3. Cluster Region Please note the inference region / cluster location to the backend team. 4. WIP: Need to create a list for customers contracting with German entity BFL GmbH 5. WIP: We need to create a calendar / list for renewal dates. 6. WIP: Need logo list. ## Dev commercial license 1. Please launch the deal in our CRM Attio and fill out all the fields in the “Licensing customers” list. 2. Please upload the signed agreement in the “Customers” folder on GDrive [drive.google.com](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1NzWdEBycyBh-hVf7qdnv4AtjCkb40sdP). In case there is no specific folder the customer yet, please create one. The name of the folder is the customers name, e.g. “ByteDance”. In case there are different entities within a customer, create a sub-folder, e.g. “TikTok US”. Within this folder, create another folder called “contracts”. Upload the agreement here. Our accountants Attivo have access to this folder and will use it for billing. 3. Legal and Commercial Ops: 1. WIP: We need to create a list attribute in Attio ## "}
